astro-ai-designed-trajectory-flown.title: Missions fly AI-designed trajectories
astro-ai-designed-trajectory-flown.description: A lunar, cislunar or deep-space mission whose baseline trajectory and contingency set were produced primarily by an AI design agent and verified by the flight-dynamics team.
astro-ai-designed-trajectory-flown.why: Designs freeze 6-18 months before launch (general), and there are many small lunar and cislunar missions (more than 30 planned 2024-2030), whose launches routinely slip months to years (physclock slip table). Chain (S2): design agents trusted by flight-dynamics teams 2027-28 -> an agent-designed baseline accepted and re-verified 2028 -> design freeze 6-18 months before launch -> launch 2029 with normal slip margin -> public credit in a press kit or AAS/AIAA paper. S3 cannot compress the manifest, so it matches S2. Small lunar and cislunar missions are outside customers: as of late June 2026 SpaceX had closed new Transporter and Bandwagon bookings beyond late 2028 or early 2029 (SpaceNews; TODO(source)), and Mach33 Launch Keystone v1.3 opens Starship spare capacity to customers in 2031. Designing the path stays cheap; flying it now waits on customer access (physclock-customer-launch-access), so these missions slip months to years and the odds reach Medium in 2031, not 2029.
astro-ai-designed-trajectory-flown.strongest_case_small: Attribution: flight-dynamics teams re-optimize in heritage tools, so the 'AI-designed' label may be cosmetic and the delta-v or time benefit marginal.
astro-ai-designed-trajectory-flown.signpost: A mission press kit or AAS/AIAA paper crediting an AI agent for the baseline trajectory.

astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.title: Proof-backed guidance software in operational spacecraft
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.description: Operational uncrewed spacecraft (constellation satellites, landers, servicers) run GNC or collision-avoidance software whose safety case relies materially on AI-produced machine-checked proofs.
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.status_oct2026: None known. Formal methods in space flight software remain niche (NASA research programs, some ESA work). Commercial operators update fleet software frequently without regulator review of the code (general).
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.why: Uncrewed commercial systems need no tool qualification, so adoption is a cost decision: if proofs cut V&V cost and shorten update cycles, software-defined fleets adopt first. This precedes crewed certification by years. Chain (S2): proof agents and FDIR model checking 2027 -> GNC toolchain 2028 -> first operator states that flight GNC or collision-avoidance code ships with machine-checked proofs 2029. S3 equals S2 through 2028, so adoption in the same year as the toolchain (the old S3 2028) is not credible; S3 is 2029, with High kept because cognitive work is near-free from 2029. verif-constellation-verified-updates is a fleet-wide instance of this node and is dated and banded no earlier or higher.
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.strongest_case_small: Testing culture is entrenched and works; one high-profile incident with a 'proven' but mis-specified module could stall adoption.
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.signpost: An operator or prime stating publicly that flight GNC or collision-avoidance code ships with machine-checked proofs.
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic: S3 2028 -> 2029 (adoption-gated; its toolchain prerequisite moves to S3 2028; S3 equals S2 until 2028). astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.title: Autonomous cross-operator collision avoidance
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.description: Satellites of at least two large constellation operators (for example Starlink, Amazon Leo, OneWeb; Guowang and Qianfan would need a US-China agreement) detect, negotiate and execute avoidance maneuvers autonomously under a shared protocol with formal safety guarantees, in operational use at the active population then in orbit (roughly 25,000-40,000 active satellites by 2030-31 on current deployment paths, judgment) and analyzed to scale to 100,000-plus.
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.status_oct2026: Starlink is autonomous within its own fleet; ESA CREAM's AutoCA and AutoSTM components are in pilot use with in-orbit demos being prepared; cross-operator coordination is manual or bilateral; there is no US-China ephemeris sharing (Kinetica-1 payload close pass to Starlink-6079, Dec 2025; reported distance about 200 m, unverified). SpaceX Stargaze (Jan 30, 2026) turns about 30,000 Starlink star trackers into an SSA network (~30 million transits a day, orbit estimates and conjunction predictions within minutes) and offers screening to other operators free. Five moderate-to-high-risk Starlink conjunctions clustered on Aug 9-13, 2026, one reported at a 24% maximum collision probability (a worst-case screening metric, not an operator Pc; one of the five was Starlink-Starlink).
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.why: The coordination math (astro-coordination-protocols) is ready around 2028 in S2 and certified screening in 2029. No regulator approves bilateral machine-to-machine coordination (the FCC requires disclosure and reports), so the gate is adoption: a standard (CCSDS, ISO or CONFERS; typically 3-5 years, general) or a bilateral protocol agreement, then multi-operator software rollout. Chain (S2): protocols 2028 and certified screening 2029 -> draft standard or bilateral maneuver-intent agreement 2030 (3-5 years at the tree's 1.5-2x regulatory/standards multiplier, identical in S2 and S3) -> software rollout across two operators -> operational 2031. S3 gets 2030 from cheaper guarantees and faster rollout, not from faster standards or politics. Inclusion of Chinese constellations is a geopolitical gate the math cannot move. SpaceX's free hosted screening (Stargaze) is a non-formal route that removes much of the demand for a formally guaranteed shared protocol, which is why S2 is Low. Proof-carrying GNC code accelerates but does not gate: Starlink already maneuvers autonomously without it.
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.strongest_case_small: Bilateral automation between Western operators will arrive without formal guarantees and will handle most of the risk, and free hosted screening (Stargaze) may become the de facto shared layer; proofs add assurance, not capability.
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.signpost: A public automated maneuver-coordination agreement between two megaconstellation operators; an FCC license condition requiring machine-readable maneuver intent.
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.revision_note: E-safe-orbits (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. S1 '>2031' -> 2033 (S1 screening 2031, then standards work and rollout). band_2035 S2 Low -> Medium. S4 = S3. | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2 Medium 2032 (seed 2033): a bilateral maneuver-intent agreement does not need a standards body, and S3 gains only a year on guarantees and rollout, so S2 trails S3 (Medium 2031, was 2030) by one year. Skeptic (free Stargaze screening makes formal guarantees optional, 2034) against advocate (informal bilateral coordination already exists, 2031): 2032. Bands unchanged.
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.note_2035: S1 arrives about 2033, two years after its screening tool. By 2035 two Western operators probably coordinate machine to machine, but free hosted screening may make formal guarantees optional, so bands stay Medium. S4 adds nothing because standards and adoption set the pace.
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.gate_note: A shared protocol agreed and rolled out across operators (adoption) binds; certified catalog-scale screening (formalization) is the runner-up.

astro-cislunar-traffic-management.title: Traffic management service for Earth-Moon space
astro-cislunar-traffic-management.description: An operational catalog, conjunction-screening and coordination service for cislunar space (low lunar orbit, NRHO, DRO, transfers, Earth-Moon L1/L2), comparable to TraCSS for LEO.
astro-cislunar-traffic-management.status_oct2026: JPL's MADCAP screens NASA spacecraft at the Moon and Mars against other spacecraft's predicted ephemerides (first described in 2012) and accepts ephemerides from non-NASA operators (NASA CARA). No catalog of non-cooperative cislunar objects and no service covering transfers and Earth-Moon L1/L2 exist. NASA paused Gateway in its current form on Mar 24, 2026, redirecting resources to a roughly $20B, seven-year lunar surface base (NASA via 33FG); Moonlight relay and navigation services 2028-2030; AFRL's Oracle-Prime cislunar demonstrator is past PDR (Dec 2025) with no launch date announced.
astro-cislunar-traffic-management.why: Algorithms are ready by 2028-29 in S2; space-based cislunar sensors and a funded operator are the gates, and US civil SSA funding is under pressure (Office of Space Commerce FY2027 request down about 80%). Screening tens of cislunar objects uses ordinary propagation, so certified million-object screening, provably safe coordination protocols and a certified stability atlas improve the service but do not gate it. Chain (S2): certified collision-probability math 2028 -> cislunar tracking with honest uncertainty in chaotic dynamics (astro-cislunar-od-uq, 2028) -> algorithms ready 2028-29 -> space-based cislunar sensors and a funded operator, which AI math does not supply -> a basic service 2031 at the earliest. Band (F2 audit): S2 Low, down from Medium. The P7 default is Speculative, AI math supplies neither gate, Gateway's pause removes the main planned NRHO traffic, and the S2 earliest year (2031) leaves no slack, so a basic military or commercial service by 2031 is plausible but less likely than not. S3 Medium (judgment): one year of slack and faster physical clocks. S1 Low. Bands are judgments, not computed probabilities.
astro-cislunar-traffic-management.strongest_case_small: Cislunar traffic remains tens of objects; demand for a formal service may lag the capability; Gateway's pause in its current form removes the most congested planned orbit for now.
astro-cislunar-traffic-management.signpost: A Space Force, NASA or commercial announcement of a cislunar catalog or screening service; extension of TraCSS-like screening beyond GEO.

astro-leo-safety-at-scale.title: Low Earth orbit stays safe at 100,000 satellites
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.description: Collision risk and avoidance-maneuver burden per satellite stop rising, and begin to fall, while the active LEO population grows 3-10x toward 50,000-100,000-plus.
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.status_oct2026: Maneuvers per Starlink satellite rose to more than 40 per year (Jun 2025-May 2026), with yearly totals more than 3x 2024; ESA puts LEO collision risk up 20% since 2024; close approaches under 1 km occur every 22 minutes in the 550 km Starlink shell (Thiele et al.). SpaceX Stargaze (Jan 2026) adds minutes-latency tracking of the trackable population, and Starlink's lowering from 550 to 480 km is under way during 2026.
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.why: AI math contributes three levers: certified Pc (fewer false alarms, though the maneuver count is set mainly by each operator's threshold policy), verified coordination (no maneuver-into-each-other events) and better capacity models (P5 confidence that informs policy but removes no risk physically). The dominant residual risk is about 1.2 million untracked 1-10 cm fragments that no math can see (astro-small-debris-catalog), plus drag-forecast limits and non-cooperating operators. Heavy launch cadence is a stressor, not an accelerant: it grows the population and the conjunction rate. The physical gate (sensors that track smaller objects, and their deployment) binds, so even S2 does not deliver this by 2031. Chain (S3): certified Pc 2028 and certified screening 2029 -> cross-operator autonomous collision avoidance 2030 -> screening-grade small-debris catalog 2030 -> at least two semiannual reports with conjunctions per satellite flat or falling while the fleet grows -> earliest evidence 2031, and only for the tracked population. Sensors compress about 1.0-1.3x and politics 1.0x even in S3, so S3 is Low.
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.strongest_case_small: Most per-satellite risk reduction will come from non-math moves already under way: lower altitudes (Starlink 550 to 480 km; SpaceX cites a more-than-80% cut in ballistic decay time at solar minimum, unverified), five-year disposal rules and better sensors.
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.signpost: Conjunctions under 1 km per satellite per year (threshold-independent) flat or falling while the fleet grows; ESA's 2027-28 environment reports showing LEO risk growth slowing.
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.revision_note: E-safe-orbits (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. S1 '>2031' -> 2034 (a year after S1 cross-operator avoidance, 2033). S2 '>2031' -> 2032 (a year after its 2031 prerequisites). band_2035 S1 Speculative -> Low, S2-S4 Low -> Medium. S4 = S3. | E-safe-orbits resolver (2026-10-07): band_2035 S2 Medium -> Low (skeptic): 2032-35 is the launch clock's peak growth, the metric scales with shell density, and a child of three prerequisites that are each Medium by 2035 in S2 should not match them. S3 and S4 stay Medium. | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S3/S4 Medium 2034 (seed 2033): all three hard prerequisites reach Medium in 2031, and the evidence needs two semiannual reports, so the joint odds pass 30% around 2034. Skeptic (fleet growth outpaces screening) against advocate (Cycle 26 drag clears lower shells): 2034. S2/S1 Low only. Bands unchanged.
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.note_2035: By 2035 the tracked population can be screened and coordinated in S3 and S4, and Cycle 26 drag clears lower shells faster. In S2 the fleet grows fastest in 2032-35, close approaches per satellite rise with shell density, and the three hard prerequisites land only in 2031, so S2 stays Low. Untracked 1-10 cm debris and non-cooperating operators remain. The cm-custody, removal and cross-bloc soft edges bear on staying safe after the first evidence. They do not move the year. astro-capacity-licensing.title: Licensing satellites against an orbital capacity budget
astro-capacity-licensing.description: Regulators (FCC, national agencies, eventually ITU) license megaconstellations against an aggregate, model-based orbital capacity or risk budget, using verifiable debris-evolution and conjunction models.
astro-capacity-licensing.status_oct2026: The FCC has a five-year post-mission disposal rule (2022) but no aggregate capacity regime. Its 2020 orbital-debris FNPRM sought comment on a system-wide (aggregate) collision-risk assessment for multi-satellite systems using the ODMSP 0.001 probability as a threshold or safe harbor; the Space Bureau refreshed that record in May 2024 (comments June-July 2024), and no order had been adopted by Oct 2026. SpaceX filed for up to 1 million orbital data center satellites at 500-2,000 km on Jan 30, 2026; China filed for roughly 200k satellites at the ITU (Dec 2025).
astro-capacity-licensing.why: Filings at the million-satellite scale press for a capacity framework this decade regardless of AI. AI math changes whether the framework rests on defensible, auditable models (proven thresholds, quantified uncertainty) or on rules of thumb, a P5 contribution to quality, not timing. The closest FCC step has been pending since 2020, and the 2026 FCC moved fast toward faster licensing (performance-based EPFD rules Apr 30, Part 100 Jul 22, NEPA exclusion late Sep), not toward caps. Uncompressed rulemaking (notice, comment, order) takes 2-4 years (general); at the tree's 1.5-2x regulatory multiplier, identical in S2 and S3, an order by 2031 needs an NPRM by about 2029, and politics runs at 1.0x, so S3 cannot beat S2. A license condition on the 1-million-satellite application is the faster route (see signpost). Capped at Medium because it needs regulator acceptance; Low on the record above. Verified million-object screening helps but is not required: aggregate-risk rules use environment models and disclosure.
astro-capacity-licensing.strongest_case_small: Policy will be set by politics and spectrum economics; regulators can adopt simple per-operator rules without sophisticated models.
astro-capacity-licensing.signpost: An FCC notice of proposed rulemaking or license condition using an aggregate collision-risk or capacity metric, triggered by the 1-million-satellite application.
astro-capacity-licensing.revision_note: E-safe-orbits (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. S1 '>2031' -> 2032 (S1 debris models 2030; politics runs at 1.0x). band_2035 all Low -> Medium (four more years of filings pressure; regulatory cap Medium). S4 = S3. | E-safe-orbits resolver (2026-10-07): band_2035 S1 Medium -> Low and note rewritten (skeptic): the regulatory cap is a ceiling and does not license the top value. S2-S4 stay Medium on filing pressure. | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2-S4 Medium 2034 (seed 2033): Medium needs an aggregate-risk NPRM or a license condition by about 2032, and an order takes two more years at 1.0x politics; the 2026 FCC moved toward faster licensing instead. Skeptic (2035) against advocate (another national regulator acts first, 2032): 2034. Bands unchanged.
astro-capacity-licensing.note_2035: Medium needs an aggregate-risk NPRM, or a license condition on the 1-million-satellite application, by about 2032. The 2026 FCC moved toward faster licensing instead. Another national regulator acting first is the main upside. S1 stays Low because its debris models arrive later and rulemaking takes 2-4 years. S4 adds nothing because rulemaking binds.
astro-capacity-licensing.gate_note: Rulemaking (regulatory) binds; defensible debris-evolution inputs (data) are the runner-up.

astro-gnc-assurance-cost.title: Verified autonomy becomes cheap
astro-gnc-assurance-cost.description: At early adopters the cost of verifying GNC and autonomy software falls by about half, making formally assured autonomy standard for smallsats and commercial landers rather than a NASA-only luxury. At program level (DAL-A rigor, including integration and system test) software cost falls about 2x (1.8-2.4x; claim moved here from verif-assurance-cost-collapse); certified DO-178C or NPR 7150.2 Class A programs realize it only after certification credit (infra-tool-qualification). Re-verification turnaround for software-only changes falls from weeks to days, but total verification calendar time falls only about 20-30%, because HIL and integration testing bind.
astro-gnc-assurance-cost.status_oct2026: Formal methods are confined to a few high-value programs (general).
astro-gnc-assurance-cost.why: Program cost model (general, our assumptions; verification-domain cost table). Starting shares of a Level-A software budget with S2 multipliers: requirements and design 20% x0.7-1.0, code 10% x0.3, unit verification 35% x0.1 (replaced by proof), software integration 15% x0.4, hardware/software integration and system test 20% x0.8. With x0.7 on requirements the total is 42.5% of baseline (2.4x cheaper); with x1.0, reflecting DO-333's shift of effort into formal specification and its review, it is 48.5% (2.1x). Central about 2x. Under S1 the total is about 70-80% of baseline; under S3, with AI-run test rigs, about 30-35%. Calendar time follows the physical clock: experiment and test compress only 1.1-1.3x in S2, and HIL rig time often sets schedule. Chain (S2): per-line cost collapse 2028 -> proof-backed GNC at early uncrewed adopters 2029 -> first published program cost comparison 2030-31. Commercial uncrewed fleets realize it first; regulated crewed programs last.

auton-mass-action-permanence.title: Reaction networks that never lose an ingredient
auton-mass-action-permanence.description: Family 149 claims boundedness and persistence for every finite weakly reversible mass-action network with positive constant rates: each solution from a strictly positive start stays between epsilon and 1/epsilon for all time, with epsilon depending on network, rates and initial state (the catalog headline says permanence, the stronger uniform property). Once independently confirmed it becomes a theorem-level guarantee for idealized closed chemical and microbial loop models.
auton-mass-action-permanence.status_oct2026: Family 149, T1 per the release overview and the analyst catalog (no entry in lean/formalization.yaml). Newer detail found in the repo: lean/docs/149.md describes a Lean formalization of global boundedness and persistence with a Comparator statement (ComparatorChallenges/MassAction.lean). If that holds up it would be T3 for the formal part. No outside Comparator run reported as of 2026-10-07; repo has a single commit (Oct 6). MassAction.json targets OAI.Problem326.global_bounded_persistent_solution, and 149 is absent from formalization.yaml main_results. Statement-gap modifier: the headline stays T1, and only the formal part could reach T3 or T4.
auton-mass-action-permanence.premise_tier: T1 (149 has no Lean main result in the catalog)
auton-mass-action-permanence.why: Persistence and permanence of weakly reversible networks sit at the core of chemical reaction network theory (the global attractor conjecture family, open for decades, general). 'Achieved' here means independently checked (Comparator run plus statement audit) or reconstructed by CRN theorists. Because a formal statement already exists, verification is a checking task, not a research task; under S2/S3 checking bandwidth is abundant. Under S1 the field is niche and may not be prioritized by volunteer checkers, so a checking-only judgment would be Medium in S1 and High in S2/S3. Conditional: the catalog lists no Lean main result for 149, so the premise is T1 and the band is one step below a checking-only judgment.
auton-mass-action-permanence.strongest_case_small: Real life-support loops are not closed weakly reversible mass-action systems: they include harvesting, control inputs, light-limited and saturating kinetics (Monod, Michaelis-Menten), growth and death, contamination and small-population noise. The epsilon in the theorem depends on network, rates and initial state and may be numerically useless. The result raises confidence in a modeling idealization, not in any habitat.
auton-mass-action-permanence.signpost: An independent Comparator run on MassAction.lean posted to Hexagon or by a recognized checker (Buzzard, Tao, Mathlib maintainers), plus reuse by CRN theorists within 12 months.
auton-mass-action-permanence.calibration_note: A3: T1 premise rule: the catalog lists no Lean main result for family 149, so the premise is T1 (not T3) and confirmation rests on an unverified manuscript. One band down in every scenario: Medium/High/High -> Low/Medium/Medium; why now says conditional. A4: Why text updated to match the A3 years and bands; it had still described the v0 values. A3's conditional sentence is kept.
auton-mass-action-permanence.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Auditor (grounding): the description now states the formal scope (boundedness plus persistence with a state-dependent epsilon) rather than uniform permanence, and the status notes the statement gap (tr-position-2). auton-contact-wellposedness.title: Rigorous theory of frictional contact
auton-contact-wellposedness.description: Existence, uniqueness or explicit selection rules for rigid and near-rigid bodies with many frictional contacts and impacts (the Painleve paradox regime), plus convergence proofs and rates for the time-stepping schemes that robot simulators actually use. This is the mathematics under every grasp, docking latch, connector mate, wheel-soil contact and assembly simulation.
auton-contact-wellposedness.status_oct2026: Open (general). Rigid-body Coulomb friction can admit no solution or many; measure-differential-inclusion time-stepping schemes (Stewart-Trinkle, Anitescu-Potra) converge only in weak senses and without practical rates. No catalog family addresses it. The pattern is the same as family 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness): an equation that does not by itself pin down the physics, so a selection principle is needed.
auton-contact-wellposedness.why: Outside teams can pose this only once research-grade math is purchasable (S2: 2027). It is a hard but well-specified applied-analysis problem of the kind the release shows the capability can now reach (cf. the forced Navier-Stokes blowup claim of Sep 2026 and the PDE families). Under S2's 6-9 month doubling of solvable depth, a convergence theorem for at least one widely used regularization with computable rates is plausible by 2028. A negative result (nonuniqueness in configurations robots actually hit) would be equally useful: it tells simulator developers where results are artifacts of the chosen regularization.
auton-contact-wellposedness.strongest_case_small: Practitioners already get usable results from compliant contact tuned to test data; the residual sim-to-real gap in grasping and assembly is dominated by unknown parameters (friction coefficients, dust adhesion, cable stiffness), which a theorem about idealized Coulomb friction does not touch.
auton-contact-wellposedness.signpost: An AI-produced paper resolving a named contact-mechanics question (convergence with rates for a mainstream time-stepping scheme, or classification of Painleve non-uniqueness) accepted in an applied-math or mechanics venue, or formalized in Lean, by end-2028.
auton-contact-wellposedness.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (timing): S3 2027 -> 2028. The only prerequisite, cap-research-math-public, is 2027 in both S2 and S3, and capability.json gives S3 the same capability as S2 through 2028 (~150 h horizon at end-2027). A genuinely open nonsmooth-mechanics problem cannot be solved earlier in S3 than in S2 while capability is identical. Bands unchanged. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): S1 year >2031 -> 2032; band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High. S3 equals S2 through 2028, then recursion brings High to 2030. S1 trails S2 by four years (2032/2033). Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

auton-contact-wellposedness.gate_note: The mathematics itself binds; checking a nonsmooth-mechanics convergence proof (formalization) is the runner-up.

auton-granular-wellposedness.title: Reliable equations for flowing lunar soil
auton-granular-wellposedness.description: Prove well-posedness (or pinpoint ill-posedness and its minimal regularization) for continuum models of dense granular flow such as mu(I) rheology and nonlocal granular-fluidity models, so excavation, conveying, berm-building and plume-cratering codes converge under mesh refinement for physical reasons rather than tuned numerics.
auton-granular-wellposedness.status_oct2026: Open (general). mu(I) rheology is known to be ill-posed at low and high inertial numbers (Barker et al., J. Fluid Mech. 2015, general); nonlocal models exist without a global well-posedness theory. No catalog family addresses granular media.
auton-granular-wellposedness.why: Regolith handling is simulated today with DEM (10^6-10^8 particles, days to weeks per design point, general) or with continuum/MPM codes built on rheologies that are not well-posed and are regularized ad hoc. Continuum/MPM codes are already roughly 100-1,000x cheaper than DEM (general), and a well-posedness theorem does not make them cheaper. What it adds is confidence that results converge under mesh refinement for physical rather than numerical reasons (P5; tl-position-2), so the cheaper continuum codes can stand in for DEM in excavation and sintering design with less calibration doubt. Under S2 this is an AI-applied-math problem of 2028-29 difficulty; S3 a year earlier. It accelerates the calibrated regolith model but does not gate it.
auton-granular-wellposedness.strongest_case_small: Engineers already regularize empirically and DEM is adequate for bucket-scale design. The spread in excavation energy between plausible ice forms (52x within ice-cemented simulant alone as ice rises from 1 to 12 wt%, and two to three orders of magnitude between ice-cemented and pressure-sintered simulant) dwarfs any modeling error a theorem removes.
auton-granular-wellposedness.signpost: An AI-produced well-posedness or ill-posedness theorem for a named granular rheology, then adoption of the selected model in an open-source MPM or continuum granular code.
auton-granular-wellposedness.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (claim): the why had credited the theorem with a 100-1,000x speedup over DEM. Continuum codes already have that cost advantage, so the theorem's contribution is confidence (P5, tl-position-2), not speed. Pathway stays P1->P5. Skeptic and auditor (fact): the '52x across plausible polar ice forms' wording is corrected. 52x is the spread across ice content within ice-cemented simulant; across forms the spread is far larger (doi:10.1007/s44461-026-00015-w). Advocate and skeptic: the edge into auton-granular-regolith-model is now soft. S1 2033/2034. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.title: Mission planners that are correct by design
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.description: Planners, schedulers and fault responses generated automatically from temporal-logic specifications (reactive synthesis, energy/mean-payoff games, probabilistic model checking) at the scale of real surface operations, each shipped with a proof that the plan meets the spec under the modeled environment.
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.status_oct2026: Theory mature, flight use rare: synthesis works for small specs, but abstractions (terrain, energy, comm windows) and specs are built by scarce experts (general). Family 104 claims quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games. Only the randomized quasipolynomial mean-payoff algorithm and a counterexample to Truffet's procedure are formalized (T3, unchecked); the stochastic-game part is T1, conditional. Mean-payoff ('energy') objectives match battery-constrained rovers.
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.premise_tier: n/a (capability); 104 is T3 for the randomized mean-payoff part only and T1 (conditional) for the stochastic-game part
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.why: The cost of synthesis is building a sound abstraction and a correct spec, which is exactly bespoke expert math. An agent that proposes the abstraction, proves it sound, writes the spec, synthesizes the controller and emits Lean or model-checker certificates turns months of formal-methods work into days. 'Achieved' = a synthesized planner for a realistic multi-day surface scenario (energy, thermal, comm windows, faults) with machine-checked certificate, produced with under 10% specialist effort. Family 104 changes the theoretical ceiling for stochastic and mean-payoff games, but practical solvers (Zielonka, strategy iteration) already handle realistic sizes, so its own contribution is P3, small.
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.strongest_case_small: Mission operations culture values human-readable, human-reviewed plans; even the AI-planned Perseverance drives were validated by simulation, not proof. Specs, not proofs, are the hard part, and a proof of the wrong property adds little (tl-position-6; tr-position-2).
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.signpost: A CLPS, LTV or NASA surface payload announces spec-to-plan synthesized autonomy in flight software, or ESA/NASA solicitations require correct-by-construction planners.

auton-ops-planning-ceilings.title: Known limits for robot fleet scheduling
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.description: Hardness and optimality results tell surface-ops planners which multi-robot task-allocation, scheduling, partitioning and depot-siting problems can be solved near-optimally and which cannot, so effort moves to problem structure, exact solvers on small instances and heuristics.
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.status_oct2026: 102 Unique Games Conjecture (T3) fixes optimal approximation ratios for many labeling and partitioning problems; 125 metric k-median threshold 1+2/e (T3) bounds depot, charging-pad and relay siting; 124 polynomial-time unit-job scheduling on three identical machines with precedence (T1 per release overview; repo lean/docs/124.md lists a Comparator statement, so possibly T3); 110 optimal randomized k-server (T1) and 111 one-sample matroid prophet inequalities (T1; competitive ratio 2^-310, no polynomial-time implementation asserted) for online dispatch. lean/docs/110.md and 111.md also carry Comparator statements (KServer.lean, MatroidProphet.lean) that are absent from formalization.yaml, so they stay T1. For 125 the yaml main result is the KMedianRecovery (below-2) statement; the 1+2/e threshold appears only in lean/docs/125.md (KMedianThreshold.lean).
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.pathway: P3 (102 hardness; 125 lower bound) + P4 (124, 110, 111 and the 125 algorithm; constants unstated or galactic, not counted as practical)
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.premise_tier: T3 (102, 125); T1 (124, 110, 111): conditional for those parts
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.why: A lunar base with dozens of robots and crew visits every six months is an online scheduling and allocation problem with precedence constraints. Ceilings act in months: they stop teams chasing general-purpose 'optimal' fleet planners and let them judge vendor claims. 124 is a cute fit for a three-robot team with precedence-constrained unit tasks. The parts resting on 124, 110 and 111 are conditional (T1).
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.strongest_case_small: Real instances are small and structured and are solved well by MILP/CP solvers; worst-case hardness and galactic constants (111's 2^-310) say little about them. Most of these results were already believed; the change is from belief to theorem.
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.signpost: Planning papers or vendor documentation for lunar and Mars operations cite these ceilings when scoping fleet planners; otherwise no measurable change expected.

auton-certified-contact-sim.title: Contact simulators with error bars
auton-certified-contact-sim.description: Physics engines for grasping, latching, digging and assembly that carry proven convergence and computable error bounds for stated friction and compliance parameters, so a simulation run can count as verification evidence instead of a physical test.
auton-certified-contact-sim.status_oct2026: Not available (general): mainstream engines (MuJoCo, Drake, PhysX/Isaac) use different contact regularizations with no certified error bounds. Not addressed by the catalog.
auton-certified-contact-sim.why: Space robotics qualification leans on physical testing in low-fidelity analogs (air-bearing tables, parabolic flights, dirty thermal-vacuum chambers). A certified simulator, validated against a modest set of vacuum and dust experiments, could replace a large share of those tests with analysis. The math is cognitive-clock work under S2; the binding gate is the validation experiments for dusty, cold, vacuum contact.
auton-certified-contact-sim.strongest_case_small: Error bounds will be conditional on parameters measured in the lab; for lunar dust (electrostatic adhesion, cold welding, abrasion) parameter uncertainty dominates and certified numerics only shrink the smaller error term.
auton-certified-contact-sim.signpost: A contact solver released with a formal convergence proof (e.g. inside Drake or MuJoCo), and a NASA ISAM or Moon Base program accepting its results as verification evidence.

auton-ecls-reliability-uq.title: Honest reliability numbers for life support
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.description: System-of-systems reliability, sparing and crew-maintenance models for regenerative life support with Bayesian uncertainty from ISS failure history: the analysis that decides how many tonnes of spares a Mars crew carries and how much crew time maintenance eats.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.status_oct2026: Methods exist (Langley's EMAT, semi-Markov sparing, Bayesian estimation) but scale poorly to system-of-systems; last public ECLSS reliability data release was 2004 (ICES 2025). A 2025 Bayesian study estimates 907 crew-hours of ECLSS maintenance (~45 min/day) and availability 0.9687 for a 1,200-day mission. 'Solved in principle, expert-scarce and data-limited'.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.why: In the 2025 study the 5th-percentile spares mass corresponds to a 10x MTBF improvement, so the uncertainty band spans an order of magnitude in MTBF. A model that uses every ISS failure record, component physics and shelf-life data, with uncertainty propagated end to end, can narrow that band only if new failure data arrive. Conditional on new failure data: halving MTBF uncertainty (lognormal sigma 0.70 -> 0.35) cuts the 95th-percentile failure-rate multiplier from ~3.2x to ~1.8x, so spares mass at fixed risk falls ~20-40% only if the median holds. Better data can also move the median toward worse reliability, and remodeling the existing 2004-era public data alone narrows the band little (general derivation). The binding gate is data: the last public ECLSS failure release was 2004, and releasing more is an institutional decision that compresses 1.0x. Under S2 the modeling is routine AI applied statistics from 2027, but a credible result waits for released data or NASA in-house work (2028, Medium). Under S3, near-free cognition makes it likely that NASA's own analysts do it in-house with the full record, hence High (judgment).
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.strongest_case_small: Thin data cannot be cured by better math; failure data accrue only with operating hours, and ISS, the only large source, retires around 2030-2032 (extension to 2032 proposed). Better UQ may simply confirm the wide band.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.signpost: NASA publishes an updated ISS ECLSS failure and replacement dataset; Mars architecture studies cite AI-built sparing models.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (band and timing): S2/S3 2027 -> 2028 and S2 High -> Medium. The node's own gate is data, and the last public ECLSS failure release was 2004 (ICES 2025, verified by the auditor). A data release is an institutional decision (1.0x), so the cognitive date (2027) is not the outcome date. The 20-40% spares claim is reworded as conditional on new data, with the skeptic's lognormal arithmetic, which I checked (exp(1.645 x 0.70) = 3.2; exp(1.645 x 0.35) = 1.8). Partly accepted: S3 stays High, because with near-free cognition NASA can do the work in-house without a public release. Skeptic (edge): the outgoing edge to auton-earth-independent-fdir is now soft. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): band_2035 S2 Medium -> High. S3 High 2030 with near-free in-house cognition, not in its earliest year. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

auton-isru-rom-control.title: Fast, trustworthy models of oxygen reactors
auton-isru-rom-control.description: Reduced-order multiphysics models (electrochemistry, melt flow and heat transfer, gas evolution, composition drift) of molten-regolith electrolysis, carbothermal and solid-oxide reactors, with error bounds, used for model-predictive control, optimal test design and scale-up decisions.
auton-isru-rom-control.status_oct2026: Bespoke per team. LR-1 MRE: 0.07 kg O2/h for 9 h on 25 kg simulant in vacuum (ICES 2026); CaRD solar-carbothermal integrated test completed Feb 2026 (no public rate); MOXIE peak 12 g/h; OxEon MOMS designing for 1-3 kg/h O2 with >65% CO2-to-CH4 conversion and 5,000+ h stack tests. Melt composition, liquidus and viscosity drift during electrolysis (Acta Astronautica 2025).
auton-isru-rom-control.why: Going from 0.07 kg/h to a 10 t/yr plant (~1.1 kg/h continuous at under 30 kW, 2025 systems study) is a ~16x step for MRE; MOXIE to MOMS is ~80-250x. Each build-test cycle costs months; good ROMs plus Bayesian experiment design cut the number of cycles, and MPC handles regolith composition drift. Under S2 this is routine AI applied math by 2028.
auton-isru-rom-control.strongest_case_small: The uncertainty sits in property data at 1,600 C (melt viscosity and conductivity vs composition, anode corrosion), not in model reduction; teams already run COMSOL-class models. Plant performance is capped by hardware life and power, which models do not change.
auton-isru-rom-control.signpost: An ISRU payload flies with model-predictive control built on a published reduced-order model; ICES or Acta Astronautica papers report AI-generated reactor ROMs validated against test data.
auton-isru-rom-control.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and advocate (both lenses): infra-verified-numerics moved from hard prerequisite to soft accelerator. Reactor ROMs and MPC get their error bounds from a-posteriori estimators and validation against test data, and melt-property data at 1,600 C dominate the error budget. Skeptic: S3 2027 -> 2028, because the node is data-gated and S3 equals S2 in capability through 2028. This also matches the trunk resolver's infra-verified-numerics S3 2028. Advocate's S1 2030 -> 2029 rejected: neither S1 prerequisite (cap-applied-math, verified numerics) is earlier than 2029, and the data gate does not move. Auditor: pathway relabeled P1 (P6 only for scale-up tools); P6's default band is Low, so High is consistent only with P1. Skeptic and advocate: the outgoing edges to auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo and auton-mars-isru-demo are now soft. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): band_2035 S1 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2-S4 Medium 2029 and High 2030: routine ROMs from 2028, but trustworthy error bounds need a year of reactor data; S3 equals S2 because the node is data-gated. S1 High 2034, held at cap-applied-math's seeded S1 High (2034); 2033 would fit if the trunk review's 2032 stands. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-isru-rom-control.note_2035: S1 has routine AI reactor models by about 2030-31, so every scenario is High by 2035. S4 equals S3 because reactor modeling is cognitive work.
auton-isru-rom-control.gate_note: Reactor and melt-property data bind; build-and-test cycles on 1,600 C rigs (experiment) are the runner-up.

auton-granular-regolith-model.title: Validated models of digging icy regolith
auton-granular-regolith-model.description: Calibrated continuum-plus-DEM models (well-posed where theory allows, empirically regularized otherwise) of excavation, conveying and trafficability for polar regolith, including ice-cemented and vapor-deposited ice forms, predictive enough to size excavators and water-extraction feeders.
auton-granular-regolith-model.status_oct2026: Lab-only. Ice-cemented simulant: excavation energy 2.74 to 143 J/g as ice rises from 1 to 12 wt% (52x, reported as 52 times less efficient). Pressure-sintered simulant: 0.35 to 0.11 J/g, 3.2 times more efficient with more ice. A vapor-deposited sample was much stronger than pressure-sintered and Apollo 16 samples (Space and Planetary Resources, Sep 2026). The authors conclude that icy regolith 'may be easier to excavate and traverse than previously thought' and question ice-cemented simulants as universal proxies. DEM calibration with realistic particle shapes and agglutinates is ongoing (2024-2026). The ice form at the poles is unknown.
auton-granular-regolith-model.why: Without knowing the ice form, excavator power and wear sizing is uncertain by more than 10x. A model calibrated on lab simulants with empirical regularization (today's practice) and then tested blind against the first in-situ polar data (2028 at the earliest) becomes a design basis. A well-posedness theorem raises confidence but is not a precondition (tl-position-2). S3 cannot beat S2 here because the gate is the ground-truth mission, not cognition. S1 lags a year because AI applied math arrives in 2029 in S1, although human teams can do the calibration.
auton-granular-regolith-model.strongest_case_small: One or two landing sites may not represent the variability across permanently shadowed regions; designers will overbuild regardless, and early ice mining may target easier deposits.
auton-granular-regolith-model.signpost: VIPER or another polar lander returns geotechnical data, and a published model predicts it blind within a factor of two.
auton-granular-regolith-model.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Advocate (edges): auton-granular-wellposedness and cap-physics-theory moved from hard prerequisites to soft accelerators, and cap-applied-math added as a hard prerequisite. Calibrated DEM/MPM with empirical regularization is how excavators are sized today, a well-posedness proof changes confidence and not the model (tl-position-2), and the skeptic makes the same point on the wellposedness node. The polar ground-truth data stay the hard gate. Advocate: S1 >2031 -> 2030 (band Low kept), because the binding gate is the 2028 data and not the theorem. Auditor's knock-on (S2/S3 2029 -> 2030) not applied, because ground truth stays 2028 (see that node). Auditor (fact): the status now reports both ice forms and the authors' conclusion (verified against the Crossref abstract). | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High, S3 Medium -> High, S4 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium 2031 in S2-S4, a year after the first usable polar dataset reaches Medium (2030), because the model must be tested blind against it; High 2034, a year after ground truth is High. S3 equals S2 because the ground-truth missions set the date. S1 Medium 2033. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-granular-regolith-model.note_2035: By 2035 several polar landers and Moon Base digging have returned ice data, so a validated model is High in S2-S4 and Medium in S1. S4 equals S3 because the data come from landers.
auton-granular-regolith-model.gate_note: In-situ ice data bind; lab calibration on representative icy simulants (experiment) is the runner-up.

auton-mre-anode-materials.title: Anodes that survive molten regolith
auton-mre-anode-materials.description: Discovery and life prediction of inert anode and crucible materials for oxygen-evolving electrolysis of molten regolith at ~1,600 C, the component that limits molten-regolith-electrolysis plant life.
auton-mre-anode-materials.status_oct2026: Active research: iridium anodes (costly), zirconia-based hollow anodes (Acta Astronautica, Jun 2025). Longest reported integrated large-scale run: hours (LR-1, 9 h). Plants need thousands of hours.
auton-mre-anode-materials.why: A 10 t/yr plant (~1.1 kg/h, about 8,800 operating hours a year) with anodes lasting 1,000 h needs ~9 anode swaps a year, each a robotic maintenance operation in a 1,600 C cell; at 10,000 h it needs fewer than one. AI-guided and autonomous-lab materials search (S2/S3) can shortlist compositions quickly. But autonomous labs cannot yet process refractory ceramics and superalloys (materials-closed-loop-discovery), and each candidate still needs fabrication and a multi-thousand-hour endurance test at 1,600 C: a 1,000 h screen takes ~6 weeks and a 10,000 h confirmation ~14 months. AI-run test stands can run candidates in parallel, which cuts the number of serial cycles but not the length of any one test. Chain (S2): discovery capability 2029 -> candidate fabricated and screened at 1,000 h, 2030 -> published with endurance data 2030-31 (Medium). S3 lands in the same year, because the discovery prerequisite is no earlier (2029) and endurance hours do not compress.
auton-mre-anode-materials.strongest_case_small: Endurance testing is inherently slow (10,000 h is about 14 months per test) and AI cannot compress it; and the carbothermal route avoids the inert-anode problem entirely, so the whole node may be bypassed.
auton-mre-anode-materials.signpost: A continuous MRE run longer than 1,000 h reported; an AI-discovered anode composition published with endurance data.
auton-mre-anode-materials.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (timing): S3 2029 -> 2030. S3 2029 equalled the hard prerequisite materials-closed-loop-discovery (S3 2029), which leaves no time to fabricate a refractory candidate and run even a 1,000 h screen. Skeptic's S2 2030 -> 2031 and Medium -> Low rejected: a 1,000 h screen is six weeks, so the 2029 -> 2030 lag is enough for a first endurance-backed candidate. Advocate's S3 Medium -> High rejected: parallel stands shorten serial cycles but not single tests, and refractory processing is a stated limit of autonomous labs. Both lenses: new soft edge to auton-lunar-oxygen-ops (anode life limits plant life). Advocate: soft input from physclock-ai-run-test-stands. Auditor (arithmetic): ~8 -> ~9 swaps a year (10,000 kg / 1.14 kg/h = ~8,770 h). | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): S1 year >2031 -> 2032; band_2035 S3 Medium -> High, S4 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R-moon-mars resolver (2026-10-07): band_2035 S2 Medium -> High (advocate). S2 and S3 share the year (2030) and the discovery prerequisite year (2029), and the draft's S2 reason (carbothermal funding) applies equally to S3. Every hard parent is High in S2 by 2035. | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium 2031 (published with endurance data 2030-31). High needs 10,000 h runs of about 14 months: S3 2033; S2 2034, held at materials-closed-loop-discovery's S2 High 2034. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-mre-anode-materials.note_2035: S1 lags to about 2032 with slower discovery labs. By 2035 runs of 10,000 h are done in S2-S4 (High): one run takes about 14 months, so 2030-35 fits three or four campaigns on autonomous labs. S4 equals S3 because endurance hours are a physics clock.
auton-mre-anode-materials.gate_note: Multi-thousand-hour endurance tests at 1,600 C bind; fabricating refractory candidates that autonomous labs cannot yet process is the runner-up.

auton-blss-stability-theory.title: Biological life-support loops with stability guarantees
auton-blss-stability-theory.description: Multi-compartment models of bioregenerative life support (bacteria, algae, higher plants, crew) with certified stability and recovery margins, and controllers designed against those margins.
auton-blss-stability-theory.status_oct2026: MELiSSA pilot plant has integrated liquid streams of three compartments and prepared gas closure across four (ICES 2025). China's Lunar Palace 365 ran 370 days at 98.2% closure (bioRxiv 2021). A 2025 npj Microgravity review flags critical US capability gaps in bioregenerative systems. Family 149 (T1; the formal part is possibly T3 per repo docs) claims a proof of boundedness and persistence for closed weakly reversible mass-action networks, an idealized building block.
auton-blss-stability-theory.premise_tier: n/a (capability); 149 enters only as a soft, conditional (T1) accelerator
auton-blss-stability-theory.why: Instability (microbial washout, crop failure, CO2/O2 imbalance) is the main operational risk of bioregenerative systems and the reason they carry large physico-chemical backups. Certified stability margins define safe operating envelopes and shrink buffer stocks. The value is AI building validated reduced models and Lyapunov or permanence-type certificates for the controlled loop, which do not need family 149. Real loops have Monod and light-limited kinetics, harvesting, control inputs and contamination, so they are not closed weakly reversible mass-action networks. 149 (T1, conditional) contributes only the idealized guarantee that a closed mass-action core cannot lose a species, and it accelerates the work without gating it. Validation uses existing closed-run data (MELiSSA, Lunar Palace), so the gate is data access, not a new test.
auton-blss-stability-theory.strongest_case_small: Biology is not mass-action and real failures come from contamination, disease and equipment; validation needs months-to-years closed tests, so the model may only re-describe what operators already manage empirically.
auton-blss-stability-theory.signpost: Stability certificates and model-based controllers validated against existing MELiSSA or Lunar Palace closed-run data, published by those teams or a NASA or commercial analog group.
auton-blss-stability-theory.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (edge): auton-mass-action-permanence (149, T1) moved from hard prerequisite to soft accelerator. Real BLSS loops are not closed weakly reversible mass-action systems, the node's own why already said 149 contributes only the idealized guarantee, and Lunar Palace 365 ran 370 days at 98.2% closure with no such theorem. Skeptic (gate): experiment -> data, and the signpost now validates against existing closed-run data, which removes the circularity with its own child node auton-blss-closed-test. Auditor (grounding): 'proves permanence' -> 'claims a proof of boundedness and persistence' (T1 wording, formal scope). S3 2028 -> 2029 (resolver): this aligns with the trunk resolver's cap-physics-theory S3 2029 (a hard prerequisite) and with S3 equalling S2 through 2028. Bands unchanged. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): S1 year >2031 -> 2033; band_2035 S3 Medium -> High, S4 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium 2030 in S2-S4, a year after the physics-theory capability; S3 High 2034, held at cap-physics-theory's seeded S3 High (2034); 2033 would fit if the trunk review's 2032 stands. S2 stays Medium on data access. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-blss-stability-theory.note_2035: S1 needs its physics-theory capability (2032), so its first certificates come about 2033. S3 and S4 reach High by 2035 as near-free modeling meets existing MELiSSA and Lunar Palace data, while S2 stays Medium on data access; S4 equals S3 because the gate is data.
auton-blss-stability-theory.gate_note: Access to closed-run data binds; the reduced models and stability certificates (cognitive, after cap-physics-theory) are the runner-up.

auton-radiation-risk-uq.title: Narrower uncertainty on crew radiation risk
auton-radiation-risk-uq.description: Mechanistic radiobiology models (high-LET track structure, non-targeted effects, dose-rate) that shrink the uncertainty on cancer and cardiovascular risk per unit dose for Moon and Mars crews.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.status_oct2026: NASA limit: 600 mSv career effective dose, independent of age and sex. Space Weather (Mar 2026): staying under 600 mSv on a Mars mission requires flying near solar maximum or faster transfers. Tomography review (Jul 2026): recent NASA Space Cancer Risk model revisions and non-targeted-effect scenarios suggest risks may be higher than earlier estimates; uncertainty remains substantial for high-LET radiobiology. Transport models predict dose well (blind Artemis I validation, 2025).
auton-radiation-risk-uq.why: Risk-per-dose uncertainty drives shielding mass and allowed mission duration. Halving it could relax design margins, but that requires new biological data: animal cohorts (years to cancer endpoints), organoid and beam studies at NSRL (limited beam time). S3's autonomous labs could scale in-vitro work, but in-vivo latency is a fixed physical clock.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.strongest_case_small: The 600 mSv limit is a policy choice, not a model output, and is unlikely to move within five years whatever models say; dose physics (not math) sets the mass needed to shield.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.signpost: NASA revises its Space Cancer Risk model with mechanistic components, or changes the 600 mSv standard.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.note_2035: In-vivo cancer endpoints take years, so S2 lands about 2033 and S1 about 2034, and S3 reaches Medium by 2035. S4 equals S3 because biology and beam time set the clock.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.revision_note: E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): S1 year >2031 -> 2034; S2 year >2031 -> 2033; band_2035 S1 Speculative -> Low, S3 Low -> Medium, S4 Low -> Medium. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S3 Medium 2034. Skeptic: in-vivo cancer endpoints take years and NSRL beam time is scarce, so 2035. Advocate: S3 autonomous labs scale organoid and in-vitro work, so 2033. Resolved 2034: cohorts started about 2029-30 reach endpoints about 2033-34. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.gate_note: In-vivo biological endpoints bind; beam time at NSRL (experiment) is the runner-up.

auton-verified-surface-autonomy.title: Proof-checked autonomy software for lunar robots
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.description: Flight software for uncrewed rovers, excavators and other robotic surface assets whose planner, fault responses and safety monitors ship with machine-checked proofs: a synthesized planner plus a runtime-assurance wrapper around learned perception, produced by AI agents at a cost a commercial lunar company can afford. LTV software is out of scope, because it is human-rated even when the vehicle drives without crew (see verif-hls-autonomy-certification).
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.status_oct2026: Not flown. CADRE (late 2026, IM-3) demonstrates multi-robot autonomy (leader election, task re-allocation, cooperative mapping) without proofs; Perseverance's AI-planned drives (Dec 2025) used digital-twin checking. LTV awards (May 2026: Astrolab $219M, Lunar Outpost $220M; Pegasus offers manual, autonomous and remote modes).
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.premise_tier: n/a (capability); 104 is T3 for the randomized mean-payoff part only
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.why: Moon Base Phase 1 (up to 30 CLPS landings from 2027) puts many robots on the surface with small operations teams, and the verification cost of each autonomous behavior becomes the binding cost of autonomy. Agents that synthesize and prove planners and wrap learned components in proven monitors collapse that cost. The scope is uncrewed operation. CLPS is a commercial service buy with low NASA oversight, and uncrewed commercial robots need only an Article VI mission authorization (EO 14335 directs a streamlined process), so no certification step applies and the gate is supplier adoption. P2's default of Medium assumes a certification step; with none here, S2/S3 High rests on cheap proof tooling (2028) and many Moon Base Phase 1 suppliers. Crew-carrying LTV autonomy would trigger the Medium cap and is excluded.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.strongest_case_small: Most lunar robot losses so far are hardware and environment (landers tipping, thermal, dust, comms), not logic errors; proofs cover the model, not the Moon.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.signpost: A CLPS, LTV or NASA payload provider advertises formally verified autonomy with published proof artifacts; NASA's Fly Foundational Robotics mission or CADRE follow-ons adopt them.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (gate vs band) against the advocate (gate). Both cappers offered the same alternative: drop the crew-carrying LTV from scope, set the gate to adoption, and keep S2 High. The advocate argued for adoption. All three are reconciled by narrowing the scope to uncrewed robots (LTVs excluded, because their software is human-rated) and setting binding_gate qualification -> adoption. Bands Medium/High/High kept. The why no longer both invokes NASA acceptance and denies the cap. Auditor: 104's scope note added to premise_tier. The outgoing edges to auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops and auton-surface-productivity are now soft (all three lenses). | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): band_2035 S1 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium 2029 and High 2030 in S2-S4, as Moon Base Phase 1 suppliers adopt cheap proof tooling. S1 High 2034, held at verif-runtime-assurance's S1 High 2034. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.note_2035: S1 adopts proof-carrying autonomy by about 2031-32, so every scenario is High by 2035. S4 equals S3 because the gate is supplier adoption.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.gate_note: Supplier adoption binds; cheap machine-checked proofs for planners and monitors (formalization) are the runner-up.

auton-earth-independent-fdir.title: Crew-side fault diagnosis without Mission Control
auton-earth-independent-fdir.description: Onboard diagnosis and repair guidance for habitats, life support and crew medicine that a crew 3-22 light-minutes (one way) from Earth can trust: model-based reasoning and AI assistants whose conclusions are cross-checked against verified system models.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.status_oct2026: Research prototypes: the DARIA/STAMPS anomaly-response architecture (AIAA SciTech, Jan 2026; naming unverified); NASA's progressively Earth-independent medical operations (EIMO) framework, which names clinical AI as a high-value target (2025); AI-assisted medical diagnostics tests on ISS reported in Mar 2026 (press headline only, unverified). ISS relies on ground engineering teams.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.why: Mars crews face light-time delays and blackouts, and ECLSS maintenance alone is estimated at ~45 min/day. Faster, trustworthy diagnosis cuts downtime, spares and risk. Flying it on ISS or an Artemis mission (the signpost) puts a crew-facing safety function, including clinical decision support, under NASA flight-software and medical-operations acceptance, so the band is capped at Medium in every scenario. Sparing and MTBF models (auton-ecls-reliability-uq) inform priors but do not perform diagnosis, so they accelerate this node rather than gate it. Gateway's pause (Mar 2026) moves the uncrewed-habitat testbed role to ISS and the Moon base.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.strongest_case_small: Advisory AI is already available; trust, training and procedures, not mathematics, limit adoption, and for the Moon (1.3 s delay) NASA will keep the ground in the loop.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.signpost: NASA flies an onboard diagnostic assistant with a formal cross-check component on ISS or an Artemis landing mission.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (both lenses, certification cap): S2 High -> Medium. The node covers crew medicine and ECLSS repair guidance, and its signpost is a flight on ISS or Artemis, which needs NASA acceptance. S3 High -> Medium as well (auditor): the scorecard cap applies in every scenario, and the skeptic gave no S3-specific reason to keep High. Skeptic (edge): auton-ecls-reliability-uq moved from hard to soft, because sparing models do not diagnose. Its outgoing edges to auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops (skeptic) and auton-closed-loop-habitat (skeptic) are now soft. Auditor (fact): Earth-Mars one-way light time is ~3-22 min; the two unverifiable status items are marked. Gate adoption -> qualification, so the label matches the acceptance gate the why now names. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): years and bands unchanged. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium 2029 in S2-S4, not 2028: flying a crew-facing assistant needs a flight opportunity after the tools exist. S1 Medium 2031. Capped at Medium in every scenario. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.note_2035: Diagnostic assistants fly on Artemis missions and commercial stations in 2030-35, but NASA crew-safety acceptance has no named fast path, so every scenario stays capped at Medium. S4 equals S3 because the gate is acceptance.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.gate_note: NASA crew-safety acceptance binds; programs choosing to fly the assistant on ISS or Artemis (adoption) is the runner-up.

auton-excavation-design.title: Design excavators from models, not guesses
auton-excavation-design.description: Model-based sizing and design optimization of excavators, conveyors and ice-processing feeders for polar regolith, replacing much of today's build-and-dig-in-simulant iteration.
auton-excavation-design.status_oct2026: NASA's IPEx is designed to excavate on the order of 20 t of regolith per mission; designs are iterated in simulant test bins. 2026 work on bucket design uses vision-based fill analysis (arXiv 2609.25724).
auton-excavation-design.why: With a validated regolith model, AI multiphysics design optimization can trade bucket geometry, power and wear against the in-situ ice form, avoiding a 10x over- or under-sized machine. The gate is the ground-truth data and model validation, not the optimizer.
auton-excavation-design.strongest_case_small: Excavator mass is a small share of a lunar base; conservative over-design costs little compared with landing slots, so precision design may not change what flies.
auton-excavation-design.signpost: An ISRU excavator or ice-mining payload selected for a 2029-2031 flight with a model-based design report validated against in-situ data.
auton-excavation-design.note_2035: With ice data in hand and design optimization cheap, model-based excavators are High in S2-S4 by 2035, and S1 follows about 2032. S4 equals S3 because the gate is data.
auton-excavation-design.revision_note: E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): S1 year >2031 -> 2032; band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High, S3 Medium -> High, S4 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium 2031 with the validated regolith model (S2 and S3 alike, since ice data set the date); High 2035 in S2 and 2034 in S3. S1 Medium 2034. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-excavation-design.gate_note: In-situ ice data bind; dig tests in representative simulant (experiment) are the runner-up.

auton-sinter-process-control.title: Reliable recipes for sintering regolith
auton-sinter-process-control.description: Process windows and closed-loop control for microwave, solar or laser sintering and melting of regolith into landing pads, roads and blast berms, avoiding thermal-stress cracking in lunar thermal extremes.
auton-sinter-process-control.status_oct2026: Multiphysics modeling (Coatings, Feb 2026) finds microwave-sintered bodies crack when cooled faster than ~16 C/min (safe below 15 C/min). Startups pursuing lunar construction: Lunar Forge (Jul 2026), Astroport with Vermeer on autonomous construction machinery (Apr 2026). Plume-surface interaction models that set pad requirements are immature (see prop-psi-models).
auton-sinter-process-control.why: Coupled electromagnetic-thermal-stress models are expert-scarce but well-posed; AI can map process windows across regolith compositions and design controllers that hold cooling rates, cutting the test matrix. Pads matter because landing plumes eject regolith at high speed, a hazard that grows with Starship-class landers.
auton-sinter-process-control.strongest_case_small: Regolith composition and grain size vary by site; vacuum-thermal test facilities are scarce; and on the Moon the binding constraint is kW-to-100s-of-kW power for sintering, not recipes.
auton-sinter-process-control.signpost: A relevant-environment test produces sintered pads that survive a rocket-plume test; a CLPS manifest includes a construction demo.
auton-sinter-process-control.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (both lenses): S2 High -> Medium and S1 Medium -> Low (S3 High kept). The node ends in P6 (default Low) and is gated by scarce relevant-environment vacuum-thermal tests (1.1-1.3x in S2) plus a plume-test signpost. A model-derived process window already exists without AI (Coatings 2026), and S1 Medium did not fit a 2031 earliest year. New soft input from prop-psi-models (skeptic: PSI sets pad requirements). New hard output to auton-robotic-landing-pad (advocate), which gives this formerly dangling node a downstream use. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S3 High 2031, three years after its earliest year rather than in it; S2 Medium 2030 and High 2033 once plume-tested pads exist. S1 Medium 2033. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-sinter-process-control.note_2035: By 2035 plume-tested sintered pads exist in S2-S4 (High) and possibly in S1 (Medium). S4 equals S3 because the year precedes robot onset and vacuum test facilities set the pace.
auton-sinter-process-control.gate_note: Vacuum-thermal tests bind; the coupled electromagnetic-thermal-stress modeling (cognitive) is the runner-up.

auton-certified-assembly-skills.title: Robot assembly skills with proven safety envelopes
auton-certified-assembly-skills.description: Learned or optimized manipulation skills (connector mating, truss and solar-array assembly, cable routing, refueling interfaces) wrapped in certified contact simulation and runtime assurance, so qualification can lean on analysis rather than exhaustive physical testing.
auton-certified-assembly-skills.status_oct2026: Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle launched Jul 22, 2026 with two NRL robotic arms and three Mission Extension Pods; NASA's Fly Foundational Robotics mission (Motiv arm, PickNik MoveIt Pro on Space ROS, Feb 2026) targets autonomous and ground-supervised manipulation. auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.title: First measurements of how hard polar ice is to dig
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.description: In-situ geotechnical and volatile data from lunar south-pole regolith (VIPER, CLPS drills, Chang'e-7, LUPEX, Moon Base Phase 1 rovers): the physical data gate for every excavation and water-extraction model.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.status_oct2026: PRIME-1 drill on IM-2 (Mar 2025) returned limited data after the lander tipped over (general). VIPER: CS-7 task order to Blue Origin (Sep 19, 2025, up to $190M); the lunar-delivery option is exercised only after Blue Moon Mk1's first flight, and the target was late 2027. The May 28, 2026 New Glenn static-fire explosion destroyed the LC-36 transporter-erector and damaged the gantry (best-case pad restoration ~15 months per reporting), and NASA is evaluating Falcon Heavy. Chang'e-7 missed its Aug 2026 window and now targets 2027; its hopper and rover carry water and volatile analyzers, spectrometers and radar but no geotechnical drill. ESA's PROSPECT (ProSEED drill to ~1 m) flies on an Intuitive Machines Nova-C in 2027 to ~84.5 S, a site chosen for sunlight where ice-bearing layers may be out of reach. LUPEX (drill) is planned around 2028-29. Moon Base Phase 1 targets up to 30 CLPS landings from 2027.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.why: Not an AI-math implication: an exogenous physical anchor set by lander manifests, landing success and drill reach, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply. This node exists to show a gate AI cannot move: the excavation models above cannot be validated until a polar lander digs into ice-bearing regolith and returns strength or excavation data, not just detection. Chain: CS-7 base task -> Mk1 pathfinder (slipped by the LC-36 loss; New Glenn return to flight or Falcon Heavy) -> delivery option exercised -> VIPER on a second Mk1 (NET 2028, realistically 2029) -> landing -> TRIDENT drilling in ice-bearing regolith. Alternates: PROSPECT's drill (2027, sunlit site, ice possibly out of reach), LUPEX's drill (~2028-29) and Chang'e-8 (~2028-29). Chang'e-7 (2027) gives water data only. Landing success in the CLPS era has been near half (IM-1 and IM-2 tipped, Peregrine failed, ispace M1 and M2 crashed, Blue Ghost 1 succeeded; general), and ice-bearing layers may lie beyond drill reach. At least one usable dataset by 2031 is therefore Medium (judgment, roughly 50-65%), the same in every scenario because the gate is physical. The earliest year stays 2028, given several independent 2027-28 attempts.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.strongest_case_small: Data from one or two sites may not generalize across permanently shadowed regions, leaving models under-constrained even after first contact.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.signpost: Blue Moon Mk1 pathfinder flies and the VIPER delivery option is exercised; PROSPECT drilling results at ~84.5 S (2027); LUPEX or Chang'e-8 drill data from ice-bearing regolith.

auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.title: First oxygen made on the Moon
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.description: A flight demonstration that extracts at least 1 g of oxygen from lunar regolith on the surface (grams to kilograms), by carbothermal reduction, molten-regolith electrolysis, hydrogen reduction or another route. Sub-gram analytical runs, such as ProSPA's hydrogen-reduction oven test, are precursors and do not count.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.status_oct2026: Ground prototypes only: CaRD integrated solar-carbothermal test (Feb 2026, no flight date), LR-1 MRE (0.07 kg/h, late 2024), Blue Origin Air Pioneer MRE (Jun 2026). NASA's lunar ISRU strategy is a leader/follower sequence of flight demos leading to a pilot plant (NTRS 2025). NASA's LIFT-1 O2-extraction demo was planned in 2023 for a 2027 launch at $200-250M including landing (2026 status unconfirmed). ESA's ProSPA flies a sub-gram hydrogen-reduction test on an Intuitive Machines Nova-C in 2027. Helios (MRE) has reported plans to fly with ispace (date unconfirmed), and ASI's ORACLE carbothermal demo was proposed for a CLPS slot NET 2028 (IAC-23 paper). No payload making 1 g or more of oxygen is confirmed manifested as of Oct 2026; NASA's Mar 24, 2026 RFI seeks payloads for 2027-28 CLPS flights.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.why: Not an AI-math implication: an exogenous physical anchor, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply; the scenario spread comes from general AI help with test design, anomaly closure and launch cadence. The date is set by CLPS manifests, payload funding and lander success, not by AI math, and the demo would happen on roughly this schedule without it. AI reactor models are therefore an accelerator: they can shorten the cognitive third or so of a payload schedule, worth at most about a year between S1 and S2 (Amdahl ~18% vs ~38%). Chain (S1): a LIFT-1-class or commercial MRE or carbothermal payload manifested 2027-28 -> 12-18 months of integration plus typical slips (announced schedules run 1.5-3x long) -> landing 2030. Chain (S2): the same payloads with AI-assisted test design and anomaly closure from 2027 -> landing 2029. Chain (S3): ROM-tuned flight unit and faster integration -> landing 2028. With several independent candidates (LIFT-1, Helios, ORACLE, and Moon Base Phase 1's up to 30 landings) at CLPS-era landing odds of roughly 50-65% (general), at least one success by 2031 is Medium in S1 and S2, where no qualifying payload is yet manifested. It is High in S3, where launch cadence runs 0.5-1 year earlier and more attempts fit before 2031. Bands are judgments, not computed probabilities.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.strongest_case_small: The demo would happen on roughly this schedule without AI math; oxygen chemistry from regolith was shown on the ground decades ago, and the bottleneck is a landing slot, power and dust-tolerant hardware.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.signpost: An ISRU oxygen payload manifested on a named 2027-2029 CLPS mission.

auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.title: A lunar robot operates with proof-checked autonomy
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.description: An uncrewed rover, excavator or other robotic surface asset operates on the Moon using autonomy software whose planner and safety monitors carry machine-checked proofs.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.status_oct2026: None. CADRE (late 2026) will be the first autonomous multi-robot team on the Moon, without proofs.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.why: Once proof-carrying autonomy is cheap (S2 2028), adoption needs only one willing payload provider and one successful landing. No certifier is involved: CLPS is a commercial service buy, and uncrewed commercial robots need only an Article VI mission authorization (EO 14335). Chain (S2): proof-carrying autonomy tool 2028 -> integration and a software freeze 12-18 months before landing -> landing 2029. Software uplinks to long-lived robots already on the surface avoid the freeze lag. Chain (S3): the same tool date (S3 equals S2 through 2028) -> landing 2029. Each attempt carries CLPS-era landing odds of roughly 50-65% (general) and depends on a provider choosing proofs without customer pull. The band is therefore Medium in S2 and S3 (judgment), because S3's cheaper cognition raises neither landing reliability nor demand.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.strongest_case_small: Providers may see no customer pull for proofs on uncrewed robots, and landing failures may consume the opportunities.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.signpost: A lunar mission press kit or NASA payload description lists formally verified autonomy as a feature.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.calibration_note: A3: Lag ladder. auton-blss-closed-test.title: Long closed life-support test run by certified control
auton-blss-closed-test.description: A ground test of 180+ days in which a bioregenerative or hybrid life-support loop runs under model-based control with stability certificates, at 95% or more material closure (food, O2, water). Lunar Palace 365 reached 98.2% over 370 days without such control.
auton-blss-closed-test.status_oct2026: Precedent: China's Lunar Palace 1 ran a 370-day crewed closed test in 2017-18 (general); MELiSSA pilot plant progressing toward full loop closure with rat crew mock-up (2025).
auton-blss-closed-test.why: Crop cycles (60-120 days, general) and the need to observe disturbances and recoveries make the test inherently months long. Chain (S2): stability theory and controllers 2029 -> a funded facility (MELiSSA, a Lunar Palace successor or a US analog) adopts them -> a 180+ day run in 2030-31. That is Low, because it needs a funded facility and campaign inside two years. Chain (S3): theory 2029 with near-free controller design and AI-run parallel small loops -> crew-scale run 2030 (Medium). The US gap is funding, not modeling (npj Microgravity 2025).
auton-blss-closed-test.strongest_case_small: Funding, not modeling, has limited US bioregenerative work (npj Microgravity 2025); a better controller does not create a test facility.
auton-blss-closed-test.signpost: Announcement of a new long-duration closed-loop campaign (MELiSSA full loop, Lunar Palace successor, or a NASA/commercial analog) citing model-based stability control.
