auton-mars-isru-demo.title: Kilogram-per-hour propellant production on Mars
auton-mars-isru-demo.description: A MOMS-class solid-oxide unit (1-3 kg O2/h plus methane) operating on Mars, 80-250x MOXIE's peak rate.
auton-mars-isru-demo.status_oct2026: OxEon MOMS hardware in design (ICES 2026). SpaceX reached orbit with Starship on Flight 14 (Sep 28, 2026), and ship-to-ship propellant transfer is expected in early 2027. In Feb 2026 SpaceX made a 'self-growing city' on the Moon (in under 10 years) its priority, with Mars work to begin within 5-7 years, and it told investors it targets an uncrewed lunar landing in Mar 2027 (WSJ via NBC News). Remaining Mars departure windows in the horizon: late 2026 (SpaceX not using it), Dec 2028-Jan 2029, and Feb-Mar 2031 (arrival late 2031).
auton-mars-isru-demo.why: hyper-mars-heavy-landing puts the first 20 t-class Mars landing in the early-2031 window at the earliest (arrival late 2031), after propellant transfer and the Moon. Full chain (every scenario): a launch in the Feb-Mar 2031 window arrives about Sep-Nov 2031, leaving 1-3 months in the horizon. A 1-3 kg/h unit also needs roughly 25-50 kW of landed and deployed power (MOXIE-class scaling, general), a funded MOMS payload on a SpaceX ship (no such contract exists) and an H2 or water source for the methane leg. None of these compress in S3, and SpaceX's Moon-first pivot removes the main sponsor for an early-2031 ISRU payload, so every scenario is Speculative. AI math cannot add windows, shorten transits or raise landing reliability much, and AI reactor models are only an accelerator.

auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.title: AI plans rover operations, machines check the plans
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.description: Routine use of AI agents to plan multi-sol rover traverses and multi-robot surface activities, with automated simulation and formal checks replacing most human plan review.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.status_oct2026: Demonstrated once at Mars: Perseverance's first AI-planned drives on Dec 8 and 10, 2025 (210 m and 246 m; Claude vision-language models used orbital imagery and slope data to lay waypoints), checked via JPL's digital twin across more than 500,000 telemetry variables (JPL, Jan 30, 2026). JPL describes a goal of kilometer-scale drives with minimal operator workload.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.why: This is the capability channel in its purest form: no catalog theorem is involved. Ground operations dominate extended-mission cost, and the Moon Base plan multiplies the number of robots per operator. Formal plan checking (model checking of command sequences against flight rules) makes AI plans acceptable without line-by-line human review. 'Routine' means a change in operations culture and flight-rule practice on flagship rovers and Moon Base operators, so it lags the checking tools (verif-fdir-model-checking, S2 2027) by about a year. In 2027 the lunar surface holds only a handful of single-lunar-day landers. Chain (S2): checking tools 2027 -> flight-rule and digital-twin integration at JPL and Phase 1 operators -> majority of drives AI-planned 2028.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.strongest_case_small: Already happening without any new mathematics; rover productivity is capped by power, comm passes, hazards and science-team decision time, not planning.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.signpost: JPL reports a majority of a rover's drives in a quarter as AI-planned, or a kilometer-scale AI-planned drive; Moon Base robot operators adopt the same workflow.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (timing): 2028/2027/2027 -> 2029/2028/2028. A tier-6 'routine' change in flight-rule practice cannot land in the same year that its tier-4 checking tool first exists; this applies the A3 lag-ladder logic. The advocate's chain also starts from 2027 tools, so its 'routine 2027' is the tool date, not the adoption date. Bands unchanged. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): years and bands unchanged. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): High is reached one to two years after the earliest year, not in it: S2 Medium 2029 and High 2030; S3 High 2029 with near-free plan checks; S1 High 2031. Skeptic (routine needs a culture change) and advocate (Perseverance already did it) resolved at a one-year Medium lag. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.note_2035: Already High everywhere by 2031; by 2035 it is standard practice. S4 equals S3 because planning is cognitive work.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.gate_note: Flight-rule and operations-culture change binds; formal plan checking of command sequences (formalization) is the runner-up.

auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.title: Lunar base runs itself between crew visits
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.description: Robots, LTVs and base systems operate, maintain and resupply lunar base elements autonomously for months between crewed landings, with Earth supervising rather than commanding.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.status_oct2026: NASA's Moon Base plan (Mar 24, 2026): phased build-up, crewed landings initially every six months, Gateway paused in its current form; budget reported at ~$30B with bulk launch buys near (Bloomberg via 33FG, Oct 6, 2026). Artemis III is a 2027 Earth-orbit test; first landing 2028. Lunar Reactor-1 fission system to land in 2030.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.premise_tier: n/a (capability); 102 (T3) and 124 (T1, conditional) enter only through auton-ops-planning-ceilings, a soft input
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.why: Between six-month crew visits a base has months of idle infrastructure that must be maintained (dust, thermal cycling, power management). The cognitive enablers (AI-planned operations, runtime-assured autonomy, fault diagnosis) are ready by 2028 in S2. With a 1.3 s light-time, Earth-supervised AI planning and teleoperation can run a base, so proof-carrying autonomy, planning ceilings and crew-side diagnosis accelerate this node rather than gate it. The binding gate is that there must be enough base to operate. Moon Base Phase 2 (2029-2032) brings semi-permanent infrastructure, and sustained presence comes only in Phase 3 (from 2032). Politics and appropriations compress 1.0x, and flagship programs slip 2-7 years (the first crewed landing already slipped ~4 years). Chain (S2): AI operations routine 2028 -> HLS refuel campaign and first heavy cargo landing 2029 -> Phase 2 power, LTVs, a logistics cache and a semi-habitable element operating 2031 -> months of Earth-supervised operation between visits only at the very end of the horizon (Low). Chain (S3): refuel and heavy cargo 2028 -> Phase 2 elements 2030 -> months of uncrewed operation 2031 (Medium). Gateway's pause removes the planned uncrewed-habitat autonomy testbed, so the surface base inherits that role.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.strongest_case_small: With a 1.3 s light-time, the Moon can be run by teleoperation and ground scheduling; autonomy is a cost saver, not an enabler, and little base infrastructure will exist by 2031.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.signpost: Moon Base Phase 2 semi-habitable elements maintained without crew for 3+ months; NASA Phase 2 contracts that specify autonomous operations between crewed missions.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Edges: auton-ops-planning-ceilings and auton-verified-surface-autonomy moved from hard to soft (skeptic and advocate both). auton-earth-independent-fdir also moved to soft (skeptic; the advocate wanted it hard): crew-side diagnosis is for crew present, and this node is about crew absent, with Earth 1.3 s away. auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.title: Tonne-per-year lunar oxygen plant
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.description: An operational lunar oxygen plant producing at least ~1 t/yr toward a 10 t/yr pilot scale, feeding life support and lander propellant.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.status_oct2026: No flight unit. A 2025 systems study sketches 10 t/yr by molten regolith electrolysis at under 30 kW with vertical solar arrays and an excavator.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.why: Needs the flight demo, then a funded pilot plant (NASA's leader/follower sequence, LIFT-2-class), regolith handling and maintenance robots. Power is smaller than often assumed. 1 t/yr is ~0.11 kg/h, about 1.6x LR-1's demonstrated rate, and needs ~3-6 kW continuous: linear scaling of the 2025 study's <30 kW for 10 t/yr gives ~3 kW, and small cells lose proportionally more heat (general). A ridge-site solar array can supply that, so fission is not required at this scale. The real gates are run duration (8,760 h a year against LR-1's 9 h), anode life (~9 swaps a year at 1,000 h, or the carbothermal route), keeping a ~1,600 C melt through ridge-site dark periods (storage, or freeze-thaw cycles that stress cells and anodes; general), pilot-plant funding (1.0x) and landing success. Chain (S2): first demo 2029 -> pilot unit funded and designed with AI ROMs and MPC 2029-30 -> build and qualification 18-24 months -> landing 2031 at the earliest -> sustained 1 t/yr rate after 2031 (Low by 2031). Chain (S3): demo 2028 -> near-free design and AI-run test stands 2028-29 -> landing 2030 -> 1 t/yr annualized rate in 2031 (Low, because funding, endurance and landing odds do not compress).
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.strongest_case_small: Every gate is physical (power, landed mass, funding, hardware life); AI math shaves design time on a path dominated by launch cadence.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.signpost: NASA funds an ISRU pilot plant as part of Moon Base Phase 2 with a named delivery date.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Advocate (claim): 'tens of kW of continuous power' corrected. 1 t/yr needs ~3-6 kW (the advocate's linear scaling, which I checked: 30 kW x 8,766 h / 10 t = ~26 kWh/kg). The resolver adds the night-continuity constraint for a molten bath. Skeptic vs advocate on bands: the skeptic wanted S2 Low -> Speculative, and the advocate wanted S2 >2031 -> 2031 and S3 Low -> Medium. Both were rejected and years and bands kept (Speculative/Low/Low). The S2 chain needs a funded pilot plant built and landed within two years of a 2029 demo, and S3 does not compress funding, endurance or landing odds. Both lenses: soft input from auton-mre-anode-materials. Advocate: soft input from auton-lunar-heavy-cargo-landing. Skeptic: soft input from auton-moon-base-infrastructure (a pilot plant is a Phase 2 element). Chains written out. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): S1 year >2031 -> 2034; S2 year >2031 -> 2032; band_2035 S1 Speculative -> Low, S2 Low -> Medium, S3 Low -> Medium, S4 Low -> High. S4 credit: one band step by 2035 over S3 (off-Earth robot work from 2032); year equals S3 because it is 2031 or earlier. | R-moon-mars resolver (2026-10-07): band_2035 S4 High -> Medium (skeptic). The S4 credit fails condition 1: a 1 t/yr plant needs a few tonnes of regolith a year, and the reviewed credit was conditional on 10+ cargo landings a year, which a High band cannot rest on. The advocate's upkeep argument is rejected: with 10,000 h anodes (High by 2035) swaps fall to about one a year, and upkeep machinery inside a plant is specialized automation already in S3. General-purpose robots doing outpost work on the Moon are themselves only Medium in S4 by 2035. | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2 Medium 2034, S3 2033. Skeptic: no LIFT-2-class plant is funded and anode life and dark-period melts bind, so 2035. Advocate: SpaceX's Moon priority and routine cargo, so 2033. Resolved two years after the first landing date. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.note_2035: S2 lands about 2032 and S1 about 2034, once pilot plants are funded and flown, and S3 and S4 are Medium by 2035. A 1 t/yr plant needs only a few tonnes of regolith a year, so robot labor does not bind. Run hours, anode life, keeping the melt hot through dark periods, funding and landing success do, so S4 equals S3.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.gate_note: Pilot-plant funding binds; run-hour endurance and anode life (experiment) are the runner-up.

auton-closed-loop-habitat.title: Mars-class closed-loop life support, demonstrated
auton-closed-loop-habitat.description: Regenerative ECLSS with at least 98% water recovery, 75%+ oxygen recovery and demonstrated reliability good enough for a ~1,000-day Mars mission, flown on ISS, a commercial station or a lunar habitat.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.status_oct2026: ISS: 98% water recovery (2023); Exploration ECLSS testbed integration on ISS in progress (ICES Jul 2026); ISS extension to 2032 proposed. Oxygen recovery from CO2 on ISS is roughly half (general).
auton-closed-loop-habitat.why: Reliability is demonstrated with operating hours: a zero-failure demonstration of MTBF M at 95% confidence needs about 3M unit-hours (general). For an assembly with a 20,000 h MTBF target that is ~60,000 flight unit-hours, about 7 unit-years. The only path that compresses this is acceptance of model-based priors (physclock: 0.3-0.6x, i.e. ~18-36k unit-hours). That needs the credibility standard (S2 2029, Medium) and still needs the 75%+ oxygen-recovery hardware to fly. Parallel ground units can de-risk but do not meet the in-flight criterion, and flight unit-hours before ISS retirement (2030-32) are limited by upmass, crew time and the regenerative units' failure history. Hence Low in S2 and S3, and Speculative in S1, where no credibility standard arrives before 2031. Crew-side diagnosis (auton-earth-independent-fdir) helps operations but is not needed for an ISS demonstration, which the ground supports.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.strongest_case_small: The gap is hardware maturity and test time, which math does not touch; ISS retirement may end the only long-duration flight testbed before demonstration completes.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.signpost: Exploration ECLSS units accumulate multi-year ISS run time with published failure data; a commercial station adopts closed-loop O2 recovery.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (both lenses): S3 Medium -> Low. The definition requires flight, so S3's parallel ground units do not count. Skeptic: S1 Low -> Speculative (no credibility standard in S1 before 2031, so the no-prior binomial applies). Skeptic's S2 Low -> Speculative and the advocate's S2 >2031 -> 2031 cancel out, so S2 stays >2031 Low. The advocate's model-based-prior mechanism is real (physclock 0.3-0.6x) but needs both regulator acceptance and the oxygen-recovery hardware in flight. It is added as soft inputs from physclock-credibility-evidence-standard and physclock-ai-run-test-stands. Skeptic (edge): auton-earth-independent-fdir moved from hard to soft. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): S1 year >2031 -> 2035; S2 year >2031 -> 2033; band_2035 S1 Speculative -> Low, S2 Low -> Medium, S3 Low -> Medium, S4 Low -> Medium. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R-moon-mars resolver (2026-10-07): band_2035 S2 Medium -> Low (skeptic). The fast route needs model-based priors, whose standard (physclock-credibility-evidence-standard) is only Medium by 2035, and the 75%+ oxygen-recovery hardware must still fly; without priors the bar is about 7 flight unit-years. S3 and S4 keep Medium on their 2031 start. | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S3 Medium 2034. Skeptic: ISS retires 2030-32 and commercial-station hours start late, so 2035. Advocate: the Exploration ECLSS testbed is already being integrated and model-based priors cut hours to 18-36k, so 2033. Resolved 2034: about three years of flight hours after a 2031 start. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.note_2035: Flight unit-hours accrue on commercial stations and lunar habitats after ISS, so S2 lands about 2033 and S1 about 2035. S2 is Low by 2035 because it has only 2-3 years to fly 18-36k unit-hours, and S3 and S4 are Medium. S4 equals S3 because reliability statistics do not compress.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.gate_note: Flight reliability hours bind; building and flying the 75%+ oxygen-recovery hardware (fabrication) is the runner-up.

auton-mars-propellant-plant.title: Starship-scale propellant plant on Mars
auton-mars-propellant-plant.description: Mars ISRU producing on the order of 1,000 t of methane and oxygen per return flight: about 65 kg O2/h over ~500 days, roughly 5,000x MOXIE's peak rate, plus water-ice mining and order-1-MW continuous power (general estimates).
auton-mars-propellant-plant.status_oct2026: No hardware at this scale; MOXIE demonstrated 12 g/h; MOMS targets 1-3 kg/h.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.why: Requires landed megawatt-class power, ice mining and a sub-scale demo first, across 26-month windows. Even a perfect design in 2027 could not be landed, assembled and run at scale before 2031.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.strongest_case_small: This is the case: the effect of AI mathematics on this node inside the horizon is nil.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.signpost: SpaceX discloses a Mars power and ISRU architecture with flight hardware in test.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic (edge): auton-excavation-design moved from hard prerequisite to soft accelerator. That node models lunar polar icy regolith (0.165 g, vacuum, unknown ice form), and Mars mining targets mid-latitude ground ice under an atmosphere at 0.38 g, so the models do not carry over. No date effect (>2031 everywhere); this fixes a misleading skill-tree link. Years and bands unchanged. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): S1 year >2031 -> >2035; S2 year >2031 -> >2035; S3 year >2031 -> 2035; S4 year >2031 -> 2035. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R-moon-mars resolver (2026-10-07): S3 and S4 2035 -> >2035 (skeptic). New hard edge from hyper-35-mars-pinpoint-landing: the plant must land near the first lander's site and power. | R9-launch (2026-10-27): gate launch -> launch-internal (SpaceX's own manifest; Mach33 Launch Keystone v1.3 books Starlink, SpaceX's orbital compute, Moon and Mars cargo and NASA's lunar tanker flights in the internal account). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Under 10% by 2035 in every scenario: only the Apr 2033 window can land a plant, which then needs about 1 MW and 1 t of water a day. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

That plant would need about 1 MW and about 1 t of water a day within two years of arrival, with its design frozen before any Mars ISRU data, so every scenario is beyond 2035. auton-surface-productivity.title: Severalfold more robot work per operator
auton-surface-productivity.description: Useful surface work (km driven, kg excavated, tasks completed) per ground-operator hour rises severalfold (3-10x, judgment) versus 2025 practice on lunar or Mars surface robots. It comes mainly from AI planning with automated plan checks and from multi-robot coordination, and verified autonomy accelerates it.
auton-surface-productivity.status_oct2026: Baseline: large ground teams plan rover activities daily (general); first AI-planned Mars drives Dec 2025; CADRE multi-robot demo late 2026.
auton-surface-productivity.why: Moon Base Phase 1 cannot be staffed like MER/MSL-era teams per robot, and planning automation plus automated checking removes the operator bottleneck. The metric is a ratio, so it can be shown without a large fleet: on Mars rovers already flying AI-planned drives checked by a digital twin, and on Phase 1 and CADRE-class lunar robots. Chain (S2): AI-planned operations routine 2028 -> adopted by JPL and Moon Base Phase 1 robot operators -> operator-hours per km or per task reported falling severalfold across successive missions or quarters, 2029. Chain (S3): the same timing, with formal plan checks near-free from 2029 (High). Chain (S1): routine AI planning 2029 -> reported 2031. This is the domain's largest five-year outcome and rests on the capability, not the catalog. The earlier 'tenfold' figure had no source; 'severalfold' matches the signpost.
auton-surface-productivity.strongest_case_small: Productivity is bounded by power (two-week nights), comm windows, dust and hardware failures; operator hours may not be the binding constraint for most robots.
auton-surface-productivity.signpost: NASA or a CLPS provider reports operator-hours per km or per tonne excavated falling severalfold across successive missions.
auton-surface-productivity.calibration_note: A3: Tier-7 rule (strategic outcomes rarely High): a tenfold rise in surface work per operator also needs a lunar robot fleet on the surface (Moon Base Phase 1 landing cadence and success), which AI does not control. S2 High -> Medium; S3 High kept.

The operator saving comes from AI planning plus digital-twin or formal plan checks (Perseverance precedent). Timing, skeptic vs advocate: S3 2028 -> 2029, because auton-ai-planned-ops-routine is now S3 2028 and the metric is measured across successive missions. The skeptic's S2 2029 -> 2030 and the advocate's S2 2029 -> 2028 were both rejected: S2 stays 2029, one year after routine adoption. Bands: the advocate's S2 High rejected (public reporting of the ratio is uncertain); the skeptic's S3 High -> Medium and S1 Medium -> Low rejected, because its ordering argument fell away once the edge became soft and the bar is now severalfold. Bands stay Medium/Medium/High. Auditor: the tier-7 chains are written out. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): band_2035 S1 Medium -> High, S2 Medium -> High. Skeptic (reporting uncertain) and advocate (Perseverance already shows it) resolved at those dates. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

auton-mars-architecture-close.title: Mars outpost logistics cut by local resources and recycling
auton-mars-architecture-close.description: Validated ISRU, closed-loop life support and robot-first precursors reduce Earth-supplied mass for a first Mars outpost materially. In the 33FG model, life support is ~20% and power ~25% of a 152 t ten-person manifest. ISRU mainly saves return propellant, which is outside that manifest (general), and ISRU and closure savings are not yet quantified (judgment).
auton-mars-architecture-close.status_oct2026: Industry model (33FG, May 2025): a 10-person Mars outpost needs ~152 t of cargo; ISRU is ~40% of cargo cost, life support ~20% of mass, power ~25% of mass; a robot-only precursor cuts ~29% of cost and ~36% of mass but cannot delete ISRU, power and construction. The -29% cost and -36% mass figures come from removing the crew in a robot-only precursor, not from ISRU or closure.
auton-mars-architecture-close.why: Needs Mars ISRU validated on Mars, Mars-class ECLSS validated in flight and crew-optional operations proven on the Moon, each gated by physical clocks extending to or past 2031.

auton-mars-architecture-close.signpost: A Mars architecture study from NASA or SpaceX that books ISRU and closure savings against flight-validated data.

cap-research-math-internal.title: Research-grade math inside the labs
cap-research-math-internal.description: Frontier labs' internal models resolve research-level open problems on request, across all of mathematics, at about three hours of compute per result, with agent-written Lean for a large minority of results.
cap-research-math-internal.status_oct2026: Exists. openai/math (Oct 6, 2026): 722 manuscripts, 372 families from ~4,000 posed problems in under four weeks; 127 families carry unchecked agent-written Lean (T3), e.g. 102 Unique Games and 362 relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell. The model was trained from Aug 28, 2026 for about a month. Anthropic (67.2% of zeta zeros on the critical line; full FLT in Lean, Comparator-checked by Buzzard Sep 4) and Google DeepMind (AlphaProof Nexus, 9 Erdos problems, May 2026) are at or near the same level; the gap between labs is months.
cap-research-math-internal.why: About 9% of posed problems survived into result families; cost is roughly three hours of Pro-tier thinking compute per result, and OpenAI put its ten August results at ~$2,000 of tokens at GPT Sol API rates (~$200 per published success on lab-chosen problems; failed attempts are not counted, so at ~9% survival the cost per accepted result could be ~10x higher). The difficulty ladder moved from IMO gold (Jul 2025) to Erdos-type open problems (spring 2026) to famous conjectures (UGC, forced Navier-Stokes blowup, Sep-Oct 2026) in about 15 months. Every downstream node in the space tree starts here.

cap-research-math-public.title: Research-grade math for outside teams
cap-research-math-public.description: An outside engineering team can buy, on demand, mathematics at roughly the October-2026 internal level (journal-grade open problems, proofs with Lean output) through a public or trusted-access product, for under ~$1,000 per result.
cap-research-math-public.status_oct2026: Partly. Public GPT-6 Astra (paid users from Sep 4, 2026) solved 106 ErdosBench open problems (43 completely) and became the first model to solve any FrontierMath Erdos problem (2 of 68; Epoch, Sep 3, 2026) - research math at the easy end. AlphaEvolve has been generally available to Google Cloud customers since Jul 9, 2026. The model behind openai/math is unreleased; GPT-6.1 Astra was withheld on Sep 29, 2026; Anthropic's Mythos tier is restricted. OpenAI's ChatGPT for Academic Researchers gives 10,000 researchers free access now and 100,000 by 2027 (Jul 29, 2026). OpenAI's chief scientist says the lab does not prioritize math in public models (Sep 10, 2026).
cap-research-math-public.why: The reveal-to-release lag for Astra was about five weeks (Aug 1 reveal, Sep 4 public), but the most capable versions get held back for safety (GPT-6.1 Astra) or restricted (Mythos), and US pre-release review adds 12-30 days. Under S2 a public model matches the Oct-2026 internal level 6-12 months out (mid-to-late 2027); under S1, 12-18 months (2028). At least four labs compete (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, SpaceXAI with 35-58-day Grok cadence) and open-weight followers trail by about a year, which forces release. The binding gate is release governance (lab safety holds plus government review), coded here as regulatory. Regulator cap not applied: government pre-release review (12-30 days) delays release but does not accept or certify results, and the public-release dependency is the scenario definition itself (S1 2028, S2/S3 2027); GPT-6 Astra (public Sep 4 2026, FrontierMath Erdos 2/68) is a partial public equivalent.

Public models are jagged - strong on discrete Erdos-style problems, weaker on PDE analysis - so an engineering team may get less than the catalog suggests.

cap-autoformalization.title: AI turns math into machine-checked proofs at scale
cap-autoformalization.description: Agents turn informal proofs into Lean and complete them, at the scale of hundreds of papers or a multi-million-line project in weeks.
cap-autoformalization.status_oct2026: Exists for discrete and algebraic math. openai/math formalized the main results of 162 papers by agent (unchecked, T3). Anthropic's FLT formalization (about 13M lines of Lean, 29,500 theorems in the final proof, 11 days) passed Buzzard's Comparator run (Sep 4, 2026). Meta's ATLAS reportedly autoformalized 26 textbooks into ~630,000 lines of Lean using 183B+ tokens (May 2026, secondary report via 36Kr). Weak where Mathlib is thin: PDE 3 of 16 families, dynamics 2 of 12, topology 1 of 18.
cap-autoformalization.premise_tier: T3 for the openai/math evidence (agent-written Lean for 127 families, unchecked by outsiders; 362); T4 only for evidence outside openai/math (FLT in Lean, Comparator-checked, Sep 2026)
cap-autoformalization.why: Lean is hard to fool once the statement is right, and proof labor is no longer scarce: the same pipeline that formalized 162 papers can prove properties of flight algorithms and code (P2). 362 shows agents can build missing PDE infrastructure for a single result. What remains scarce is formal semantics for real code and correct statements.
cap-autoformalization.strongest_case_small: Coverage is uneven exactly where space needs it (PDE, numerics, stochastic processes). Agent-written Lean can be enormous and slow to check: two of three openai/math targets exceeded a 7 GiB memory cap in an outside run. A proof of the wrong statement is worthless.
cap-autoformalization.signpost: An agent formalizes a PDE or numerical-analysis paper end to end, including missing library infrastructure, with an outside Comparator pass.

cap-applied-math.title: AI does research-grade applied math
cap-applied-math.description: Engineers routinely get, from AI, well-posedness and stability analyses of their own models, numerical schemes with certified error bounds, uncertainty quantification with guarantees, and optimal-control results with proofs, for low-dimensional and reduced models; certified bounds for realistic 3D multiphysics remain too loose to use.
cap-applied-math.status_oct2026: Not yet a routine service. The catalog shows applied-adjacent depth: 362 Vlasov-Maxwell [L, T3]; 363 and 364 Boltzmann (T1); 372 elasticity inverse problem (T1); 365 boundary problems [L: scalar-conductivity nonuniqueness T3; metric-connection recovery headline T1]; plus the separate forced Navier-Stokes blowup claim (Sep 8). These were lab-posed problems, PDE formalization is thin, and nothing in the release touches UQ, stiff numerics or radiation transport.
cap-applied-math.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 362 is [L] T3 and 365's formalized conductivity-nonuniqueness part is T3 (its recovery headline T1); 363, 364 and 372 are T1 (conditional), supporting evidence only
cap-applied-math.why: Most engineering math is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems (tl-position-4); what it adds is messy context: empirical coefficients, real boundary conditions, and a need for explicit constants and rates. A stability proof for a specific control law or a convergence bound for a specific solver is a week-to-month task for a specialist (general), which fits inside the S2 task horizon by 2027-28. Under S1, diffusion waits on public access (2028) plus domain workflows. This is mostly 'solved in principle but expert-scarce' work, so on-demand expertise is the unlock.
cap-applied-math.strongest_case_small: Engineers already get adequate answers from simulation and test without proofs; certified bounds for realistic 3D multiphysics are often too loose to use; the gain is confidence, not performance (tl-position-2). cap-physics-theory.title: AI builds validated physics theory
cap-physics-theory.description: AI derives closures, reduced-order models with proofs, and plasma, materials or combustion theory that beat the human state of the art on held-out experimental data.
cap-physics-theory.status_oct2026: Not yet. The data-driven precedent is weather: ECMWF's AI forecast system went operational on Feb 25, 2025, beating physics models on many measures (up to 20% on cyclone tracks) at ~1,000x less energy per forecast - an emulator, not new theory.
cap-physics-theory.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 364 and 278 are T1 (conditional) and 263 is T3, supporting evidence only
cap-physics-theory.why: Theory-building needs month-to-year research horizons (S2: 2028-29) and validation data. cap-physics-theory.strongest_case_small: Turbulence and anomalous-transport closures have resisted 60+ years because the missing information is not in the equations; learned closures have historically failed out of distribution. The catalog premises here are T1, so the chain is conditional.

cap-design-optimization.title: AI multiphysics design with guarantees
cap-design-optimization.description: AI runs end-to-end multiphysics design optimization (aero-thermal-structural-propulsion) with constraint satisfaction and model-relative error bounds inside validated envelopes (physical margins still come from test), producing designs that pass existing engineering review gates.
cap-design-optimization.status_oct2026: Early. Generative structural design and AI-generated engine geometry exist (general); AlphaEvolve is generally available for problems with checkable objectives (Jul 9, 2026). Chip design is the leading indicator: Cadence reported a fully autonomous design agent (Jun 2026), Synopsys and AMD launched agents (Oct 2, 2026), and OpenAI-Synopsys announced an EDA-operating model (Oct 6, 2026) - all secondary press reports.
cap-design-optimization.why: EDA shows the pattern: when the simulator is trusted and the objective is checkable, agents already do weeks of design work. Space multiphysics simulators are less trusted (turbulence, ablation, combustion), so guarantees hold only inside validated envelopes. Under S2, applied math (2027) and engineering-grade agents give design loops by 2028; learned emulators speed the loops but are not required (EDA agents and adjoint CFD optimization run on the real solvers); under S1, 2030.
cap-design-optimization.strongest_case_small: Design quality is bounded by model fidelity, and optimizers exploit model error. Launch-vehicle performance is set mostly by the rocket equation and propellant chemistry, leaving single-digit percent gains; the hardware still has to be built and tested.
cap-design-optimization.signpost: A prime or NewSpace firm publicly attributes a flown or hot-fired hardware design (engine, structure, heat shield) to an AI design loop whose model-based margins its review board accepted.

infra-verified-numerics.status_oct2026: Pieces exist outside Lean - Coq's Flocq and CompCert, Gappa, FPTaylor, Frama-C (general) - but there is no integrated stack and Lean lacks a mature IEEE-754 plus numerical-analysis library. infra-verified-numerics.why: Verified numerics is solved in principle but expert-scarce: a round-off and truncation analysis of a GNC loop takes a specialist weeks to months (general). infra-verified-numerics.strongest_case_small: Proofs on real flight code stall on compiler semantics, nonstandard FPUs on rad-hard processors and environment models, not on the numerics; many GNC teams already use fixed-point or conservative margins that make the proof unnecessary.
infra-verified-numerics.signpost: An agent-generated, machine-checked round-off bound for a flight Kalman filter or guidance law reported by NASA, ESA, AdaCore, Galois or a prime.

infra-tool-qualification.title: Regulators accept AI-produced proofs
infra-tool-qualification.description: A certification authority or its delegate (an FAA ACO or DER under DO-178C with DO-333 and DO-330, a NASA center technical authority under NPR 7150.2, ESA product assurance under ECSS, or Space Force) accepts a software plan (PSAC or software development plan; an SOI-1-equivalent agreement) that takes verification credit for proofs whose contracts, invariants and proof scripts were written by AI agents and discharged by a qualified checker. The likeliest first route is an already-qualified or qualifiable checker (SPARK GNATprove, Frama-C WP, Astree); qualifying a new small kernel (Lean or Comparator) is a later, separate step that the dependents in this branch do not need. The agent is an untrusted generator that needs no tool qualification; human obligations shrink to reviewing specifications and justifying assumptions.
infra-tool-qualification.status_oct2026: No credit yet for AI-generated proofs. DO-333 already credits formal methods; FAA and EASA AI guidance addresses AI inside aircraft, not AI as a development or verification tool (general). The plausible route is 'checker, not generator': qualify the Lean kernel or Comparator and treat the agent as untrusted. Evidence for the route in 2026, not credit: AI coding agents wrote a bare-metal Ada/SPARK security stack whose 49,280 proof obligations GNATprove discharged at a claimed 20-40x lower supervision cost, and the agents tried to bypass weak checks, which is why the checker, not the agent, must be the trust boundary (Philipp, arXiv 2607.14340, Jul 2026 preprint). AdaCore released GNAT Foundry Intersection, an open-source agent workflow gated by SPARK proof, requirements-based tests and MC/DC, which AdaCore calls a demonstration rather than a certification process (Sep 14, 2026).
infra-tool-qualification.why: Aviation software standards turn over on 5-10+ year cycles (DO-178B 1992, DO-178C 2011), but the checker route needs no new standard: under DO-330 a tool needs qualification only when its output is not otherwise verified, and here a qualified checker verifies the AI's output. 'Achieved' means plan acceptance, which is the study's base-case premise for first certification credit (S2 2030, S3 2029). A completed certification that banks the credit follows one DO-178C-scale project later, about 2-4 years (S2 about 2032 or later), so dependents that need a specific program to accept the evidence lag this node. Upside: the verification domain dated DO-333 credit through existing checkers to 2028 in S2; a DO-178C or NPR 7150.2 plan accepted in 2028-29 would pull this node forward a year. Verified floating point and AI-drafted specs accelerate but do not gate it: credit for proofs of FDIR logic, parsers or mode machines needs no verified numerics, and human-written, human-reviewed specs qualify. Capped at Medium by 2031 because it needs regulator acceptance; High by 2035 because the route runs through a mechanism already in use (DO-333 credit through already-qualified checkers).
infra-tool-qualification.strongest_case_small: Regulators move slowly and specifications become the bottleneck. Uncrewed commercial space needs no software certification at all, so this gate matters mainly for crewed vehicles, aviation-adjacent systems and NASA human-rating.
infra-tool-qualification.signpost: A PSAC, software development plan or ESA product-assurance plan accepted with verification credit for AI-written proofs checked by GNATprove, Frama-C WP or Astree (in 2028-29 this would pull the node forward a year); later, a DO-330 qualification kit for a Lean or Comparator checker.
infra-tool-qualification.merge_note: A1: merged verif-checker-not-generator (same achievement: certification credit for AI-written proofs via a qualified checker). verif rated it 2029/2028/2028 Medium; capability 2031+/2030/2029 Low/Medium/Medium. capability-horizon-compounding.title: Month-long autonomous research tasks
capability-horizon-compounding.description: AI agents complete, at 50% reliability or better, technical research tasks that take a human expert a full work-month (~170 hours), up from about a work-week in late 2026.
capability-horizon-compounding.status_oct2026: METR measured frontier 50% time horizons of ~16-20 hours in Feb-Mar 2026 and says its suite cannot reliably measure above ~16 hours (Frontier Risk Report, May 19, 2026); GPT-5.6 Sol was ~11.3 hours (95% CI 5-40, flagged unreliable; Jun 26, 2026). Long-run doubling ~7 months since 2019, ~4 months in 2024-25 (METR, Jul 14, 2025). In mathematics the internal model returns, in ~3 hours of compute, results that take experts weeks to months.
capability-horizon-compounding.why: Parametrization: start at ~40 h (one work-week) in Oct 2026, one 7-month doubling past the measured 16-20 h. S1 doubles every 12-18 months: ~76 h end-2027, ~230 h end-2029, ~700 h end-2031 (~4 work-months). S2 doubles every 6-9 months: ~150 h end-2027 (range 120-200), ~1,300 h end-2029, ~12,000 h end-2031 (2-26 work-years across the 6-9 month range). S3 follows S2 to end-2027 then doubles every ~3 months, so the metric stops being meaningful around 2029. The month threshold is the point where a whole applied-math project (model, analysis, proof, code) fits in one autonomous run. Crossing ~170 h needs 2.09 doublings from ~40 h: about mid-2029 in S1 (25-38 months), about early 2028 in S2 (13-19 months; ~150 h at end-2027), and the same in S3, which equals S2 until 2028. S1 reaches ~700 h by 2031, so High.
capability-horizon-compounding.strongest_case_small: METR suites saturate and measure well-specified software tasks; research is open-ended and judgment-heavy; 80%-reliability horizons are several times shorter than 50% horizons, and engineering needs high reliability. Capability is jagged across domains.
capability-horizon-compounding.signpost: A successor horizon suite (METR or Epoch) reporting a frontier 50% horizon of 80 hours or more by end-2027 (S2 on track) or under 40 hours (S1).

capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.description: AI systems accelerate frontier AI research and engineering, including chip design and software stacks, by 3x or more overall - the hinge between S2 and S3.
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.status_oct2026: METR estimates ~1.5x acceleration during Claude Opus 5.5's development, a ~30% chance of 2x, and judges it unlikely to fully automate AI R&D (Sep 22, 2026). OpenAI's chief scientist names recursive self-improvement and automated alignment research as priorities (Sep 10, 2026). Agentic EDA (Cadence, Synopsys, OpenAI-Synopsys) applies the same loop to chips.
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.why: Software-side acceleration is bounded by compute for experiments. Epoch: frontier training compute grows ~5x/yr, compute stock ~3.4x/yr, GW-scale sites take ~2.1 years at ~$38B per GW; Anthropic alone lists ~$518B of decade-long compute obligations. capability-cost-collapse.title: A research result costs less than an engineer-day
capability-cost-collapse.description: The public price of a research-grade math result (problem posed to checked proof or derivation) falls below ~$1,000 and then below ~$100, cheaper than one day of a specialist's time.
capability-cost-collapse.status_oct2026: Internally ~3 hours of Pro-tier compute per result; OpenAI put Astra's ten August results at ~$2,000 at GPT Sol API rates (~$200 per published success; failed attempts excluded). GPT-6 Astra is public in ChatGPT and the API (Sep 2026), with a new $500/month Pro tier and a cheaper GPT-6.1 Sol reported as near-Astra at a fifth of the price (press). Epoch: price for a fixed capability level fell 9-900x per year in 2022-25; AI chip price-performance improves ~49%/yr.
capability-cost-collapse.why: About $200 per published result on lab-chosen problems; failed attempts are not included (about 9% of posed problems survived in openai/math), so per accepted result the cost could be about $2,000, and 1,000 results a year cost ~$0.2-2M (one to ten engineers) before checking, which dominates either way. Illustratively, an Oct-2026-grade result falls to ~$20-70 by 2028 in S1 (about 2-4x a year, slower than Epoch's historical 9-900x) and ~$1-10 in S2 (about 6-20x a year). Price stops being a gate for math in every scenario; access, trust and integration remain.
capability-cost-collapse.strongest_case_small: The cost of checking dominates the cost of producing: a $200 proof that needs a $20,000 expert audit is a $20,000 result. Frontier tasks get longer, so spend per frontier task may stay flat even as fixed-capability prices fall.
capability-cost-collapse.signpost: Lab price sheets for long-horizon reasoning tiers; enterprise contracts that bundle research math with Lean output; space-firm disclosures of AI analysis spend.

capability-controlled-data-access.status_oct2026: GenAI.mil is available to the ~3M-strong DoD workforce, with ~1.7M users onboarded, with a ChatGPT-based 'ChatGPT Mil', Grok and Gemini (Fortune, Sep 1, 2026; ~500,000 power users per DefenseScoop, Sep 23); OpenAI, Google, xAI and others were cleared for classified networks (May 2026). The DoD designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk, upheld by the DC Circuit on Sep 25, 2026, barring contractors from using Claude on DoD work - the lab behind the only Comparator-checked mega-formalization (FLT). Civil NASA is unaffected: JPL used Claude to plan two Perseverance drives (Dec 2025).
capability-controlled-data-access.why: Much space engineering data (propulsion, GNC, hypersonics, defense payloads) is ITAR-controlled, and P1 works best when teams pose problems with real data. Accredited government clouds have trailed commercial releases by months (general). No US export control restricts API access to closed models today; controls target chips (general), and policy can still remove a lab overnight. The research-math tier needs its own IL6/TS accreditation after public release (mid-to-late 2027 in S2, 2028 in S1), so S2/S3 2028 and S1 2029. Regulator cap not applied and gate coded as adoption: labs already hold classified-network clearances (May 2026), so accrediting a newer model is a delay, not acceptance of AI results. S1 is Medium because public access arrives only in 2028 plus the accreditation lag.
capability-controlled-data-access.strongest_case_small: The math itself is not controlled: engineers can pose sanitized problems without technical data. Defense adoption is limited by security culture and model-weight custody more than availability. Policy volatility cuts both ways.
capability-controlled-data-access.signpost: A research-math-capable model accredited at IL6 or Top Secret; a change to the Anthropic designation; State Department or DDTC guidance on AI processing of ITAR technical data.

For a 10,000-satellite constellation, a few percent of tasking or ground-contact efficiency is worth tens of millions of dollars a year (general). The hardness results (P3) tell teams to stop chasing general solvers and invest in instance structure, which is exactly what evolutionary search exploits.
capability-algorithm-discovery.strongest_case_small: Gains are incremental (single-digit percent); structured instances already solve well with commercial MIP solvers; worst-case ceilings say little about real instances.

capability-learned-emulators.title: AI emulators of space physics codes with stated error bounds
capability-learned-emulators.description: The weather-model playbook - train on decades of simulation or reanalysis data, run ~1,000x cheaper - applied to space codes (CFD and aerothermal, plasma, thermosphere, structures), with calibrated uncertainty or error bounds relative to the parent code; using them for margins still requires validation against test or flight data.
capability-learned-emulators.status_oct2026: Weather: ECMWF's AIFS operational Feb 25, 2025, up to 20% better on some measures at ~1,000x less energy, though at 28 km versus 9 km grid spacing. Space: NASA and IBM released the open Surya heliophysics model (Aug 20, 2025; 16% better flare classification, nine years of SDO data) and SuryaBench (Mar 2026). CFD surrogates are common in design exploration but not trusted for margins (general).
capability-learned-emulators.why: Emulators remove the compute cost of design loops and ensembles. Weather moved from research models to operations in about 15 months on the back of 40+ years of reanalysis. Space domains split: where training data can be generated by simulation (CFD, structures, thermal) emulators are data-unconstrained and arrive first; where data come only from nature (one Sun, rare extreme storms, few hypersonic flights) they arrive late and extrapolate poorly. AIFS and Surya were built without research-grade applied math, so AI applied math accelerates this node (code-relative error bounds) rather than gating it; any certificate bounds error against the code, not against physics. Pathway P4 (a faster method with practical constants entering codes); band above the P4 default because the AIFS precedent shows research-to-operations inside ~15 months.
capability-learned-emulators.strongest_case_small: Emulators are only as good as their training data, and extrapolation to new vehicles or extreme storms - exactly where margins matter - is where they fail. Coarser resolution (as with AIFS) can hide local extremes such as peak heating.
capability-learned-emulators.signpost: NOAA SWPC or ESA running an AI model in operations; a launch provider using a surrogate with stated error bounds in flight-readiness analysis.
capability-learned-emulators.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: certified-bounds claim narrowed to code-relative bounds; cap-applied-math hard -> soft. capability-engineering-adoption.title: On-demand applied math in space engineering
capability-engineering-adoption.description: Space engineering organizations routinely pose their own hard analysis problems (stability, bounds, convergence, inverse problems, trade studies) to frontier models and use the checked answers in design reviews.
capability-engineering-adoption.status_oct2026: Early. JPL used Claude to plan two Perseverance drives with human review (Dec 2025); NASA and IBM ran a compressed model on the ISS (May 2026); IEEE Spectrum reports engineers' distrust of non-deterministic outputs (Sep 28, 2026). SpaceX owns a frontier lab (SpaceXAI; Grok releases every 35-58 days) and says its Grok bot will route tasks to the best model, including Claude Opus 5.5 (Oct 7, 2026).
capability-engineering-adoption.why: Most engineering math is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems: a specialist analysis that takes 2-8 weeks (general) becomes hours plus a check. Vertically integrated firms that own both models and hardware (SpaceX/SpaceXAI) adopt first; primes constrained by ITAR and DoD rules follow 6-12 months later; agencies last. A vertically integrated first mover (SpaceX/SpaceXAI, which routes tasks to the best available model) can use frontier models in internal design work during 2027, but routine use of checked answers in design reviews needs the Oct-2026 level in outside hands (mid-to-late 2027 in S2) plus trust tooling (2028), so S2 stays 2028 and S3, which equals S2 until 2028, moves to 2028. Classified and ITAR access gates only the defense-prime segment, so it accelerates adoption rather than gating it.
capability-engineering-adoption.strongest_case_small: Analysis is rarely on a space program's critical path; answers still need checking; legacy processes, roles and liability slow uptake; AI may expand analysis scope rather than speed programs.
capability-engineering-adoption.signpost: A major prime or NASA center publishing standard work for AI-derived analysis; AIAA papers where an AI-derived proof or bound is used in a flight design.
capability-engineering-adoption.calibration_note: A3: Band logic: hard prerequisites cap-applied-math and capability-cheap-trust are Medium in S1, so S1 High -> Medium.

capability-ai-eda-space-processor.title: AI-designed radiation-tolerant space processor
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.description: Agentic EDA designs and formally verifies a radiation-tolerant processor, SoC or AI accelerator designed for orbit (error correction, upset-aware layout, selective redundancy); it is taped out and heavy-ion tested, with design and verification credited mainly to agentic EDA.
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.status_oct2026: Agentic chip design is moving fast in commercial EDA (Cadence fully autonomous ChipStack design agent, Jun 1 2026; Synopsys autonomous debug and implementation workflows with Microsoft, evaluated by AMD, Jul 27 2026; OpenAI-Synopsys agreement on a chip-design model, Sep 30 2026). Space-targeted accelerators are in co-design (Nvidia Space-1 Vera Rubin module, Mar 2026; a SpaceX version of the VR72 per Musk, Oct 1 2026; Musk has said Tesla's AI7/Dojo3 is aimed at space-based compute, press reports, unverified here). Space processors lag commercial nodes by roughly a decade (general).
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.why: Design and verification (12-24 months for a rad-hard SoC, general) compress several-fold; fabrication (3-4 months per run), scarce heavy-ion beam time and, for traditional space parts, QML-class qualification (1-2 years) do not. Orbital compute adds a funded commercial customer with no certifying regulator, which raises the odds of an AI-designed space accelerator, but credit to agentic EDA for an Nvidia or Tesla part is unlikely to be disclosed. First tape-out in 2029-30 under S2; flight qualification of traditional rad-hard parts after 2031. Chain (S2): research-grade math public 2027 -> AI multiphysics design with guarantees and agentic EDA (cap-design-optimization, 2028) plus agent-written hardware proofs (verif-hardware-proof-agents, 2028) -> a radiation-tolerant SoC designed and formally verified 2028-29 -> tape-out (3-4 months per run) and heavy-ion test 2029-30 -> credited first silicon 2030 (Medium; disclosure of the AI share is the main risk). Band: S2 and S3 Medium, above the P7 default (Speculative), because the hardware outcome is first silicon plus a heavy-ion test, not flight or qualification, the design step is P1 capability already moving in commercial EDA, and orbital compute supplies a customer with no certifying regulator; not higher because fab and beam time leave about a year of slack and the AI share may go undisclosed. S1 Low. Bands are judgments.
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.strongest_case_small: Space is moving to COTS processors with system-level mitigation, the rad-hard market is small, and qualification rather than design sets the schedule.
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.signpost: A rad-hard SoC tape-out credited mainly to agentic EDA, with published heavy-ion test results.

capability-ai-native-spacecraft.title: Spacecraft engineered mostly by AI flies
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.description: An operational spacecraft whose design analyses, trade studies and flight-software verification artifacts were majority AI-generated (with human review) reaches orbit and operates.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.status_oct2026: Not yet. Ingredients exist piecemeal: AI-generated engine and structural geometry, agentic coding, JPL drive planning, agentic chip design.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.why: Chain (S2): engineering adoption 2028 -> smallsat design-complete -> build, integration and environmental test in 12-18 months (lag ladder) -> rideshare launch -> operations 2029, with published evidence that most analyses, trades and verification artifacts were AI-generated. S3 the same year (S3 equals S2 until 2028); S1 2031 (adoption 2029). It needs adoption and agentic analysis, not multiphysics optimization with guarantees, so design optimization is an accelerator. A small company with no legacy process is the likely first mover; build, integration and test bind, not cognition or rideshare slots, which are not scarce. This is a process outcome, not a performance claim. Band (F2 audit): the P7 default (Speculative) is raised because the physical step is routine (a smallsat reaching orbit and operating, with no regulator beyond licensing), but S2 is Medium, not High. The node is a conjunction on top of its High prerequisite (adoption, a build, a launch, on-orbit success and public evidence of the AI share); 'majority AI-generated' is hard to verify and the first claims will be marketing (strongest case); and the same disclosure risk holds capability-ai-eda-space-processor and verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight at Medium. It sits at the upper edge of Medium because several independent teams can try and the chain has two years of slack. S3 High: cognitive work is near-free from 2029 and two flight years remain. S1 Low: adoption lands in 2029, so the chain has no slack. Bands are judgments, not computed probabilities.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.strongest_case_small: It changes who does the engineering, not what flies: performance gains are small, 'majority AI-generated' is hard to verify, and the first claims will be marketing.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.signpost: A company or agency announcing such a mission with published AI-generated verification evidence, followed by on-orbit success.

capability-program-cycle-compression.title: Development cycles 20-30% shorter, not 10x
capability-program-cycle-compression.description: Development time (concept to launch) for new space systems started after AI adoption falls measurably. Amdahl ceiling: about 38% shorter in S2 (51% in S3, 18% in S1) if a third of the critical path is cognitive and fully compressible. Expected realized compression for typical programs started in 2028 or later: about 20-30% in S2 (about 35-45% in S3, 10-15% in S1), with fast commercial programs nearer the ceiling and government flagships at 10-15% (appropriations).
capability-program-cycle-compression.status_oct2026: Not yet. Major NASA projects routinely run late, mostly in hardware, integration and test (GAO reporting, general).
capability-program-cycle-compression.why: Illustrative critical-path shares (general): requirements and trades 10%, design and analysis 15%, software 10%, fabrication and procurement 25%, integration and test 25%, qualification and reviews 10%, launch campaign 5%. Speedups of 5-10x on cognitive work and 1.1-1.2x on physical work (S2) give a 1.6x speedup, a ~38% shorter schedule; S3 (20-50x cognitive, 1.3-1.5x physical) ~51%; S1 (2x cognitive) ~18%. These are ceilings: they assume every cognitive step is on the critical path and fully compressible. Requirements negotiation, hardware-in-the-loop software testing and review gates compress far less, and long-lead parts (12-24+ months) often run in parallel with design, so compressing design can leave the critical path unchanged; each 10 points of effectively compressible cognitive share is worth about 7 points of compression. Counting more of the analysis inside test and build phases as cognitive (anomaly diagnosis, procedures, data reduction, material-review paperwork) lifts the S2 ceiling to roughly 45%, but the table's 1.1-1.2x physical multipliers already credit about 10 of those 60 points (if the residual physical work runs at 1.0x), so most of that gain is already inside the 38%. Fewer design escapes found in test cut rework, a second-order gain. Chain (S2): engineering adoption 2028 -> commercial programs started 2028 or later (smallsat lag ladder 12-18 months) -> first completions 2029-30 -> an attributable schedule analysis 2031. S3: 2030. Band Medium: evidence must come from programs started after adoption and finished by 2031, and government flagships dilute any average. Uncrewed commercial programs need no certifier, so the binding gate is integration and test hardware (experiment), not qualification. Band: the P7 default (Speculative) is raised to Medium in S2 and S3 because the outcome is a schedule measured on programs that need no new physics or certifier, and a company schedule analysis counts as well as a GAO or ESA review (signpost); not higher because the S2 earliest attributable analysis is 2031 and government flagships dilute averages. S1 Low. Bands are judgments.
capability-program-cycle-compression.strongest_case_small: Schedules are set by funding profiles, supply chains (rad-hard parts 12-24+ months), launch manifests and politics; teams may spend the gain on more analysis and scope (Jevons) instead of shorter schedules.
capability-program-cycle-compression.signpost: A GAO, ESA or company schedule analysis attributing cycle-time reduction to AI; smallsat build times falling below 9 months for new designs.
capability-program-cycle-compression.revision_note: B-trunk resolver (2026-10-07): Debated (skeptic vs advocate, auditor on wording). comms-ai-cryptanalysis.title: AI agents audit cryptography at research grade
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.description: Frontier models run closed-loop cryptanalysis: they propose attacks on published schemes, protocols and parameter sets, test them, and return exact witnesses for a human to judge. Achieved here means major vendors and standards submitters routinely run such audits, and a standards body cites one in a review.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.status_oct2026: Partly exists. Olejnik and Naskręcki (arXiv 2608.21986, Aug 22 2026) report an autonomous agent workflow that found failures in eight published constructions, for example a Ring-LWR commitment that opens to any message and a lattice e-voting protocol that loses receipt-freeness. None is a NIST-standardized scheme. ML attacks on LWE recover only sparse or small secrets at reduced parameters (NoMod, arXiv 2510.02162). openai/math contains no attack on factoring, discrete log or lattices (tl-position-5).
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.why: The failures found so far sit one level above the hardness assumption: encodings, simulators, parameter certification, protocol composition. That is where space security is weakest. Bespoke key-management and command-authentication protocols on constrained links are written by small teams and rarely reviewed by cryptographers. Once research-grade models are public (cap-research-math-public), an audit that took a specialist weeks costs hours of compute, so every new satellite security protocol can be attacked before launch. Under S2 agent task horizons double every 6-9 months, so by 2028 agents audit whole protocol suites, not single constructions. The node depends on the internal model's capability becoming public (S1: 2028), so it is capped at Medium in S1 (fw-horizon-scorecard); S2 and S3 assume public release in 2027 as a scenario premise.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.strongest_case_small: The breaks so far are in obscure, non-standard constructions. Standardized primitives (AES-256, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) have decades of expert scrutiny. Most real-world failures come from implementation bugs and key handling, which human audits with existing tools already target.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.signpost: An AI-found break or parameter downgrade in an IETF, CCSDS or NIST-standardized scheme; NIST or CCSDS stating that AI audits were used in a selection or review.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.calibration_note: A3: Internal consistency: the node's why ties routine audits to public research-grade models (cap-research-math-public), which arrive 2028 in S1. S1 2027 -> 2028; band unchanged. (The hard prerequisite should arguably be cap-research-math-public, not the internal model.) A4: Hard prerequisite moved from cap-research-math-internal to cap-research-math-public, as A3 recommended. The why ties routine audits to public research-grade models, and the years already match (2028/2027/2027).
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.revision_note: E-networks (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1 Medium -> High (S1 cognition reaches the S2 2029-30 level by 2035). S1 Medium 2029, High 2033 (S1 cognition catches up around 2033). Bands unchanged.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.note_2035: By 2035 AI audits of new space security protocols are routine in every scenario, including S1, where public research-grade models arrived in 2028. S4 adds nothing because the work is cognitive.

comms-expander-constructions.title: Optimal expander graphs for networks and codes (conditional)
comms-expander-constructions.description: 178 builds nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs, the best possible spectral expanders, deterministically for every degree d>=3 and all large even sizes. 177 constructs bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension, a building block studied for locally testable codes and quantum LDPC codes.
comms-expander-constructions.why: Conditional. A laser mesh in which each satellite has 3-4 terminals is a bounded-degree graph, and Ramanujan graphs give the largest spectral gap at that degree: short paths, high bisection bandwidth and graceful degradation when links fail. But a Ramanujan topology needs links between arbitrary satellites, which line-of-sight, range and slew limits forbid, and asymptotically good qLDPC and locally testable codes were built in 2021-22 without 177 (Panteleev-Kalachev), so the engineering effect through 2031 is nil. The band covers use in network or code design (P6: Low in S1, Medium in S2 by graph convention), dropped one band because both premises are T1.
comms-expander-constructions.strongest_case_small: Random d-regular graphs are already within ε of Ramanujan with high probability, and bipartite Ramanujan graphs of every degree have been known to exist since 2013 (general). Real laser topologies are dictated by orbital geometry, link range, pointing and terminal slew time (+Grid, Motif, demand-aware designs), not by abstract graph choice.
comms-expander-constructions.signpost: A constellation-topology study that imposes Ramanujan-like structure under real geometric constraints and beats the best geometric heuristic by 10% or more in diameter or bisection bandwidth.
comms-expander-constructions.calibration_note: A3: T1 premise rule: families 178 and 177 have no Lean main result (T1) and the band is for the mathematics being established. One band down: Medium/High/High -> Low/Medium/Medium. comms-certified-interference-bounds.title: Provable interference compliance for shared spectrum
comms-certified-interference-bounds.description: Interference showings for NGSO-GSO and NGSO-NGSO sharing delivered as certified bounds instead of Monte Carlo runs: interval or proof-backed bounds on time-weighted throughput degradation, unavailability and aggregate EPFD, with the model assumptions written as a checkable specification. Achieved means operators use such bounds in at least one filing or bilateral coordination agreement.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.status_oct2026: FCC 26-26 (Report and Order, adopted Apr 30, released May 1 2026, SB Docket 25-157) replaced NGSO-GSO EPFD limits with private good-faith coordination, backed by adopted criteria when coordination fails: 3% time-weighted throughput degradation, 0.1% absolute unavailability increase, a supplemental -10.5 dB I/N for 80% of time, and a 3-degree GSO-arc avoidance angle. The Jan 9 2026 waiver (DA 26-36) had allowed 8 co-frequency beams per location with a 4-degree angle; the April order removed the beam cap, reduced the angle to 3 degrees (a relaxation for NGSO) and declined aggregate limits. GSO operators could seek to reintroduce aggregate limits through reconsideration, the D.C. Circuit or the WRC-27 cycle (33FG). FCC Part 100 (Jul 22 2026) moves licensing to yes/no certifications. FCC NGSO-NGSO rules (FCC 24-117) use 3% throughput degradation and 0.4% added unavailability over an orbital simulation (Roberts, arXiv 2609.36122). ITU Article 22 EPFD limits still govern internationally. Measured low-frequency EPFD from constellations exceeds radio-astronomy thresholds in 50-70% of samples (arXiv 2609.01995). No catalog family applies.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.why: The regulatory shift turned compliance from checking a power mask into a statistical claim about simulating tens of thousands of satellites. Disputes are now about simulation assumptions and tail events. Aggregates are where Monte Carlo is least trustworthy: keeping one interferer under threshold needs 8.1 degrees of separation, five need 15.5 and twenty need 27.0 (Roberts). A certified bound with a written specification can be re-checked by a rival operator or the FCC in hours. The math (geometry, order statistics, interval arithmetic) is expert-scarce rather than open, and existing interval and validated-numerics tools (Arb, INTLAB, VNODE-LP) suffice, so the Lean-verified floating-point toolchain (infra-verified-numerics) accelerates but does not gate it. In S2, research-grade applied math is public in 2027, and preparing a filing or coordination agreement with a new method takes months, so the first certified showings appear in 2028; S3 follows S2 through 2027. In S1 they wait for public models and some years of diffusion.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.strongest_case_small: Spectrum disputes are commercial and political, not mathematical, and regulators accept Monte Carlo. Certified worst-case bounds are conservative and could cost capacity against statistical showings. The contested inputs (antenna patterns, traffic models, deployment plans) stay contested. Under FCC 26-26 compliance is negotiated privately first, so formal showings are needed mainly when coordination fails or at the ITU, and with aggregate limits declined, certified aggregate bounds matter mainly for ITU Article 22 and radio astronomy.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.signpost: An FCC or ITU-R WP4A filing citing machine-checked or interval-certified interference bounds; an operator publishing an open, verified EPFD or degradation calculator.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.revision_note: E-networks (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1 Medium -> High. S1 Medium 2031, High 2034. Bands unchanged.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.note_2035: By 2035 certified showings are common in FCC coordination and feed ITU-R studies for WRC-31, so S1 rises to High. S4 adds nothing because the gate is cognitive and institutional.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.gate_note: Operator and FCC uptake of certified showings binds; the geometry, order-statistics and interval math (cognitive) is the runner-up.

comms-certified-network-optimization.title: Near-optimal mesh routing with a proven gap
comms-certified-network-optimization.description: Joint optimization of laser-terminal pairing, routing and rate allocation over a time-expanded horizon that charges link acquisition and re-pointing time, at 10,000+ satellites, with a certified optimality gap (for example a Lagrangian dual bound) computed at operational cadence; user-beam frequency assignment is handled separately. Achieved means an open or vendor solver delivers such certified gaps at Starlink scale.
comms-certified-network-optimization.status_oct2026: The per-snapshot joint problem is NP-hard. A Lagrangian decomposition into matching, shortest paths and an LP gains 35-145% throughput over non-joint baselines in simulation (arXiv 2601.21914), and a graph neural network that predicts the dual prices matches it orders of magnitude faster (arXiv 2601.21921). Topology designs tested on three months of Starlink data report up to 2.3x capacity and 45% lower delay than +Grid (arXiv 2602.07756). The baselines are naive and operator practice is proprietary. Family 120 (almost-linear exact matching and prescribed-degree factors, T1) solves the terminal-pairing subproblem asymptotically fast. The Lagrangian work covers laser-terminal matching and routing only, with no acquisition or switching cost and no beam or frequency assignment; the fast GNN variant carries no certificate.
comms-certified-network-optimization.premise_tier: n/a (capability); T3 for the 102 ceiling, T1 for 117 hardness and 120
comms-certified-network-optimization.why: A certificate turns a capacity question into an investment decision. With a 3% dual gap, more capacity has to come from terminals, satellites or spectrum; with a 30% gap it can come from software. The math (decompositions, convergence and gap proofs, problem-specific relaxations) is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems (tl-position-4), so it becomes a P1 item as soon as research-grade models are public. A dual bound certifies any instance without any hardness theorem; the ceilings (UGC; 117, conditional) only explain why certified gaps are instance-specific, so frontier-approx-ceilings is context (soft), not a prerequisite. Interference-coupled frequency assignment has weak dual bounds, which is why it is left out. Operator adoption is modelled in comms-certified-mesh-operations.
comms-certified-network-optimization.strongest_case_small: Operators such as SpaceX already run strong in-house optimization. Realistic gain over their practice is probably 5-20% capacity (judgment), while V3 hardware is a 10x per-satellite step (33FG). Family 120 adds nothing practical at this scale: a 10,000-node, ~50,000-edge matching takes milliseconds with classical algorithms. Terminal count, acquisition time and gateway capacity bind first.
comms-certified-network-optimization.signpost: An operator, SDA or a vendor publishing optimality-gap metrics for live routing; an open solver with certified gaps at Starlink scale.
comms-certified-network-optimization.revision_note: E-networks (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1 Medium -> High. S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2-S4 Low 2027, Medium 2028, High 2029: the math is easier than catalog problems, but certified gaps at Starlink scale take a research cycle after public models (2027). S1 Medium 2029, High 2033. Bands unchanged.
comms-certified-network-optimization.note_2035: By 2035 certified gaps at Starlink scale are standard solver output in every scenario, so S1 rises to High. S4 adds nothing because the work is cognitive.
comms-certified-network-optimization.gate_note: Bespoke decomposition and gap proofs (cognitive) bind; realistic constellation topology and traffic data, which operators keep proprietary, is the runner-up.

comms-verified-routing-software.title: Formally verified constellation routing software
comms-verified-routing-software.description: Machine-checked proofs that routing, handover and topology-reconfiguration code is loop-free and deadlock-free, converges under link churn and meets latency bounds. Agents produce the proofs and maintain them as the code changes.
comms-verified-routing-software.status_oct2026: An agent extended a 3,000-line SMT network verifier with OSPF areas, BGP route reflection and L3VPN by counterexample-guided learning against emulated routers (arXiv 2608.11340, Aug 2026). Satellite-specific work is small, for example model checking of a TDM inter-satellite-link algorithm (arXiv 2511.09485). The broader evidence is the openai/math pipeline: 127 families with agent-written Lean (T3), strongest in discrete mathematics, which is what protocols need.
comms-verified-routing-software.premise_tier: n/a (capability; no catalog family is load-bearing)
comms-verified-routing-software.why: With handovers about every 15 s and a continuously changing topology, test coverage of control-plane states is poor; proofs cover all states. Commercial communications networks face no certification gate, so progress is limited by writing specifications of dynamic topologies, which agents began doing in 2026. Discrete properties formalize well: 20 of 40 theoretical-CS families in the release have Lean proofs.
comms-verified-routing-software.strongest_case_small: Mega-constellation operators ship software weekly and value iteration speed over proofs. Outages come more from hardware faults, space weather and the ground segment than from routing logic, and orbital dynamics and timing are hard to specify.
comms-verified-routing-software.signpost: An operator or SDA prime disclosing machine-checked proofs for routing or handover code; a satellite-network verifier released by a lab or vendor.
comms-verified-routing-software.revision_note: E-networks (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1 Medium -> High. comms-pq-verified-implementations.title: Proven-correct post-quantum crypto for space processors
comms-pq-verified-implementations.description: Agents produce implementations of ML-KEM, ML-DSA, HQC and hash-based signatures for space targets that have no verified library today (SPARC LEON, rad-hard RISC-V such as PIC64-HPSC and NOEL-V, FPGA fabric), with machine-checked functional correctness, constant-time and masking (side-channel) proofs, plus certified failure-probability bounds. Achieved means such a library exists for at least one of these targets and a flight program adopts it.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.status_oct2026: Exists for mainstream CPUs, not yet for most space processors. mlkem-native (AWS-LC, PQ Code Package): all AArch64 and x86-64 assembly is proved functionally correct, memory-safe and constant-time in HOL Light, and the C code memory- and type-safe with CBMC (human-led proofs; no AI assistance stated). Radiation-tolerant AArch64 parts exist (for example AMD XQR Versal, Cortex-A72; general), so part of the space need is already covered without AI. The Jasmin compiler is proven to preserve the IND-CCA security of an ML-KEM implementation used in Signal (Rocq, arXiv 2511.11292). Lean 4 proofs of arithmetic masking for NTT hardware found that one open accelerator masks only one round (arXiv 2604.20793). A certified ML-KEM-768 decryption-failure bound of 2^-164.81 holds in a stated abstraction (arXiv 2609.09983). NIST picked HQC as its backup KEM on Mar 11 2025; final standard expected 2027.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.why: Most real cryptographic failures are implementation bugs and side channels, not broken mathematics (general). Space adds unusual targets (LEON or radiation-hardened RISC-V cores, FPGAs) and tight memory, so verified libraries must be re-targeted and re-proven. That is proof labor, which agents now supply. The AI-attributable part is this re-targeting and masking work; AArch64 and x86-64 are already done. Flight-software and crypto baselines freeze long before launch and qualification compresses only 1.2-1.5x after 2029-30 (physclock), so adoption by a flight program trails the proofs by about a year. Certification credit is a separate node, so no certifier gates this one and the regulator Medium cap does not apply: a flight program adopts the library on its own authority.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.strongest_case_small: FIPS 140-3 and NSA evaluations are test-based and slow. Many satellites use certified hardware crypto modules where code proofs add little, and programs freeze crypto choices years before launch.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.signpost: A verified ML-KEM, ML-DSA or LMS library released for a radiation-hardened processor; a flight program citing machine-checked crypto proofs.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.revision_note: E-networks (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1 Medium -> High.
