frontier-chaos-linear-response.title: How chaotic systems respond to design changes
frontier-chaos-linear-response.description: Theorems that long-time averages of chaotic systems (turbulent flows, plasma turbulence, the thermosphere) depend differentiably on design parameters, with computable bounds and convergent algorithms. This is the mathematics that would let adjoint and gradient optimization work on unsteady turbulent systems.
frontier-chaos-linear-response.status_oct2026: Linear response is proven for uniformly hyperbolic systems (Ruelle, general) but fails or is unproven for most realistic, non-hyperbolic dynamics. Shadowing-based sensitivity methods work heuristically at high cost (general). Rigorous enclosures of Lyapunov exponents exist for stochastic flows (2024). Catalog: 146 Sinai's positive-entropy conjecture for the standard map (T1), a famous non-hyperbolic chaos problem, suggests the capability has reached this terrain.
frontier-chaos-linear-response.premise_tier: n/a (target unproven); 146 is T1, conditional, context only. Depends on the unreleased internal model until public research-grade access (2027 S2, 2028 S1)
frontier-chaos-linear-response.why: Adjoint design is routine for steady flows but breaks for unsteady chaotic flows, because pathwise sensitivities grow like exp(lambda*t). Combustors, nozzles and thrusters are therefore designed by sampling, at roughly one simulation per parameter direction. A theorem saying when averaged sensitivities exist, with an algorithm, would turn chaotic-flow design into gradient optimization with thousands of parameters (frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design) for flows with few unstable modes. A linear-response theorem alone does not make gradients cheap for wall-bounded turbulence, where shadowing-type adjoints cost roughly one simulation per positive Lyapunov exponent (about 1,200-1,500 for channel flow at Re_tau=180; Blonigan et al., arXiv 1702.06809). A negative answer would also help (P3), since it ends a research line. This is an under-appreciated node: less famous than Navier-Stokes, far more consequential for design.
frontier-chaos-linear-response.strongest_case_small: Surrogate and Bayesian optimization with a few hundred simulations already handles modest parameter counts. Realistic flows may lack linear response in the needed regimes, and most design value comes from validated physics models, not gradients.
frontier-chaos-linear-response.signpost: A proof of linear response with a convergent sensitivity algorithm for a non-uniformly hyperbolic flow class (a Lorenz-type flow or a Galerkin-truncated Navier-Stokes system).
frontier-chaos-linear-response.calibration_note: A3: Premise label and internal-model dependency noted (scorecard).

frontier-approx-ceilings.title: Hardness limits for scheduling and network planning (unaudited)
frontier-approx-ceilings.description: Hardness-of-approximation ceilings for the combinatorial problems behind constellation tasking, ground-station and gateway siting, routing, beam frequency assignment and network partitioning become formal claims awaiting outside checks rather than beliefs: beating Goemans-Williamson Max-Cut (beam two-colouring) or factor-2 vertex cover (minimal link/beam sets) is NP-hard given 102 (UGC claimed with an unaudited Lean proof, T3); uniform sparsest cut (mesh partitioning) has no constant-factor algorithm (conditional, T1); metric k-median siting is pinned at 1+2/e. These are worst-case ceilings for general graphs and metrics. Operational instances are geometric (toroidal +Grid/Motif laser meshes, Earth-surface siting, disk-like beam-conflict graphs), and there approximation schemes or O(1) algorithms exist, so the ceilings bound general-purpose solver research and vendor claims about general instances, not constellation planning.
frontier-approx-ceilings.status_oct2026: Catalog: 102 Unique Games Conjecture (T3; the Lean covers UGC plus the direct Max-Cut and Vertex Cover reductions), which makes Goemans-Williamson Max-Cut (0.878) and 2-approximate vertex cover optimal; 125 metric k-median threshold 1+2/e, about 1.736 (T3; lean/docs/125.md: the deterministic (1+2/e+eps) algorithm and the threshold under P!=NP are formalized); 117 uniform sparsest cut: SDP integrality gap T3, NP-hardness T1 (statement gap: the Lean result is 'an existential sequence, not a computational hardness theorem'); 104: randomized quasipolynomial mean-payoff algorithm T3, deterministic, stochastic and parity versions T1; 124 polynomial-time scheduling on three identical machines (T1); 110 optimal randomized k-server (T1); 111 matroid prophet inequalities (T1). No outside Comparator run reported as of Oct 7, 2026; repo has a single initial commit.
frontier-approx-ceilings.premise_tier: T3 (102: UGC plus direct Max-Cut and Vertex Cover reductions formalized; 125: algorithm and threshold per lean/docs/125.md; 104: randomized mean-payoff only; 117: SDP integrality gap only); T1, conditional (117 NP-hardness headline; 104 deterministic, stochastic and parity versions; 124, 110, 111)
frontier-approx-ceilings.why: Ceilings take effect within months (P3), once they are independently checked. Most were already believed, so the change is from belief to theorem: research spending on general-purpose approximation algorithms moves to instance structure, exact MIP on small instances and learned heuristics. On the geometric instances operators actually face the ceilings do not bind: uniform multicommodity flow on graphs that exclude a fixed minor (toroidal laser grids among them) has an O(1) flow-cut gap (Klein-Plotkin-Rao 1993), k-median on Earth-surface (doubling) metrics has a PTAS, vertex cover on disk-like graphs has a PTAS (Hunt et al. 1998), and Max-Cut is exact on planar graphs (Hadlock 1975). This node bounds frontier-scalable-global-certificates. The 117-hardness, 104-extension, 124, 110 and 111 parts are conditional (T1); the band rests on the T3 parts (102, 125) and describes the mathematics, not an engineering effect.
frontier-approx-ceilings.strongest_case_small: Worst-case hardness says little about structured operational instances, and satellite scheduling already solves well in practice (branch-and-cut-and-price, EJOR 2025). These ceilings were assumed for 20 years.
frontier-approx-ceilings.signpost: An independent Comparator run plus statement audit on families 102, 125 and 117 (Hexagon or Buzzard's group).
frontier-approx-ceilings.calibration_note: A3: Wording rule only: premise mixes T3 (102, 125, 117, 104) and T1 (124, 110, 111); why now says the T1 parts are conditional. Bands unchanged. Lead decision pending (auditor): the openai/math repo has Comparator statements plus solution modules for families the catalog marks without L (273, 124, 177, 110, 111, 279); the catalog L flag may undercount. Catalog tiers kept until the lead rules.

frontier-nn-verification-complexity.title: How hard neural networks are to verify
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.description: A substantially complete complexity map for verifying the properties of neural networks used in perception and control (robustness, reachability, Lipschitz bounds), including which architectures or training regimes make verification tractable.
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.status_oct2026: ReLU network verification is NP-complete (Katz et al. 2017, general). Sep 2025: deciding positivity of an l-layer ReLU network is W[l-1]-hard in input dimension; approximating the maximum or the Lipschitz constant is NP-hard; naive n^((l-1)d) enumeration is essentially optimal under ETH (Froese et al.). Tractable classes are partly characterized. Catalog: 102 UGC (T3) supplies hardness machinery; nothing is NN-specific.
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.premise_tier: n/a (human results); T3 (102). Further results depend on the unreleased internal model until public research-grade access (2027 S2, 2028 S1)
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.why: Ceilings tell assurance architects that exact verification of large perception networks will not scale (exponential in input dimension under ETH). That confirms the existing practice of runtime assurance (simplex wrappers; ASTM F3269, 2017 and 2021; verif-runtime-assurance) and verifiable-by-construction controllers rather than pushing designs toward it; the P3 effect is expectation-setting only. Positive results on tractable classes feed verif-nn-verification-scale. Complexity theory is the area where AI math is already strongest (40 TCS families, 20 with Lean).
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.strongest_case_small: Practitioners already know NN verification is hard and already use runtime monitors. The real blocker is specification: there is no formal statement of what 'detect the docking port' means.
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.signpost: A tractability theorem for a practically used architecture class (for example Lipschitz-constrained CNNs at flight scale), or fixed-depth hardness of approximate robustness certification.
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.calibration_note: A3 note superseded (B-math-frontier, auditor): the scorecard internal-model cap (Medium unless a public model of similar capability exists) is lifted because every scenario makes research-grade capability public before 2031 (S2/S3 2027, S1 2028). If that premise fails, these bands drop to Medium.

frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.title: Capacity limits of laser and quantum links (conditional)
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.description: Proofs of the ultimate rates of the optical and quantum channels used for deep-space laser links, optical relays serving several receivers and satellite QKD: 273 (entropy photon-number inequality) makes the optical broadcast-channel capacity region and the thermal-noise optical wiretap secret-key capacity unconditional; 276 gives the exact classical capacity of every qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel; 272 (entangled states with zero distillable key; PPT-squared disproof) says link entanglement does not certify key; 266 (exactly three MUBs in dimension six) confirms prime-power dimensions for high-dimensional QKD.
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.status_oct2026: Catalog: 273 entropy photon-number inequality (T1), which would make capacity formulas for bosonic broadcast and thermal-noise wiretap channels unconditional (single-user thermal-channel classical capacity was already proved in 2014, and pure-loss in 2004, general); the repo's Lean for 273 covers the inequality only, and the broadcast and minimum-output-entropy consequences are outside it; 276 classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping (T3); 272 entanglement without secret key (T1); 266 exactly three MUBs in dimension six (T1). Quantum capacities with superadditivity remain open (general).
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.why: Point-to-point pure-loss (2004) and thermal-noise (2014) optical capacities were already proven; 273 settles, conditionally (T1), only multi-user cases (broadcast, wiretap), so deep-space and inter-satellite link budgets do not change, and wiretap secret-key bounds relevant to QKD gain exact limits (P5 confidence). Bands are one step down from the P5 default because the key premise (273) is T1. No outside Comparator run exists, so no T4 date is forecast.
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.strongest_case_small: Engineers already used the conjectured formulas, and real links run far below capacity because of pointing, atmosphere, detector efficiency and coding. Effect on hardware: nil.
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.signpost: Independent verification of 273 (Lean or expert reconstruction), and citation in CCSDS optical-link standards rationale.
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.merge_note: A1: merged comms-optical-capacity-theory (273) and comms-quantum-channel-limits (276, 266, 272); the frontier node already covered exactly this union. Years agree (2028/2027/2027, S1 2027 for the 276 part). Bands kept at frontier's Low/Medium/Medium because the headline premise 273 is T1 and the framework requires 'conditional' plus a one-band drop; the 276 component alone (Lean OAI.GAD.main, T3, unchecked by outsiders) would rate Medium/High/High, and comms' Medium/High/High for 273 did not apply the drop. frontier-p-vs-np.title: P vs NP resolved
frontier-p-vs-np.description: Resolution of P vs NP, or of the barrier problems around it (superpolynomial lower bounds for general Boolean circuits).
frontier-p-vs-np.status_oct2026: Open. The relativization, natural-proofs and algebrization barriers explain why known techniques fail (general). No catalog family.
frontier-p-vs-np.why: Harder than anything that fell. The barriers mean a proof needs genuinely new techniques, not more effort (judgment: many doublings beyond Oct 2026, possibly not bridgeable by scaling). Downstream it is nil either way: P != NP is already assumed by all cryptography and planning, and a practical P = NP algorithm is considered extremely unlikely.
frontier-p-vs-np.strongest_case_small: Even a proof of P != NP changes no engineering practice. It is included to show the ceiling of the exponential premise.
frontier-p-vs-np.signpost: Superpolynomial lower bounds for general Boolean circuits, or a method that provably evades the natural-proofs barrier.
frontier-p-vs-np.note_2035: Beyond 2035 in every scenario, so Speculative by 2035. The known barriers may not yield to scaling. Robots add nothing.

frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.title: AI cracks post-quantum or space-link crypto (watch item)
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.description: Watch item, not a forecast: an AI-produced, independently verified cryptanalytic result that materially lowers the security of a standardized primitive used on satellite command and data links, above all ML-KEM/ML-DSA or the Module-LWE problems beneath them (for example dropping a standardized parameter set below its NIST security category, or a subexponential module-lattice algorithm), but also elliptic-curve schemes or AES modes, forcing parameter or algorithm changes and in-orbit re-keying on long-lived spacecraft.
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.status_oct2026: NIST standardized FIPS 203/204/205 in Aug 2024 (general); a 2024 claimed quantum lattice algorithm was withdrawn after a bug was found (general). Aug 2026: an autonomous agent workflow broke eight published academic constructions at their stated parameters (Ring-LWR commitment, middle-product encryption, a lattice e-voting protocol, and others), none of them standardized (Olejnik-Naskrecki). Catalog: 279 exact quantum factoring over a fixed gate set (theory only) and 138 Subset Sum in 2^0.49n (T1) do not touch deployed cryptography. May 2026: a single-author claim of a probabilistic polynomial-time quantum attack on Module-LWE over power-of-two cyclotomics, the ML-KEM ring (arXiv 2605.17412), was rebutted by outside cryptographers (the target is key-independent; a dimensional error in the reduction) (postquantum.com analysis).
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.premise_tier: n/a (watch item on future capability); 138 and 279 are T1, conditional and not load-bearing
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.why: Module-LWE has survived about 20 years of study, but the capability is strongest at constructive, adversarial search, as the Aug 2026 breaks of academic schemes show (tl-position-5). The space angle: satellites fly cryptography in hardware for 5-15 years, so even a parameter-level weakening mid-life forces rekeying or algorithm changes that many buses cannot make. Crypto agility is the hedge regardless of the probability.
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.strongest_case_small: AI breaks so far hit lightly vetted academic schemes. Standardized parameters carry tens of bits of margin, and hybrid classical-plus-PQC deployment means a partial break is not exploitable.
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.signpost: Any AI-produced improvement to lattice-sieving or reduction asymptotics, or a concrete attack on a standardized or round-4 NIST scheme.
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.merge_note: A1: merged comms-lattice-weakness (S2 2028, S3 2027) and capability-crypto-watch (S2 2030, S3 2029); all three were the same watch item with Speculative/Low/Low bands and the same non-attack families (279, 138). frontier-hjb-guarantees.title: Optimal control with proven guarantees
frontier-hjb-guarantees.description: Existence, regularity and dimension-robust approximation theorems for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman and reachability equations with state constraints, plus certified a posteriori error bounds for neural and tensor solvers, so guidance and collision-avoidance policies come with proofs.
frontier-hjb-guarantees.status_oct2026: Viscosity-solution theory is mature (general). State-constrained and hybrid HJB regularity is partial. Grid solvers scale exponentially: 100 points per axis in 6 dimensions is 10^12 nodes. Neural and tensor solvers mostly lack guarantees, though verifiable error bounds for PINN Lyapunov/HJB solutions appeared (Liu, Mar 2026), along with policy iteration under control constraints (Kundu-Kunisch, Sep 2026). Catalog (weak links): 104 randomized quasipolynomial mean-payoff games (T3 for the Lean scope; the stochastic-game claim is T1, conditional) is the discrete analogue, though 104 is outside the space-math map; 139 log-concave sampling (T3) bears only on sampling-based solvers.
frontier-hjb-guarantees.why: GNC teams mostly need bespoke guarantees, such as a reachable-set bound for one vehicle or a stability certificate for one controller. These are expert-scarce rather than open and easier than catalog problems. With research-grade applied math public (S2: 2027) they become on-demand, and with the P1 adoption lag and a publication cycle the first guidance study using them lands about 2028; they can be checked formally once infra-mathlib-applied matures. Deterministic error bounds for a neural HJB solution require bounding the PDE residual over the whole state domain, which is itself a neural-network range or Lipschitz verification problem (frontier-nn-verification-complexity), whose exact worst-case cost grows exponentially with input dimension under ETH; expect deterministic certificates for small networks at about 6 states and statistical certificates beyond (12-13 states for 6-DOF relative motion). Downstream: astro-scp-guarantees, verif-closed-loop-guarantees, hyper-certified-edl-guidance, astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.
frontier-hjb-guarantees.strongest_case_small: Flight GNC already uses convex formulations (lossless convexification) that carry guarantees; the residual risk is model mismatch, not math. For general HJB classes the curse of dimensionality is a lower bound, so guarantees will cover structured cases only.

frontier-scalable-global-certificates.title: Proven best designs for hard optimization problems
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.description: Moment-SOS, tight convex relaxations, branch-and-bound and MIP methods that certify a trajectory, layout or design is globally optimal, or within a proven gap, at engineering scale, using sparsity, symmetry and convergence-rate theory. First applications: low-thrust, multi-body and rendezvous trajectories ('within 0.5% of the best possible' instead of 'best we found').
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.status_oct2026: Lasserre hierarchies converge, with finite convergence generically (general). Rate theory is advancing (Schlosser et al. 2025; Tran-Toh 2026; Henrion-Safey El Din, Sep 2026), and sparse tightness is characterized (Nie-Qu-Tang 2025). Scale is the limit: a degree-4 moment relaxation in n = 100 variables has a moment matrix of side C(102,2) = 5,151. Catalog: 102 UGC (T3) implies SDP-based ratios are worst-case optimal for many problems.
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 102 (T3) is ceiling context only
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.why: Certificates for specific instances are not ruled out by worst-case hardness, so frontier-approx-ceilings is context, not a prerequisite. Exploiting problem structure (sparsity, symmetry, term sparsity) is expert-scarce, technique-heavy work that compounds under S2. Scale binds: multi-gravity-assist dynamics are transcendental (Kepler/Lambert) and need polynomial surrogates with rigorous remainders; a degree-4 relaxation in 100 variables has C(104,4) = 4.6 million moment variables, so only first-order solvers apply, and their floating-point output is a certificate only after rigorous rounding (Jansson-Chaykin-Keil 2007, general; infra-verified-numerics helps). P4 default is Medium at best; S3 is raised to High because cognitive work is near-free from ~2029. Downstream: verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates, astro-trajectory-design-on-demand, comms-constellation-design-optimizer, and design-space closure for prop-ai-engine-design-loop. The value is assurance and an end to search; gains, if any, are limited to closing gaps that local multistart missed, so on mature benchmarks expect assurance, not percent-level delta-v (judgment).
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.strongest_case_small: Engineers rarely need global optimality, only feasible-and-good. Local optimizers with multistart already find near-optimal designs, so certification buys assurance, not performance.
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.signpost: A certified global optimum (proven gap under 1%) for a published multi-gravity-assist or constellation-design benchmark with 100+ decision variables.
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.merge_note: A1: merged astro-global-optimality-certificates (same methods and achievement; identical years 2030/2028/2027 and bands Medium/High/High). Kept the frontier id. Added astro's evidence: DA Taylor expansions plus moment-SOS with guaranteed convergence on low-thrust CR3BP station-keeping (Evans, Fossa, Armellin, Henrion, Zanetti, arXiv 2607.15801, Jul 2026); sparse Lasserre with GPU ADMM (STROM, arXiv 2406.05846). Scaling to many-revolution transfers remains open.

frontier-certified-pde-error.title: Guaranteed error bars for smooth-regime simulations
frontier-certified-pde-error.description: A posteriori estimators and computer-assisted methods that give guaranteed, not asymptotic, error bounds for nonlinear PDE solutions in smooth regimes: heat conduction, structures, laminar and steady flows, electrostatics. This is the bulk of spacecraft analysis outside turbulence.
frontier-certified-pde-error.status_oct2026: Guaranteed a posteriori bounds are mature for linear elliptic problems (general). Validated integrators exist for semilinear parabolic PDEs (van den Berg-Breden-Sheombarsing 2024; simplified Jan 2026), and computer-assisted PDE proofs are routine for special problems (Ayala-Lessard 2026). NASA-STD-7009B (Mar 2024) requires credibility assessment but accepts estimated numerical error. No catalog family.
frontier-certified-pde-error.why: The methods exist in pieces. Applying them per problem (deriving the estimator and the constants for a given nonlinear operator) is expert-scarce, and AI does it on demand once applied math is public. The gain is a guarantee, not compute: a three-level grid study (refinement ratio sqrt(2) to 2, 3D steady) adds only ~15-50% to a fine-grid production solve (3-10x only when production runs on the medium grid), and a guaranteed estimator itself costs roughly one extra adjoint or flux-equilibration solve (general). Residual-based bounds are solver-agnostic, so they also certify outputs of learned emulators and reduced-order models (capability-learned-emulators); the bound is cheap online only for affinely parametrized problems, as in certified reduced-basis methods (Rozza-Huynh-Patera 2008, general). The rigorous-numerics machinery built for computer-assisted blowup proofs (frontier-euler-blowup-r3) is the same stack. Credit in standards such as NASA-STD-7009 is a separate adoption step (capped at Medium; prop-cfd-auto-vv). Downstream: hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics, plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics, prop-cfd-auto-vv, materials-multiscale-certified, and frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.
frontier-certified-pde-error.strongest_case_small: Discretization error is rarely the dominant error in space analysis; model-form and input uncertainty dominate. Guaranteed bounds are often 10-100x loose, too loose to drive decisions.
frontier-certified-pde-error.signpost: Guaranteed (non-asymptotic) a posteriori bounds within 10x of the true error, published for a nonlinear thermal-structural or laminar-flow benchmark of spacecraft relevance and derived on demand by an AI system.

frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.title: Error bars for turbulent and shocked flows
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.description: Rigorous statistical error bounds for simulations of chaotic, turbulent and shock-laden flows (combustors, plumes, reentry wakes): a proven framework (for example statistical or measure-valued solutions) that states which LES/DNS statistics converge under mesh refinement, with computable bounds on averaged quantities rather than individual trajectories, so that 'grid-converged LES' has a defined meaning.
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.status_oct2026: No such theory exists. LES has no classical grid-convergence theory; practitioners use heuristics such as resolving ~80% of turbulent kinetic energy (general). Pathwise error grows exponentially in chaotic flows. Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation (363, T1, conditional) shows kinetic limits need not be unique, and universal computation in forced Navier-Stokes (376, T1, conditional) implies that some long-time behaviour is undecidable for some forcings, so any convergence statement has to be statistical and state its selection principle. Practice relies on grid studies and validation data; turbulence, transition and separation are the leading CFD gap (CFD Vision 2030, general).
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.premise_tier: n/a (rests on open problems: frontier-turbulence-rigorous, frontier-chaos-linear-response); 363 and 376 are T1, conditional, context only
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.why: This is the hardest applied node, and possibly impossible in pointwise form. What is achievable: bounds on statistics under ergodicity assumptions, with the selection principle stated explicitly and model-form error estimated from data. It chains four upstream nodes, two of them genuinely open (frontier-turbulence-rigorous and frontier-chaos-linear-response, each Medium), so S2 is Speculative and even S3 stays Low. If it lands, the credibility statement for an injector LES in prop-cfd-auto-vv could carry a numerical error bar instead of an expert's judgment, and closure credibility (prop-closure-theory, hyper-sbli-heating-closure) becomes a computed quantity. Computable bounds would also show analysts where design LES is under- or over-resolved; in propulsion, where design LES is usually cost-limited and under-resolved, that is more likely to raise compute than to cut it (judgment).
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.strongest_case_small: Even if achieved, closure (model-form) error dominates and is set by data, so the bound would be correct but large, and the theory may give only asymptotic rates with no usable constants. Engineers would still calibrate against tests.
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.signpost: A rigorous convergence-of-statistics theorem for LES of forced turbulence (on the torus or in 3D) with explicit rates, cited in an AIAA CFD workshop guideline.
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: the node rests on open problems, not on 363 and 376; bands already Speculative/Low/Low.

frontier-stiff-certified.title: Combustion chemistry simulated with certified error
frontier-stiff-certified.description: Error theory, reduced kinetic mechanisms and verified structure-preserving stiff ODE/DAE integrators for large reaction networks (combustion, ablation, plasma chemistry, batteries), with provable error bounds on ignition delay, heat release and key species that hold for non-dissipative chemistry. First engineering use: detailed LOX/CH4 and LOX/H2 chemistry inside engine LES at a fraction of today's cost (chemistry integration dominates reacting-flow cost: 48,000 core-hours for 2 ms of one 54-species spray LES, UConn 2023).
frontier-stiff-certified.status_oct2026: Classical stiff theory (A- and B-stability, B-convergence) assumes one-sided Lipschitz or dissipative structure that combustion chemistry lacks (general). Order reduction is understood for linear problems (2025). Verified ODE integration exists in Isabelle (IsaVODEs 2024; 'Numerical Methods in Isabelle', Jan 2026), not yet at reaction-network scale. Catalog: 149 claims a proof of boundedness and persistence for weakly reversible mass-action networks (T1, so conditional; the headline says permanence, and the formal statement is narrower) and would give structural boundedness for an important class of chemistry models.
frontier-stiff-certified.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 149 is T1, conditional, weak link
frontier-stiff-certified.why: Mostly expert-scarce: AI can derive mechanism-specific error bounds and produce reduced mechanisms with a proven bound on ignition delay or species error. Reducing a ~50-species mechanism to ~15 typically cuts chemistry cost several-fold in reacting CFD (general), but error-controlled reduction (DRG/DRGEP-class, general) already delivers that speedup; the AI-math increment is a proven bound on ignition delay or species error relative to the detailed mechanism (a P5 confidence gain), not extra speed. Rate-constant uncertainty (2-10x) still dominates. Downstream: propulsion combustion-kinetics solvers (the propulsion stiff-chemistry node is merged here), prop-flame-response, prop-start-transient (soft), hyper-gas-surface-chemistry, materials-battery-life-qual.
frontier-stiff-certified.strongest_case_small: Rate-constant uncertainty, often a factor of 2-10, dwarfs integration error, and CVODE-class solvers with tolerance control are already adequate. Certification addresses the smaller error.
frontier-stiff-certified.signpost: A certified reduced mechanism, with a proven bound on ignition delay, adopted in a rocket-engine CFD code.
frontier-stiff-certified.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: capability-driven; 149 is a weak, conditional link. A4: Why text no longer names the id that was merged into this node.

frontier-rare-event-certified.title: Certified rare-event probabilities
frontier-rare-event-certified.description: Methods with provable, non-asymptotic error bounds for very small failure probabilities in high-dimensional, non-Gaussian models: 1e-4 collision probabilities, 1e-6 structural failure, margins. Covers importance sampling with certified variance, large-deviation bounds and certified surrogate-based UQ.
frontier-rare-event-certified.status_oct2026: Practice uses multilevel Monte Carlo, subset simulation and importance sampling with asymptotic or sample-based guarantees (general). Conjunction assessment at scale relies on Gaussian approximations (Starlink: 207,152 collision-avoidance maneuvers in Dec 2025-May 2026, after 148,696 in Jun-Nov 2025), and space-weather drag uncertainty feeds directly into Pc (Parker et al. 2024). Catalog: 139 subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling (T3) and 140 memory-sample lower bounds for regression (T3) give ceilings. 360 Villani convexity/regular OT (T3) and 374 sharp 1/3 stability of OT maps (T1) bound transport-map filters (weak link).
frontier-rare-event-certified.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 139, 140 and 360 are T3; 374 is T1, conditional
frontier-rare-event-certified.why: Certified estimators are mostly expert-scarce, so on-demand AI unlocks them, but not fully: non-asymptotic bounds for black-box, high-dimensional, non-Gaussian simulators are partly open, since importance sampling degenerates in high dimension (Au-Beck 2003, general) and guaranteed bounds need regularity constants that FEM codes and propagators do not supply. Low-dimensional cases such as Pc are within reach. Data bind the answers, not the methods: no estimator beats the information in the data. Demonstrating 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence with zero failures takes ln(0.1)/ln(0.99) = 230 tests unless a validated physics model carries the extrapolation. Operators with hardware-rich fleets (Starlink, reusable stages) hold the data, so adoption binds for them first. Structural example (data-gated, already partly realized): NASA's Shell Buckling Knockdown Factor project used 8 subscale and 2 full-scale cylinder tests plus imperfection-based analysis to raise knockdown factors for stiffened launch-vehicle barrels, now used on the SLS core stage with mass and cost savings (NASA, no figure given). Certified imperfection statistics extend that credit to new shells only with measured imperfection data from the production line: the math supplies the certificate and the tests supply the number. (A blanket 0.65 has been used in NASA studies of composite shells and is now flagged as possibly unconservative; the thickness scaling t ~ sqrt(1/knockdown) holds only for unstiffened cylinders in axial compression.) The transport-map filter link via 374 is conditional (T1). Downstream: astro-nongaussian-uq-certified, hyper-certified-margin-uq, materials-allowables-stats-framework, prop-life-twin.
frontier-rare-event-certified.strongest_case_small: Engineering decisions use conservative margins anyway, and a certified estimator of a mis-specified model gives a precise wrong answer. Model-form error is not a mathematical object.
frontier-rare-event-certified.signpost: A conjunction-assessment provider publishes certified, non-asymptotic Pc bounds for non-Gaussian cases at catalog scale, or NASA-STD-7009 guidance cites certified rare-event estimators.
frontier-rare-event-certified.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: capability-driven (expert-scarce estimators); 374 is a conditional side link.

frontier-transport-certified.title: Radiation transport with error bounds
frontier-transport-certified.description: Deterministic and Monte Carlo radiation-transport methods (crew and electronics shielding, radiative heating during entry, neutronics for nuclear propulsion) with proven convergence and error bounds in the full 6+1-dimensional phase space, including asymptotic-preserving and low-rank solvers.
frontier-transport-certified.status_oct2026: Space-radiation codes predicted Artemis I absorbed dose blind, from Earth to Mars, accurately across ISS, Orion, BioSentinel and Mars-surface measurements (Slaba et al. 2025). Dominant remaining uncertainties are nuclear cross sections and biological response, not transport mathematics (general). Low-rank and asymptotic-preserving schemes lack general error guarantees (general). No catalog family.
frontier-transport-certified.why: The mathematical gap is partly open: rank-truncation error control for dynamical low-rank solvers and uniform-in-epsilon error estimates for asymptotic-preserving schemes lack general theory; the rest is expert-scarce and falls once applied math is on demand. The effect is lower V&V cost and certified low-rank solvers fast enough for design loops, not better dose accuracy. Pull is weak: DRACO, the nuclear-thermal flagship, was cancelled in 2025, and crew dose is already validated blind (Artemis I), so use in a design trade (the signpost, P6) is Medium at best in S2. Downstream: hyper-radiation-kinetics (radiative heating), prop-ntp-fuel-model (neutronics), materials-see-system-models (single-event effects).
frontier-transport-certified.strongest_case_small: Dose prediction is already validated to engineering accuracy; nuclear data and radiobiology dominate the error budget.
frontier-transport-certified.signpost: A certified low-rank transport solver used in a design analysis (an NTP core or crew-shielding trade).

frontier-inverse-stability.title: How much sensor data is enough
frontier-inverse-stability.description: Quantitative stability estimates, not just uniqueness, for the inverse problems behind structural health monitoring, heat-shield inspection, gravimetry and tomography: how measurement noise and sensor placement bound the damage or material properties that can be recovered.
frontier-inverse-stability.status_oct2026: Catalog: 372 global uniqueness for smooth isotropic Lame moduli from boundary data (T1); 365 metric-plus-connection recovery from one boundary patch (T1) and, in its Lean part, nonuniqueness of bounded measurable scalar conductivities from full boundary data (T3); 366 planar Mumford-Shah crack regularity (T1). Uniqueness typically comes with only logarithmic stability for Calderon-type problems, and that rate is optimal (Mandache 2001, general), which is why practice relies on regularized inversion calibrated by test.
frontier-inverse-stability.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise: bespoke stability estimates on demand); 372, 366 and 365-recovery are T1 conditional side links; 365 conductivity nonuniqueness is T3
frontier-inverse-stability.why: Uniqueness says the data suffice in principle; stability constants for a given sensor layout say how many sensors and what noise level are needed. Deriving them is bespoke, expert-scarce work AI does on demand (P1). Known theory sets the band: Calderon-type problems have only logarithmic stability (optimal, Mandache 2001); Lipschitz stability holds when damage is described by finitely many parameters (Alessandrini-Vessella 2005), but the constants grow exponentially with the number of unknowns (Rondi 2006), so sensor-count answers will often be impractically large outside coarse damage models (general). That, plus the P6 step to flight use, keeps the band at Medium in S2 and S3. Results resting on 372, 366 and the recovery half of 365 are conditional (T1). Downstream (soft): hyper-tps-inverse-nde, materials-am-digital-twin-qual, struct-shm-inverse-limits.
frontier-inverse-stability.strongest_case_small: Logarithmic stability means practical recovery depends on priors and regularization, not the theorem. NDE practice is calibrated by coupons and rarely changes sensor counts because of theory.
frontier-inverse-stability.signpost: A sensor-placement design derived from a stability estimate, used in a flight structural-health-monitoring system or a TPS inspection protocol.
frontier-inverse-stability.calibration_note: A3: Wording rule only: bands already one step down for T1 premises; why now uses the word conditional.
frontier-inverse-stability.revision_note: B-math-frontier: [skeptic] catalog_families 368 and 369 dropped (Ball-Evans is approximation, hot spots is spectral, neither is inverse stability); band now grounded in known stability theory (Mandache 2001; Alessandrini-Vessella 2005; Rondi 2006) instead of the T1 drop; S3 2027 -> 2028 (data gate). [advocate, partly accepted] premise is the capability, not the T1 families; Lipschitz stability for finitely parametrized damage added; band increase to Medium/High/High rejected: the stability constants grow exponentially with the number of unknowns, so sensor-count answers are often impractical, and the signpost is flight use (P6); the consumer edges are soft, not hard. [auditor] 365 scope corrected. Pathway P5->P6 -> P1->P6. | E-math-frontier (2026-10-07): band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium; S4 = S3. | R-math-frontier (2026-10-07): [skeptic] draft S3/S4 band_2035 High reverted to Medium (stability limits are properties of the problems; the signpost needs flight use); draft soft edge from robo-aerospace-tolerance-work dropped (the robot node is dated later in every scenario, describes assembly, and automated NDE is already counted). [advocate, rejected] replacement edge from robo-launch-refurb: also dated after this node, and the inspection chain already runs through hyper-tps-inverse-nde. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium a year after the earliest year (2029) in S2-S4; logarithmic stability keeps it below High; S1 Medium kept at 2033. Bands unchanged.
frontier-inverse-stability.note_2035: By 2035 cognition can derive stability constants for any coarse damage model in S2-S4. Optimal logarithmic stability and constants that grow exponentially with the number of unknowns are properties of the problems, and the signpost needs flight use (P6), so every scenario stays Medium. S4 equals S3.
frontier-inverse-stability.gate_note: Sensor and flight data bind; deriving stability constants per layout (cognitive) is the runner-up.

frontier-xc-certified.title: Quantum-chemistry shortcuts with certified error bars
frontier-xc-certified.description: Exchange-correlation functionals, learned or constructed, with statistically certified (conformal or Bayesian) error bars relative to a stated reference method (CCSD(T) or QMC) on defined chemical classes relevant to space (propellants, ablators, high-temperature alloys, electrolytes), within the limits set by hardness results. Proven two-sided bounds are out of reach: CCSD(T) has no rigorous error bound and fixed-node DMC gives only a variational upper bound.
frontier-xc-certified.status_oct2026: The exact functional exists, but computing it is QMA-hard on lattice models (Schuch-Verstraete 2009, general). The catalog claims tighter limits: 275 QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy (T1) and 278 failure of Kohn-Sham ensemble representability (T1); also 263 ionization asymptotics (T3; the bounded-excess-charge headline is T1). Learned functionals now beat hybrids at semi-local cost: Skala reaches 2.8 kcal/mol on GMTKN55 (Luise et al., Jun 2025) and was implemented in CP2K in Aug-Sep 2026. None carries an error certificate.
frontier-xc-certified.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise via cap-physics-theory); 275 and 278 are T1 ceilings (conditional), 263 is T3
frontier-xc-certified.why: The hardness results say no universal efficient functional exists. This is established for lattice models (Schuch-Verstraete 2009, general) and claimed, conditionally, for continuum Coulomb systems (275, T1) and ensemble Kohn-Sham (278, T1). So the path is class-restricted functionals with statistical certificates against high-accuracy wavefunction references. That needs no new physics theory: distribution-free calibration on a held-out class is routine applied statistics (general), and the reference data are generated by compute rather than experiment, cheaply for molecular propellant chemistry and expensively for solids and alloys, which is where the data gate binds. Defining the class is domain judgment (frontier-applied-posing helps). The signpost also needs adoption by a propulsion or materials group, so S2 2028 (Medium), S3 High with abundant compute. Downstream: materials-learned-functionals, hyper-gas-surface-chemistry, materials-energetics-design. Overlaps materials-dft-limits, which owns the hardness side.
frontier-xc-certified.strongest_case_small: Learned functionals already improve accuracy empirically, and materials programs validate by experiment anyway, so a certificate adds little. Reference-data cost binds, not mathematics.
frontier-xc-certified.signpost: A functional published with a statistically certified error bound (conformal or Bayesian, against a stated reference method) on a defined chemical class and adopted by a propulsion or materials group.
frontier-xc-certified.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: the node rests on cap-physics-theory; the T1 families are conditional ceilings.

frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.title: Gradient design of turbulent and chaotic systems
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.description: Design tools that compute reliable sensitivities of time-averaged quantities in unsteady turbulent or plasma flows (combustor stability margins, nozzle heat loads, thruster erosion), enabling gradient optimization over thousands of parameters instead of sampling.
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.status_oct2026: Steady adjoint design is routine in aerospace (general). For chaotic unsteady flows conventional adjoints diverge, and shadowing methods are costly and heuristic (general).
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.premise_tier: n/a (rests on an unproven theory node)
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.why: If frontier-chaos-linear-response lands (S2: 2029), turning it into a tool is method design plus validation of designed hardware against tests, which is the binding physical gate. Downstream (soft): prop-ai-engine-design-loop, prop-stability-design-tool, plasma-ep-predictive-design. The cost of shadowing-type chaotic adjoints (LSS, NILSS) scales with the number of positive Lyapunov exponents: O(1) extra runs for low-Reynolds bluff-body wakes (at least two positive exponents, so about three forward runs, for an axisymmetric bluff body at Re_D=900) but about 1,200-1,500 for channel flow at Re_tau=180, i.e. at least O(1000) simulations per gradient (Blonigan et al., arXiv 1702.06809; Ni and Wang, arXiv 1611.00880). Wall-bounded combustor and nozzle LES therefore pay O(1000) simulations per gradient unless the theory yields a reduced algorithm, so the near-term gain is confined to flows with few unstable modes. Even S3 stays Low: the tool rests on an open theorem (Medium in S3) plus hardware validation that compresses only 1.3-1.5x.
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.strongest_case_small: Surrogate and Bayesian optimization already handle tens of parameters well; most design value comes from validated physics models; and a theory result may come back negative.
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.signpost: A published gradient-based optimization of an LES combustor or Hall thruster with 1,000+ design parameters, validated by test.
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (claim + band, accepted). The 'two simulations per gradient' figure is the steady-adjoint cost; for chaotic flows LSS/NILSS cost scales with the number of positive Lyapunov exponents (verified: n+ ~1,200-1,500 for channel flow at Re_tau=180, >=2 for an axisymmetric bluff body at Re_D=900; Blonigan et al., ar5iv 1702.06809). S3 band Medium -> Low: P6 default Low, the hard prerequisite is an open theorem rated only Medium in S3, and hardware validation compresses 1.3-1.5x. Years unchanged. | E-engines-materials (2026-10-07): S1 >2031 -> >2035 (hard prerequisite frontier-chaos-linear-response S1 2033, then tool building and hardware validation). band_2035 S3 Low -> Medium. frontier-math-unbinds.title: Math expertise stops limiting space programs
frontier-math-unbinds.description: The scarce resource in space-program analysis is no longer people who can do research-grade applied math. Stability proofs, error bounds, optimality certificates and well-posedness checks are requested from AI like compute, and schedules are set by tests, data and certification instead.
frontier-math-unbinds.status_oct2026: Such work is expert-scarce today. Public models handle much routine analysis; research-grade capability is internal and unreleased.
frontier-math-unbinds.why: Under S2 the cognitive clock runs years ahead of the physical one. Engineering math needs, mostly easier than the catalog, are met by about 2028-29, and the binding constraints become tests, data and qualification (fc-position-3; tl-position-4). Scale (judgment on general shares): analysis and V&V take ~20-30% of development engineering hours; if about half of that is mathematical work AI can take over, S1 (~2x) saves ~5-8% of engineering hours and S2 (5-10x) ~8-14%, which is roughly 2-7% of program cost when engineering labor is ~30-50% of development cost (general). On schedule, the design-and-analysis line of the trunk's Amdahl table (15% of the critical path at 10x in S2) is worth ~13 of the ~38 points of S2 compression; most of the rest comes from non-math cognitive work (requirements, trades, software) and small physical gains. This is the domain's main point for readers: the exponential mostly accelerates what was never the long pole. The node does not require certification credit; replacing specialist analysis as certification evidence waits for infra-tool-qualification (S2 2030) and is capped at Medium. Leading adopters are vertically integrated operators that own or route to frontier models and need no certifying authority for their own mission assurance.
frontier-math-unbinds.strongest_case_small: Organizations change slowly. Liability and certification require human sign-off, and much 'math' work is modeling judgment and data interpretation that stays with people.
frontier-math-unbinds.signpost: A prime contractor, NASA center or vertically integrated operator reports that AI-produced, human-reviewed analysis (stability proofs, error bounds, optimality certificates) has replaced most specialist math effort in design iteration and trade studies on a flight program, under its own engineering sign-off rather than certification credit.
frontier-math-unbinds.revision_note: B-math-frontier: [skeptic alternative + advocate] Signpost rescoped to design iteration and trade studies under the program's own sign-off, so it needs no certification credit and the Medium cap does not apply; certification use of AI proofs is infra-tool-qualification (added as a soft link). Years and bands kept: S2 Medium (advocate High rejected: sweeping organizational claim over seven correlated hard prerequisites, two adoption-gated), S3 High (skeptic and auditor Medium rested on the certification cap, removed by the rescope). [skeptic+advocate] "halves" arithmetic replaced: S2 is 5-10x on cognitive work, and hours are not program cost. [auditor] lettered position citation fixed. Soft edges to trunk outcomes requested from trunk. | E-math-frontier (2026-10-07): S1 >2031 -> 2033; band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High; S4 = S3; extended by frontier-35-math-supply-chain and frontier-35-certification-unbinds. | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Seven prerequisites must all be Medium first, so S2 Medium 2030 (not the 2029 earliest year), High 2033 as cognitive work becomes cheap; S3/S4 Medium 2029, High 2030; S1 kept. Skeptic (primes and agencies lag, later) vs advocate (vertically integrated leaders need no certifier, earlier) resolved one year after the earliest year. Bands unchanged.

hyper-flight-data-pipeline.title: High-cadence instrumented reentry flights
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.description: A steady stream of instrumented hypersonic and orbital-reentry flights (Varda W-series, Talon-A, MACH-TB, Inversion Arc once flying, BOLT-class experiments) whose surface heating, pressure and in-depth TPS temperatures reach model builders beyond the vehicle operator. Defined as achieved at 12 or more instrumented hypersonic or reentry flights per year whose reconstructed data reach at least one modelling team beyond the operator (a government sponsor, national lab or university). Owner-only data, including most Starship data, do not count (see hyper-fleet-aerothermal-twin). Publicly released calibration datasets remain ~1-3 a year.
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.status_oct2026: Varda 2026 to date: W-5 (29 Jan, AFRL Prometheus, in-house C-PICA heat shield) and W-6 (launched 30 Mar on Transporter-16, recovered 18-19 May at Koonibba) were recovered; W-4 (launched Jun 2025) failed to re-enter properly and burned up on 22 May 2026. W-6 carried a Sandia nose tile embedded with TPS material samples and two NASA Ames instrumented eChar shoulder tiles. Varda's stated target of a monthly cadence by 2026 has slipped. Inversion's Arc has not yet flown (first flight planned for 2026). MACH-TB targets up to 50 tests a year (Task Area 3 awarded to Stratolaunch and Varda, Jan 2026), and Talon-A passed 10 hypersonic flights (Jul 2026). DoD describes test capacity as a national bottleneck across ~70 hypersonic programs.
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.why: Every AI-built aerothermal or material model in this tree has to be calibrated against flight data, because ground facilities cannot reproduce the combined flight environment. There are two data curves. Open and sponsor-shared calibration data grow roughly linearly (capsules, BOLT-class experiments, testbeds), set by rideshare cadence, capital and classification rather than cognition; this is the slope limiter for civil and shared-data model builders in all three scenarios. Owner and defense flight data ride the launch exponential: Starship reentries go from 3 in 2026 to 12+ a year from 2028 (physclock-flight-test-cadence; 2027 is about a coin flip) and to tens a year once physclock-heavy-cadence-100 is reached, MACH-TB targets up to 50 tests a year, and Talon-A is reusable. For the vehicle owner, and for AI working inside classified enclaves (capability-controlled-data-access), the data clock is much faster for its own vehicle; that channel is carried by hyper-fleet-aerothermal-twin, not by this node.
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.strongest_case_small: Much of the best data is classified (defense hypersonics) or proprietary (SpaceX) and never reaches civil model builders. Cadence claims for commercial capsules have slipped before (Varda: monthly targeted for 2026, three 2026 attempts with one loss). MACH-TB and Talon-A flights are suborbital or hypersonic-cruise, not orbital reentry.
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.signpost: Varda, Inversion or AFRL publish reconstructed flight heating data; MACH-TB passes 20 flights in FY2027.
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+auditor] Definition narrowed to data shared beyond the operator (owner-only Starship data no longer count; the node's own nil_effects say classified data will not reach civil builders). [skeptic+auditor] Status corrected: Varda's monthly target slipped; W-4 burned up 22 May 2026 (Wikipedia); W-6 carried Sandia material samples plus two Ames instrumented eChar tiles (Varda/KXAN release). [advocate] Why rewritten as two data curves; the owner-data curve is now a separate node (hyper-fleet-aerothermal-twin). [auditor] Pathway given a non-P-code 'n/a' label. Downstream hard edges whose real data source is owner data (tile damage, SRP, Mars landing) or ground/DNS data (SBLI, blackout) or capital (aerocapture) were made soft. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): Starship cadence in why re-based on B-trunk (12+ a year from 2028). hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.title: Boltzmann foundations checked and scoped
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.description: Outside experts check and scope family 363 (Boltzmann solutions that conserve mass, momentum and energy exactly yet are non-unique) and family 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian hard-sphere gases, including fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan). The scoping should state whether the non-unique solutions satisfy the entropy inequality and whether they can occur at flight conditions.
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.status_oct2026: Both families are manuscript-only (T1): no Lean proof in the repo and no outside review as of 2026-10-07. The analyst knowledge base rates the implications for rarefied modeling as Low.
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.why: If 363 holds, the kinetic equation alone does not fix the physical solution in some regime, so DSMC and deterministic Boltzmann solvers need an explicit selection principle there (entropy, molecular chaos). If 364 holds, the particle-noise statistics of DSMC have a rigorous basis rather than being numerical artifacts. Both change confidence in the models, not the heating numbers. Band: P3 defaults to High, down one in every scenario because the implications are conditional on T1 premises (363, 364); as for the sibling confirmation nodes, the band is the chance that the results are checked and confirmed by 2031. The chance that a check either way (endorsement or refutation) is published by 2031 is higher (judgment: High in S2 and S3), and a refutation would also give hyper-kinetic-solver-certification the scoping it needs. Timing: before applied Lean libraries arrive (S2 and S3 2028) the realistic check is a few dozen kinetic-theory specialists reading long manuscripts, and absorption of deep results takes 1-3 years (tr-position-5). Hence S2 and S3 2028 (S3 equals S2 through 2027), S1 2029.
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.strongest_case_small: Nonuniqueness constructions are usually low-regularity solutions that violate the H-theorem or need contrived data. DSMC has matched flight and tunnel data for decades, and no reentry heating number will change.
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.signpost: Kinetic-theory specialists publicly endorse or refute 363 within 12 months, especially on whether the counterexamples are entropy-admissible.
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.calibration_note: A3: T1 premise rule: the drop for 363 and 364 (T1) was applied only in S1; cheap verification speeds checking but does not make an unverified result true, so the drop applies in every scenario. Medium/High/High -> Medium/Medium/Medium; why reworded to say conditional.
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.revision_note: B-math-frontier: [skeptic] S1 2028 -> 2029, S2 2027 -> 2028: 363/364 are manuscript-only, PDE formalization is 3/16, the realistic check before applied Lean libraries is a few dozen specialists, absorption takes 1-3 years (tr-position-5); S3 kept at 2027 (Lean route, infra-mathlib-applied S3 2027). Gate kept as formalization. [advocate, rejected] S2/S3 band High: the band keeps the sibling semantics (results checked and confirmed), which carries the T1 drop; the higher chance of a check either way is now stated in why. Hard edge into hyper-kinetic-solver-certification (entry branch) recommended soft; left for that branch. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): S3 2027 -> 2028: the stated basis (infra-mathlib-applied S3 2027) no longer holds after B-trunk moved that anchor to S3 2028; S3 equals S2 through 2027. soft edge from infra-mathlib-applied added to match the why, which ties the year to that anchor. | E-math-frontier (2026-10-07): band_2035 = band_2031 (T1 rule); S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): A published check of 363/364 waits on applied Lean libraries (2028), so Medium 2029 (S1 2030); T1 cap keeps it below High. hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.title: On-demand airflow stability analysis for any vehicle
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.description: AI agents set up and run linear and nonlinear stability analyses (PSE, plane-marching PSE, resolvent/input-output, BiGlobal) on full 3D vehicle geometries with thermochemistry. They return N-factor maps and sensitivities to roughness and wall temperature in days rather than expert-months.
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.status_oct2026: The methods exist but only a few groups can apply them. BOLT-1B was analyzed by specialist teams using stochastically forced DNS and plane-marching PSE. The AIAA collection on transition prediction for complex geometry appeared in Mar 2026. LLM agents already automate routine CFD: OpenFOAMGPT 2.0 reports more than 450 end-to-end runs, but none for hypersonic stability.
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.why: Today a 3D stability analysis of a new vehicle takes a specialist team weeks to months (general), so most design iterations fall back on correlations (Re_theta/M_e). Once the expert labor is near-free (S2 from ~2027-28), each design iteration can carry a physics-based transition estimate, which is 10-50x more stability analyses for the same budget (judgment). P1 defaults to High. S1 is Medium because applied-math capability arrives later and diffuses slowly.
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.strongest_case_small: Stability theory gives N-factors, not a transition location. The critical N-factor and receptivity still have to be calibrated against flight, so the bottleneck moves to data rather than disappearing. Defense users may not run ITAR-controlled geometry through external AI services.
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.signpost: A published 3D hypersonic stability analysis set up end-to-end by an AI agent and validated against BOLT-1B or HIFiRE-5 data.
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic] S2/S3 2027 -> 2028: the signpost (a published, validated, AI-set-up 3D PSE/BiGlobal analysis) needs a high-fidelity base flow, HPC runs and publication (~1 year) after public applied-math access in 2027; S3 equals S2 before 2028. Soft edge from capability-controlled-data-access added (ITAR geometry). Bands unchanged. | E-entry (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 in year and both bands. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Cognitive: Medium at the earliest year and High a year later in S2-S4 (base flow, HPC and publication). S1 High 2034 (cap-applied-math). Bands unchanged.

hyper-optimal-test-design.title: Information-optimal ground and flight test design
hyper-optimal-test-design.description: Bayesian optimal experimental design and sequential model calibration choose arc-jet conditions, shock-tube shots and flight sensor placements. Each test is aimed at the uncertainties that drive TPS thickness: material conductivity, radiative excitation rates and the transition N-factor.
hyper-optimal-test-design.status_oct2026: The methods are known but rarely applied at program scale. The Ames Arc Jet Complex is the agency's sole ground test facility for reentry TPS, and its throughput is limited: in 2026 the 30 kW mARC II needed a cooling-sleeve fix just to extend run times. The Artemis I char-loss investigation took 121 tests across 8 campaigns. New U.S. arc-jet capacity is being built independently of AI: Kratos Project Helios (20-25 MW arc jet plus a 200 kW fiber laser, $68.3M, awarded 23 Oct 2025 under the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program), plus defense arc-heating capacity at AEDC (advocate source, not re-verified).
hyper-optimal-test-design.why: When facility hours are the binding constraint, the lever is information gained per run. Well-designed sequential calibration campaigns can cut the runs needed for parameter estimation by 2-5x (judgment); where envelope-coverage qualification matrices fix the test list, the gain is ~20-30%. Applied to the arc-jet and EAST queues, this multiplies the scarcest physical gate in the domain, which defense money is expanding only by a few facilities by ~2028-30. It accelerates the tier-3 physics nodes and the margin chain but is not required by any of them: SRL's probabilistic margins (2026) and the Artemis I root cause (121 conventional tests) were found without it. Domain instance of physclock-optimal-test-campaigns.
hyper-optimal-test-design.strongest_case_small: Qualification requirements (envelope coverage) often fix test matrices, not information value, and facility availability sets the schedule. The real gain may be 20-30%, not 2-5x.

hyper-certified-margin-uq.title: Heat-shield margins from on-demand uncertainty analysis
hyper-certified-margin-uq.description: Deterministic aerothermal factors and a separate material branch, combined by the traditional three-branch root-sum-square method, are replaced by a joint probabilistic budget that carries material, aerothermal and recession uncertainty across the full aeroshell to a reliability statement on bondline temperature, set up on demand by AI agents. The open part, bounding model-form error for ground-to-flight extrapolation, is split out as hyper-model-form-error-bounds.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.status_oct2026: NASA's SRL TPS design (IPPW 2026) uses Mars 2020-derived aerothermal factors (convective 1.22 forebody / 2.0 aftbody, radiative 1.5 / 1.47, pressure 1.05 / 1.25, shear 1.25 / 1.5), a FIAT Monte Carlo bondline margin and +20% recession, combined by the three-branch RSS method; material properties dominate the thickness (conductivity 2-sigma ~32%). A preliminary alternative-margining Monte Carlo at one stressing forebody location (8,000 FIAT cases; aerothermal factors sampled uniformly between 1 and the existing margins, i.e. assuming those factors bound the truth) found ~75% of baseline thickness keeps the bondline below its limit in ~99% of cases, against 0 of 8,000 exceedances at full thickness (1 at 80%, 160 at 70%); full-aeroshell analysis is listed as future work. SRL itself ended when Mars Sample Return received no FY2026 funding (appropriations passed Jan 2026).
hyper-certified-margin-uq.why: Adding deterministic factors compounds conservatism where the worst cases do not coincide. NASA's preliminary, forebody-only SRL Monte Carlo suggests the traditional thickness may be ~25% conservative at one location, but that thinning is bought by accepting ~1% per-location exceedance under an aerothermal error model capped at the existing factors, which excludes the up-to-2x VUV under-prediction found for the same 8 km/s entry. Joint UQ of this kind is solved in principle but expert-scarce, the classic case where on-demand AI applied math pays first (P1, then P5). This remains the shortest path from AI mathematics to mass on a flown vehicle, with the model-form piece (hyper-model-form-error-bounds) deciding how far the thinning can be trusted.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.strongest_case_small: The mathematics was never the barrier; risk posture is. Probabilistic TPS methods have existed for about 20 years (general), and Artemis I's char loss pushes NASA toward more margin, not less.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.signpost: A published full-aeroshell joint probabilistic TPS margin analysis (material, aerothermal and recession uncertainty propagated together to a bondline reliability statement), set up largely by AI agents, from NASA, ESA, a university or a capsule maker.

hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.title: Certified error bounds for hypersonic flow codes
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.description: Proven a-posteriori error bounds and formally verified kernels (positivity-preserving shock capturing, stiff finite-rate chemistry integrators, radiation-transport quadrature). Kernel-level properties (positivity, conservation, stiff-integrator stability) are proven and kept separate from physics-model error; whole-solution heat-flux error bars remain out of reach.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.status_oct2026: The release does not touch this: stiff numerics and radiation transport are absent, and only 3 of 16 PDE families are formalized. Practitioners study grid convergence informally, and it enters radiative-heating uncertainty budgets as a 'structural' term.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.why: Separating numerical error from model error stops grid effects from being double-counted inside physics margins. In S2, Mathlib coverage of PDE and numerics plus a verified-numerics toolchain (both ~2028 in S2) make kernel-level proofs routine, and P2 adoption in production codes typically follows 2-4 years later. Proofs about the full solution remain out of reach. Numerical error is not the dominant TPS uncertainty, so production adoption (the signpost) lacks demand pull by 2031 in S2.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.strongest_case_small: Numerical error is rarely the dominant uncertainty; transition, radiation and material properties are. Multi-D compressible Euler weak solutions are known to be non-unique, so global certified bounds need assumptions engineers cannot check.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.signpost: A Lean- or Coq-verified flux or chemistry integrator adopted in a NASA, DLR or commercial production aerothermal code.

hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.title: Certified simulation of thin upper-atmosphere flow
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.description: Hybrids of DSMC, Fokker-Planck and discrete-velocity methods, with proven consistency with the Boltzmann equation and quantified statistical error, used for high-altitude aerocapture passes, early-entry heating and plume backflow.
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.status_oct2026: DSMC (SPARTA and other codes) is standard practice, and a Fokker-Planck module in SPARTA matches DSMC at lower cost. No production solver carries certified error bounds. DSMC convergence to the Boltzmann equation is already proven (Wagner 1992, general); the dominant error is collision-model input. Families 363 and 364 are manuscript-only (T1).
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.premise_tier: n/a (capability-driven; 363/364 at T1 are supporting only)
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.why: Transitional-regime heating (Knudsen number ~0.01-1) matters for upper-atmosphere entry, early-entry heating and plume backflow; aerocapture peak heating occurs in the continuum. Today it is DSMC with expert-tuned collision models. Certified solver-to-Boltzmann error bounds raise confidence (P5) without changing predicted heat fluxes. The band rests on the capability channel; the T1 catalog results (363/364) are supportive only and conditional.
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.strongest_case_small: Rarefied contributions to total heat load are small for most capsules, because peak heating occurs in the continuum (general). Certified bounds also do nothing about collision cross-section uncertainty.
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.signpost: A kinetic code release with published, proven error estimates, or AI-derived collision models validated against shock-tube data.

hyper-tps-inverse-nde.title: Math for finding hidden heat-shield damage
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.description: Uniqueness and stability theory, plus algorithms, for recovering hidden TPS defects (bondline disbonds, subsurface cracks, density variation) from surface thermography, ultrasound and strain data. This includes which defects a given sensing mode provably cannot see.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.status_oct2026: Family 372 (global uniqueness for smooth isotropic elasticity from boundary data) is T1. Family 365: only its manuscript 'Nonuniqueness for bounded measurable scalar conductivities in three dimensions' has a formalized main result in lean/formalization.yaml (T3, unaudited); the headline joint metric-and-connection recovery result is manuscript-only (T1, conditional). Family 366 (planar Mumford-Shah crack regularity) is T1. Practice relies on visual, tap and thermographic inspection with empirical thresholds. Starship's heat shield has about 18,000 tiles; Musk has described the job as inspecting tens of thousands of tiles.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 365 formal part T3, headline T1; 372 and 366 T1; all conditional and supportive only
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.why: Rapid reuse benefits from inspect-by-exception: cheap sensors that show which tiles need attention. Uniqueness and stability results say when boundary data determine interior properties. Nonuniqueness for anisotropic conductivity and only logarithmic stability for boundary-data inversion are classical (Kohn-Vogelius 1984; Mandache 2001; general), Lipschitz scalar conductivities are already known to be uniquely determined (general), transient thermography is a different data type, and multi-modal inspection is already standard. So 365's formalized rough-coefficient nonuniqueness is at most a conditional P5 caution, not a new design rule. The main lever is P1: AI makes bespoke inversion and probability-of-detection modelling for a specific tile stack cheap. The band is Medium because the signpost needs a published POD scheme, which needs seeded-defect specimen campaigns (MIL-HDBK-1823A practice, general), and the largest operator does not publish.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.strongest_case_small: These theorems concern smooth, isotropic media, while tiles are porous, anisotropic and full of sharp interfaces. Industrial NDE runs on empirical probability-of-detection curves, and SpaceX will use cameras plus machine learning regardless.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.signpost: A reusable-vehicle operator or NASA publishes a model-based TPS inspection scheme with probability-of-detection derived from inverse theory.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.calibration_note: A3: Cross-domain parity and band logic. Its why says the capability channel drives the band, and the comparable struct-shm-inverse-limits (inverse-problem detection limits for structural inspection, same years, same data gate) is Medium/High/High. At Low/Medium/Medium it also sat below its own hard dependents hyper-tile-damage-accumulation (Medium/High/High) and hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield (S1 Medium). Bands Low/Medium/Medium -> Medium/High/High; premise relabelled n/a because the T1 families are supportive, not load-bearing.

hyper-transition-prediction-theory.title: Predicting when hypersonic airflow turns turbulent
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.description: A validated model that predicts transition onset on 3D vehicles from the freestream disturbance environment, surface roughness and ablation blowing, to within ~+/-20% in transition Reynolds number, without per-vehicle tuning.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.status_oct2026: Genuinely open. A coordinated international effort was published as an AIAA virtual collection in Mar 2026. BOLT-1B showed that flight transition differs from conventional-tunnel transition (Jan 2026), and its forebody took ~14 months and 100+ staff to build.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.why: Turbulent heating is roughly 3-5x laminar (general), so without trusted transition prediction, slender and lifting vehicles carry TPS sized for turbulent flow over much of their acreage. Predictive transition could save tens of percent of acreage TPS mass on such vehicles (judgment). Under S2, AI can produce the theory by 2029-30. Validation needs flight transition datasets: open ones remain a handful (BOLT, HIFiRE), while defense datasets grow toward dozens a year (MACH-TB up to 50 tests a year, reusable Talon-A) inside classified enclaves that S2 models can reach (capability-controlled-data-access, S2 2028) but whose results may not be published. The flight disturbance environment is poorly characterized, and a blind test needs a new instrumented article (BOLT-1B's forebody took ~14 months). The physical clock keeps S2 at Low.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.strongest_case_small: Blunt capsules and Starship's belly transition early anyway, and designs already assume turbulent heating. The payoff falls mainly on hypersonic gliders and weapons, not most space vehicles.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.signpost: A blind prediction in which an AI-assisted model lands transition onset on a new flight test within 20%.

hyper-sbli-heating-closure.title: Better heating models where shock waves hit the vehicle
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.description: AI-derived RANS and wall-model closures (non-Boussinesq, variable turbulent Prandtl number, roughness and blowing) that predict separation extent and peak heating in shock-boundary-layer interactions (flaps, control surfaces, tile steps and gaps) to within ~+/-15-20% of DNS and experiment.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.status_oct2026: Standard RANS fails on hypersonic SBLI. The 2025 review by Raje, Parish, Hickey, Cinnella and Duraisamy lists SBLI heat transfer, compressibility, turbulence-chemistry interaction and ablation roughness and blowing as open research needs. The release contains no turbulence-closure results.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.why: Flap, hinge-line and gap heating set the local TPS on Starship-class flaps and control surfaces, which today are designed with LES or DNS spot checks plus factors. Deriving closures is a theory problem that AI can attack (constraint-respecting symbolic models trained on DNS) once enough DNS data exists. DNS is compute-bound, and AI-era compute growth helps. In S2 the cognitive part lands by ~2029, and data and validation take about another year.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.strongest_case_small: Machine-learned RANS closures have repeatedly failed to generalize outside their training data (general). Wall-modeled LES on GPUs may bypass RANS closures by 2030 and make the question moot.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.signpost: A closure published with demonstrated out-of-distribution accuracy on unseen SBLI geometries in a blind comparison.

hyper-radiation-kinetics.title: Predicting glowing-gas heating on the fastest entries
hyper-radiation-kinetics.description: State-resolved excitation and dissociation kinetics (the CO 4th positive system in CO2 atmospheres; N and O VUV emission for Earth return), built from ab initio rates plus shock-tube data, that cut radiative-heating uncertainty from 30-100% to ~15-25%.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.status_oct2026: For SRL's 8 km/s Mars entry, baseline simulations under-predicted VUV by up to 2x against EAST, and three UQ methods gave 30-100% uncertainty (Hansson, 24 Sep 2026). The forebody radiative heating factor is 1.5. Mars Sample Return, including SRL, received no FY2026 funding (appropriations passed Jan 2026), removing the motivating mission; no funded crewed 12+ km/s return exists either.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.why: Radiative uncertainty sets the 1.5x factor on Mars forebody radiative heating. For large-radius Earth return at 12 km/s or more, radiation dominates and the uncertainty decides material choice (HEEET-class versus PICA). Halving the uncertainty could bring the factor toward ~1.2-1.25 and cut the radiative design heat load by ~15-20% (judgment). AI can generate rate sets and reduced kinetics for the few-electron species involved (N, O, N2, CO), but the missing physics at SRL (heavy-particle excitation) was found by measurement, EAST shot time follows mission pull, and S2 cognition does not compress the shock-tube gate.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.strongest_case_small: The gap is experimental, not theoretical. The best AI theory still needs shock-tube shots that take months to schedule, and with SRL cancelled few programs will pay for them before 2031.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.signpost: A paper at a radiation workshop (RHTGSM or IPPW) in which AI-generated rate sets match EAST VUV spectra within 20% without tuning.

hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.title: Heat-shield surface chemistry from first principles
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.description: Finite-rate oxidation, nitridation and catalytic-recombination models for carbon, SiC and silica-based (tile coating) surfaces, derived from quantum chemistry plus molecular-beam data, to replace tuned recession and catalycity parameters.
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.status_oct2026: Finite-rate models exist, for example vitreous-carbon oxidation mechanisms extended to FiberForm (the PICA precursor), but they rely on fitted mechanisms. Family 278 claims a proof that Kohn-Sham ensemble representability fails (T1, conditional); family 275 claims QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energies (T1, conditional). Both are foundational or worst-case and do not bound the approximate-functional DFT used for surface rates (general).
