hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.title: Predicting how heat-shield material burns away
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.description: Multiscale material response that goes from pore scale to volume average, with mathematically justified homogenization, calibrated permeability and pyrolysis kinetics, and criteria for spallation and char failure. It should be able to predict an Avcoat-type char loss before flight.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.status_oct2026: PATO recession predictions match plasma-tunnel data to about +/-20% (ESA conference, 2026). The Artemis I char-loss root cause (Avcoat lacking permeability, letting gas pressure build in the char) was found only after flight, through 121 tests. Artemis II splashed down on 10 Apr 2026 after a modified, non-skip entry, with reduced char loss on the same heat-shield design.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.why: Material-property uncertainty dominates TPS thickness (SRL: conductivity 2-sigma ~32%). A failure mode the models missed cost Artemis a trajectory change and an investigation of more than a year. An AI that formulates and checks thermomechanical failure criteria from micro-CT microstructure addresses the cognitive part. Validation needs arc-jet time, which in S2 is stretched by optimal test design.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.strongest_case_small: Batch-to-batch permeability in Avcoat is a manufacturing process-control problem, and better models do not make material uniform.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.signpost: A pre-test prediction of a char or spallation anomaly that arc-jet or flight data later confirms.

hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.title: Damage-accumulation model for reusable ceramic tiles
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.description: A predictive model of tile cracking, edge chipping, bond fatigue and hot-gas ingress through gaps over repeated entries, tied to inspection data, so that operators can inspect by exception and set life limits per tile zone.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.status_oct2026: Starship V3 Flight 13 (24 Jul 2026) deliberately stressed the heat shield: minimal tile loss, but cracked tiles and streaks at tile boundaries that suggest hot-gas penetration. Load-sensing tiles were flown and reflown tiles were tested. Musk said on 4 Aug 2026 that he would call the heat shield problem solved. Dan Rasky (co-inventor of PICA) called the current TPS a dead end for rapid reuse (29 Jul 2026). Flight 14 reached orbit on 28 Sep 2026 and splashed down; no ship has been caught or reflown.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.why: Shuttle-era tile programs needed extensive inspection between flights (general). Rapid reuse at Starship scale needs model-based triage that narrows inspection to flagged zones, plausibly a few percent of tiles per flight (judgment). Fatigue and fracture modeling plus Bayesian updating from load-sensing tiles is expert-scarce applied math that AI makes cheap. The data clock is the number of reflights.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.strongest_case_small: SpaceX would build this anyway with in-house ML on inspection imagery, and AI mathematics adds at most a few months. The hard problem may be material (ceramic tile fatigue under thermal cycling), and no model removes that.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.signpost: A tile-TPS operator (SpaceX, Sierra Space) states zone-level tile life limits or an inspect-by-exception policy, with per-reflight tile replacement counts.

hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.title: AI co-designs vehicle shape, entry path and heat shield
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.description: Multi-fidelity co-optimization of vehicle shape, entry trajectory and TPS layout, using AI-built surrogates (neural fields, reduced-order models) with validated or certified error bars. It cuts an entry-vehicle design cycle from months to days.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.status_oct2026: Surrogates exist in research: physics-enhanced 3D neural fields for Orion (arXiv 2603.28791, Mar 2026), and LLM CFD agents (OpenFOAMGPT 2.0, CFDAgent) that automate setup. None is used in production for certified EDL design.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.why: Entry design iterates between aerodynamics, trajectory and TPS, and each loop needs nonequilibrium CFD at 10-100 trajectory points (general). Agents plus surrogates could compress a cycle 10-30x (judgment). That opens shapes that were too costly to explore, such as lifting bodies and biconic Mars landers, and lowers the analysis-cost barrier for small companies (see the aerocapture demo). The loop can run on margin factors and transition correlations; certified margins and on-demand stability analysis improve it but do not gate it. Commercial entry-vehicle makers (SpaceX, Varda, Inversion) face no certification body for their design method, and the threshold is a design review citing AI-surrogate trade studies, not certification credit, consistent with capability-engineering-adoption (High, S2 2028). Its flown counterpart, capability-ai-native-spacecraft, is Medium in S2 (F2 audit) because it also needs a build, a launch and public evidence; this node needs only a design review.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.strongest_case_small: Design-cycle time is rarely on a program's critical path; test and fabrication are. Neural surrogates struggle with shocks and extrapolation, and high-consequence final designs will still need full CFD plus test.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.signpost: A NASA or commercial entry-vehicle design review that cites trade studies driven by AI surrogates.

hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.title: Probabilistic heat-shield sizing adopted in practice
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.description: A NASA program, an ESA mission or a commercial capsule maker formally sizes heat-shield thickness to a reliability target using joint probabilistic margins rather than stacked factors.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.status_oct2026: Shown only as a preliminary, forebody-only alternative-margining study for SRL (~75% of baseline thickness kept the bondline below its limit in ~99% of Monte Carlo cases at one location; IPPW 2026). That study sampled aerothermal error uniformly between 1 and each margin factor, so radiative error was capped at 1.5x, while the companion radiation study found VUV under-predicted by up to 2x against EAST. SRL no longer proceeds: Mars Sample Return received no FY2026 funding (Jan 2026). Varda makes its C-PICA heat shields in-house; it lost W-4 on reentry in May 2026 (cause not public).
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.why: Applying SRL-style thinning frees up to ~1-3% of entry mass for Mars-class entries (judgment; an upper bound, since bond, carrier structure and aftbody mass do not scale with ablator thickness) and less for LEO-return capsules, whose margin stack lacks the 1.5 radiative factor. On ablator-shielded NASA 20 t-class Mars lander concepts that is plausibly 0.5-1 t (judgment); it does not apply to Starship's reusable tiles. Commercial capsule makers are not bound by NASA margin policy, but adoption happens at a design review about a year after the method is available, is visible only if disclosed, and post-Artemis I and post-W-4 risk posture pushes operators to spend margin on reliability. A NASA crewed adopter would be capped at Medium.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.strongest_case_small: For small capsules TPS mass is small in absolute terms and reliability matters more. Post-Artemis I, NASA flagship and crewed programs will resist thinner margins.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.signpost: A NASA EDL margin-policy update, or Varda, Inversion or another capsule maker disclosing reliability-based TPS sizing or reduced TPS mass.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+auditor] S2/S3 High -> Medium: adoption is a cultural/policy clock (~1.0x) that S3 cognition does not compress, the nearest NASA adopter (SRL) was cancelled with MSR, and commercial adoption is mostly unobservable. hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.title: Validated models of braking with engines at supersonic speed
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.description: Predictive models of plume-shock interaction, aerodynamic forces and moments, and heating during supersonic retropropulsion (SRP) for 20-100 t Mars landers, reduced to control-oriented models with quantified uncertainty and accepted by a lander program.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.status_oct2026: NASA's EDL Architecture Study found that all its 20 t human-scale concepts need SRP. Large DES and CFD runs on leadership supercomputers are the main tool (general). Falcon 9 and Starship Earth-reentry burns are the only full-scale data; most are proprietary, though a limited NASA-SpaceX Falcon 9 reentry-burn dataset from the 2014-era data-sharing agreement is public (general; NTRS 20180006608).
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.why: Uncertainty in aero-propulsive interaction feeds GNC control margins and the propellant budget, and SRP propellant is a large share of landed mass (general). On-demand applied math turns expensive unsteady CFD campaigns into reduced-order models with uncertainty bounds. Validation needs flight data that only SpaceX holds at scale.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will validate empirically through Earth flights and accept risk on early Mars attempts. NASA's human Mars EDL has no decision driver before 2031.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.signpost: Published SRP models validated against Starship or Falcon flight data and accepted by a lander program.

hyper-certified-edl-guidance.title: Proven-correct guidance for entry and landing
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.description: Entry, aerocapture and powered-descent guidance (numerical predictor-corrector, convex powered-descent guidance) delivered with machine-checked proofs of convergence, constraint satisfaction and floating-point error bounds for the flight implementation, and accepted as verification evidence.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.status_oct2026: Convex powered-descent guidance has pen-and-paper proofs (general). Flight code is verified by test and Monte Carlo. The release shows agentic Lean at scale for mathematics, not for flight code, and no tool is qualified.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.why: Proofs of robust convergence under atmospheric-density and dispersion assumptions reduce Monte Carlo burden and perceived risk, and certification regimes already give credit for formal methods. The node is conjunctive: general credit (infra-tool-qualification, plan acceptance S2 2030, Medium) plus one specific EDL project accepting proofs within about a year, so S2 is Low (the A4 logic used for verif-hls-autonomy-certification); S3 stays Medium. No aerocapture mission is manifested before 2031: NASA's ARRIVAL Earth-orbit aerocapture demonstration was at conceptual design in June 2025, so its guidance baseline freezes before credit exists. The realistic first cases are CLPS or HLS powered descent and commercial reentry capsules. Capped at Medium in every scenario because acceptance is required.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.strongest_case_small: Guidance mishaps have historically come from requirements, sensor and integration errors, not from algorithm convergence, and a proof of the wrong specification is worthless.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.signpost: A NASA or commercial EDL flight-software release with formal proof artifacts accepted as verification evidence.

hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.title: Predicting radio blackout during reentry
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.description: Coupled tools for nonequilibrium flowfield, electron density and full-wave electromagnetics that predict and minimize RF blackout through antenna placement, aft-side relay to constellations, and magnetic or electrostatic windows.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.status_oct2026: Starship relays through Starlink during reentry. Magnetic-window theory is at the screening-model stage (Lieu, arXiv 2608.10018, Aug 2026). The reentry sheath is collisional and weakly ionized, so family 362 (collisionless relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell, T3) does not bear on it.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.why: This is a coupled-physics analysis that is solved in principle but expert-scarce, so AI makes it routine for every vehicle. Better electron-density prediction also benefits from the ionization kinetics in the radiation node.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.strongest_case_small: Relaying through the wake to Starlink already largely solves the operational problem. Magnetic windows need heavy, high-field magnets, so the practical impact is small.

hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.title: Rapidly reusable orbital heat shield (ship scale)
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.description: One Starship-class orbital vehicle reflies at least 5 times, with heat-shield turnaround under ~2 weeks and tile replacement limited to a small fraction per flight.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.status_oct2026: First orbital flight on 28 Sep 2026 (Flight 14, two orbits, early deorbit, splashdown). No ship has been caught or reflown; Musk gives the Flight 15 ship-catch attempt 'at least 50 or 60 percent' odds. The tile stress test on Flight 13 showed cracking and gap streaks; Musk called the heat-shield problem solved (4 Aug 2026) while Dan Rasky called the current tile TPS a dead end for rapid reuse (29 Jul 2026).
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.why: Not an AI-math implication: an exogenous physical anchor paced by SpaceX's flight count and tile hardware, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply; the AI soft inputs described below are the whole scenario spread. Ship catch, then reflight, then 5 reflights is a hardware-iteration sequence paced by flight count. Super Heavy: first catch Oct 2024 and first caught-booster reflight ~7 months later, yet V3 boosters failed landing burns on Flights 12-13 in 2026, so booster reflight is not routine two years on. Falcon 9 took ~4 years from first landing to a booster's 5th flight (general), and each life data point costs a flight (physclock reuse-learning row, 0.8-0.9x in S2). Mach33's base case has 3.3, 4.8, 8.9 and 18 flights per stack in 2027-30; 18 implies a ~20-day average turnaround in 2030, so a ship with 5 reflights and under-2-week heat-shield turnaround is on the base path around 2030 in S2. AI damage models, fleet-trained heating models and inspection theory pull it forward by perhaps 6-12 months; they do not change the ceramic material or the flight clock. The band stays Medium in every scenario: this node is strictly harder than physclock-heavy-cadence-100 (High in S2), and the dead-end risk is real.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.strongest_case_small: SpaceX gets there through empirical hardware iteration, with or without AI mathematics. If the tile concept is a dead end for rapid reuse (Rasky), the fix is a new TPS architecture, a fabrication and qualification problem measured in years.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.signpost: First ship catch and reflight (2027?), with published turnaround time and tile replacement counts.

hyper-thinner-tps-flown.title: Flown heat shield sized with reduced, model-based margins
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.description: A flown reentry capsule or planetary probe whose TPS was sized by probabilistic, model-based margins and is at least ~10% thinner (or lighter) than the same operator's previous flown design for a comparable entry, with the reduction attributed to probabilistic sizing and flight data confirming the bondline predictions.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.status_oct2026: Commercial capsules fly every few months: Varda W-5 (Jan 2026) and W-6 (recovered May 2026) were recovered, W-4 burned up on reentry (22 May 2026). W-6 flew two NASA Ames instrumented eChar shoulder tiles and a Sandia nose tile with TPS material samples, so the instrumented flight-experiment channel exists. Varda holds an FAA Part 450 operator licence (Jun 2025, issued for W-4) that covers repeated W-series reentries without mission-by-mission approval (valid through 2028 per The Register, 2029 per Wikipedia). NASA's preliminary SRL study suggests ~25% thinning at one location under stated assumptions.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.why: This is the shortest chain in the domain from AI mathematics to flown hardware. Chain (S2): cap-applied-math (2027) -> joint margin budgets on demand (hyper-certified-margin-uq, 2028) -> a capsule maker adopts probabilistic sizing at a design review (2029) -> shield build and arc-jet check (12-18 months on the lag ladder) -> a commercial reentry with an instrumented bondline (2030). The transferable thinning for LEO capsules (~7.5-7.8 km/s, little radiative heating) is smaller than SRL's Mars figure, hence the >=10% threshold. It frees up to ~1-3% of entry mass (judgment) and turns each flight into a calibration point. P7 defaults to Speculative; the band is raised to Medium in S2 and S3 because commercial capsules iterate in months, operator licensing no longer gates each flight, and no certification body must accept margins. Through 2031 it cannot exceed its adoption prerequisite (Medium); by 2035 operator choice and disclosure hold it at Medium even where that prerequisite is High, and S3 adds no physical speed-up to the launch and adoption gates that bind here.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.strongest_case_small: Capsule makers may prefer to spend the margin on reliability and reuse rather than mass, so the change may be invisible from outside. Payload mass is rarely the binding constraint on small capsules.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.signpost: A capsule operator reports flight-measured bondline temperatures matching pre-flight probabilistic predictions on a thinned heat shield.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.calibration_note: A3: Lag ladder. S3 2028 equalled its prerequisite hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing (S3 2028). A capsule heat shield sized by the new method is a derivative payload: 12-18 months design-complete to flight (8-14 months at S3 physical speed). Chain (S3): probabilistic sizing 2028 -> shield build and arc-jet check -> commercial capsule reentry 2029. S3 2028 -> 2029; band unchanged.

hyper-aerocapture-demo.title: First aerocapture flight demonstration
hyper-aerocapture-demo.description: A vehicle uses a single atmospheric pass to capture into orbit (an Earth demonstration), validating the guidance, aerothermal and model-correlation performance that a planetary flagship would need before relying on aerocapture.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.status_oct2026: Aerocapture has never flown. On 11 Sep 2026 Inversion received a $350k firm-fixed-price NASA order to study an Arc-based Earth aerocapture demo, running to 30 Jun 2027 with NASA Ames support. Inversion's Arc, a maneuvering lifting reentry vehicle, is planned to fly first in 2026, so a candidate demo vehicle exists. Uranus studies find MSL-heritage aeroshells adequate; that a flight demo must precede flagship reliance is widely assumed (general, unverified against the cited abstract).
hyper-aerocapture-demo.why: Chain (S2): the $350k NASA/Inversion study ends 30 Jun 2027 -> a NASA flight award in FY2028 at the earliest, or Inversion self-funding (capital and appropriations, 1.0x; continuing resolutions are common) -> Arc modification and guidance, dispersion, aerothermal and rarefied analysis (AI-compressed) -> rideshare launch -> single-pass Earth aerocapture, 2030 at the earliest. AI collapses analysis cost, so a small commercial vehicle could attempt the demo for tens of millions of dollars, but analysis cost was never the barrier: funding and a ride bind, and S3 cannot speed a 2027-28 funding decision because S3 equals S2 until 2028. Without an award by 2028 the domain's own signpost keeps this Low.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.strongest_case_small: Analysis cost was never the barrier; NASA funding is, and the planetary budget is under pressure. The study is only $350k.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.signpost: NASA awards a flight contract for an aerocapture demo after the study ends in June 2027.

hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.title: Ground-validated design basis for 12-14 km/s Earth return
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.description: A validated aerothermal environment (radiative plus convective) and TPS response model (HEEET-class 3D woven material) for crewed Mars-return or other large-radius (nose radius above ~2-3 m) Earth entries at 12-14 km/s, where radiation dominates, with radiative uncertainty of 25% or less, accepted by a mission project.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.status_oct2026: HEEET is qualified for ~1,500-8,000 W/cm2 and 1-10 atm (HEEET-1004). Radiation becomes first-order above ~12 km/s for large nose radii. Small fast sample-return capsules already fly ~12-13 km/s entries on heritage PICA-class TPS (Stardust, OSIRIS-REx; general), where radiative heating is minor at small nose radius; CNSA's Tianwen-2 capsule (landing planned 29 Nov 2027) and JAXA's MMX (launch NET 19 Oct 2026, sample return 2031) are funded examples (~12 km/s class, general). No funded large-radius or crewed 12+ km/s entry is planned before 2031.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.why: Specific kinetic energy is ~72 MJ/kg at 12 km/s against ~30 MJ/kg from LEO, and for large-radius bodies radiation dominates. Radiative uncertainty sets material choice and thickness. Chain (S2): mission pull -> AI-built kinetics and ablator models (2030) -> EAST and arc-jet validation (1-2 years) -> project acceptance, 2031 at the earliest. Without a mission to pull the work, nobody spends the shock-tube and arc-jet time.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.strongest_case_small: No funded large-radius or crewed mission needs it before 2031. Ground facilities cannot replicate the combined environment, and flight tests at these speeds are extremely rare.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.signpost: NASA or ESA selects a mission with Earth entry at 12 km/s or more and a radiative heating factor below 1.3.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+auditor] 'No funded mission needs this before 2031' was false for small sample-return capsules (Tianwen-2 landing date verified on Wikipedia; its entry speed is not stated there, so given as ~12 km/s class, general); scope narrowed to large-radius or crewed entries. hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.title: Next large inflatable or folding heat shield flies
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.description: An orbital-entry flight of an inflatable (HIAD) or mechanically deployable (ADEPT) aeroshell of 10 m class or larger, the scale path toward the 16-18 m aeroshells studied for heavy Mars landers.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.status_oct2026: LOFTID (6 m) flew in Nov 2022. No funded 10 m-class follow-on was found as of Oct 2026. Commercial inflatable decelerators now fly on rideshare: ATMOS Space Cargo's Phoenix 1 inflated its heat shield before entry interface on Bandwagon-3 (Apr 2025), though it was not recovered; none is 10 m class. NASA's EDL Architecture Study considered HIAD and ADEPT for 20 t Mars payloads.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.why: Coupled fluid-structure-thermal behavior of flexible TPS (nonlinear membrane mechanics, flutter, fabric permeability) suits AI applied math well, but LOFTID flew without it. Chain: NASA STMD, ULA or a commercial firm funds a 10 m+ HIAD or ADEPT flight (no line as of Oct 2026) -> multi-year build (LOFTID took several years; general) -> secondary ride on a LEO launch -> orbital entry, 2030 at the earliest in every scenario, because the capital gate compresses 1.0x.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.strongest_case_small: Starship's rigid-body approach to heavy Mars EDL may make deployables irrelevant for cargo, and no budget line exists.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.signpost: NASA or ULA announces a LOFTID follow-on flight.

hyper-mars-heavy-landing.title: First landing of 20 t or more on Mars
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.description: A Starship-class or other vehicle lands 20 t or more intact on Mars, demonstrating heavy Mars EDL: entry at ~6-7.5 km/s, aerobraking, then retropropulsive descent.
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.status_oct2026: On 8 Feb 2026 Musk said SpaceX had shifted focus to a city on the Moon, with Mars to follow in roughly 5-7 years. The S-1 (20 May 2026) gives no Mars date. Starship reached orbit on 28 Sep 2026 and has not yet attempted propellant transfer. The late-2026 window is effectively not being used for a landing attempt (general inference).
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.why: The binding clock is the 26-month synodic window. Chain: first ship-to-ship propellant transfer (prop-ship-transfer-demo, 2027?) -> tanker campaign for trans-Mars injection -> uncrewed launch in the late-2028/early-2029 window or the Feb-Mar 2031 window -> 6-7 month cruise -> entry at ~6-7.5 km/s in CO2 plus supersonic retropropulsive landing, arriving ~Sep-Nov 2031 for the later window. SpaceX has made no 2028-window commitment and in Feb 2026 put Mars about 5-7 years out behind a Moon-first priority, so a landing by end-2031 most likely needs first-attempt success on the last window. AI mathematics improves SRP and aerothermal models, which raises the odds of a first attempt succeeding but cannot add windows; the gates (windows, propellant transfer at scale, corporate priority) compress ~1.0x in every scenario, so the band is Low in all three. Radiative heating matters more than for Earth return at this speed for a ~9 m vehicle (hyper-radiation-kinetics).
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.strongest_case_small: AI mathematics has a near-nil effect on whether or when this happens. SpaceX's strategic choice and orbital refilling decide.
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.signpost: A SpaceX commitment to the late-2028 window, or the first ship-to-ship propellant transfer (2027?).

hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.title: Point-to-point rocket cargo, repeated demonstration flights
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.description: At least 3 suborbital point-to-point flights deliver 30 t or more of cargo to remote landing sites, with the vehicle recovered, per the Space Force Point-to-Point Delivery (P2PD) concept.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.status_oct2026: AFRL awarded SpaceX a $102M, 5-year contract (2022) to demonstrate rocket cargo; the program goal is ~100 short tons anywhere within an hour, and a demonstration was targeted as early as 2026. The Johnston Atoll environmental assessment (filed Feb 2025; up to 10 reentry-vehicle landings a year) was suspended in July 2025. No demonstration as of Oct 2026.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.why: Chain: ship catch and reflight (physclock-starship-full-reuse) -> landing at a remote pad under a new environmental assessment -> range, overflight and host-nation approvals -> 3 recovered cargo flights. Three demo flights need a ship that survives entry and lands, not 5 reflights at 2-week turnaround, and suborbital P2P entries are below orbital speed. Of the remaining gates only the aerothermal design is cognitive, and it is already adequate. AI mathematics has essentially no effect on the regulatory and range gates. It also needs a ship that can land at a remote site (legs or a catch tower there) and a way to recover it; current ships are built for tower catch (general).
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.strongest_case_small: The effect is nil. The program's fate turns on DoD priorities and SpaceX's manifest.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.signpost: A new environmental assessment or range agreement for P2PD landing sites.

hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.title: Routine, cheap reentry: 50+ commercial returns a year
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.description: Commercial capsule returns (in-space manufacturing, defense hypersonic testbeds, cargo) exceed ~50 a year worldwide, and TPS is no longer a pacing or major cost item. Counts free-flying return capsules only; excludes Starship and other launch-vehicle stage returns and ISS crew and cargo vehicles.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.status_oct2026: Varda 2026 to date: W-5 (29 Jan) and W-6 (18-19 May) recovered, W-4 failed and burned up (22 May); its stated monthly-by-2026 target has slipped. Varda's FAA Part 450 operator licence (Jun 2025) removes mission-by-mission approval for W-series reentries. Inversion's Arc has not yet flown (first flight planned 2026); The Exploration Company and others are developing capsules (general). Landing sites are limited, for example Koonibba in South Australia.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.pathway: P7 (market and physical clock; AI-math effect marginal)
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.why: Going from ~3-5 commercial returns a year (2026) to 50+ is a >10x increase, and announced cadences in this tree have missed by 1.5-3x or more (physclock slip table). Chain (S2): Varda reaches monthly (2027-28) -> 3-4 more operators reach monthly cadence -> MACH-TB Task Area 3 capsule tests and in-space manufacturing demand fill manifests -> 50+ a year, 2031 at the earliest. Binding: demand for returned products, rideshare slots, landing-site licensing and operations staffing. AI mathematics contributes at the margin: cheaper qualification by analysis for each new capsule variant, thinner and partly reusable TPS (up to ~1-3% of entry mass), faster design iterations and some operations automation (S3). Licensing reform (physclock-licensing-in-weeks) and cheap launch (physclock-heavy-cadence-100) matter more than any of these.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.strongest_case_small: Demand is unproven, TPS is already a small share of cost, and launch rideshare cadence and reentry licensing bind first.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.signpost: A count of commercial reentries in 2028 above 20, with more than one operator.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic+advocate+auditor] Hard edge from hyper-thinner-tps-flown made soft (the node's own why says TPS is a marginal contributor); soft edges added from physclock-licensing-in-weeks and physclock-heavy-cadence-100. materials-dft-limits.title: Claimed limits of the workhorse quantum-chemistry method
materials-dft-limits.description: Theorems marking where Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT), and any efficient universal method for electronic energies, must fail: some ensemble densities have no Kohn-Sham representation (278), the ground-state energy of continuum Coulomb systems is QMA-hard (275), and an atom can bind only a bounded number of extra electrons (263, conditional; only its large-ionization asymptotics are formalized).
materials-dft-limits.status_oct2026: Claimed in openai/math (Oct 6, 2026). 278 and 275 are manuscript-only (T1). 263's Lean part covers only large-ionization asymptotics for the nonrelativistic two-spin Coulomb atom (I_m(Z)/m^(7/3) tends to a Thomas-Fermi constant), T3; the bounded-excess-charge (ionization conjecture) headline is manuscript-only (T1). No named outside expert endorsement or Comparator run found as of Oct 7, 2026.
materials-dft-limits.why: DFT is the workhorse for screening alloys, ceramics, semiconductors, battery electrolytes and propellant chemistry. If 278 holds, some ensemble densities have no Kohn-Sham representation even with the exact functional; whether physically relevant open-shell or defect systems fall in that class is not shown (conditional, speculative mapping). If 275 holds, no efficient classical or quantum algorithm computes ground-state energies of all molecules and solids, assuming QMA is not contained in BQP. Ceiling results act within months (P3): they tell method developers to stop seeking one universal functional and to invest in domain-specific, data-driven corrections and targeted high-level methods. Band: P3 defaults to High; one band down in every scenario because the ceilings are conditional on 278 and 275 (T1). Formalization of continuum quantum mechanics catching up by ~2028 (S2/S3) speeds checking but does not raise the chance that an unverified result is correct.
materials-dft-limits.strongest_case_small: Practitioners already treat DFT as an uncontrolled approximation, and QMA-hardness of the universal functional on lattice models has been known since 2009 (general). Worst-case hardness says nothing about the structured instances space engineers compute. No code, workflow or flown material changes because of these theorems.
materials-dft-limits.signpost: A named electronic-structure theorist endorses or refutes 278/275 (moving them to T2), or an outside Comparator run of 263, by mid-2027; 278 cited in a functional-development paper as the reason for a design choice.
materials-dft-limits.calibration_note: A3: T1 premise rule: the drop for 278 and 275 (T1) was applied only in S1; future formalization speeds checking but does not raise the chance an unverified result is correct. Medium/High/High -> Medium/Medium/Medium; why reworded to say conditional.

materials-mlip-certified-uq.title: Atomistic AI models with trustworthy error bars
materials-mlip-certified-uq.description: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) that report calibrated, property-level uncertainty (melting point, diffusion barrier, elastic constants) with documented coverage on held-out chemistries (formal coverage only under stated distribution-shift assumptions) and out-of-distribution flags, so atomistic predictions can feed design decisions without case-by-case DFT checks.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.status_oct2026: Universal MLIPs are fast but uncertified. Meta's UMA family was trained on ~500M structures; UMA-M-1.1 scores F1 = 0.929 on Matbench Discovery, and UMA-S runs 1,000 atoms at ~16 steps/s on one GPU and fits >100,000 atoms in 80 GB (arXiv 2506.23971). Ensemble and conformal uncertainty methods exist, but without guarantees for properties derived from long molecular-dynamics runs; distribution-free conformal coverage does not survive covariate shift unless the likelihood ratio is known (Tibshirani et al., arXiv 1904.06019), and otherwise degrades with the size of the shift (Barber et al., arXiv 2202.13415). No catalog family addresses this.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.why: MLIPs are roughly 10^4-10^5 times cheaper than DFT for the same atoms (general), enabling nanosecond simulations of 10^5-atom cells, the scale where creep-relevant diffusion, grain-boundary oxidation and radiation-damage cascades happen. What blocks engineering use is trust: errors in unfamiliar configurations propagate unpredictably into derived properties. Bounding that propagation (perturbation bounds for stochastic dynamics, conformal coverage under distribution shift) is bespoke applied math that S2's research-grade capability attacks directly; the binding gate then becomes high-level reference data to test coverage, which is why the node lands in 2028, a year after cap-applied-math. Coverage on novel chemistries is conditional on the stated shift assumptions by construction. Unlocks high-throughput alloy, ceramic and electrolyte screening with error bars.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.strongest_case_small: Certification is only relative to the reference method, which inherits DFT's own errors (see 278); and the properties engineers qualify (creep, fatigue, toughness) are governed by microstructure at micron-to-millimetre scales that atomistics never reaches.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.signpost: A major MLIP release (UMA, MACE or Orb successors) ships property-level uncertainty with published coverage tests on held-out chemistries by end-2027, and NASA or AFRL ICME workflows adopt it.

materials-multiscale-certified.title: Certified bridges from microstructure to part properties
materials-multiscale-certified.description: Quantitative homogenization and coarse-graining theorems with computable error bounds for nonlinear, inelastic, random microstructures (printed metals, ceramic-matrix composites), so effective properties and their scatter follow from microstructure statistics with certified error.
materials-multiscale-certified.status_oct2026: Quantitative stochastic homogenization exists for linear elliptic problems; plasticity, damage and fatigue in random microstructures remain open (general). No catalog family addresses it, and the release's PDE formalization is thin (3 of 16 PDE families have Lean).
materials-multiscale-certified.why: This is a genuinely open research problem, not an expert-scarcity problem: today engineers bridge scales with calibrated empirical models and test scatter. Under S2, AI does research-grade PDE analysis by 2027-28, making a usable certified bound for one engineering class (for example elasto-viscoplastic polycrystals with porosity) plausible by 2029. Payoff: predicted scatter of fatigue and creep properties from microstructure, the missing link that would let allowables lean on models instead of hundreds of coupons.
materials-multiscale-certified.strongest_case_small: Rigorous bounds for nonlinear problems tend to be loose; engineers already get usable answers from calibrated crystal-plasticity finite elements; and fatigue is governed by rare worst defects (extreme-value statistics), not homogenized averages.
materials-multiscale-certified.signpost: A peer-reviewed or Comparator-checked quantitative homogenization result for a nonlinear inelastic random medium with explicit constants by 2028; Mathlib gains Sobolev-space and homogenization infrastructure.
materials-multiscale-certified.note_2035: S1 reaches the needed research-grade PDE work about 2034. In S2-S4 a usable certified bound for one engineering class is likely by 2035 as cognitive work becomes cheap. S4 equals S3 because the problem is cognitive.

materials-allowables-stats-framework.title: Material strength limits from far fewer test samples
materials-allowables-stats-framework.description: Statistical methods with proven coverage (hierarchical Bayesian, ICME-informed, transfer learning across machines and lots) that yield A- and B-basis design allowables from far fewer physical tests, accepted in MMPDS Volume II, CMH-17 and NASA-STD-6030 practice.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.status_oct2026: MMPDS created Volume II for process-sensitive materials such as additively manufactured (AM) metals; Senvol's machine-learning approach was shown equivalent to the conventional approach in America Makes work; America Makes still funds conventional allowables (GOTHAAM, $5.5M, 2026 call, AM 7075-class aluminium across three machine classes). NASA is characterizing ~50 AM materials across 8,000+ samples. NASA-STD-6030 (2021) ties allowables to statistical process control of each qualified process.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.why: Directly computed MMPDS-style A/B values traditionally need about 100 observations from at least 10 heats or lots, and a nonparametric A-basis needs 299 (general). For AM, 'a new process means a new material' (NASA AMRL framework, Apr 2026), so each machine and parameter set restarts the clock. Methods that pool information across machines and lots with provable tolerance-bound coverage could cut coupons 40-60% (assumption) and, more importantly, lots and calendar time. The math is solved in principle but expert-scarce, exactly what on-demand AI supplies; handbook-committee acceptance binds, so the band is capped at Medium. 139 (subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling, Lean, T3) is theory for the posterior sampling these methods use; constants unknown, effect marginal.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.strongest_case_small: Statistics were never the hard part: regulators want physical lot-to-lot variability that only production time generates; handbook committees revise on multi-year cycles; and any coverage proof rests on assumptions (exchangeability across machines) that reviewers will dispute.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.signpost: An MMPDS or CMH-17 coordination group approves a model-informed or Bayesian allowables method, or a NASA-STD-6030 revision references model-based allowables, by 2029.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.calibration_note: A3: Cross-domain consistency: handbook acceptance (MMPDS, CMH-17, NASA-STD-6030) of AI-derived allowables methods is a standards revision, which physclock-credibility-evidence-standard puts at S2 2029 (standards revise on 3-6 year cycles). materials-autonomous-characterization.title: Reliable automated structure identification
materials-autonomous-characterization.description: Robust, uncertainty-aware solution of the characterization inverse problem (automated Rietveld refinement, disorder-aware phase identification, fusion of X-ray, neutron and electron-microscopy data) so autonomous labs' claims of new materials survive expert scrutiny.
materials-autonomous-characterization.status_oct2026: The A-Lab's 41 claimed novel compounds (from 58 targets) were disputed by Palgrave, Schoop and colleagues (ChemRxiv Jan 2024; PRX Energy 2024), who judged automated Rietveld analysis unreliable and concluded no new materials had been shown; Jakob, Margraf et al. (Adv. Mater. 2025) estimate that 80-84% of GNoME's predicted stable compounds are likely disordered in practice.
materials-autonomous-characterization.why: Autonomous-lab throughput (DeepMind's UK lab plans hundreds of materials per day) is worthless if phase identification is wrong. Structure refinement is a non-convex inverse problem with identifiability limits; AI applied math can supply identifiability analysis, Bayesian refinement with calibrated posteriors and explicit disorder models. This unlocks credible closed-loop discovery, which the space chains (PV absorbers, coatings, electrolytes) need first.
materials-autonomous-characterization.strongest_case_small: Some ambiguities are physical (powder X-ray diffraction cannot distinguish certain orderings), so resolving them needs neutron, synchrotron or electron-microscope time, a facility gate that math cannot remove.
materials-autonomous-characterization.signpost: A blind round-robin in which automated characterization matches expert refinement on at least 90% of samples, or an autonomous-lab discovery paper that passes a published expert audit, by 2027.
materials-autonomous-characterization.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (fact, contradicted): the A-Lab claimed 41 novel compounds (from 58 targets), not 43; the 80-84% disorder estimate comes from Jakob, Margraf et al. materials-learned-functionals.title: Chemical accuracy from cheap quantum chemistry
materials-learned-functionals.description: Machine-learned exchange-correlation functionals and atomistic models trained on wavefunction-level data that reach about 1 kcal/mol accuracy at semi-local DFT cost, extended from main-group molecules to transition metals, oxides and solids.
materials-learned-functionals.status_oct2026: Microsoft's Skala (preprint Jun 2025) reaches 2.8 kcal/mol on the GMTKN55 benchmark and chemical accuracy on small-molecule atomization energies at semi-local cost; transition metals and solids are not yet covered. 278 (T1, conditional) marks a class of ensemble densities that no Kohn-Sham scheme can represent.
materials-learned-functionals.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 278 is T1, conditional, bounds the scope only
materials-learned-functionals.why: Cutting energy errors from ~3-5 kcal/mol (hybrid functionals, general) to ~1 kcal/mol changes the reliability of rankings for propellant decomposition pathways, oxide-scale formation on ceramics and superalloys, defect levels in radiation-damaged semiconductors and electrolyte stability windows. Reference data bind: coupled-cluster and quantum Monte Carlo labels are compute-expensive, so S2 brings the node forward mainly through AI-derived exact constraints and active learning that cut data needs. For multireference transition-metal chemistry the coupled-cluster references are themselves rarely accurate to 1 kcal/mol (general), so the target is partly limited by its own benchmarks; that keeps the band at Medium even in S3. 278 (T1, conditional) tells developers where Kohn-Sham-based learning must fail (strong static correlation), steering effort to embedding methods there. Alloy design and main-group energetics do not need this node (soft links): alloys run on CALPHAD and kinetics, energetics on main-group chemistry Skala-class functionals already cover.
materials-learned-functionals.strongest_case_small: Most space-materials properties are limited by temperature, kinetics and microstructure, not by 1-3 kcal/mol of electronic energy; and 278/275 (T1, conditional) set worst-case limits for strongly correlated systems.
materials-learned-functionals.signpost: A learned functional with documented error of 1 kcal/mol or less on transition-metal and solid-state benchmarks, released openly, by 2028.
materials-learned-functionals.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: 278 bounds scope; the band rests on capability.

materials-quantum-chem-advantage.title: Quantum computers beat classical chemistry
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.description: A fault-tolerant quantum computation delivers a chemically accurate result for an industrially relevant molecule or material that the best classical methods (DMRG, AFQMC, coupled cluster, neural wavefunctions) cannot match.
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.status_oct2026: Quantinuum Helios (2025): 98 physical qubits, demonstrations of up to 50 logical qubits, about 10 logical spin orbitals usable for chemistry. A Quantinuum-SoftBank white paper (Jul 2026) places Apollo (2029) at ~100 logical spin orbitals, a range classical DMRG and AFQMC already reach, and chemically accurate simulation above 100 spin orbitals in its 2030s 'Lumos' generation; FeMoco needs 152. FeMoco estimates: ~2,142 logical qubits, ~4M physical qubits, ~4 days (2021), with 2025 reductions of 4-195x from algorithms and 278x specific to one architecture (PsiQuantum active volume). 275 (T1, conditional) shows continuum Coulomb ground energies are QMA-hard in the worst case, so no quantum algorithm is guaranteed efficient on all instances; it says nothing about typical molecules. 265 (T1, conditional; 2D gapped area law) strengthens classical tensor-network methods for gapped 2D systems.
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.premise_tier: n/a (hardware and algorithm race); 275 and 265 are T1, conditional context only
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.why: AI math acts on the algorithm side: resource estimates fell 4-195x algorithmically in 2025 (278x on one architecture), and S2/S3 assume a further 10-100x (assumption). Qubit fabrication binds (1.05-1.15x in S2, 1.2-1.3x in S3): the vendor roadmap places chemically accurate >100-spin-orbital simulation in Lumos (2030s), while Apollo (2029) reaches ~100 logical spin orbitals, which classical methods already handle, and vendor roadmaps historically slip. A beyond-classical industrial result by 2031 is therefore Low even in S3. For space the payoff is indirect: catalysts for propellant decomposition and in-situ resource processing, and correlated-electron materials, not alloys or PV.
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.strongest_case_small: Classical methods, now AI-accelerated, keep moving the goalposts. 275 and 265 cut both ways: there is no universal quantum advantage, and classical tensor networks provably work for gapped 2D systems. Most space-materials problems are not strongly correlated.
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.signpost: A peer-reviewed beyond-classical chemistry result with error bars on logical qubits by 2030; published FeMoco-class resource estimates below 10^5 physical qubits.
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: 275 and 265 are context, not load-bearing.

materials-am-defect-physics.title: Predictive physics of 3D-printed metal parts
materials-am-defect-physics.description: Validated process-structure-property models for laser powder-bed fusion and directed-energy deposition that predict porosity, microstructure, residual stress and fatigue scatter from process parameters and in-situ sensor signals, with quantified uncertainty.
materials-am-defect-physics.status_oct2026: Active research, not yet qualification-grade: ASME's 2026 special issue on AM qualification calls for physics-informed machine learning, digital twins and uncertainty quantification; NASA's AMRL framework (Apr 2026) stresses that a new process means a new material; Washington State University used AI to find laser settings that make NASA's GRCop-42 printable on standard commercial machines.
materials-am-defect-physics.why: Fatigue life of printed parts is set by the largest lack-of-fusion pores and surface defects, giving one to two orders of magnitude of scatter in cycles to failure (general). A model mapping melt-pool signals to a defect population and then to a life distribution turns AM qualification from 'test every lot' into 'monitor and predict'. The cognitive pieces (multiscale melt-pool models, extreme-value statistics, inverse calibration) compress under S2; the binding gate is paired data (sensor logs, CT scans, fatigue results), generated at autonomous-lab speed from ~2028.
materials-am-defect-physics.strongest_case_small: Melt-pool physics is stochastic (spatter, powder variability, machine drift), so models stay statistical and machine-specific and physical testing remains the evidence regulators accept.
materials-am-defect-physics.signpost: A blind prediction challenge (for example NIST AM-Bench) in which models predict fatigue-life distributions of unseen builds within a factor of two, by 2028.
materials-am-defect-physics.note_2035: Blind AM-Bench-style challenges recur every few years, so S3-S4 likely succeed by 2035; S2 stays Medium because melt-pool scatter is stochastic and machine-specific. S4 equals S3: autonomous labs are already in S3, and builds, CT scans and fatigue rigs are machine-bound.
materials-am-defect-physics.revision_note: E-certification (2026-10-07): 2035 horizon and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1-S4 Medium/Medium/High/High. materials-am-defect-physics.gate_note: Paired sensor, CT and fatigue data bind; builds, CT scans and fatigue rigs (experiment) are the runner-up.

materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.title: Long-life predictions from short tests
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.description: Mechanism-based models with validated uncertainty that predict 10,000-hour creep rupture, oxidation and thermomechanical fatigue of high-temperature alloys and coatings from roughly 1,000-hour tests.
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.status_oct2026: Extrapolation relies on empirical parametric methods (for example Larson-Miller) and long tests. NASA's GRX-810, built for temperatures above 2,000 F (~1,100 C), claims more than 1,000 times the creep life of conventional superalloys, a claim that itself needed long tests. No catalog family addresses this.
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.why: A 10,000-hour creep test takes about 14 months of real time; it is the physical clock on any new hot-section alloy. Models linking atomistic diffusion to dislocation climb, precipitate coarsening and oxide growth could justify qualification decisions at ~1,000 hours with confirmatory long tests running in parallel, saving roughly a year per alloy (assumption). Validation can start on held-out legacy long-term creep data (tests beyond 100,000 h exist for heritage alloys, general), but credibility for new chemistries needs a prospective blind prediction, either against long tests already under way when the model is built or against new ones, so the experiment clock, not data, binds. Bulk diffusion coefficients for most alloy systems are measured; the open problem is mesoscale bridging (climb, coarsening, oxide spallation), so certified MLIPs (materials-mlip-certified-uq) help but do not gate it.
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.strongest_case_small: New mechanisms (brittle-phase formation, oxide spallation, coarsening) appear only at long times, so practice rarely accepts extrapolation beyond about three times the test duration (general); engine primes and regulators will keep the long tests.
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.signpost: A published blind prediction of 10,000-hour rupture life from 1,000-hour or shorter data, within a factor of two, for a new alloy by 2029.
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Gate data -> experiment (skeptic, accepted: the signpost needs a blind check against a 10,000-h, ~14-month test). materials-mlip-certified-uq hard -> soft (skeptic: bulk diffusion is mostly measured; the open problem is mesoscale bridging). Soft edges from cap-autonomous-labs and physclock-ai-run-test-stands (advocate). Years kept (skeptic's S2 2030 / S3 2029 not applied): a blind prediction can be checked against long tests already under way when the model is built, so the 14-month clock overlaps model development rather than following it. Advocate's S3 High not applied: legacy hold-out data validate heritage alloys but not new chemistries, where long-time mechanisms appear; P6 default Low. | E-engines-materials (2026-10-07): band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S3 Medium -> High. Robot-tended frames add specimens in parallel, but each test still runs about 14 months, so S4 equals S3.

materials-see-system-models.title: Predicting radiation errors in commercial AI chips
materials-see-system-models.description: Hierarchical stochastic models that turn limited proton and heavy-ion beam data into mission-level rates of silent data corruption and functional interrupts for complex commercial processors, GPUs/TPUs and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) running real AI workloads.
materials-see-system-models.status_oct2026: Google tested Trillium TPUs in a 67 MeV proton beam (Nov 2025): HBM irregularities appeared only after 2 krad(Si) versus a 750 rad(Si) shielded five-year dose, with no hard failures up to 15 krad(Si). Starcloud flew an Nvidia H100 in Nov 2025. Google's first Suncatcher prototype (built with Planet; four TPUs per press reports) launched on SpaceX Transporter-18 on Oct 1 2026; first on-orbit error statistics are expected in 2027. Nvidia announced the Space-1 Vera Rubin module at GTC (Mar 2026; up to 25x H100 AI compute; 2027 availability per secondary reports only). ESA's CORHA-2 project (2024-27) is reported to add machine learning to radiation hardness assurance (unverified: the cited abstract is no longer online).
materials-see-system-models.why: With billions of transistors, device-by-device rate prediction is impossible; operators need workload-level error rates to size mitigation. Commercial orbital-compute operators already fly unmitigated COTS accelerators with ECC and checkpointing (Starcloud H100, Google Suncatcher), not triple modular redundancy, so there is no 2.5x gain to capture. Validated mission-level error rates let them right-size checkpoint intervals, memory scrubbing, spares and derating, worth roughly 5-20% of useful compute per watt (assumption), mostly for training and long jobs rather than inference, which tolerates high raw HBM error rates (arXiv 2507.02654); they also bound silent data corruption for in-orbit training and long-context inference and, beyond 2031, help open higher-radiation orbits, since the dawn-dusk sun-synchronous corridor is only ~1% of usable LEO volume (33FG, Dec 2025). This is a confidence gain (P5-like), not a performance step. The math (composition of Poisson fault processes, fault propagation through architectures, Bayesian fusion of beam and flight data) is bespoke and suited to AI. The data gate is being met by commercial flights regardless of AI math, so the S1-S2 gap reflects analysis speed, not data.
materials-see-system-models.strongest_case_small: Commercial operators may simply fly, measure and iterate, since on-orbit statistics beat models; and the dose margins Google measured suggest radiation is not binding in benign dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbits anyway.
materials-see-system-models.signpost: Published on-orbit error statistics from the Suncatcher prototype (in orbit since Oct 1 2026), Starcloud or Space-1 users, compared with pre-flight model predictions, in 2027-28.
materials-see-system-models.revision_note: B-orbital-compute-power resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + advocate + auditor: the ~2.5x compute-per-watt lever (TMR replaced by ABFT) removed; no orbital-compute operator flies accelerators in TMR, so the lever is right-sized mitigation (~5-20%, assumption) and confidence. Skeptic: S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 equals S2 through 2027; the first TPU flight only reached orbit Oct 1 2026). Auditor: CORHA-2 marked unverified; Space-1 2027 date flagged as secondary. Status and signpost updated for the Transporter-18 launch. Advocate's outgoing soft edges to physclock-satellite-gen-cadence and capability-ai-native-spacecraft left to those branches (see notes). | E-orbital-compute-power (2026-10-07): 2035/S4 extension. band_2035: S1 Medium -> High. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium from 2028 (Google beam data, Starcloud and Suncatcher already flying); High waits for a year or two of 100-kW-class fleet error statistics: 2030 in S2, 2029 in S3/S4, 2034 in S1 (with its applied-math prerequisite). Was High from 2028 in the seed.

materials-perovskite-degradation-models.title: Knowing how long perovskite cells last in orbit
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.description: Mechanistic, predictive models of perovskite and perovskite-tandem degradation (ion migration, phase segregation, proton and electron damage, ultraviolet, thermal cycling, self-healing) that map accelerated ground tests to on-orbit lifetime.
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.status_oct2026: A perovskite/silicon tandem reached a certified 27.49% AM0 efficiency on 12.56 cm2, kept 93% after 1e12 protons/cm2 (150 keV) and ~80% after 1e14 electrons/cm2 (1 MeV), and flew stably on a 29.7 km balloon (reported Aug 2026). Potsdam/HZB tandems have been in orbit since Jul 2024; RIT is testing cells on a CubeSat; Hanwha Qcells is supplying tandems for a NASA-backed lunar demo. Mechanisms are known qualitatively, not predictively.
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.why: Perovskites tolerate particle radiation well, but their failure modes are coupled ion-electron-thermal processes with unknown acceleration factors, so no one can yet say what a three-year ground test means for a seven-year mission. AI applied math (coupled drift-diffusion-reaction models, Bayesian model identification) plus autonomous-lab degradation data can make acceleration factors quantitative. On-orbit exposure data to validate the mapping bind.
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.strongest_case_small: Buyers accept flight heritage, not models, and encapsulation and interconnect failures (packaging engineering) often dominate absorber chemistry.
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.signpost: At least one year of published on-orbit current-voltage data from the Potsdam/HZB (OOV-Cube) or RIT CubeSat tandems with under 10% relative loss, plus a model that predicted it, by 2027-28.
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.revision_note: B-orbital-compute-power resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic: materials-learned-functionals hard -> soft (ion-migration and defect parameters can be fit from experiment). Auditor: cap-autonomous-labs hard -> soft (zero lag behind it was implausible; first models can use published aging and flight data); signpost no longer cites Chinese tandems in orbit (the Tianjin-led 27.49% cell flew on a balloon). S1 Medium from 2032.

materials-perovskite-degradation-models.gate_note: On-orbit exposure data to validate acceleration factors bind; the coupled ion-electron-thermal modelling itself (cognitive) is the runner-up.

materials-microgravity-process-models.title: Knowing what is worth making in orbit
materials-microgravity-process-models.description: Validated models of microgravity processing (ZBLAN fiber crystallization; vapor-phase growth of GaN, SiC, AlN and diamond; pharmaceutical crystallization) that quantify the quality gain over the best terrestrial processes and predict which products justify launch and return.
materials-microgravity-process-models.status_oct2026: Flawless Photonics drew 11.9 km of ZBLAN fiber on the ISS (Feb-Mar 2024; longest single draw 1,141 m). As of early 2026 no attenuation comparison with ground-drawn fiber has been published. Space Forge's ForgeStar-1 first generated ~1,000 C plasma on orbit on Dec 31, 2025, for wide-bandgap crystal growth. Varda re-entered capsules W-5 (Jan 2026) and W-6 (May 2026).
materials-microgravity-process-models.why: The in-space-manufacturing business case turns on a quantitative quality gain (defect density, optical attenuation) over terrestrial best practice. Models of convection suppression, nucleation and transport are applied math that AI can do on demand; validation data come from a handful of flights a year, which binds.
materials-microgravity-process-models.strongest_case_small: Terrestrial processes keep improving and may erase the microgravity advantage; launch, return and volume economics dominate over physics knowledge.
materials-microgravity-process-models.signpost: Space Forge or Flawless Photonics publishes measured defect-density or attenuation advantages for a sellable product, with a model that predicted the gain, by 2028.
materials-microgravity-process-models.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Auditor (contradicted and unverifiable facts): removed 'lower attenuation than ground-drawn fiber'. No published source supports it, the cited article said properties were still to be assessed, and it is the core quantity this node exists to predict. materials-ht-alloy-design.title: AI designs new rocket-engine alloys in weeks
materials-ht-alloy-design.description: AI agents run the full integrated computational materials engineering (ICME) loop (composition, phase stability, printability, heat treatment, predicted creep, oxidation and hydrogen resistance) for printed high-temperature alloys, with a high hit rate on first validation coupons.
materials-ht-alloy-design.status_oct2026: Human-led ICME is already fast: GRX-810's composition was set by thermodynamic modeling in weeks rather than years (NASA, 2022); a NASA burn-resistant alloy went from concept to test specimens in about three months (AMAA, Jul 2026); QuesTek's Ferrium M54 was designed in under a year. AI-driven loops are arriving: a University of Toronto self-driving lab used active learning to find six printable Ni-Co-Cr alloys in a few weeks, one beating Inconel 625 hardness at 600 C by 4.5% and another its oxidation resistance at 1,000 C by 85% (npj Advanced Manufacturing; U of T, Jul 13, 2026). DARPA's METALS program funds multi-objective alloy-and-structure design.
materials-ht-alloy-design.why: Design is already the short pole (weeks to months); AI agents push it toward days and widen the search to multi-principal-element and oxide-dispersion-strengthened chemistries tuned for printability. The loop runs on CALPHAD thermodynamics, precipitation, creep and oxidation kinetics, printability models and MLIP screening with error bars; sub-1 kcal/mol functionals and multiphysics design guarantees help but are not required (GRX-810 was found with thermodynamic modeling alone). The value is hit rate: fewer failed powder lots and builds, each a months-long physical cycle, which is why AM defect physics (printability) matters. Validation coupons, creep tests and hot-fire bind.
materials-ht-alloy-design.strongest_case_small: Design time is already a small share of the 6-20-year insertion timeline, so compressing it further saves little calendar time on its own.
materials-ht-alloy-design.signpost: An engine maker or NASA announces an AI-agent-designed alloy validated on coupons (AMRL 3) by 2029 and entering AMRL 4-5 (parameter development and property characterization) by 2030.
materials-ht-alloy-design.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Edges: materials-learned-functionals hard -> soft (all three lenses); cap-design-optimization hard -> soft and cap-applied-math added as hard (advocate; mechanism accepted: alloy ICME runs on CALPHAD, kinetics, printability models, MLIP screening and active learning, and GRX-810 and the U of T self-driving lab found alloys without 'multiphysics design with guarantees'); materials-am-defect-physics added as soft (skeptic: hit rate on powder lots and builds is printability). Advocate's S2/S3 2028 -> 2027 rejected: the hard prerequisite materials-mlip-certified-uq moved to 2028 (two lenses) and a high coupon hit rate needs coupons tested after the capability arrives. materials-uhtc-tps-design.title: AI-designed heat shields and hot structures
materials-uhtc-tps-design.description: Computational design of ultra-high-temperature ceramics, high-entropy carbides and borides, ceramic-matrix composites and ablators, with predicted oxidation, ablation and fracture behaviour for reentry and hypersonic thermal protection systems (TPS).
materials-uhtc-tps-design.status_oct2026: AI-driven, high-throughput design of ultra-high-temperature high-entropy ceramics is an active field (Engineering, 2026); ML-accelerated simulations have predicted high-entropy carbides melting above ~4,400 K (general). Varda manufactures C-PICA heat shields in-house. Family 366 (scalar planar Mumford-Shah regularity, T1) was considered and judged near-nil: phase-field fracture uses the vectorial Griffith energy, and Ambrosio-Tortorelli convergence was already known (general).
materials-uhtc-tps-design.why: TPS performance is set by surface chemistry (oxide-scale formation and volatilization above ~1,800 C), ablation kinetics and thermal-shock fracture, each a multiphysics model AI can build and optimize. The signpost needs a synthesized, densified and machined coupon plus an arc-jet slot (6-18 months; arc-jet capacity binds), and UHTC oxidation in arc jets depends strongly on microstructure and facility conditions, so 'matching pre-test predictions' is a high bar: Medium in S2. S3 is High because closed-loop labs compress materials iteration there.
materials-uhtc-tps-design.strongest_case_small: Reusable-TPS gains often come from manufacturing, attachment and inspection (tile gaps, bonding), not chemistry, and arc-jet facility time is scarce.
materials-uhtc-tps-design.signpost: A new AI-designed ultra-high-temperature ceramic or ablator tested in an arc jet with performance matching pre-test predictions, by 2029.
materials-uhtc-tps-design.revision_note: B-entry: [skeptic] S2/S3 2028 -> 2029 (same year as cap-design-optimization assumed zero lag; coupon fabrication and an arc-jet slot take 6-18 months) and S2 High -> Medium (high bar; P6 default Low); S3 High kept. materials-energetics-design.title: AI-designed green and high-energy propellants
materials-energetics-design.description: Multi-objective molecular and formulation design of propellants that jointly predicts performance (specific impulse, density), sensitivity, thermal stability, toxicity and synthesizability, closing the loop with automated small-scale synthesis.
materials-energetics-design.status_oct2026: Machine learning plus genetic algorithms screened >1,000 candidates down to 7 energetic compounds with predicted specific impulse up to 278 s for solid propellants (NWPU); transfer-learned message-passing networks predict impact sensitivity and vapour pressure from small datasets (UC Irvine seminar, Mar 2026).
materials-energetics-design.why: Propellant design is a constrained multi-objective search in which sensitivity and stability, not specific impulse, eliminate most candidates; impact sensitivity is a crystal and mesoscale property, not one limited by electronic-energy accuracy. Energetic molecules are main-group CHNO chemistry, where Skala-class functionals and composite methods with isodesmic schemes already give heats of formation to ~1-2 kcal/mol (general), so the transition-metal extension in materials-learned-functionals accelerates this node but does not gate it. Autonomous microsynthesis supplies data. Synthesis and hazard testing in the few labs licensed for energetics bind.
materials-energetics-design.strongest_case_small: Chemical propellants sit near thermochemical ceilings; realistic gains are handling, toxicity and density worth single-digit percent.
materials-energetics-design.signpost: An AI-designed energetic molecule synthesized and hazard-tested with measured sensitivity matching prediction, by 2028.
materials-energetics-design.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor (edge, two lenses): materials-learned-functionals hard -> soft; energetics are main-group CHNO chemistry already covered by Skala-class functionals and composite methods. materials-am-digital-twin-qual.title: Certify each printed part from its build data
materials-am-digital-twin-qual.description: In-situ monitoring plus a validated physics/ML digital twin certifies each printed part ('print and fly') with reduced CT and witness testing, accepted first for non-fracture-critical and then for fracture-critical spaceflight hardware.
materials-am-digital-twin-qual.status_oct2026: Described as the ideal end-state in 2026 TMS and ASME qualification work; NASA-STD-6030 requires per-machine qualification and statistical process control; no regulator credit for twin-based part certification of the most critical hardware as of Oct 2026. 372 (T1 per KB catalog, conditional: smooth isotropic Lame moduli in 3D are uniquely determined by boundary data) and 365 (headline metric and connection recovery is T1, conditional; only the 3D bounded-measurable scalar-conductivity nonuniqueness is formalized, T3) bear only peripherally on full-field nondestructive evaluation.
materials-am-digital-twin-qual.premise_tier: n/a (capability and acceptance chain); 372 T1 per KB catalog (conditional) and 365 headline T1 with formal part T3, both peripheral
materials-am-digital-twin-qual.why: Inspection, witness coupons and proof testing are a large share of the cost and schedule of the most critical printed parts (general). If the defect-physics model predicts part life from sensor data, CT can be targeted and lot testing shrinks. 372 (T1, conditional) claims elastic property maps are identifiable from boundary measurements, but only for smooth isotropic media; printed metals are textured and anisotropic and pores are discontinuities, so it does not bear on reducing CT inspection. 365's nonuniqueness concerns rough 3D scalar conductivities and does not constrain eddy-current inspection (a frequency-domain Maxwell problem) of piecewise-regular defects (general). Acceptance by NASA and customers binds; band capped at Medium.
materials-am-digital-twin-qual.strongest_case_small: For fracture-critical engine parts, programs will demand physical evidence for years, so first credit will be partial (less critical parts); uniqueness theorems (372, 365) say nothing about stability under noise, which is the practical inspection limit.
materials-am-digital-twin-qual.signpost: NASA, the FAA or a launch provider grants formal credit for in-situ-monitoring-based acceptance of a flight part, by 2030.
materials-am-digital-twin-qual.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: the why calls both families peripheral.
materials-am-digital-twin-qual.revision_note: B-certification: [skeptic+auditor] Grounding fixes: 372 worded as a conditional T1 claim limited to smooth isotropic media; 365 split into T1 headline and T3 formal part, and its eddy-current ceiling claim replaced. [auditor] signpost date 2029 -> 2030 to match the S2 year. Skeptic's forced S1 2031 -> >2031 not needed because physclock-credibility-evidence-standard keeps S1 2031. Years and bands unchanged. | E-certification (2026-10-07): 2035 horizon and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1-S4 Low/Medium/Medium/Medium. materials-verified-fault-tolerance.title: Proven radiation-fault tolerance for orbital AI
materials-verified-fault-tolerance.description: Machine-checked proofs that fault-tolerance layers (error-correcting codes, memory scrubbing, checkpointing, algorithm-based fault tolerance for matrix operations, voting logic) bound the probability of undetected errors under a stated radiation fault model.
materials-verified-fault-tolerance.status_oct2026: Fault tolerance for commercial chips in space is designed with margins and tested empirically. 127 families in the openai/math release carry agent-written Lean proofs, unaudited by outsiders (T3 at most; none T4 as of 2026-10-07), and verified floating-point and numerics toolchains are immature. No catalog family addresses fault-tolerance proofs; families 177 and 178 (bounded-degree coboundary expanders; deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs; no Lean, T1) touch code construction only via P6, a nil link inside the window.
materials-verified-fault-tolerance.why: Formal verification is the bridge to safety-critical use. Here the property is crisp and the systems are commercial, so no regulator gate binds: for example, a checksum-protected floating-point matrix multiply flags every fault whose induced error exceeds a proven round-off threshold tau, and the undetectable faults (low-order mantissa flips) are bounded in effect by tau, which is exactly where verified numerics come in. Proven bounds let operators trim mitigation overhead with stated confidence (a few percent to ~20% of useful compute per watt, assumption), worth most for in-orbit training and long jobs. Demand is weak: operators already fly unmitigated commercial accelerators and Google judged raw error rates tolerable, so adoption, not proof technology, sets the date. As a P2 node it needs time after its 2028 prerequisites (2-4 years to certified use; compressed here because no certifier is involved).
materials-verified-fault-tolerance.strongest_case_small: Proofs are only as good as the fault model: multi-bit upsets, latch-ups and memory-controller failures may fall outside it, and operators may trust empirical flight data over proofs.
materials-verified-fault-tolerance.signpost: An orbital-compute operator or Nvidia publishes a verified algorithm-based-fault-tolerance or error-correction library used in flight, by 2029.
materials-verified-fault-tolerance.revision_note: B-orbital-compute-power resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S2 2028 -> 2029 and S3 2027 -> 2028 (zero lag behind 2028 prerequisites; P2 lag); S2 High -> Medium (P2 default Medium, adoption gate, weak demand). materials-battery-life-qual.title: Battery qualification without years of cycling
materials-battery-life-qual.description: Physics-based and data-driven degradation models (solid-electrolyte-interphase growth, lithium plating, silicon-anode swelling, solid-state interfaces) that predict end-of-life capacity under low-Earth-orbit cycling from early-cycle data, with validated uncertainty.
materials-battery-life-qual.status_oct2026: ISRO flight-demonstrated 10 Ah silicon-graphite cells (190 vs 157 Wh/kg) for 21 h over 15 orbits on PSLV-C58/POEM-3 (Jan 5 2024) and expects 35-40% battery mass saving; JAXA is testing an all-solid-state battery on the ISS. Low-Earth-orbit cycling at ~15 orbits/day means ~5,500 cycles a year and ~27,000 over five years (general).
materials-battery-life-qual.why: Life testing at orbital cadence takes years, and accelerated cycling changes degradation mechanisms, so new chemistries (silicon anodes, solid state) wait for real-time data. Validated early-life prediction could cut qualification life testing from ~3-5 years to ~1-2 (assumption), letting electric-vehicle cell gains reach spacecraft sooner. Early-cycle life prediction already works without chemical-accuracy DFT or autonomous labs (Severson et al., Nature Energy 2019, general), so what binds is a customer accepting model-based prediction in place of real-time cycling. Dawn-dusk sun-synchronous compute satellites barely cycle their batteries (the battery covers basic loads through brief eclipses, 33FG), so this node matters for broadband and other LEO buses, not orbital compute.
materials-battery-life-qual.strongest_case_small: Battery progress is driven by the electric-vehicle industry, and constellations already fly screened commercial cells; the space-specific contribution of AI math is small.
materials-battery-life-qual.signpost: A space battery supplier qualifies a new cell chemistry using model-based life prediction with reduced real-time cycling, by 2029.

materials-closed-loop-discovery.title: Autonomous labs discover real new materials
materials-closed-loop-discovery.description: AI-run labs deliver independently replicated new functional materials (PV absorbers, coatings, electrolytes, catalysts, alloys) at more than ten times the human discovery rate.
materials-closed-loop-discovery.status_oct2026: Periodic Labs ($300M seed, Sep 2025; superconductors as its north star), Lila Sciences (~$450M raised; 'hundreds of thousands' of AI-driven experiments in catalysts, thin films and ultra-stable metals) and Google DeepMind's UK automated lab (announced Dec 2025, opening 2026, planning hundreds of materials per day). No independently replicated space-relevant discovery found as of Oct 2026.
materials-closed-loop-discovery.why: Robotic powder synthesis is now cheap and repeatable; with reliable characterization and trustworthy screening, discovery rates can rise roughly tenfold. The node stacks two criteria: independent replication, which needs other groups to synthesize and characterize the material (6-18 months), and a >10x rate for which no agreed baseline exists; High is defensible only for replication alone, so S2 is Medium. For space, the first beneficiaries are materials made by simple routes (PV absorbers, coatings, electrolytes), not superalloys or ceramic composites whose processing autonomous labs cannot yet do. Chain (S2): applied math public 2027 -> reliable automated characterization (2027) and atomistic models with trustworthy error bars (2028) -> autonomous labs at scale (2028) -> candidate materials synthesized 2028-29 -> independent replication 6-18 months later, so first credited discoveries 2029-30 (Medium). Band: the P7 default (Speculative) is raised because the physical step is laboratory synthesis and outside replication in funded, operating labs (Periodic Labs, Lila, DeepMind's UK lab), not a flown system. S2 Medium for the two stacked criteria above; S3 High because labs at scale and candidates arrive earlier and replication fits before 2031. S1 Low (F2 audit, down from Medium): all three hard prerequisites are Medium and land in 2029, leaving one to two years for candidates plus 6-18 months of outside replication. Bands are judgments.
materials-closed-loop-discovery.strongest_case_small: Discovery is not space's bottleneck; insertion is (more than 20 years and ~$400M for aerospace materials by Materials Genome Initiative-era estimates). More candidates only lengthen the qualification queue.
materials-closed-loop-discovery.signpost: The first independently replicated discovery from Periodic Labs, Lila or DeepMind's UK lab, with full characterization, by end-2027.
materials-closed-loop-discovery.calibration_note: A3: Lag ladder (experiment gate). S2 and S3 2028 equalled cap-autonomous-labs (2028); the node requires independently replicated discoveries, and replication adds months to a year that experiment gates compress only 1.1-1.5x. Chain (S2): labs at scale 2028 -> candidate discoveries -> outside replication 2029. S2/S3 2028 -> 2029; bands unchanged.
