plasma-kinetic-closures.title: Simpler plasma models with proven error bounds
plasma-kinetic-closures.description: Physics theory that derives fluid closures (electron heat flux, anomalous resistivity, pressure anisotropy, Landau-fluid terms) from kinetic theory with stated validity domains and error bounds, replacing ad hoc closures in thruster, magnetic-nozzle and magnetospheric fluid codes.
plasma-kinetic-closures.status_oct2026: Engineering plasma codes are fluid or hybrid with hand-tuned closures; magnetic-nozzle expansion is nearly collisionless and needs a non-trivial electron closure (Kim et al., PSST 2023). No catalog family addresses closures. Family 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian gases, with fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan; T1, conditional) is a step in the same particles-to-kinetic-to-fluid derivation program, methodological relevance only.
plasma-kinetic-closures.premise_tier: n/a (capability-driven); family 364 is T1 and used only as methodological context, so any reliance on it would be conditional
plasma-kinetic-closures.why: S2 assumes AI builds and validates physics theory and reduced models from 2028-29; closures are the canonical such task. Validation needs kinetic simulation data (plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale) and diagnostics such as incoherent Thomson scattering, which already exist at university labs. Landau-damping theorems (frontier-landau-damping-general) add confidence but are not needed: Landau-fluid closures were built from linear theory (Hammett-Perkins 1990, general). Data-driven closures with UQ count. This general theory accelerates, but does not gate, the Hall-thruster closure and magnetic-nozzle theory.
plasma-kinetic-closures.strongest_case_small: Closures in turbulent, wall-bounded plasmas may not exist in closed form (they are non-local and history-dependent); the best achievable may be data-driven closures with UQ, which do not need frontier math.
plasma-kinetic-closures.signpost: A closure derived with AI assistance is adopted in a production code (HallThruster.jl, Hall2De, BATS-R-US) and cuts the number of calibrated parameters.

plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.title: Solving the 60-year Hall-thruster electron transport puzzle
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.description: A validated model of anomalous cross-field electron transport in Hall thrusters, first-principles or data-driven (trained on whole-device kinetic simulations and non-invasive measurements), that predicts transport from the local plasma state across thrusters and operating points without per-condition calibration.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.status_oct2026: Open research problem since the 1960s. Codes calibrate an anomalous collision frequency to each operating point. A self-consistent closure using plasma density, neutral density and electron temperature captures peak electron temperature and performance on a 9 kW magnetically shielded thruster but cannot place electron temperature and ion velocity profiles correctly at the same time (Brick, Roberts, Jorns, IEPC-2025-361). NASA's Joint Advanced Propulsion Institute (JANUS) Predictive Engineering Model, with one pressure-parameterized transport model, fits SPT-140 calibration data within 7% (thrust) and 15% (discharge current), with 8%/17% when extrapolated to orbit; the authors note discharge current is not reliably predicted at higher power (Whittaker et al., AIAA 2026). Thomson scattering finds electron temperatures ~2x higher than probes.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.why: The candidate mechanisms (electron-cyclotron drift, gradient-drift and ionization instabilities, near-wall conductivity) are known. What is missing is affordable whole-device kinetic simulation plus a reduction to a closure, first-principles or data-driven. Data-driven model discovery on thruster data already exists in published form (Jorns, PSST 27:104007, 2018; Jorns, Marks, Dale, AIAA 2020-3622). A general kinetic-closure theory (plasma-kinetic-closures) helps but is not required. S2 delivers the cognitive steps by ~2029. The binding gate is a validation campaign across several thrusters with non-invasive electron diagnostics at low background pressure, which takes about a year, so 2030. Band S2 Low: P6 default, two Medium hard prerequisites (kinetic solvers, cap-physics-theory) and a strict criterion; S3 Medium.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.strongest_case_small: Sixty years of failure suggests transport is multi-mechanism, geometry-specific and coupled to the test facility; even a good closure may only reach ~5% accuracy, a modest gain over today's calibrated 7-15%. Thrust is already predicted well by calibration, and programs qualify by test regardless.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.signpost: A closure that predicts discharge current within 5% across at least three different thrusters (e.g. H9, SPT-140, AEPS) without refitting, published by end-2030.

plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.title: How plasma leaves a magnetic nozzle, settled
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.description: Accepted kinetic theory and validated simulation of how plasma detaches from a magnetic nozzle and how electrons cool during the expansion: the thrust-producing stage of VASIMR, helicon thrusters and most fusion-drive concepts.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.status_oct2026: Kinetic electron cooling governs energy balance, ion acceleration and detachment (Kim et al., PSST 2023); fully kinetic PIC studies attribute electron detachment to inertia and gyroviscous effects. Ground chambers distort far-plume detachment measurements (general).
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.why: Once kinetic solvers are cheap (S2 2028), fully kinetic simulation can settle detachment without a general closure theory, which accelerates but does not gate it (plasma-kinetic-closures, soft). The gate is validation: detachment happens far downstream, where vacuum chambers have walls and background gas, so an in-space measurement would settle it. The only named candidate (Pulsar Fusion's Sunbird in-orbit demonstration, 2027) has no committed far-field diagnostic. Band S2 Low (P6 default); S3 Medium.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.strongest_case_small: Detachment may be handled empirically well enough for current thrusters; the binding constraints for VASIMR-class and fusion drives are power supply mass and thermal rejection, not nozzle physics.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.signpost: Far-field plume measurements in orbit from a magnetic-nozzle thruster (Pulsar Fusion's Sunbird exhaust test is targeted for orbit in 2027) that match a pre-registered kinetic prediction.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Advocate: hard edge from plasma-kinetic-closures -> soft (the fully kinetic route needs only the solvers). plasma-thermo-density-uq.title: Upper-atmosphere density and drag with honest error bars
plasma-thermo-density-uq.description: Thermospheric density nowcasts and 1-3 day forecasts with calibrated uncertainty that bring public, operator-usable products from empirical-model spread (20-40% disagreement even in quiet times) to HASDM-class error (about 10-15%) and keep them calibrated through 2-6x storm enhancements, by assimilating drag observed on thousands of constellation satellites (which needs operator attitude and thrust data, since constellation satellites station-keep continuously), so LEO orbit predictions and covariances stay realistic through geomagnetic storms. Storm-time forecast skill beyond about a day stays bounded by CME arrival and magnetic-orientation forecasts.
plasma-thermo-density-uq.status_oct2026: Density is the dominant error in low-orbit prediction; storms raise it 2-5x within hours and empirical models disagree by 20-40% even in quiet times (CPAESS 2026 abstract). Gannon storm, May 2024: density up to ~6x baseline within 12 h, decay of tracked objects 38 -> 180 m/day, thousands of satellites maneuvered, Ap forecasts underpredicted by 100-300 at 1-3 day lead (Parker and Linares 2024). Feb 2022: a minor (G1-G2) storm raised drag up to 50% at the ~210 km deployment altitude (SpaceX update, Feb 2022) and 38 of 49 new Starlink satellites reentered. The Space Force's High Accuracy Satellite Drag Model (HASDM; Storz et al. 2005) already assimilates calibration-satellite drag into JB2008-based nowcasts and is described as the state of the art; its 2000-2019 archive is public as the SET HASDM database, and ML emulators of it reach <10% MAE (Licata et al., arXiv 2109.07651) and 11% with well-calibrated uncertainty (Licata and Mehta, arXiv 2201.02067). Starlink ephemerides are posted publicly via Space-Track and CelesTrak supplemental GP (general).
plasma-thermo-density-uq.why: Thousands of GNSS-tracked constellation satellites are potential drag probes. Using them requires joint estimation of density and each satellite's unknown, attitude-dependent ballistic coefficient, net of continuous thrusting, an identifiability and estimation problem that is solved in principle but expert-scarce, which S2's on-demand applied math supplies by 2028; an operational product with data access follows in 2029. The increment over HASDM is scale (thousands of probes rather than a calibration set), public access and calibrated 1-3 day forecasts, so the AI-math share is modest. The gates are data access (the attitude, ballistic-coefficient, thrust and maneuver logs that density inversion needs are proprietary, although Starlink ephemerides themselves are public) and storm-driver forecasts. Sun-to-Earth assimilation helps the 1-3 day forecast but is not needed for the nowcast, so it is a soft input.
plasma-thermo-density-uq.strongest_case_small: At storm time most error comes from the driver forecast (Kp/Ap and the CME's magnetic field), not from the density model, so nowcast gains matter less to operators than 24-72 h forecasts, which stay data-limited (see plasma-bz-forecast).
plasma-thermo-density-uq.signpost: NOAA, Space Force or the Commerce space-traffic system adopts an assimilative density product built on commercial constellation ephemerides, with published calibrated uncertainty, by 2029.
plasma-thermo-density-uq.merge_note: A1: merged astro-thermosphere-drag-uq (same achievement viewed from the conjunction side; astro >2031/2029/2028 Low/Medium/Medium, plasma 2030/2029/2028 Medium/High/High). Kept the plasma id (space-weather physics owner) and its better-sourced data-assimilation view (Gannon storm, Parker-Linares 2024; Feb 2022 Starlink loss; CPAESS 2026), so years and bands follow plasma. Astro's caution is recorded in the description (storm drivers forecast at most 1-2 days ahead; Starlink lowering shells to ~480 km raises drag sensitivity). Astro's hard prerequisites cap-physics-theory and astro-nongaussian-uq-certified were converted to soft: calibrated density estimation is an estimation problem that needs neither new physics theory nor certified Pc math. astro-leo-safety-at-scale now depends on this node.

plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.title: Deuterium-helium-3 fusion demonstrated at useful rates
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.description: Experimental demonstration of significant deuterium-helium-3 fusion power, the fuel most fusion-propulsion concepts assume because only ~5% of its energy comes out as neutrons versus ~80% for D-T (general), at the several-times-higher temperatures it requires.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.status_oct2026: Helion's Polaris reported the first private D-T fusion and 150 million deg C plasma (Feb 2026) and says it is working toward D-He3 temperatures; Helion's 50 MW Microsoft target is 2028. No D-He3 burn at meaningful power anywhere. Fuel arithmetic (18.3 MeV per reaction): a 1 GW(fusion) D-He3 engine burns ~54 kg of He-3 per year of operation, against a terrestrial supply from tritium decay of a few kilograms per year (supply figure general), while a 1 MW demonstrator running 1,000 h needs ~6 g. Helion plans to make He-3 itself via D-D fusion (TechCrunch, Feb 2026). About 0.37 GW-yr of D-D fusion breeds 50 kg directly (about 0.18 GW-yr if bred tritium is also left to decay), so at scale the fuel gate becomes D-D fusion capacity, coupled to plasma-fusion-net-gain, not natural supply.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.why: This is a physical-clock node: it needs hotter, better-confined plasma and He-3 fuel. AI theory and AI-run campaigns (plasma-ai-fusion-operations) help optimize pulsed FRC operation and interpret diagnostics, but they do not heat plasma; under S3 autonomous experimental campaigns could compress the program by a year or so. Chain (S3): Polaris D-T at ~13 keV (150 million deg C, Feb 2026) -> D-He3 needs several-times-higher ion temperature plus a He-3 supply -> Orion-class device (2028 target) -> peer-reviewed D-He3 rates in 2031 at the earliest.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.strongest_case_small: The AI-math effect here is close to nil; it is included to show where the chain to fusion propulsion is actually gated.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.signpost: Helion or another group publishes measured D-He3 fusion rates (14.7 MeV proton spectra, neutron fraction) in a peer-reviewed venue, with D-He3 fusion energy at least 1% of the energy delivered to the plasma.

plasma-ep-predictive-design.title: Design-before-build electric thrusters
plasma-ep-predictive-design.description: Engineering codes that predict a new Hall or gridded-ion thruster's thrust, efficiency, oscillations and plume within a few percent before hardware exists, and extrapolate ground tests to space with quantified uncertainty.
plasma-ep-predictive-design.status_oct2026: The JANUS Predictive Engineering Model, with one pressure-parameterized transport model, fits SPT-140 calibration data within 7% (thrust) and 15% (discharge current) and extrapolates ground data to orbit within 8%/17% for the SPT-140 flown on Psyche; discharge current is not reliably predicted when extrapolating at higher power (Whittaker et al., AIAA 2026). Higher-fidelity Hall2De must be recalibrated per operating condition. NASA states its VF-5 facility reproduces known ground-to-flight differences for AEPS (Williams et al., Space Propulsion 2026).
plasma-ep-predictive-design.why: Predictive design has two routes. (1) A validated transport closure (plasma-hall-anomalous-closure), first-principles or data-driven, inside cheap fluid or hybrid codes, or surrogates trained on many kinetic runs, which amounts to the same thing. (2) From 2033 in S3 and 2034 in S2, direct optimization on full-device kinetic runs (plasma-35-kinetic-design-loop). Before then, whole-device kinetic simulation only supplies training and validation data: at days per run on a leadership-class machine it cannot serve the hundreds of evaluations a design loop needs (arithmetic in plasma-kinetic-solvers-at-scale). Either route is enough, so both are soft edges; the years (S3 2029, S2 2030, S1 2035) come from the closure route. A new Hall thruster typically takes several build-test iterations at roughly a year each (general); a predictive code could cut iterations from ~3-4 to ~1-2 (general, judgment). Validation needs test data across designs, which binds the year. The band follows the closure: S2 Low and S3 Medium by 2031. The two routes share wall and emission physics and the need for test data, so together they do not lift the band to High by 2035.
plasma-ep-predictive-design.strongest_case_small: Industry already builds thrusters successfully by build-test-iterate, and small-satellite thrusters iterate cheaply. The value concentrates in high-power devices where testing is hard, a small part of the market.
plasma-ep-predictive-design.signpost: A thruster designed with a predictive tool meets performance within 5% on its first hot fire, documented at IEPC or AIAA by 2030.

plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.title: Thruster life proven with shorter wear tests
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.description: Erosion and wear models (low-energy sputter yields, pole-cover and cathode-keeper erosion, near-wall plasma) validated well enough that NASA or ESA credits model-based extrapolation for part of the 100% demonstrated-life (wear-test) requirement, not just the margin. Today's practice is 100% test plus 50% margin by analysis. The credit shortens multi-year wear tests.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.status_oct2026: NASA already qualifies EP thruster life by 100% test with 50% margin by analysis (Anderson 2009 standard, cited in Williams et al. 2026). AEPS (12 kW; the PPE bus is now repurposed for SR-1 Freedom): three flight thrusters delivered 2025, environmental qualification complete, contract closeout mid-to-late 2027. The QM-2 wear test runs fall 2026 to Sep 2029 to at least 100% of per-thruster throughput (1,770 kg xenon requirement, 50% margin by analysis), and the SEP project closes out in 2029. SEP tracked insufficient validation of the margin-setting erosion model as a boarded red risk. JPL near-field plume data and JANUS modeling have since reduced plasma-interaction uncertainty (Williams et al., Space Propulsion 2026). Pole erosion is now the life limiter in magnetically shielded thrusters, and erosion models have underpredicted measured rates (U. Washington thesis 2025).
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.why: A 23,000-hour wear test is 2.6 years of continuous firing. Running ~10,000 hours and extrapolating with an accepted model would save ~1.5 years and tens of millions in facility time (general). The step beyond today's practice is predicting how erosion evolves as surfaces wear, beyond the tested duration. That needs a near-wall transport model that stays valid as geometry changes (plasma-hall-anomalous-closure, hard) and a rule for crediting model evidence (physclock-credibility-evidence-standard, hard). Design-before-build (plasma-ep-predictive-design) and certification of AI-written proofs (infra-tool-qualification, which covers software proof credit, not physics wear models) help but are not required. Chain (S3): closure validated 2029 -> a wear test planned for partial credit accumulates ~10,000 h (about 16 months at a normal wear-test duty cycle), checked against long-duration data (AEPS QM-2 completes Sep 2029) -> qualification review -> 2031 at the earliest. S2 lands at the horizon, one step later. Full-device kinetic runs (plasma-35-kinetic-design-loop, soft, S3 2033) can resolve near-wall erosion later, but low-energy sputter yields and agency practice still bind. The regulator rule caps the band at Medium. After compounding it is Low in all scenarios at both checkpoints.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.strongest_case_small: Agencies are conservative and the decisive inputs are materials data (sputter yields at tens of eV), not plasma mathematics; the worst life limiters (e.g. pole erosion) were discovered in test, not predicted. AEPS lessons learned center on risk management, contract oversight and requirements, not physics. Commercial and NASA programs have long used erosion models to project life beyond a test's duration for mission studies (general), so the new step is institutional.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.signpost: NASA or ESA revises its EP life-qualification standard, or a NASA or ESA program accepts a life qualification in which less than 100% of the throughput requirement is demonstrated by test and the rest by a validated model, by 2031.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): All three lenses (verified in Williams et al. 2026): NASA already qualifies EP life by 100% test with 50% margin by analysis, and the AEPS QM-2 wear test runs fall 2026 to Sep 2029, so the node is redefined to the real increment (credit for part of the 100% test) and the AEPS-by-2029 signpost dropped. Skeptic: S3 2030 -> 2031 and S3 Medium -> Low; advocate's S2 2030 Medium / S3 2029 rejected (see debates). Soft edge from new plasma-aeps-life-qual. | E-plasma-nuclear (2026-10-07): 2035/S4 extension. plasma-stellarator-design-loop.title: AI design loop for stellarator fusion machines
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.description: Integrated optimization of stellarator (and other) magnetic configurations against turbulence, fast-ion losses, coil buildability and manufacturing tolerances in weeks, producing designs whose confinement is predicted with error bars.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.status_oct2026: Surrogates in the optimization loop already enable objectives such as full radial heat-flux profiles (arXiv 2609.28730); open optimizers exist (general) and Proxima's ConStellaration benchmark dataset is public (arXiv 2506.19583). Proxima Fusion raised EUR 130M (Jun 2025): Stellarator Model Coil 2027, Alpha demonstration 2031. Type One Energy plans Infinity Two (350 MWe) for the mid-2030s (general; the cited WNN article covers Infinity One only). Family 146 (Sinai's positive-entropy conjecture for the standard map, T1, conditional) concerns the textbook model of magnetic-island overlap and field-line chaos: confidence in theory only.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.premise_tier: n/a (capability-driven); family 146 is T1 and context only, so any reliance on it would be conditional
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.why: S2's multiphysics design optimization (2028) plus trusted surrogates closes the loop, and the pieces already exist (surrogates inside optimization loops, open benchmarks, DOE STELLAR-AI). The node is the tool, so its gate is data (validated surrogates and benchmarks). Fabrication gates the machines it designs: coil tolerances of millimetres over metre-scale coils decide whether designs perform as optimized. It has no space-technology unlock except as a soft accelerator of compact fusion-drive design (plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure), because the same loop applies to FRC-plus-nozzle configurations.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.strongest_case_small: Stellarator design is already highly optimized; the binding constraint for fusion is building and operating devices, so better paper designs add no fusion power before 2031.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.signpost: A stellarator company or national lab adopts as its design of record an end-to-end optimized configuration (surrogate turbulence, fast-ion losses, coil buildability and tolerances) produced in weeks. Predicted-versus-measured field errors on a built coil set (Proxima's 2027 model coil is the first chance) are the follow-on check.

The design shows specific power >= 1 kW/kg and multi-year life and closes gaps that today's concept studies wave away.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.status_oct2026: Direct Fusion Drive is a concept modeled by Princeton Satellite Systems and tested at small scale at PPPL (PFRC); reports that PSS and Pulsar Fusion apply ML to the PFRC experiment are unverified. Pulsar's Sunbird exhaust reportedly achieved first plasma with krypton in March 2026 with no fusion (unverified: the source could not be retrieved); its in-orbit demonstration is targeted for 2027 (pulsarfusion.com).

Band S3 Low: P6 default, and a conditional design cannot sit above its burn-physics premise.

plasma-fusion-net-gain.title: First magnetic-fusion net energy gain
plasma-fusion-net-gain.description: A magnetic-confinement device reaches scientific gain Q > 1, or Helion delivers net electricity, establishing the energy source that fusion propulsion would ultimately need.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.status_oct2026: CFS SPARC: the first of 18 toroidal-field magnets was placed on its assembly jig in Jan 2026; first plasma is targeted for 2027 (slipped from 2025 and 2026), with Q > 1 targeted shortly after (Wikipedia). Helion Polaris: first private D-T fusion, 150 million deg C (Feb 2026); Microsoft PPA target 2028 for Orion. TAE announced a merger with Trump Media (Dec 2025, close expected mid-2026; completion not confirmed as of Oct 2026). Its Copernicus device was cancelled in Nov 2025 because the Norm device made it unnecessary, and its Da Vinci device aims at net fusion energy in the late 2020s (Wikipedia).
plasma-fusion-net-gain.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
plasma-fusion-net-gain.why: Not an AI-math implication: an exogenous physical-clock anchor, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply. Physical-clock anchor: magnets, vacuum vessel, assembly, commissioning and tritium operations set the date. Chain: SPARC TF magnets installed 2026-27 -> first plasma 2027 -> D-D then D-T campaign -> Q>1 in 2028 at the earliest; Helion Orion (50 MW, Microsoft PPA) targeted 2028. AI contributes through plasma control and scenario design (plasma-ai-fusion-operations, soft) and faster commissioning in S3, not through mathematics. S3's 1.3-1.5x experiment multiplier applies only after 2028 and cannot pull Q>1 into SPARC's first-plasma year. Medium in every scenario (judgment): SPARC's Q > 1 needs first plasma (2027, already slipped from 2025 and 2026) and then a D-T campaign, and Helion's 2028 Orion target is unproven; two independent attempts with about three years of slack keep it at Medium rather than Low.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.strongest_case_small: The AI-math contribution is close to nil; this node is in the tree to show the gate on fusion propulsion is hardware.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.signpost: SPARC first plasma date and the start of its D-T campaign; Helion's first electricity from Orion.

plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.title: AI-designed thruster flies and performs as predicted
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.description: First in-space operation of an electric thruster whose magnetic circuit, channel and cathode were designed mainly by an AI optimization loop over physics-based (calibrated or kinetic) models, with on-orbit performance inside the pre-flight predicted band and the design attribution published.
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.status_oct2026: No such thruster exists. Small-satellite Hall and ion thrusters go from design to flight in roughly 18-36 months (general); Starlink flies thousands of Hall thrusters (krypton, then argon) designed by conventional iteration (general). Today's calibrated engineering models carry 8% (thrust) and 17% (discharge current) ground-to-orbit errors on the SPT-140 (Whittaker et al., AIAA 2026). LEAP 71's computational loop already designs rocket engines (prop-ai-engine-design-loop).
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.why: Two routes. (1) Generic AI design (P1): an optimization loop over Bayesian-calibrated engineering models designs the magnetic circuit, channel and cathode, as LEAP 71's loop does for rocket engines. Without a predictive transport closure the first article will likely miss its targets, so one extra build-test iteration is expected. (2) With predictive design (plasma-ep-predictive-design, soft), the first article is right first time and a year is saved. Chain (S2): cap-design-optimization 2028 -> first article and ground test 2029 -> second iteration and acceptance 2030 -> rideshare or the operator's own constellation (smallsat lag 12-18 months, physclock) -> first flight 2031. Commercial operators carry their own EP risk with no certifying authority above them (general), so qualification is not the gate. S3: AI-run test stands (2028) shorten the iteration -> 2030. Band: S2 Low because the chain lands at the horizon with no slack and the node needs published flight data with the design attributed mainly to AI; S3 Medium with one year of slack. A spacecraft majority AI-engineered (capability-ai-native-spacecraft, S2 2029) is a different claim: it concerns engineering labor on known designs, not a new plasma device performing as predicted.
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.strongest_case_small: The gain may be a few points of efficiency or a lighter magnetic circuit; the EP market is driven by cost, propellant (xenon/krypton/argon) supply, power-processing-unit mass and production rate, not design optimality.
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.signpost: A startup or prime announces a thruster 'designed in simulation, first-article meets spec' and manifests it for flight.

plasma-high-power-ep-life.title: 100 kW-class thruster runs for thousands of hours
plasma-high-power-ep-life.description: A >= 100 kW electric thruster (nested Hall, lithium MPD or VASIMR-type) demonstrates >= 5,000 hours of ground operation with validated wear projections toward the ~23,000 hours a crewed Mars nuclear-electric mission needs.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.status_oct2026: NASA/JPL's lithium MPD thruster reached 120 kW (Feb 24, 2026); next phases target 500 kW-1 MW per thruster; a crewed mission needs 2-4 MW total and >23,000 h of thruster operation (NASA). VASIMR VX-200SS ran 88 h at 80 kW (Jul 2021), with no newer public endurance result found.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.why: 5,000 h is seven months of continuous firing, which cannot start until a flight-like 100 kW unit and a facility able to hold low background pressure at that power exist (~2028-29 at best). Wall-clock test time does not compress with cognition.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.strongest_case_small: The AI-math effect is close to nil on this node; model-based life credit (plasma-ep-life-by-analysis) is the only lever and it needs the test data first.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.signpost: NASA announces a >1,000 h test of a >=100 kW thruster by 2028.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.note_2035: Resolved to 2032 in S3, 2033 in S2 and 2034 in S1: a flight-like 100 kW unit after design iterations, then about eight months of firing at a normal wear-test duty cycle. A funded start binds in every scenario. A lithium MPD can run in an existing facility because lithium condenses on the walls; a xenon unit needs a facility that takes 2-4 years to build. Low everywhere by 2035 because no funded program yet targets 5,000 h and NASA's stated path clusters 12 kW thrusters. Wear hours do not compress, so S4 equals S3.

plasma-abep-demo.title: Air-breathing electric propulsion flight test
plasma-abep-demo.description: A very-low-orbit satellite that scoops residual atmosphere and uses it as electric-propulsion propellant to cancel drag, demonstrated in orbit.
plasma-abep-demo.status_oct2026: Laboratory demonstrations only (general). Intake design is a rarefied-gas (Boltzmann/DSMC) problem; families 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation) and 364 (Boltzmann from Newtonian gases) are T1 and bear on confidence in the kinetic equations used, conditional, not on intake designs. Albedo's Clarity-1 (launched Mar 14, 2025) flew at 350-380 km on xenon ion propulsion for nine months with a drag coefficient 12% better than design (Albedo, Jan 2026).
plasma-abep-demo.premise_tier: n/a (funding and hardware gate); 363 and 364 are T1, conditional and not load-bearing
plasma-abep-demo.why: AI design optimization of intakes and discharge chambers is cognitive and fast under S2, but a flight demo needs funding, an atomic-oxygen-tolerant discharge and a ride, which binds. Conventional design can also produce the demo, so AI design (cap-design-optimization) accelerates it but is not a prerequisite. Chain (S2): AI-optimized intake and discharge design 2028 -> atomic-oxygen-tolerant discharge endurance test 2029 -> funded demo plus rideshare (18-24 months) -> flight 2031. S3 runs one year earlier.
plasma-abep-demo.strongest_case_small: Atomic-oxygen erosion of discharge parts, low intake efficiency and power-per-drag are physics and materials limits. Conventional EP at 350-380 km already works, as Clarity-1 showed (275 km was its design altitude, not demonstrated), which weakens the business case.

plasma-active-shielding.title: Magnetic radiation shield for crews
plasma-active-shielding.description: A superconducting-magnet active shield demonstrated in space that meaningfully reduces crew dose from solar particle events and galactic cosmic rays at acceptable mass.
plasma-active-shielding.status_oct2026: EU SR2S reached TRL 3 overall (some components TRL 4). A 2022 NASA NIAC Phase I studied CREW HaT, an open Halbach-torus HTS configuration (final report Feb 21, 2024; NTRS 20250002403).
plasma-active-shielding.why: AI design optimization can trim coil mass and stress, but deflecting GeV-scale cosmic rays requires a large field-times-length product over a crew-sized volume (general), which sets a mass floor; space qualification of large HTS coils and cryogenics is a multi-year hardware program. Conventional design can produce a demo, so AI design accelerates it but is not a prerequisite.
plasma-active-shielding.strongest_case_small: Physics-bound: the Stormer deflection physics is already understood, so better math does not change the mass floor.

plasma-cme-arrival-skill.title: Solar-storm arrival forecast within about 8 hours
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.description: Operational CME arrival-time forecasts whose best routinely-run ensemble reaches mean absolute error <= 8 h (vs 10.3 h for NASA M2M's Ensemble WSA-Enlil+Cone and 13.2 h across all CCMC scoreboard submissions), with calibrated probability windows.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.status_oct2026: CCMC Arrival Time Scoreboard, 2013-2023: 1,702 predictions of 256 impacting CMEs, bias -2.5 h, mean absolute error 13.2 h, standard deviation 17.4 h, only slight improvement; the most established models do better (EnsWEC M2M: MAE 10.3 h on 95 predictions), and errors are dominated by CME reconstruction and background solar wind (Kay et al., Space Weather 2024). STEREO-A is 70.6 degrees ahead of Earth (Oct 7, 2026, STEREO Science Center) and gives a side view now; PUNCH (2025) adds polarimetric 3D imaging and CCOR coronagraphs fly on GOES-19 and SOLAR-1. ESA's Vigil at L5 (carrying NOAA's CCOR coronagraph) is planned to launch in 2031.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.why: AI-built ensembles, multi-view assimilation and better background-solar-wind modeling (coronal field extrapolation, an ill-posed inverse problem where mathematics genuinely helps) could cut the best ensemble's MAE by roughly 20-30% (judgment, illustrative), enough to reach 8 h before Vigil data exist. Validation runs on an event-count clock that does not compress: about 24 impacting CMEs a year on average, fewer near the next solar minimum around 2030, and with an error SD near 17 h about 40 events (roughly two years) are needed to show 8 h against 10.3 h. Chain (S2): assimilation methods 2028 -> real-time scoreboard submissions 2028-30 -> operational transition 2031. S3 saves a year on methods and transition, not on events.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.strongest_case_small: Eleven years of model development barely moved the error, including periods when STEREO-A gave a side view (roughly 2020-22, general); the limit is input reconstruction and background wind, and robust day-ahead skill may need Vigil.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.signpost: The best routinely-submitting scoreboard model posts MAE below 9 h over at least 40 impacting CMEs (about a 24-month window) during 2027-29.

plasma-bz-forecast.title: Knowing a solar storm's magnetic punch a day ahead
plasma-bz-forecast.description: Forecasting the southward magnetic field (Bz) of an incoming CME 12-24+ hours before arrival: the main driver of geomagnetic storm severity and of the storm-time density errors that hit satellites.
plasma-bz-forecast.status_oct2026: Magnetic structure is recognized as the main bottleneck; operationally Bz is known only as the CME passes L1, roughly 30-60 minutes before impact (SOLAR-1 operational 2026; timing general). Established short-term in-situ reconstruction tools mostly need a human in the loop; arXiv 2602.06926 (Feb 2026) automates one pipeline from partial L1 passage (~5 h timing and ~10 nT field errors), at lead times of hours.
plasma-bz-forecast.why: Requires either routine coronal magnetic-field measurement or in-situ monitors well upstream of L1, neither of which will exist by 2031. AI theory can extract partial skill from source-region magnetograms (flux-rope chirality and orientation rules), which is why S2/S3 are Low rather than Speculative. Real-time skill must be shown on events. Near the 2030-31 minimum only about 5-15 CMEs a year reach Earth (judgment), and the signpost asks for 50+ events. Counting every impacting CME and rising rates from 2032, 50 events take about three years from a working method: S3 methods about 2030 and 50 events about 2033, S2 a year later. Hindcasts on Cycle 24-25 events speed method development but do not replace the real-time count.
plasma-bz-forecast.strongest_case_small: This is an observation limit, not a mathematics limit.
plasma-bz-forecast.signpost: Funding of a sub-L1 or off-Sun-Earth-line in-situ monitor, or a source-region method with Bz-sign skill above 70% on 50+ events.

plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.title: Storm-proof low-orbit operations
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.description: Constellation operators and space-traffic services run conjunction screening and station-keeping on probabilistic density forecasts with realistic covariance, so that at the next G4+ storm the number of objects losing custody and of emergency maneuvers is at least halved versus May 2024.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.status_oct2026: During the May 2024 storm thousands of satellites maneuvered and conjunction assessment was poorly predictable even a day ahead (Parker and Linares 2024); KANOPUS-V 3 lost ~917 m of semi-major axis within days (CPAESS 2026 abstract). SpaceX's response to the Feb 2022 loss was operational (higher insertion orbits) (general).
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.why: Once density products carry calibrated uncertainty (2029 in S2), propagating it into covariance and screening is mature astrodynamics; the gate is adoption by operators and the government catalog, which typically takes 1-2 years and faces the FY2027 Office of Space Commerce cut. The May 2024 degradation came mostly from storm-driver forecasts (Ap underpredicted by 100-300 at 1-3 days), which stay data-limited (plasma-bz-forecast), and the government catalog already runs assimilative density (HASDM), so the achievable gain is partial. Validating the outcome also needs a G4+ storm in 2029-31, in the declining phase of Cycle 25 (maximum Oct 2024, SIDC), when G4 storms still occur but less often (general).
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.strongest_case_small: The largest operators already manage storms with margin and autonomy; the benefit concentrates in smaller operators and the public catalog. Losses like Feb 2022 were an operations choice and were fixed operationally. Fast-revisit sensing (SpaceX Stargaze, minutes-latency orbit updates) can deliver much of the custody gain without new density math.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.signpost: At the next G4+ storm, count objects losing custody and emergency maneuvers versus May 2024.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.revision_note: E-safe-orbits (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2-S4 Medium -> High. S1 unchanged. Bands unchanged.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.note_2035: Solar Cycle 26 rises toward a maximum in the mid-2030s, so a G4+ test storm by 2035 is likely. Fast-revisit tracking also cuts custody loss, so the outcome is likely in S2-S4. S4 adds nothing because adoption binds.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.gate_note: Operator and catalog adoption binds; storm-driver forecasts and the need for a G4+ test storm (data) are the runner-up.

plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.title: Radiation-belt and charging risk forecasts days ahead
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.description: Probabilistic, physics-consistent forecasts of MeV electron flux and surface/internal charging hazard, 1-3 days ahead for CME-driven enhancements and up to about a week for recurrent high-speed-stream driving, used in satellite operations (for example deferring an orbit-raise or electric-propulsion firing through a charging peak).
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.status_oct2026: SWPC's operational Relativistic Electron Forecast Model (REFM) already gives deterministic 1-3 day >2 MeV electron fluence forecasts at GEO from 30 days of solar-wind speed (SWPC). Random-forest models (VAMPIRE/COVEN, Jun 2026) forecast ~2 MeV flux threshold crossings up to 6 days ahead from the AL index history alone (Northumbria); SPARTAI gives multi-day MeV forecasts (Oct 2025); transformer and LSTM pipelines forecast 1 MeV flux 6 h ahead (arXiv 2605.15752). Charging codes (SPIS, NASCAP-2K) are mature; PAGER internal-charging models were validated against GEO anomalies (IEEE TPS 2026).
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.why: ML forecasts and a deterministic operational baseline exist; AI applied math adds coupling to physics-based diffusion models and calibrated probabilities so operators can act on them. Week-ahead skill exists only for recurrent high-speed-stream driving (27-day recurrence); CME-driven enhancements stay at 1-3 days. The binding step is adoption: an agency product (SWPC or ESA) and an operator or insurer procedure citing it. Chain (S2): calibrated physics-coupled methods 2028 -> SWPC or ESA pre-operational probabilistic product 2029 -> an operator or insurer procedure citing it 2029-30. Software-only, so no hardware lag; agency R2O and operator uptake set the pace, which is why S2 is Medium.
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.strongest_case_small: Already ML-driven, so the math increment is modest; designers will keep worst-case design environments (e.g. AE9/AP9) regardless of forecasts, so design margins do not shrink.
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.signpost: SWPC or ESA adopts a multi-day MeV electron probability product and an operator or insurer cites it in procedures.
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.revision_note: E-safe-orbits (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High. plasma-vleo-at-scale.title: Commercial constellations below 300 km
plasma-vleo-at-scale.description: At least 100 commercial satellites operating sustainably below 300 km altitude, with propellant and drag margins sized from validated density statistics.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.status_oct2026: Albedo's Clarity-1 operated at 350-380 km for nine months (Mar-Dec 2025) and projects five-year life at 275 km averaged over solar cycles; it lost contact due to a radio memory fault, not drag (Albedo, Jan 2026). Solar Cycle 25 peaked Oct 2024; the declining phase runs to ~2030, lowering mean density but still producing large storms.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.why: Validated density statistics trim only the model-error share of the drag reserve; most of the reserve at 250-300 km covers solar-cycle and storm variability (density varies several-fold over a cycle, general), which no density model removes, so plausible savings are ~10-20% of drag propellant (illustrative). That helps VLEO business cases at the margin, but constellations need capital, launches and production first.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.strongest_case_small: Capital, demand for very-high-resolution imagery, EP throughput and atomic-oxygen-tolerant hardware bind this, not density mathematics.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.signpost: A sub-300 km operator raises >= $100M and orders >= 50 satellites by 2028.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.revision_note: E-safe-orbits (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. S1 '>2031' -> 2033 (physclock-cheap-mass-customer S1 2032). band_2035 S2 Low -> Medium. Fleets fielded near the 2030-31 minimum must be sized for Cycle 26 drag, which rises several-fold at 250-300 km toward its mid-2030s maximum, and few operators plan sub-300 km fleets. S2 stays Low. S3 and S4 keep their 2031 Medium. S4 adds nothing because capital and launch bind.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.gate_note: Capital for sub-300 km fleets binds; launch for customers (launch-external) is the runner-up.

plasma-nep-mars-cargo.title: Megawatt electric cargo ships to Mars
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.description: An operational nuclear-electric (or megawatt solar-electric) cargo vehicle with MW-class electric propulsion flying to Mars.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.status_oct2026: NASA estimates 2-4 MW and >23,000 h thruster life for crewed nuclear-electric missions. Earlier NASA Glenn COMPASS work sized a ~1.9 MWe system for a 2-year crewed round trip and ~200 t cargo stages (general). Highest demonstrated single-thruster power: 120 kW lithium MPD (Feb 2026). NASA says NEP architectures needing up to 300 kW of EP can be built by clustering 12 kW AEPS thrusters, with Xe and Kr cluster tests under way (Williams et al. 2026). SR-1 Freedom (>20 kWe, Dec 2028 target, Gateway PPE bus with three 12 kW AEPS and four 6 kW Hall thrusters) would be the first NEP flight, at about 1% of MW class.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.why: Needs a flight reactor or MW-class arrays, launch approval for a space reactor, and life-tested MW-scale EP; each is a multi-year hardware and regulatory program. Clusters of qualified 12 kW thrusters cover the few-hundred-kW range, so MW class still needs higher-power thrusters (plasma-high-power-ep-life) or impractically large clusters (~80-330 units). The solar route rides on compute-satellite power buses (AI1's superseded June 2026 spec: ~150 kW array at ~127 W/kg on a ~2.1 t satellite, 33FG reconstruction; the Aug-Sep 2026 revision runs 175 kW average / 250 kW peak under 4,000 kg; struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet, soft). That route could enable 100 kW-class solar-electric tugs, but not MW cargo before 2031.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.strongest_case_small: Not applicable: this node records a nil effect inside the horizon.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.signpost: A funded flight-reactor program with a launch date, or a >= 500 kW thruster test campaign announced.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor: COMPASS figure marked (general); SR-1 calibration point added. Advocate: NASA's clustering path (up to 300 kW from 12 kW thrusters) added; its proposal to soften plasma-high-power-ep-life and add a compute-bus tug as a hard prerequisite rejected (MW class lies beyond NASA's stated cluster range; the tug is not a causal precondition). plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.title: Faster, cheaper electric-propulsion development
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.description: Development-to-qualification time for new EP thrusters falls ~15-30% (S2), up to ~40% (S3), and build-test iterations roughly halve because physics-based models replace parts of empirical iteration and, where an agency accepts it, of wear testing. The ceiling is the Amdahl bound on whole-program compression (~38% S2, ~51% S3; capability.json); EP schedules are dominated by wear-test hours and by program, supplier and requirements problems.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.status_oct2026: AEPS: contract awarded 2016 (general); AEPS contract closeout mid-to-late 2027, but the QM-2 life wear test runs fall 2026 to Sep 2029 and the SEP project closes out in 2029, about 13 years (Williams et al., Space Propulsion 2026).
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.why: Predictive design (fewer iterations) is enough for commercial thrusters, where no certifier sits above the operator: cutting 1.5-2 years from a 4-6 year program is 25-40%, which meets the S2 threshold (plasma-ep-predictive-design). Model-based life credit (plasma-ep-life-by-analysis, soft) would shorten agency wear tests further, but it is Low by 2035, so it is off the critical path. The outcome needs at least one full development-to-qualification cycle started after predictive design is validated, still with a full wear test. Chain (S3): predictive design 2029 -> program started 2030 -> design, one or two build-test iterations and a full wear test in about three years -> 2033. S2: predictive design 2030 -> 2034. S1: predictive design 2035 -> after 2035. Band Low in S2-S4: predictive design is Medium by 2035, and the cut must be shown on a real program and published.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.strongest_case_small: Program management, supply chain and funding dominate EP schedules; AEPS's own lessons learned are about risk management, contract oversight and requirement definition, not physics.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.signpost: A new Hall or gridded-ion thruster in a class that took four to six years reaches qualification within three years of program start, citing predictive design or model-based life credit.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 2031 -> >2031 (a full program cycle must start after life credit, which now lands 2031 at the earliest); S2 Low -> Speculative. Auditor: S3 Low -> Speculative (skeptic kept Low; resolver sided with the auditor because the hard prerequisite lands at the horizon). Skeptic: magnitude 30-50% -> ~15-30% (S2), up to ~40% (S3), within the Amdahl bounds. Skeptic + auditor (verified): AEPS took ~13 years including the life test, not 11. Skeptic (the cut must be shown and published on a real program) vs advocate (commercial programs iterate fast with no certifier): Low kept; predictive design is only Medium by 2033 in S2.

prop-ns-forced-verified.title: Forced Navier–Stokes blowup independently checked
prop-ns-forced-verified.description: Outside experts run Comparator on the Lean proof and audit the statement of OpenAI's Sep 8, 2026 claim that the forced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations can blow up from smooth, finite-energy data. This moves that claim from T3 to T4. The concurrent Buckmaster-Alpöge Euler, Boussinesq and porous-medium blowup proofs are a parallel, separate check. Whether the result also satisfies Clay's breakdown statements (C)/(D) is a separate institutional question (frontier-ns-clay-cd-ruling).
prop-ns-forced-verified.status_oct2026: Claimed Sep 8, 2026 with a 166-page manuscript and Lean repository (~17 h formalization; ~88 h of ~10,000 agents). OpenAI frames the result as establishing Clay statement (C), and also (D); Clay still lists the problem unsolved. Buckmaster and Alpöge posted Euler/Boussinesq/IPM blowup preprints with Lean formalizations about 12 h before the announcement (Decrypt reported the most advanced result still awaiting a final Lean check at disclosure), followed by a public credit dispute. Santibañez-Leal (Zenodo, Sep 17) replayed the NS and Euler Lean certificates through the kernel with zero sorryAx; that is not a Comparator run or statement audit, so the tier is unchanged. No independent review found as of Oct 7, 2026: T3. Duraiswami (arXiv 2609.17642, Sep 15, 2026) found nothing to suggest the mechanism is reachable in a flow one computes or builds. Related but separate: family 376 (universal computation in forced NS) is a catalog family, manuscript-only (T1).
prop-ns-forced-verified.why: The Lean code is public and the dispute guarantees scrutiny, so a Comparator run plus a statement audit is likely within about 12 months in every scenario. The engineering consequence is a confidence change only (tl-position-2): the forced equations alone can fail to determine the flow, which CFD practice already assumes by adding numerical or model dissipation. No solver, closure or engine design changes. It is a stepping stone (soft link) to frontier-ns-unforced, not a prerequisite.
prop-ns-forced-verified.strongest_case_small: The forcing is engineered to drive the singularity, and real propellants would cavitate or form shocks long before it occurs (Duraiswami 2026). Rocket CFD resolves or models scales where the continuum assumption itself fails. The propulsion impact is essentially nil. The node is on the tree to mark a dead end readers would otherwise take for a breakthrough.
prop-ns-forced-verified.signpost: First published Comparator report and statement audit for the NS Lean repository (via Hexagon or the IAS advisory group), expected within 6-12 months. A gap would drop the claim to T1.
prop-ns-forced-verified.revision_note: B-math-frontier: [skeptic] catalog_families 376 removed (the Sep 8 claim is outside the 722-paper catalog; 376 stays in status as a related, separate T1 family); description scoped to the OpenAI claim, Buckmaster-Alpoge as a parallel check. [auditor] status: kernel replay, Clay framing, Alpoge-Buckmaster Lean status; lettered position citation fixed. [advocate S2/S3 2026 rejected: signpost itself expects 6-12 months; no outside Comparator run a month after the claim; Hexagon has no deposits.] Hard edge into frontier-ns-unforced made soft; edge into prop-les-convergence-theory (engines-materials) left for that branch. | E-math-frontier (2026-10-07): band_2035 = band_2031; S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): The why expects a check within about 12 months of the Sep 2026 claim, so Medium 2027 and High 2028 (no outside run a month in). Bands unchanged.
prop-ns-forced-verified.note_2035: Settled well before 2032 in every scenario, so 2032-35 changes nothing. S4 equals S3.
prop-ns-forced-verified.gate_note: The Comparator run and statement audit bind; experts willing to do the audit (adoption) are the runner-up.

prop-certified-stability-rom.title: Certified combustion-stability models
prop-certified-stability-rom.description: Low-order acoustic-network or Galerkin models of chamber thermoacoustics, delivered with rigorous linear and nonlinear stability margins: Lyapunov or sum-of-squares certificates and bounds on Hopf bifurcation and triggering amplitude under an uncertain flame-response band.
prop-certified-stability-rom.status_oct2026: Solved in principle but expert-scarce. DLR/TU Delft network models predict acoustic frequencies within <5% on two research combustors (de Jong Cantarino et al., IJSCD 2026). Growth rates and triggering thresholds still hinge on flame response, and reliable, efficient instability prediction remains rare (JAXA 2025). Family 143 [L] (uniform limit-cycle bounds, Hilbert's 16th) is T3 but theory only: it bounds how many oscillation states can coexist in planar polynomial amplitude models, with no practical constant.
prop-certified-stability-rom.why: Stability analysis of a given model is bespoke but routine mathematics, exactly the kind that becomes on-demand under tl-position-4. With public research-grade models in 2027 (S2), a team can get certified margins for every injector variant in days instead of a specialist's months. The value is capped by the flame-response input (prop-flame-response).
prop-certified-stability-rom.strongest_case_small: Certifying the stability of a model with the wrong flame response gives false comfort: a proof of the wrong property. Bomb tests stay mandatory. The F-1 lesson is that triggered (nonlinear) instability is what destroys engines, and its inputs are physical.
prop-certified-stability-rom.signpost: A published AI-produced stability analysis that predicts unstable modes and triggering thresholds on a rig (DLR BKD/BKH, Purdue CVRC) before the test.
prop-certified-stability-rom.revision_note: B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 equals S2 through 2027; cap-applied-math is 2027 in both, so the same one-year lag applies). lettered citation 'under position (a' replaced with the KB position id under tl-position-4. | E-engines-materials (2026-10-07): band_2035 S1 Medium -> High. Years kept. S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Cognitive and routine once public research-grade models exist, so Medium at the earliest year and High a year later in S2-S4; S1 Medium 2030, High 2034. Bands unchanged.
prop-certified-stability-rom.note_2035: Certified stability margins are a routine design check in every scenario by 2035, including Plateau. Their value still hangs on measured flame response. The work is analysis, so S4 equals S3.
prop-certified-stability-rom.gate_note: The stability mathematics binds; measured flame response, which caps what the margins mean (data), is the runner-up.

prop-cfd-auto-vv.title: Automated checks that engine flow simulations are right
prop-cfd-auto-vv.description: AI agents run code verification (manufactured solutions), solution verification (grid and time-step refinement; adjoint or a-posteriori error estimates for steady and RANS cases), uncertainty quantification and NASA-STD-7009-style credibility assessment on every propulsion simulation at near-zero marginal labor. Compute for solution verification of unsteady LES stays several times the base run (a 2x refinement of a 3D unsteady case costs ~8-16x, general), adjoint error estimates do not apply to chaotic LES, and credibility (validation) remains capped by test data.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.status_oct2026: Solved in principle, but rarely done in full on engine-design CFD because it is labor-intensive (general). CFD Vision 2030 progress reviews flag separated-flow prediction and UQ as persistent gaps (Aerospace America, Dec 2022).
prop-cfd-auto-vv.why: Every CFD result becomes a number with an error bar that separates numerical error from model-form error. That ends two expensive failure modes: hardware built on an unconverged simulation, and tests run to settle a question the simulation had already answered. It is also a prerequisite for any regulator credit for simulation.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.strongest_case_small: Validation data, not verification labor, limit V&V. Error bars on RANS are dominated by closure error, which verification cannot remove.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.signpost: An AI-generated credibility assessment accepted in a NASA or prime-contractor design review, or AI-automated solution verification in AIAA CFD Prediction Workshop entries.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (claim, accepted): labor collapses but compute does not; solution verification of unsteady LES costs several times the base run and adjoint error estimates diverge on chaotic LES. prop-mass-gauging.title: Limits on measuring propellant in low gravity
prop-mass-gauging.description: Proofs of which tank-fill states can be identified in microgravity from boundary sensors (capacitance, radio-frequency or impedance-type tomography), plus gauging algorithms with guaranteed error bounds.
prop-mass-gauging.status_oct2026: Gauging is a focus area of NASA's CFM portfolio, alongside boil-off and transfer. Family 365 [L]: its formalized main result is nonuniqueness of bounded measurable scalar conductivities on a 3D ball (T3, unaudited by outsiders), the part used here as a ceiling: some rough interior configurations cannot be told apart from boundary data alone without priors or extra sensing. Its headline, joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch, is unformalized (T1, conditional).
prop-mass-gauging.pathway: P1 (+P3 via classical log-stability limits, general)
prop-mass-gauging.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 365's formalized part (3D scalar-conductivity nonuniqueness, used as the imaging ceiling) is T3; its metric/connection recovery headline is T1 (conditional, context only)
prop-mass-gauging.why: Gauging uncertainty turns into reserve propellant: 1% of a 1,200 t depot load is ~12 t, about 0.1 of a 120 t tanker (illustrative, general), so the economic stake is small. Gauging needs a scalar (total mass), which can be identifiable even when the interior configuration is not; 365's formalized part concerns rough (bounded measurable) 3D scalar conductivities and its T1 headline concerns joint metric and connection recovery, so it bounds full tomographic imaging, not mass estimation. The practical ceiling for few-electrode capacitance gauging is classical logarithmic instability (general). The ceiling side tells designers not to rely on full tomographic reconstruction and to fuse sensors with thermodynamic models.
prop-mass-gauging.strongest_case_small: Operators can gauge after a settling burn with conventional sensors and accept the margin. The formalized nonuniqueness in family 365 concerns rough (bounded measurable) 3D conductivities, which may not match real tank fill states.
prop-mass-gauging.signpost: Flight gauging accuracy reported from LOXSAT or the Starship transfer demo (target <=1%).
prop-mass-gauging.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (grounding, accepted): 365's formalized main result is T3 but the nonuniqueness companion used as the ceiling is T1 unless shown formalized, so the ceiling is conditional; premise_tier and pathway relabelled (the practical ceiling for few-electrode capacitance gauging is classical log-instability). Skeptic (claim, accepted): gauging needs a scalar (total mass), which can be identifiable when the configuration is not, so 365 bounds tomographic imaging, not mass estimation; economic stake ~0.1 tanker per 1% error. Soft edge from new node prop-loxsat-cfm-flight-data. Years and bands unchanged. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): S3 2027 -> 2028 (S3 equals S2 through 2027; cap-applied-math is 2027 in both). 365 tiering corrected to match frontier-inverse-stability, struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations, hyper-tps-inverse-nde, struct-shm-inverse-limits and materials-am-digital-twin-qual (lean/docs/365.md formalizes only the scalar-conductivity nonuniqueness): the ceiling is T3, the recovery headline T1. S1 High 2034. Bands unchanged.

prop-closure-theory.title: Turbulence and combustion models with guarantees
prop-closure-theory.description: AI-built RANS, LES subgrid and flamelet closures that are realizable, frame-invariant and consistent in known limits, carry generalization bounds, and are validated across separated, swirling and reacting benchmark classes without per-case tuning.
prop-closure-theory.status_oct2026: Open; this is the field's central modeling problem. RANS cannot reliably predict separated flows (CFD Vision 2030). ML closures often fail to generalize beyond their training data (JFM 2025; arXiv 2604.25824, Apr 2026). A propulsion example: k-omega SST under-predicts LH2 tank self-pressurization by 15-16% and vapor temperature by up to 40%, versus 3% for laminar and 7% for IDDES (Kartuzova et al., SciTech 2025).
prop-closure-theory.why: Closure error is the dominant model-form error in propulsion CFD: wall heat flux for cooling, mixing, nozzle separation. Under S2 the cognitive part (deriving constrained closures, proving consistency) is fast. What binds is high-fidelity data at engine conditions. DNS at engine Reynolds numbers is infeasible even at exascale (Pele's largest run: 60 billion cells), and high-pressure reacting validation experiments take years. Success requires validation across separated, swirling and reacting classes without per-case tuning plus a blind workshop result; blind AIAA workshops run on roughly 2-3-year cycles (general), so a closure derived when cap-physics-theory lands cannot be blind-validated the same year. P6 defaults to Low. Flame-response and turbopump tools benefit (soft links) but do not need closure guarantees.
prop-closure-theory.strongest_case_small: Turbulence closure has resisted 60 years of work and may be fundamentally underdetermined, because averaging loses information. A provably consistent closure need not beat a tuned one on a specific engine. LES and hybrid methods are already replacing RANS in design-critical areas.
prop-closure-theory.signpost: An AI-derived closure tops the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource separated-flow cases and a blind AIAA workshop case without retuning.
prop-closure-theory.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (timing/band, concrete mechanism accepted): S2 2029 -> 2030, S3 2028 -> 2029, S2 Medium -> Low. The success criterion includes a blind workshop win, which cannot happen in the year the theory capability lands (cap-physics-theory S2 2029 / S3 2028); data at engine conditions bind; P6 default Low. Edges to prop-turbopump-tool (skeptic + advocate) and prop-flame-response (skeptic + advocate) made soft. S3 Medium kept. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): S3 2029 -> 2030: the why says a closure cannot be blind-validated in the year cap-physics-theory lands, and B-trunk moved that anchor to S3 2029. prop-flame-response.title: Predictive flame response at engine pressures
prop-flame-response.description: First-principles prediction of injector flame transfer functions and transcritical real-fluid mixing for LOX/CH4 and LOX/H2 at 100-350 bar. This is the missing input that decides whether a chamber mode grows.
prop-flame-response.status_oct2026: Measured on subscale rigs or extracted from costly LES; wall-modeled LES at engine conditions is described as prohibitively expensive (JAXA 2025). Raptor reached 350 bar chamber pressure in a development test that Musk reported in May 2023 (per newspaceeconomy, Apr 16, 2026), deep in the supercritical regime where injection models lack validation (general).
prop-flame-response.why: With flame response predicted, certified reduced models (prop-certified-stability-rom) predict growth rates, not just frequencies. Flame transfer functions are already computed by LES with existing subgrid models; what is missing is validated real-fluid, transcritical injection physics at 100-350 bar and rig data, so closure theory (prop-closure-theory) accelerates the work but is not required. Validation can start against decades of archived rig data, but it then needs about a year of blind rig tests. That experimental year binds in S2 and S3 alike: chain (S2) cap-physics-theory (2029) -> model -> blind rig year -> 2030; (S3) 2029 (cap-physics-theory, moved from 2028 by B-trunk) -> 2030.
prop-flame-response.strongest_case_small: Flame response depends on manufacturing detail (injector tolerances, additive-manufacturing roughness) and on transient states that models won't capture. Rigs remain necessary for every new injector family.
prop-flame-response.signpost: Blind prediction of an unstable mode's frequency and amplitude to within ~10% on a JANNAF, ESA or DLR combustor before the test.
prop-flame-response.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor (timing, two lenses): S2 2029 -> 2030; the node's own text says a year of blind rig tests binds, yet S2 equalled its prerequisites' year. prop-closure-theory hard -> soft (skeptic + advocate: flame transfer functions are computed by LES with existing subgrid models; what is missing is transcritical real-fluid injection physics and rig data). prop-rde-mode-theory.title: Predictive theory of detonation-engine wave modes
prop-rde-mode-theory.description: A validated model of how many detonation waves an RDRE runs, when it switches modes, and how injectors couple to the waves, as functions of flow rate, mixture and back-pressure, so that engines can be designed to hold one stable mode.
prop-rde-mode-theory.status_oct2026: Open research: wave-mode bifurcation (APS DFD 2025), dynamic injector-response models (Mar 2025), and model equations that capture qualitative mode-locking (arXiv 2003.06655). Hardware is ahead of theory: NASA's InRoDES 10,000 lbf-class LOX/LCH4 thrust chamber, tested from Sep 2025, fired for just over 340 s in Dec 2025, and an earlier full-scale NASA RDRE combustor ran 251 s at more than 5,800 lbf (NASA).
prop-rde-mode-theory.why: Higher specific impulse at equal average chamber pressure is a theoretical potential that NASA is still assessing; the demonstrated RDRE benefit is a much shorter combustor and an engine 10-50% shorter overall (NASA NTRS 20240000933). Either benefit needs stable, predictable modes. This is nonlinear-dynamics mathematics that S2 makes cheap. Hot-fire campaigns take days to weeks, but blind validation needs a new geometry designed, printed and hot-fired after the model exists (months), so S2 lands in 2029.
prop-rde-mode-theory.strongest_case_small: RDRE development is advancing empirically (340-s firings, Venus flight). Theory may mostly explain what tests already found; the real gates are thermal management of a compact chamber and nozzle integration.
prop-rde-mode-theory.signpost: A published model that predicts mode transitions on a new RDRE geometry blind, confirmed by NASA or AFRL tests.
prop-rde-mode-theory.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (claim, verified at NTRS 20240000933): the Isp gain is a 'potential ... currently being assessed', the demonstrated benefit is a 10-50% shorter engine, and the record does not mention a 5x lower feed pressure (removed). Timing (skeptic, accepted): S2 2028 -> 2029; blind validation needs a new geometry designed, printed and hot-fired after the model exists. Fact fix (auditor, re-verified on nasa.gov): only the Dec 2025 InRoDES firing exceeded 340 s; the 251 s figure belongs to an earlier full-scale RDRE combustor test, not Sep 2025. Soft edge from physclock-ai-run-test-stands. Years kept. S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium a year after the earliest year (a new geometry must be printed and hot-fired after the model). S3 High 2033 after several programs run blind tests on AI-run stands; S1 Medium 2033, two years after its earliest year. Advocate (S3 High 2032) and skeptic (modes hinge on build detail, High 2035) weighed; 2033. Bands unchanged.
prop-rde-mode-theory.note_2035: By 2035 several RDRE programs have given models blind tests, so S3 rises to High. The base case stays Medium because wave modes may hinge on build detail that models miss. Hot fire binds and S3 already has AI-run stands, so S4 equals S3.
prop-rde-mode-theory.gate_note: Blind hot-fire validation binds; the nonlinear wave-mode theory itself (cognitive) is the runner-up.

prop-cfm-models.title: Validated models of cryogenic propellant in microgravity
prop-cfm-models.description: Predictive models of self-pressurization, slosh, line chilldown and tank-to-tank transfer in low gravity, validated on flight data with quantified uncertainty (tank pressure within ~5%, boil-off within ~10%).
prop-cfm-models.status_oct2026: In 1 g, CFD reaches 3% (laminar) to 7% (IDDES) on tank pressure, but results hinge on the turbulence model and a tuned evaporation accommodation coefficient (Kartuzova et al., SciTech 2025). Microgravity data are scarce (ZBOT on ISS). NASA's CFM portfolio lists maturing predictive models through flight-prediction comparisons as an objective. LOXSAT (Eta Space/Rocket Lab, a 9-month LOX demo) was set for no earlier than Jul 17, 2026; the sources found do not confirm whether it has flown.
prop-cfm-models.why: Boil-off and transfer losses drive the tanker count (SpaceX '10-ish' vs NASA 'high teens'). In an illustrative depot model (tables), boil-off of 0.05-0.3%/day costs ~1 extra tanker at one tanker per 6 days, and 0.3-0.5%/day costs 3-5 extra at one per 12 days. These are the physical losses; a validated model recovers only the margin held against their uncertainty (re-running the same model, planning for +50% boil-off instead of a validated +/-10% costs 0-1 tanker at a 6-day cadence, more only at slow cadence and high loss). In S2 the analysis is near-instant once flight data exist, but the data arrive on the launch clock: validation within ~5% on pressure and ~10% on boil-off across fill levels, coasts and attitudes needs several transfer flights and weeks-long storage, which come with the 2028-29 depot campaigns. Conditional on SpaceX or NASA publishing transfer and boil-off data (LOXSAT gives a small-tank public LOX dataset); otherwise the model exists only inside SpaceX and the node is unobservable.
prop-cfm-models.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will learn empirically from its own flights and keep the data, and margins will follow measured performance whether or not a public model exists.
prop-cfm-models.signpost: Publication of transferred mass, boil-off and chilldown losses from the first Starship ship-to-ship transfer, or NASA model-vs-flight comparisons from LOXSAT.
prop-cfm-models.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (timing, concrete mechanism accepted): S2 2028 -> 2029. The data gate runs on the launch clock; the first ship-to-ship transfer is S2 2027 and was still unscheduled in Sep 2026, and validation across fill levels, coasts and attitudes needs several transfer flights and weeks-long storage, which arrive with the 2028-29 depot campaigns; prop.json itself rated this 'High by 2028 if flight data are shared'. Added the data-sharing conditional and the 'physical loss vs model margin' correction (skeptic + auditor; depot table reproduced and margin re-simulated). Soft edge from new node prop-loxsat-cfm-flight-data (auditor). S1/S3 and bands unchanged. | E-engines-materials (2026-10-07): band_2035 S1 Medium -> High. Years kept. S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Validation within 5%/10% needs several transfer flights and weeks-long storage, so S2 Medium 2030 and High 2031 (not High in the first data year); S3 a year earlier; S1 High 2034 on depot and lunar campaign data. Bands unchanged.
prop-cfm-models.note_2035: Depot, lunar and Mars-window campaigns in 2029-35 supply flight data in every scenario, so Plateau reaches High by 2035. The data arrive on the launch clock, so S4 equals S3.
prop-cfm-models.gate_note: Microgravity transfer and boil-off flight data bind; building the validated two-phase models (cognitive) is the runner-up.

prop-psi-models.title: Predicting how lander exhaust erodes the surface
prop-psi-models.description: Validated models of how lander engine plumes erode regolith (rarefied-to-continuum gas flow, granular ejecta, cratering), used to set landing-site and engine-placement requirements.
prop-psi-models.status_oct2026: NASA reports that poorly constrained flight data inhibit accurate PSI prediction. Langley's vacuum-sphere PSI tests run through spring 2026, and MSFC PSI tools support HLS (NTRS 2023). Families 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation) and 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian gases, incl. fluctuations) are T1 and touch the kinetic theory beneath DSMC. Conditional; P5 confidence only.
prop-psi-models.pathway: P1->P6 (363/364 P5 link has nil engineering effect)
prop-psi-models.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise via cap-applied-math); 363 and 364 are T1, conditional, with nil engineering effect
prop-psi-models.why: Starship HLS already uses smaller mid-body methalox landing thrusters for terminal descent to raise the plume impingement point (general). Predictive PSI now sets standoff and throttle limits, landing-site and pad requirements, and keep-out zones for nearby base assets under repeated landings at one site, and it decides whether sintered pads are needed (auton-sinter-process-control). This is applied numerics plus data: DSMC for the rarefied gas phase (already adequate) coupled to CFD-DEM ejecta models calibrated on flight imagery. The data gate eases with landing cadence: SCALPSS 1.1 on Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Mar 2025) returned plume-surface imagery and stereo elevation maps, so every instrumented CLPS or HLS landing is a PSI experiment. Families 363 and 364 have nil engineering effect: DSMC's convergence to the Boltzmann equation is already proven (Wagner 1992, general), so new foundations for Boltzmann do not change DSMC practice. They are noted only as conditional (T1) theory context.
prop-psi-models.strongest_case_small: DSMC already works for the gas phase. The gaps are granular physics and lunar flight data, which no theorem supplies, and operators can engineer around PSI with pads, throttling or thruster placement.
prop-psi-models.signpost: Pre-landing PSI predictions matched by post-landing imagery from CLPS or Artemis landers.
prop-psi-models.calibration_note: A3: Premise label only: bands match capability-driven T3 physics nodes (no T1 drop was applied or needed).
prop-psi-models.revision_note: B-moon-mars: Skeptic and auditor (fact): the Raptor-plume framing was outdated, because Starship HLS uses mid-body landing thrusters for terminal descent. The why now lists what PSI still decides. Skeptic: 363/364 labeled nil engineering effect (Wagner 1992); pathway P5+P6 -> P1->P6. Advocate (edge): cap-physics-theory moved from hard to soft and cap-applied-math added as hard. Predictive PSI is DSMC plus CFD-DEM calibrated on flight data, which is applied numerics plus data and not new theory. Advocate's S3 2029 -> 2028 rejected: the gate is validation against landing imagery, and S3 cognition equals S2 through 2028, so S2 = S3 = 2029. New soft input from auton-lunar-heavy-cargo-landing; new soft outputs to auton-sinter-process-control (skeptic), auton-robotic-landing-pad and auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops (advocate). Bands unchanged. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): S1 year >2031 -> 2032; band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High, S3 Medium -> High, S4 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 (fails the four-condition rule). | R8 (2026-10-08): band set to Speculative where earliest year is after the checkpoint | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium 2030 once the first heavy and CLPS landings are instrumented; High 2033 in S2 and 2032 in S3, where heavy landings start a year earlier. S1 Medium 2034. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
prop-psi-models.note_2035: Each instrumented heavy landing in 2028-35 is a plume test, so validated predictions are High in S2-S4 by 2035; S1 arrives about 2032 with slower applied math. S4 equals S3 because landing cadence supplies the data.
prop-psi-models.gate_note: Instrumented landing data bind; the coupled gas-ejecta numerics (cognitive) are the runner-up.

prop-ntp-fuel-model.title: Nuclear thermal fuel behavior model
prop-ntp-fuel-model.description: A validated multiphysics model of carbide or CERMET fuel corrosion, cracking and fission-product release in 2,500-3,000 K hydrogen under irradiation and thermal cycling. These are the physics that set NTP temperature, Isp and life.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.status_oct2026: GA-EMS fuel survived six thermal cycles to 2,600 K in flowing hydrogen at MSFC (Jan 2025), without irradiation. Core materials that endure 2,500-3,000 K hydrogen at >3 MPa remain the critical obstacle (general literature). Neutron transport (Monte Carlo) is mature (general). Families 278 (Kohn-Sham ensemble representability fails) and 275 (QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy) are T1 ceilings on DFT-based materials modeling (P3, conditional). They are context only: fuel-performance codes use fitted potentials and empirical correlations, so neither bears on how NTP fuel models are built.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 278 and 275 are T1 ceilings, conditional, context only
prop-ntp-fuel-model.why: Fuel life and temperature set NTP's ~900 s Isp, against ~450 s for LOX/LH2 (general). A predictive model narrows the irradiation test matrix. But 'validated under irradiation' needs test-reactor fluence plus post-irradiation examination (1-3 years combined, general), and no combined irradiation-plus-hot-hydrogen test facility exists (general). Autonomous labs speed up non-nuclear hot-hydrogen tests, not neutron dose, so S3 lands 2030 at Low.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.strongest_case_small: Fuel qualification is inherently empirical and regulators will require data. Families 278 and 275 confirm DFT limits that practitioners already work around.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.signpost: Release of a combined hot-hydrogen plus irradiation dataset (INL/MSFC) with blind model predictions.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: S3 Medium -> Low; skeptic: S3 2029 -> 2030 (irradiation fluence plus post-irradiation examination take 1-3 years that no cognitive multiplier shortens).
