There is no NTP program of record, so the band stays Low by 2035 in every scenario. Fluence and hot-cell exams bind, and robots shorten neither, so S4 equals S3.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.gate_note: Test-reactor fluence and post-irradiation exams (experiment) bind; the lack of an NTP program to fund them (capital) is the runner-up.

prop-stability-design-tool.title: Design out combustion instability before hot fire
prop-stability-design-tool.description: An integrated workflow (predicted flame response, a certified reduced-order stability model and uncertainty quantification) that ranks injector and chamber designs by stability margin before hardware is built, used on a real engine program.
prop-stability-design-tool.status_oct2026: Instability is still found and fixed on the test stand. For the F-1, 'Project Go' ran 2,000 tests on 210 injector designs over two years before bomb tests showed damping within 45 ms (enginehistory.org; NASA History, Jul 12, 2019). Modern programs iterate faster with cheap additive injectors, but the loop remains test-driven.
prop-stability-design-tool.why: If even a third of instability redesign loops are avoided, a new engine saves months to a year and tens of hardware sets (judgment, general). The math (stability certificates) is fast under S2; flame-response validation on rigs is not, and the tool must then be used on a real engine program (the F-1 stability campaign took two years of tests). Chain (S2): prop-certified-stability-rom (2028) + prop-flame-response (2030) -> ranking injector designs on an engine program before hardware (2031 at the earliest). The gate is rig and hot-fire validation of the tool's rankings, not customer qualification.
prop-stability-design-tool.strongest_case_small: For well-funded teams, SpaceX-style rapid iteration with cheap 3D-printed injectors already makes testing cheaper than prediction (600+ Raptors built by Apr 2026). Bomb tests and stability rating stay mandatory, so the tests saved are development tests, not qualification tests.
prop-stability-design-tool.signpost: An engine program reports first-article stability qualification with no injector redesign and credits predictive tools.
prop-stability-design-tool.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor (timing/band, two lenses): S2 2030 -> 2031 and S2 Medium -> Low (needs validated flame response, now S2 2030, then use on a real engine program). S3 2029 -> 2030 (skeptic; same lag after flame response S3 2029). Gate convention (advocate, accepted): the first mover is a self-certifying commercial operator; FAA Part 450 regulates public safety, not engine materials or test counts, so the regulator/certification Medium cap does not apply unless the node needs NASA crew, NSSL or other customer certification. The band here rests on physical clocks, not on that cap. S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2 Medium 2033: flame response passes 30% in 2031 and the tool then needs an engine program's hot-fire campaign (F-1 took two years). S3 Medium 2032 on AI-run stands (1.3-1.5x). Skeptic (instability still found on stands, 2035) and advocate (2032 programs) weighed. Bands unchanged.
prop-stability-design-tool.note_2035: Plateau gets flame response only about 2034, so S1 is 2035 at the earliest and stays Speculative. In the base and Recursive cases, engine programs in 2032-35 give the tool several chances to rank designs before hot fire, so both reach Medium. Rig and hot-fire validation bind, so S4 equals S3.
prop-stability-design-tool.gate_note: Rig and hot-fire validation of rankings binds; an engine program choosing to rank injectors with the tool (adoption) is the runner-up.

prop-ai-engine-design-loop.title: AI-generated engines at scale
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.description: Computational engineering models generate complete additively-manufactured engines (geometry, regenerative cooling, injectors) in weeks. The node counts as achieved when a >=200 kN AI-generated engine completes a full-duration hot fire.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.status_oct2026: LEAP 71's Noyron generated a 5 kN LOX/kerosene aerospike that worked on its first firing (Dec 18, 2024). In Dec 2025 two Noyron-designed 20 kN LOX/CH4 engines (a bell and an aerospike) went from specification to first flame in under three weeks; the bell ran above 93% combustion efficiency over a week-long campaign, while the aerospike reached full chamber pressure (50 bar) but fired only once because of start-transient problems (LEAP 71, Dec 11, 2025). The 200 kN LOX/CH4 XRA-2E5, intended for the upper stage of the Oryx reusable launcher being developed with Aspire Space, was printed as one Inconel 718 part in 289 h (Mar 2026); its hot fire, planned before 2027, was not confirmed as of Oct 7, 2026. The Exploration Company licensed Noyron (Mar 24, 2026). Venus Aerospace credits 'AI-enabled design software' for its RDRE (Mercury Fund, Jul 21, 2026).
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.why: Design labor collapses toward zero, so the loop period is set by print time (~2 weeks for a large part) and test-stand availability. Once cap-design-optimization arrives, AI math adds guarantees such as proven cooling-channel thermal margins, but the loop already exists without it.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.strongest_case_small: Design labor was never the long pole for large engines; reliability growth and qualification are. Noyron-style tools encode engineering rules rather than frontier mathematics, so the openai/math release adds little here.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.signpost: A full-duration XRA-2E5 hot fire, and the first orbital flight on an AI-generated main engine.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (grounding, accepted): pathway relabelled 'P1 (marginal; not AI-math-driven)' since the node itself says Noyron encodes engineering rules. prop-ai-engine-design-loop.note_2035: Generative engine design is standard by 2035 in every scenario. The loop period is set by print time and stand availability; robots speed both at leading firms, but the node is already met, so S4 equals S3.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.gate_note: Print time binds; hot-fire stand availability (experiment) is the runner-up.

prop-turbopump-tool.title: Predictive turbopump cavitation and stability
prop-turbopump-tool.description: Models that predict rotating cavitation, cavitation surge and rotordynamic instability for new inducer and pump designs before water-flow and hot-fire tests.
prop-turbopump-tool.status_oct2026: CFD predictions of cavitation instabilities depend strongly on the chosen cavitation and turbulence models, and 3D linear perturbation theories with dynamic transfer matrices are advancing (Pisa thesis, Jun 2025). On Starship Flight 12 (May 22, 2026) the booster lost an engine on ascent and more during boostback, ending in a hard Gulf landing (SpaceNews via 33FG); on Flight 13 (Jul 24, 2026) only 10 of 13 landing engines relit (Spaceflight Now). No official cause has been given.
prop-turbopump-tool.why: Turbopump instabilities are a leading cause of engine failures (general). Stability analysis of transfer-matrix and rotordynamic models is applied math that S2 makes cheap. The uncertain inputs (cavitation compliance, mass-flow gain) are calibrated on water-flow rigs, which are cheap and fast, so closure guarantees help but are not required. Chain (S2): cap-applied-math (2027) -> transfer-matrix models calibrated on archived inducer data (2027-28) -> blind water-rig confirmation on a new inducer (2029 at the earliest).
prop-turbopump-tool.strongest_case_small: Water-flow rig tests are cheap compared with hot fire, and design rules are mature, so prediction may save little.
prop-turbopump-tool.signpost: A blind prediction of rotating-cavitation onset for a new inducer, confirmed in a rig test.
prop-turbopump-tool.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Edge: prop-closure-theory hard -> soft (advocate + skeptic). Timing (advocate, concrete mechanism accepted): with closure guarantees no longer gating, the remaining gate is blind water-rig confirmation, which the node itself calls cheap; S2 2030 -> 2029, S3 2029 -> 2028. High 2033 in S2 and 2032 in S3 after several cheap blind water-rig confirmations. S1 Medium 2033, a year after its 2032 blind rig test. Bands unchanged.

prop-turbopump-tool.gate_note: Blind water-rig confirmation binds; transfer-matrix and rotordynamic stability analysis (cognitive) is the runner-up.

prop-life-twin.title: Probabilistic engine life prediction for reuse
prop-life-twin.description: Physics-based life models for thermomechanical fatigue, low-cycle fatigue and creep in chambers, turbines and additively-manufactured parts, with uncertainty quantification, updated after each flight from sensors and inspection.
prop-life-twin.status_oct2026: Life estimation is hampered by heat-flux uncertainty, the choice of plasticity model and a lack of specimen characterization (Lisbon thesis 2024; Polito 2025). The methods are Morrow, Norton and Miner, validated on SSME-era data. Families 372 (global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity) and 366 (planar Mumford–Shah crack regularity) are T1 links to inspection inverse problems. Conditional, P5.
prop-life-twin.why: Reuse economics turn on refurbishment intervals. Probabilistic life models with UQ are expert-scarce applied math, the category S2 makes cheap; automated CFD V&V (prop-cfd-auto-vv) improves the heat-flux input but is not required, since thermal loads can come from engine instrumentation. Merlin fleet data are deep, but Raptor 3 (first flight May 2026; full-flow staged combustion with an oxygen-rich preburner, so different failure modes from kerosene gas-generator Merlins) has little, so data still bind for Starship-class engines.
prop-life-twin.strongest_case_small: Operators extend life through fleet-leader experience anyway, so any gain is internal and hard to observe. Heat-flux uncertainty (a closure problem) limits physics-based accuracy.
prop-life-twin.signpost: An operator or NASA discloses model-based (not fleet-leader-only) engine life limits, or NASA accepts probabilistic life analysis for crewed reuse.
prop-life-twin.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (edge + claim, accepted): prop-cfd-auto-vv hard -> soft (life models are calibrated on instrumented engines, inspection and fleet data; CFD V&V improves the heat-flux input but is not required). The 'data binds less' sentence contradicted the node's own data gate: the reflown fleet is kerosene gas-generator Merlins, whose wear does not transfer to Raptor 3. Years unchanged (cap-applied-math 2027 still precedes 2028). | E-engines-materials (2026-10-07): band_2035 S1 Medium -> High. Years kept. S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2 Medium 2029, High 2030 as Raptor 3 fleet data accumulate. S1 High 2034. Bands unchanged.
prop-life-twin.note_2035: Probabilistic life models are standard for reusable engines in every scenario by 2035, fed by hundreds of flights a year. Flights supply the data, so S4 equals S3.
prop-life-twin.gate_note: Raptor 3 fleet data bind; probabilistic life modelling with UQ (cognitive) is the runner-up.

prop-start-transient.title: Predictive engine start and relight transients
prop-start-transient.description: Validated system-level models of line chilldown, ignition, turbopump spin-up and combustion onset for in-flight relights after a coast, used to design start sequences with quantified margin.
prop-start-transient.status_oct2026: A live 2026 problem: on Flight 13 (Jul 24, 2026) only 10 of 13 booster engines relit for landing, and about five were running at splashdown (Spaceflight Now). Start transients are stiff differential-algebraic systems with uncertain two-phase chilldown physics (general).
prop-start-transient.why: Relight reliability gates booster catch, ship landing and, most critically, HLS lunar descent after days to weeks in orbit. Relight failures come mainly from propellant conditioning and gas ingestion, two-phase line chilldown, igniter performance and turbopump spin-up; chemistry-integration error is negligible next to rate-constant and two-phase uncertainty, so certified stiff solvers (frontier-stiff-certified) help but do not gate it, while line chilldown (prop-cfm-models) does. Every flight supplies validation data for short coasts; the long-coast regime that matters for HLS gets data only with the depot campaigns, which keeps S2 at Medium.
prop-start-transient.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will probably fix relight empirically within a few flights, and models will follow the data rather than lead it.
prop-start-transient.signpost: Several consecutive Starship flights with full booster and ship relight success, especially after long coasts.
prop-start-transient.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (band): S1 Medium -> Low (S1 earliest year is 2031, the window edge). Skeptic (edge, accepted): frontier-stiff-certified hard -> soft; chemistry-integration error is negligible next to rate-constant and two-phase uncertainty (the stiff node admits it); prop-cfm-models stays hard. Soft edge from physclock-ai-run-test-stands (advocate). Advocate's S2 Medium -> High rejected: booster relights after minutes of coast are plentiful, but the HLS case (days to weeks in orbit) has little data before the 2029 campaigns, and prop-cfm-models is now S2 2029. | B-fix (integrator, 2026-10-07): Flight 13 date harmonized to Jul 24, 2026 (launch date per 33FG news 596 / Wikipedia flight list; trunk and verif already used Jul 24). | E-engines-materials (2026-10-07): band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High. Years kept. S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Follows prop-cfm-models: S2 Medium 2030, High 2032 once lunar and depot campaigns supply long-coast relights; S3 High 2031; S1 Medium 2032 on the same flights with slower models. Bands unchanged.
prop-start-transient.note_2035: Long-coast relight data arrive with depot, lunar and Mars-window campaigns in 2028-33, so by 2035 the base case is High and Plateau Medium. Flight data bind, so S4 equals S3.
prop-start-transient.gate_note: Relight testing binds; long-coast flight data that arrive only with depot campaigns (data) are the runner-up.

prop-verified-engine-software.title: Formally verified engine control software
prop-verified-engine-software.description: Machine-checked proofs that engine-controller and health-management logic (start sequencing, redlines, abort logic, numerical filters) meets its specification, produced by AI agents at low cost and accepted as verification evidence in a NASA human-rating or crewed-program review.
prop-verified-engine-software.status_oct2026: Certification standards already give credit for formal methods (DO-178C/DO-333), but AI agents and Lean are not qualified tools. The agentic formalization capability exists: openai/math formalized the main results of 162 papers in weeks. Redline logic matters: newsletter commentary named a sensor trip as one hypothesis for the 2026 Raptor 3 boostback shutdowns (unverified; no primary source).
prop-verified-engine-software.why: Engine controllers are safety-critical, and false or missed shutdowns from redline logic recur as a failure mode (general). Launch engines are not type-certified, and Part 450 licenses public safety, not engines, so the acceptors are crewed programs (RS-25 on SLS, Raptor on HLS, Merlin on crewed Falcon 9, BE-7 on Blue Moon): a handful of programs whose software baselines change slowly. The node needs general credit (infra-tool-qualification, plan acceptance S2 2030) plus a human-rating review that accepts the evidence, so by the A4 conjunctive rule used for verif-hls-autonomy-certification it sits a year later and a band lower: S2 2031 Low, S3 2030 Low, S1 Speculative. The uncertified counterpart, launch operators re-proving engine and abort logic on every flight, is verif-launch-fsw-per-flight.
prop-verified-engine-software.strongest_case_small: Most engine failures are physical rather than software. Commercial launch licensing does not require formal verification, and writing correct specifications remains the bottleneck.
prop-verified-engine-software.signpost: The first NASA crewed-program review that accepts AI-generated formal proofs as verification evidence for propulsion controller software.
prop-verified-engine-software.revision_note: B-verified-autonomy: Skeptic + auditor: S2 2030 -> 2031, S3 2029 -> 2030 and S2 band Medium -> Low (zero lag after the general-credit premise; only crewed programs can accept the evidence). Auditor: S1 Low -> Speculative and S3 Medium -> Low under the A4 rule (a dependent of a Medium regulatory node with a further uncertain human-rating step belongs below Medium); skeptic's S3 Medium rejected for consistency with verif-hls-autonomy-certification. Skeptic: description 'accepted in certification' -> crewed-program review; Raptor sensor-trip claim labeled as unverified commentary. Advocate's re-pointing to a separate checker-route node rejected with that node; its uncertified counterpart is added as verif-launch-fsw-per-flight. | E-verified-autonomy (2035 horizon, S4): S1 >2031 -> 2033 (A4 conjunctive rule: a year after infra-tool-qualification S1 2032); band_2035 S1 Speculative -> Low, S2-S4 Low -> Medium (regulatory cap). S4 = S3 (no four-condition credit). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium S2 2034, S3-S4 2033: general credit is Medium in 2031 (S2) and 2030 (S3), then a crewed engine baseline must take a block update and pass a human-rating review, about three years. Capped at Medium (no named route for AI proofs in human rating). Skeptic (post-Starliner caution, few programs) vs advocate (SpaceX changes Raptor and Merlin software often and owns an AI lab): the advocate's route is the uncertified verif-launch-fsw-per-flight, so 2034 stands.
prop-verified-engine-software.note_2035: S1 follows S1 regulator credit (2032) by a year, so 2033. By 2035 S2-S4 reach Medium, capped there because a human-rating review must accept the evidence and no named route for AI proofs is in motion; S4 equals S3.
prop-verified-engine-software.gate_note: A human-rating review accepting the evidence binds; crewed programs choosing a block update of slowly changing engine software (adoption) is the runner-up.

prop-ship-transfer-demo.title: Ship-to-ship cryogenic transfer demonstrated
prop-ship-transfer-demo.description: Two Starships dock in low Earth orbit and transfer tens to 100+ tonnes of LOX and liquid methane, with measured boil-off, chilldown loss and transfer efficiency.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.status_oct2026: Starship reached orbit for the first time on Flight 14 (Sep 28, 2026) and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites (Mach33, Sep 30, 2026). Ship-to-ship transfer has not flown and was not yet scheduled as of Sep 2026 (Wikipedia); Flight 15 (NET Oct 19, 2026) targets the first ship catch and begins testing docking and hatch mechanisms for the transfer demonstration (Basenor). Internal tank-to-tank transfer was done on Mar 14, 2024. NASA OIG (Mar 2026) calls cryogenic transfer 'one of the most significant technical challenges'.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
prop-ship-transfer-demo.why: Not an AI-math implication: an exogenous physical anchor (flight tests and vehicle readiness), so the P7 Speculative default does not apply. Flights and vehicle readiness set the timing, and AI mathematics moves this node by roughly zero. It is on the tree because its data unlock prop-cfm-models and, downstream, the refueling economy. High in every scenario (judgment): NASA's administrator expects the demonstration in early 2027 and every HLS landing needs it, so even a multi-year slip lands inside the window.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.strongest_case_small: Not applicable: this node exists to show the physical clock. The AI-math effect on its date is nil.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.signpost: Announcement and flight of the propellant-transfer mission, with the transferred mass disclosed.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Auditor (fact, contradicted; verified): Flight 15 is a single-vehicle flight and cannot perform ship-to-ship transfer; the transfer demo was not yet scheduled as of Sep 2026 (Wikipedia, updated Oct 4, 2026), and Flight 15 (NET Oct 19, 2026) targets the first ship catch and begins docking and hatch tests (Basenor). prop-rde-flight-demo.title: Detonation engine flies in space
prop-rde-flight-demo.description: A rotating detonation rocket engine of about 1,000 lbf or more operates as primary propulsion in a space or lander flight demonstration, beyond suborbital hops.
prop-rde-flight-demo.status_oct2026: Venus Aerospace flew a 2,000 lbf RDRE to 4,400 ft (May 2025). Juno Propulsion won a NASA TechLeap prize for a NASA-funded flight test later in 2026 (small thruster). NASA's InRoDES is a 10,000 lbf-class pump-fed LOX/LCH4 engine whose thrust chamber fired for just over 340 s in Dec 2025 (NASA); a vacuum test comes next, then transfer to industry.
prop-rde-flight-demo.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
prop-rde-flight-demo.why: Not an AI-math implication: an exogenous physical anchor (vacuum testing, funding and a flight slot), so the P7 Speculative default does not apply; cheaper analysis is a marginal soft input. Hardware is limited by testing and funding. Cheaper analysis under S2 (mode theory, thermal design) trims iterations but cannot shorten vacuum testing, flight integration or the wait for a funded flight slot. S3 equals S2 until 2028, and autonomous test stands (S3 2028) cannot pull a funded flight into the same year, so all three scenarios share 2029. Chain: InRoDES vacuum test and industry transfer, or a Venus- or Juno-class program (2026-28) -> funded >=1,000 lbf space or lander demonstration (2029 at the earliest). Medium in every scenario (judgment): several programs (NASA InRoDES, Venus, Juno) could fly a demonstration of 1,000 lbf or more by 2031, but it depends on a customer and money (strongest case).
prop-rde-flight-demo.strongest_case_small: A small in-space RDRE firing (Juno) may come in 2026-27 regardless of AI math. The >=1,000 lbf demo depends on a customer and money, not mathematics.
prop-rde-flight-demo.signpost: A Juno Propulsion in-space RDRE firing, NASA InRoDES vacuum-test results, or a lander provider baselining an RDRE.
prop-rde-flight-demo.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (timing, accepted): S3 2028 -> 2029; S3 equals S2 until 2028, and autonomous test stands (S3 2028) cannot pull a funded flight into the same year. prop-ntp-ground-test.title: Nuclear thermal engine ground hot fire
prop-ntp-ground-test.description: A fission-heated hydrogen engine (5-12.5 klbf subscale) fired on the ground with full exhaust capture: the first U.S. NTP reactor test since NERVA (1972).
prop-ntp-ground-test.status_oct2026: DRACO was cancelled in the FY2026 budget request (May 2025) because falling launch costs eroded its ROI (DARPA's McHenry, Breaking Defense, Jun 27, 2025). Congress directed >=$110M for NTP in FY2026, and Administrator Isaacman committed to execute it (Sen. Britt, Apr 29, 2026). The White House Space Nuclear Initiative (Apr 14, 2026) prioritizes NEP (SR-1 Freedom, 20 kWe, Mars launch at end-2028) and lunar surface power, with 'common NEP/NTP components'. A high-pressure exhaust capture system for 5-12.5 klbf tests exists as a design (NASA, 2023).
prop-ntp-ground-test.why: As of Oct 2026 there is no funded NTP engine program of record. A reactor ground test needs a program start, a fueled reactor, an exhaust-capture facility and nuclear safety approval, which on historical precedent takes 5+ years from start (general). AI compresses design and safety-analysis documentation (S2/S3) but not facility construction, fuel fabrication or approvals. Chain: no program of record -> earliest program start FY2027-28 -> fueled reactor and a new exhaust-capture facility (a design only today), likely with an EIS (2-4 years) -> 2032 at the earliest even at S3's 0.8-0.9x. Appropriations compress 1.0x, so the node is Speculative by 2031 in every scenario.
prop-ntp-ground-test.strongest_case_small: Policy and money decide this node, and the policy pivot to NEP was driven by cost and launch prices, not mathematics.
prop-ntp-ground-test.signpost: FY2027 or FY2028 budgets fund an NTP ground-test facility and reactor, or DOE and NASA announce an NTP program of record.
prop-ntp-ground-test.revision_note: B-plasma-nuclear resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (mechanism checked against the physclock gate table): S3 2031 -> >2031; S2 and S3 Low -> Speculative. No program of record; a 5+ year precedent at 0.8-0.9x plus an EIS of 2-4 years gives 2032 at the earliest; appropriations compress 1.0x. | E-plasma-nuclear (2026-10-07): 2035/S4 extension. >2031 -> S1 2034, S2 2033, S3/S4 2032 (program start FY2027-28 + 5+ years, at 0.8-0.9x in S3 and 0.9x in S2). band_2035 S2/S3/S4 Speculative -> Low; S1 stays Speculative (one year of slack). | Resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic's S3/S4 2032 -> 2033 rejected: EIS drafting is cognitive work (the S4 analysis rates NEPA work 1.5-2x in S3), the sequential floor (start 2027, EIS about 2 years, construction about 2 years, test) still reaches 2032, and Congress put at least $110M into NTP for FY2026. Note rewritten with the construction-after-decision sequence. Soft edge from robo-construction-trades dropped: the facility is built 2029-31, before construction-trade robots are useful, and the robot node is the same S4 year as this node. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Unchanged: Low from 2033 in S2-S4 and after 2035 in S1; no program of record.
prop-ntp-ground-test.note_2035: Resolved to 2032 in S3, 2033 in S2 and 2034 in S1. The chain is a program start, an EIS of 2-4 years, 2-4 years to build an exhaust-capture facility after the record of decision, then a fueled reactor test. Comment periods and construction do not compress; AI shortens EIS drafting and design documents, which gives S3 its one-year lead at the floor. Low by 2035 at best because there is no program of record. Policy binds, so S4 equals S3.
prop-ntp-ground-test.gate_note: A program of record (capital) binds; the environmental impact statement and nuclear approval (regulatory) are the runner-up.

prop-hls-refuel-campaign.title: Full lunar-lander refueling campaign
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.description: Roughly 10-20 tanker flights fill a depot in LEO, which transfers a full load to Starship HLS for a lunar landing (uncrewed demo or crewed).
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.status_oct2026: NASA OIG (Mar 2026): more than 10 tankers are needed, the landing is planned for 2028, and NASA tracks a 'top risk' that cryogenic technologies won't be mature. ASAP (Sep 2025) warned HLS could be 'years late'. Estimates run from SpaceX's '10-ish' to NASA's 'high teens'. NASA plans an interim Artemis test flight in LEO in 2027 before landing attempts (Spaceflight Now, Jul 2026).
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.why: Not an AI-math implication: an exogenous physical anchor (launch cadence, vehicle reliability, docking and pad turnaround), so the P7 Speculative default does not apply; AI models trim planning margin and shorten anomaly closure only. Launch cadence binds. At one tanker every ~6 days a campaign takes about 2 months, and every slip in cadence multiplies boil-off losses (tables). Validated boil-off and transfer models (prop-cfm-models) trim ~0-1 tanker of planning margin per mission at a 6-day cadence, more only at slow cadence and high boil-off, a regime operators avoid by flying faster. Reliable relights (prop-start-transient) protect the landing rather than the tanker count. Schedule gain: weeks to months. Chain (S2): prop-ship-transfer-demo (2027) -> 10-20-tanker depot fill on the launch clock -> transfer to HLS (2029 at the earliest). S1 and S2 share the date and band because launch cadence runs on its own curve (physclock: 0-0.5 year earlier in S2); S3's broader acceleration of hardware iteration and mishap closure (launch 0.5-1 year earlier) lifts it to 2028 and High. Medium in S1 and S2 (judgment): NASA's OIG tracks cryogenic-transfer maturity as a top risk and ASAP warned HLS could be years late, but the campaign has two years of slack before 2031.
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.strongest_case_small: AI mathematics is not on the critical path. Vehicle reliability, launch cadence, docking and pad turnaround are.
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.signpost: The first depot-filling campaign with >=5 tankers flown, and NASA confirming a landing date after the 2027 LEO test.
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor (claim, two lenses): '~1-4 tankers saved' conflated the physical boil-off loss with a model's value; corrected to ~0-1 tanker of planning margin (depot table reproduced; margin re-simulated). Soft edges added (advocate): prop-cfm-models, prop-start-transient, prop-mass-gauging, physclock-ai-mishap-analysis, physclock-heavy-cadence-100, so the tree shows what the text already credits. Years kept. S4 = S3. | R9-launch (2026-10-27): gate launch -> launch-internal (SpaceX's own manifest; Mach33 Launch Keystone v1.3 books Starlink, SpaceX's orbital compute, Moon and Mars cargo and NASA's lunar tanker flights in the internal account). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S3/S4 Medium 2028 -> 2029: ship-to-ship transfer has not flown, and a 10-20-tanker campaign a year later is not 30% likely by end-2028. prop-rde-operational.title: Detonation engines in operational service
prop-rde-operational.description: RDREs used as production propulsion on a commercial lander, upper stage or in-space vehicle, with predictable, qualified behavior.
prop-rde-operational.status_oct2026: There is no operational RDRE anywhere; only demonstrations exist (see prop-rde-flight-demo).
prop-rde-operational.why: Operational use requires a qualified engine whose mode behavior is predictable across throttle and mixture ranges. Mode theory buys that predictability faster, but empirical envelope mapping can also supply it, so it accelerates rather than gates. Qualifying a new combustion mode for operational use has historically taken several years after the first flight demo (general), and a customer must commit. Chain (S2): prop-rde-flight-demo (2029, physical) [+ prop-rde-mode-theory 2029, soft] -> envelope qualification -> production contract (2031 at the earliest; P1->P6->P7). P7 defaults to Speculative.
prop-rde-operational.strongest_case_small: Even with perfect theory, an Isp gain that is still unproven and a shorter chamber may not justify the qualification cost for most missions. Defense missiles and hypersonics, not space, may be the first operational users.
prop-rde-operational.signpost: A lander or upper-stage provider contracting an RDRE as baseline propulsion.
prop-rde-operational.revision_note: B-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (band/timing/edge, accepted): S2 Low -> Speculative (P7 default; needs flight demo, then several years of envelope qualification, then a customer); S3 2030 -> 2031 (flight demo now S3 2029); prop-rde-mode-theory hard -> soft (empirical envelope mapping can also deliver predictability). Claim fix: the ~10% Isp gain is unproven (NTRS 20240000933). Chain written out (grounding rule). | E-engines-materials (2026-10-07): S1 >2031 -> 2033. band_2035 S1 Speculative -> Low, S2 Speculative -> Low, S3 Low -> Medium. S4 = S3. | E-engines-materials resolver (2026-10-07): band_2035 S3/S4 Medium -> Low (skeptic, accepted): the node cannot be as likely as its hard prerequisite prop-rde-flight-demo (Medium by 2035) when it needs years of qualification and a customer after it, and those gates are not cognitive. Advocate's flight-demo High rejected (see that node). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Seed years kept: Low 2033 in S1/S2 and 2031 in S3/S4; it cannot pass its Medium prerequisite. Bands unchanged.
prop-rde-operational.note_2035: Qualification and a customer take several years after the 2029 demonstrations, which are themselves only Medium by 2035, so every scenario is Low; Plateau lands about 2033 at the earliest. Qualification and customers bind, so S4 equals S3.
prop-rde-operational.gate_note: Envelope qualification binds; a customer committing to a production engine (capital) is the runner-up.

prop-reuse-extended.title: Model-based engine reuse life
prop-reuse-extended.description: Reusable engines whose overhaul and inspection intervals are set by validated probabilistic life models, extending the flights between overhauls (for example 2x) without added risk.
prop-reuse-extended.status_oct2026: Reuse life today is extended mainly by fleet-leader experience (general). Raptor 3 had accumulated >40,000 s of runtime by Apr 2026 (newspaceeconomy).
prop-reuse-extended.why: Cheaper refurbishment and faster turnaround feed directly into launch cost. Life models pull fleet-leader life extension forward by roughly 6-12 months (physclock reuse-learning row, 0.8-0.9x in S2); a 2x interval is an illustration that still has to be earned in flight cycles, because each life data point costs a flight. prop-engine-dev-compression.title: Engine development time and cost cut
prop-engine-dev-compression.description: New liquid engines reach qualification with materially fewer hot-fire tests and redesign loops (for example >=30% fewer than the same organization's previous engine program of similar thrust class), with the saving attributed to predictive tools.
prop-engine-dev-compression.status_oct2026: Development remains test-driven. SpaceX has built 600+ Raptors through large-scale test-fail-fix iteration (newspaceeconomy, Apr 2026).
prop-engine-dev-compression.why: Design and analysis compress (P1), but reliability demonstration is statistical. Showing 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence with zero failures takes ~230 trials (n = ln 0.1 / ln 0.99) unless customers accept model-based Bayesian credit. For a high-cadence operator, flight starts accumulate fast (a Starship flight logs roughly 65-70 engine starts, general), but starts on one vehicle and build lot are correlated and each failure found resets the clock, so what paces a new engine is finding and fixing failure modes. Models cut redesign loops, not demonstration tests. Combustion instability is the historical driver of those loops, so the stability tool is the hard gate; generative design (prop-ai-engine-design-loop), turbopump prediction and information-optimal test campaigns help but are not individually necessary. New engines take 6-13 years and major versions ~3 years, compressing only 0.8-0.9x (S2) and 0.7-0.8x (S3), so few programs started with S2 or S3 tools qualify by 2031. Chain (S2): cap-applied-math (2027) -> prop-cfd-auto-vv + prop-certified-stability-rom (2028) -> prop-flame-response (2030) -> prop-stability-design-tool (2031) -> a major version designed with the tool qualifies about two years later, since most development tests come before qualification (2033). Chain (S3): stability tool (2031), built on precursor models a program can adopt as they land in 2028-30 -> a program near qualification cuts its last test campaign and attributes fewer tests (2031 at the earliest, Low).
prop-engine-dev-compression.strongest_case_small: The cheapest route to reliability is already high-rate testing of cheap hardware, so prediction competes with a very fast empirical loop.
prop-engine-dev-compression.signpost: A program publicly attributing a reduced hot-fire count to predictive tools, or a customer (NASA, USSF) accepting model-based reliability credit.

prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.title: Routine orbital refueling economy
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.description: Depots and tankers operate routinely, with dozens of cryogenic transfers per year supporting lunar landers, Mars ships and high-energy missions, and boil-off and transfer losses are predicted rather than padded.
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.status_oct2026: Not yet demonstrated. Eta Space targets a commercial LOX depot (Cryo-Dock) by 2030 (satnews, May 2026).
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.why: The economics depend on tankers per delivered tonne. Boil-off costs ~1-5 extra tankers per HLS-class campaign (illustrative table). Validated boil-off and transfer models recover only the planning margin on top of that, ~0-1 tanker at <=6-day cadence; gauging error at 1% of a 1,200 t load is ~12 t, ~0.1 tanker. Together that is a few percent of campaign launches. The rest comes down to cadence and vehicle reuse. Chain (S2): prop-ship-transfer-demo (2027) -> prop-cfm-models (2029) + prop-hls-refuel-campaign (2029) + physclock-heavy-cadence-100 (2030, after B-trunk) -> more than 20 transfers in a year (2030 at the earliest, from two lunar-lander campaigns of more than 10 tankers each; P1->P6->P7). Chain (S3): the same prerequisites in 2028-29 (heavy cadence 2029) -> lunar campaigns under SpaceX's Moon-first plan (2029). The 2031 band stays Medium: the earliest years are optimistic and AI mathematics is not on the critical path. Against the P7 default (Speculative): the physical outcome rides on exogenous prerequisites (heavy cadence, the refuel campaign), and the AI-math share is a model whose output is a planning number, not a hardware change, so Medium is the ceiling set by prop-hls-refuel-campaign (Medium in S2). S1 is Low by 2031. By 2035 every hard prerequisite is High in every scenario and AI mathematics is off the critical path, so Plateau is High as well.

science-gr-foundations.title: Black-hole foundations settled and checked
science-gr-foundations.description: Independent experts confirm the 2026 wave of mathematical general relativity: nonlinear stability of Kerr black holes across the full subextremal range (human preprints, Jun and Sep 2026), the AI-claimed strong cosmic censorship near Kerr (family 264) and the AI-claimed spacetime Penrose inequalities (family 260). Together they make 'perturbed black holes settle down to Kerr, and their mass bounds their horizon area' a theorem rather than an assumption.
science-gr-foundations.status_oct2026: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range claimed by Hintz (arXiv 2606.28253, Jun 2026) and Szeftel (arXiv 2609.40068, Sep 2026), human work, not yet refereed. Family 264 (strong cosmic censorship near two-ended Kerr data): T1, manuscript only. Family 260 (spacetime Penrose inequalities): T1 for the main inequalities; only a supporting construction (Cha-Khuri-Sakovich end replacement, Comparator target CKSBondiPenrose) has an agent-written Lean proof, unchecked, and the repo's lean/docs/260.md states the paper's general inequality 'remains unformalized'. Neither family appears in formalization.yaml as a formalized main result.
science-gr-foundations.premise_tier: T1 (families 260 main results and 264); human Kerr-stability preprints unrefereed
science-gr-foundations.why: Ringdown spectroscopy (LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA now, LISA after 2035) and EHT/BHEX photon-ring tests all assume a perturbed black hole relaxes to Kerr. Kerr stability proves it from outside; strong cosmic censorship near Kerr (264) says the interior generically cannot be continued past the Cauchy horizon with square-integrable connection; Penrose inequalities (260) bound mass below by horizon area for moving, charged and rotating data. 'Settled and checked' means independent experts confirm hundreds of pages of new human proof (Hintz, 339 pp, Jun 2026, with companion papers; Szeftel, Sep 2026, relying on companion papers) plus the two AI-claimed families; the 801-page small-angular-momentum predecessor (Klainerman-Szeftel, Apr 2021) still lists no journal reference on arXiv. Review bandwidth, an adoption gate, binds: a few dozen people can referee these, and 722 manuscripts arrived at once (tr-position-5). AI-assisted refereeing in S2/S3 shortens this but does not make confirmation of late-2026 papers credible in 2027. Formal checking is further off because Lean lacks Lorentzian geometry. On review bandwidth alone S1 would be Medium and S2/S3 High; conditional: the node needs two unformalized T1 premises (260, 264) jointly plus unrefereed preprints, so bands drop two steps (fw-horizon-scorecard). Bands are judgments. Science only: the soft link to LISA science is confidence, not a model change (tl-position-2).
science-gr-foundations.strongest_case_small: No working astrophysicist doubted the Kerr final state. Waveform models, ringdown tests and EHT analyses already assume it, so nothing in any instrument or mission changes; this removes a theoretical doubt only (tl-position-2).
science-gr-foundations.signpost: A named GR expert publicly endorses or finds a gap in families 260 or 264 by end-2027; Hintz or Szeftel accepted by a journal; first Lean library for Lorentzian causal structure.

science-energy-condition-nogo.title: Warp drives: sharp no-go theorems
science-energy-condition-nogo.description: Theorems stating, for every metric in a broad class, how much negative energy a 'warp' or 'propellantless' spacetime needs, or how much positive mass a positive-energy version must carry. Superluminal bubbles must violate the null energy condition. The only published positive-energy subluminal shell (Fuchs et al. 2024) carries 2.365 Jupiter masses within a 10-20 m shell for a 0.02c internal shift; no theorem yet fixes the minimum mass of such shells. Sharp constants for the negative-energy cases are now being computed.
science-energy-condition-nogo.status_oct2026: Human literature, mostly T5: generic warp drives violate the null energy condition (Santiago-Schuster-Visser, arXiv 2105.03079, May 2021), which answered the 2020-21 positive-energy claims of Lentz, Bobrick-Martire and Fell-Heisenberg within months; a direct computation showing negative Eulerian energy density and errors in Lentz's construction followed in Nov 2025 (arXiv 2511.18251). A subluminal warp satisfies all energy conditions only by adding a matter shell with positive ADM mass (Fuchs et al., arXiv 2405.02709, 2024: 4.49e27 kg, about 2.4 Jupiter masses, inner radius 10 m). New no-go theorems and classification (arXiv 2602.16495, Feb 2026); exact minimum Eulerian negative energy for Natario drives, E_min ~ v^2 R^4/(4 Delta^3) (arXiv 2609.36211, Sep 28 2026, unrefereed). The spacetime positive mass theorem (zero ADM mass with dominant energy forces flat spacetime) is established. Family 260 (T1) extends Penrose mass-area bounds to data with arbitrary momentum, a marginal addition.
science-energy-condition-nogo.premise_tier: T5 for the null-energy and positive-mass results; Natario sharp constant unrefereed (Sep 2026); T1 for the family 260 extension (not load-bearing)
science-energy-condition-nogo.why: Ceilings act within months (fc-position-1). (1) By the Natario result (an unrefereed human preprint, Sep 28 2026), halving the bubble wall thickness multiplies the negative energy needed 8x and doubling the bubble radius multiplies it 16x; for R/Delta = 100 the sharp bound is 2,500x the older v^2R^2/Delta estimate. (2) Penrose-type mass bounds (family 260 for moving data, conditional on T1) apply only to data containing trapped surfaces, that is, black holes, which warp shells avoid: the Fuchs et al. shell has a Schwarzschild radius of about 6.7 m, inside its 10 m inner radius, so it has no trapped surface and these bounds do not bind any published design. (3) Any 'zero-mass' warp metric that is not flat must violate the dominant energy condition (positive mass rigidity). An exponentially improving model can extend these to every published warp class with sharp constants, and could prove a minimum mass for positive-energy shells, which is cognitive work only. Outside teams must pose the warp-class questions, so the node follows public access (cap-research-math-public).
science-energy-condition-nogo.strongest_case_small: The answer was already 'no' before AI: the null-energy result dates from 2021 and positive mass from 1979-81. Family 260 applies only to energy-respecting data with trapped surfaces, which typical subluminal warp shells lack, so the catalog adds almost nothing to propulsion. Nothing that could fly is removed.
science-energy-condition-nogo.signpost: An AI-produced general theorem covering all published warp classes (Alcubierre, Natario, Lentz, Bobrick-Martire, Fell-Heisenberg, Fuchs et al.) with interval-certified or formal checks; or a credible counterexample class that survives audit.

science-qei-curved.title: Hard limits on negative energy from quantum fields
science-qei-curved.description: Quantum energy inequalities cap how much negative energy a quantum field can hold and for how long. They are proven for free fields on arbitrary globally hyperbolic spacetimes (Fewster 2000) and for one interacting two-dimensional model (the massive Ising model, 2013); interacting four-dimensional theories remain open. A QEI, or a proven absence of one, for an interacting 4D theory (at least perturbatively) would close the remaining 'quantum loophole' that warp and wormhole proposals point to.
science-qei-curved.status_oct2026: Worldline QEIs for free scalar fields on arbitrary globally hyperbolic spacetimes with Hadamard states (Fewster, arXiv gr-qc/9910060, 2000); the first QEI for an interacting theory with nontrivial S-matrix, the massive Ising model in two dimensions (Bostelmann-Cadamuro-Fewster, arXiv 1304.7682, 2013); quantum inequalities applied to Alcubierre walls in 1997 give walls a few hundred Planck lengths thick and an unattainable total energy (Pfenning-Ford, arXiv gr-qc/9702026, using flat-space inequalities on short sampling times). Averaged null energy condition proven for flat-space QFT (2016-17, general). Open: interacting 4D theories. Not in the catalog.
science-qei-curved.why: Exotic-propulsion proposals concede classical matter cannot supply negative energy and point to quantum effects. For free fields the quantum loophole for warp walls was already closed in 1997 (Pfenning-Ford), and curved-spacetime inequalities followed in 2000; what remains is interacting 4D theory, which would complete the ceiling started by the classical theorems. Research-grade mathematical physics is routine by 2028-29 in S2, but the target may not even be rigorously statable because interacting 4D QFTs are not constructed, so S2 is Low and only S3 Medium; S1 Speculative. Bands are judgments.
science-qei-curved.strongest_case_small: Interacting four-dimensional quantum field theories are not rigorously constructed, so the fully general theorem may not even be statable; and the classical no-go results already exclude every macroscopic proposal at absurd energy scales.
science-qei-curved.signpost: A QEI, or a proven absence of one, for an interacting four-dimensional quantum field theory (at least perturbatively), with AI credited.
science-qei-curved.revision_note: B-science resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (facts checked by resolver): free-field QEIs on arbitrary globally hyperbolic spacetimes (Fewster, gr-qc/9910060, 2000) and an interacting 2D QEI (massive Ising, arXiv 1304.7682, 2013) already exist, and Pfenning-Ford (gr-qc/9702026, 1997) applied QIs to Alcubierre walls, so description, status and signpost now target interacting 4D theories; S2 Medium->Low (target may not be statable). science-beyond-gr-wellposed.title: Beyond-Einstein gravity made simulable
science-beyond-gr-wellposed.description: Proving which modified-gravity theories have a well-posed initial-value problem, so black-hole mergers can be simulated and turned into templates, or proving they do not. Without it, gravitational-wave tests of general relativity rely on parametrized, theory-agnostic deviations.
science-beyond-gr-wellposed.status_oct2026: Well-posedness shown for Horndeski and Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet at weak coupling in modified harmonic gauge (Kovacs-Reall 2020, general); puncture-gauge formulation for four-derivative scalar-tensor theories (Phys. Rev. D, Oct 2023); first fully nonlinear Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet scattering simulations (arXiv 2605.04224, May 2026). Dynamical Chern-Simons and strong coupling open, usually handled by order-reduction schemes without proofs. No catalog family.
science-beyond-gr-wellposed.why: A well-posedness proof lets numerical-relativity groups produce merger waveforms in a specific alternative theory, so LISA (2035+) and ground detectors can test that theory directly. A negative result is just as useful (tl-position-2): it marks theories that can only be treated as effective field theories, telling analysts which tests are meaningful. Pure PDE analysis, exactly the S2 2027-28 capability, but strong-coupling results may be partial (loss of hyperbolicity is regime-dependent), so S2 is Medium and only S3 High. S3 equals S2 through 2027, so 2028. It accelerates LISA's theory-specific tests rather than gating LISA science.
science-beyond-gr-wellposed.strongest_case_small: Most strong-field tests already use parametrized deviations, general relativity has passed every test so far, and LISA does not fly until 2035, so the payoff is mostly bounds on theories rather than a discovery.

science-second-order-self-force.title: LISA's hardest waveforms computed for spinning black holes
science-second-order-self-force.description: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (a stellar-mass black hole spiraling ~1e5 orbits into a massive one) can only be decoded if the phase is modeled to better than about a radian over the whole signal. That requires second-order gravitational self-force for generic (eccentric, inclined) orbits around spinning Kerr black holes.
science-second-order-self-force.status_oct2026: Second-order calculations exist only for quasicircular orbits around non-spinning (Schwarzschild) black holes (arXiv 2112.12265; effective-source paper arXiv 2508.00087, 2025); a June 2026 paper states 'these calculations have only been attempted for the simplest case of circular orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime' and demonstrates a numerical-relativity route in Kerr for a scalar charge (arXiv 2606.04998); Lorenz-gauge elliptic methods in progress (arXiv 2608.07934, Aug 2026). Adiabatic-order Kerr waveforms for equatorial orbits exist in the FastEMRIWaveforms framework (Phys. Rev. D, Apr 2025); interpolation errors in such fast models are themselves a bias source (PRD, Mar 2026). The second-order formalism (puncture field, two-timescale field equations) was extended to eccentric Schwarzschild orbits (Wei, Zhu, Zhang, Mei, PRD 112, 064048, 2025; arXiv 2504.09640); waveforms still exist only for quasicircular Schwarzschild.
science-second-order-self-force.why: The phase expands as phi = phi_0/epsilon + phi_1 + O(epsilon) with mass ratio epsilon ~1e-5 to 1e-6; adiabatic waveforms carry only phi_0, and the O(1) post-adiabatic term phi_1 needs second-order self-force (general). Part of what remains is research, not labor: metric reconstruction and gauge choice at second order in Kerr are open (the separable Teukolsky machinery does not carry over cleanly, which is why groups are trying numerical-relativity and Lorenz-gauge elliptic routes), and first-order adiabatic Kerr inputs exist only for equatorial orbits. The rest is expert labor (renormalized sources, mode coupling, eccentric and inclined orbits) by a few dozen specialists, the class where on-demand AI applied math (P1) acts first, followed by a compute campaign: second-order sources over a 4-D grid (spin, p, e, inclination) with mode coupling that grows quadratically in the number of modes, plus agreement between independent codes. Chain (S2): cap-applied-math 2027 -> Kerr second-order formalism and gauge 2028 -> eccentric and inclined sources and codes 2029 -> compute and cross-code validation, results 2030. That is roughly three to five years ahead of a pre-AI path that aimed to finish before the 2035 launch (analyst judgment, no source). In S3 cognition is near-free from 2029, but compute and independent-code validation still bind, so S3 is a year earlier and still Medium. Bands are judgments.
science-second-order-self-force.strongest_case_small: LISA's science date is fixed by its 2035 launch, so finishing early buys risk reduction, not earlier science; and offline-online surrogates still need validation against independent codes.
science-second-order-self-force.signpost: First second-order self-force results for eccentric orbits or a Kerr background by 2028, with AI credited in methods or authorship.
science-second-order-self-force.revision_note: B-science resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic (resolver checked): generic Kerr orbits are partly research-hard (second-order metric reconstruction and gauge in Kerr are open; first-order adiabatic Kerr inputs exist only for equatorial orbits) and then compute- and validation-bound, so S2 2029->2030, S3 2028->2029, S3 High->Medium; 'four to six years' replaced by 'roughly three to five years (analyst judgment)', as the auditor asked. science-nr-precision.title: Merger simulations precise enough for LISA's loudest signals
science-nr-precision.description: LISA will see massive black-hole mergers at signal-to-noise ratios in the hundreds to thousands, where waveform error dominates the error budget. Simulations need mismatches near 1e-6 (indistinguishability scales as ~1/(2 SNR^2), general) at mass ratios above 10 and spins near 0.9, versus a median resolution difference of ~4e-4 today.
science-nr-precision.status_oct2026: SXS third catalog (CQG, Oct 2025; arXiv 2505.13378): 3,756 configurations at about 480 million core-hours in total; median resolution difference 4e-4; precessing runs cover q<=8 and |chi|<=0.8, plus over 100 runs between q=8 and q=20 (mostly with spin only on the larger hole); longest run 148 orbits. Mismatch reaches ~1e-1 for ~180-orbit runs (arXiv 2502.14025). Bias studies show neglected harmonics and eccentricity bias LISA parameters (arXiv 2502.12237, 2602.09088, 2601.07739). GPU code generation for NR emerging (arXiv 2501.14030; up to 16x single-precision speedups for an elliptic solver).
science-nr-precision.why: A ~400x accuracy gain (from 4e-4 to ~1e-6), at mass ratios and spins beyond current precessing coverage, requires better formulations, a-posteriori error estimators, high-order codes, local time-stepping and GPU ports (cognitive, compresses under S2; AI-discovered algorithms help), then very large compute allocations: the current catalog alone took about 480 million core-hours (capital, compresses little). That is why S3 is no better than Medium: compute time and wall-clock at high mass ratio bind even when cognition is free. Bands are judgments.
science-nr-precision.strongest_case_small: Accuracy can also be bought by hybridizing NR with self-force and effective-one-body models, which the field already does; AI mostly speeds code work, and the 2035 launch sets the deadline.
science-nr-precision.signpost: A public catalog with precessing runs at mass ratio >= 16 and mismatch <= 1e-5; NR codes shipping certified error estimates.

science-retrieval-identifiability.title: Exoplanet atmosphere readings with honest error bars
science-retrieval-identifiability.description: Theorems and certified tools stating which molecules, abundances and temperature structures a given spectrum can and cannot determine (identifiability), plus retrieval methods robust to wrong one-dimensional model assumptions. Turns today's 'parallel interpretations' into quantified, comparable claims.
science-retrieval-identifiability.status_oct2026: JWST shows 'established inverse methods ... can lead to disparate interpretations even with JWST's quality of data' (Seager et al., PNAS, Sep 2025). The K2-18 b DMS signal remains disputed (homogeneous MIRI survey, ApJL Sep 2026; 661-molecule agnostic search, ApJL May 2026; Hycean vs mini-Neptune debate, arXiv 2605.17803). Linearized information-content theory (Rodgers optimal estimation, averaging kernels) is standard and has been applied to exoplanet retrievals for over a decade (general); missing is identifiability under nonlinearity, multimodality and model misspecification (1D versus 3D).
science-retrieval-identifiability.why: Identifiability maps tell observers which wavelength range, resolution and SNR make a molecule recoverable; robust inference stops 1D-model misspecification from producing false detections. That shortens claim-and-rebuttal cycles and feeds HWO's wavelength and resolution requirements (as acceleration, not a prerequisite). Pure applied mathematics and statistics; the gate is community adoption. S3 equals S2 through 2027, so 2028.
science-retrieval-identifiability.strongest_case_small: Degeneracies are physics, not math: if the spectrum lacks the information, no theorem creates it. JWST's noise floor, stellar contamination and opacity errors are the real limits.

science-coronagraph-limits.title: Proven limits for starlight suppression
science-coronagraph-limits.description: Sharp, provable bounds on how much planet light any coronagraph can deliver at a given inner working angle, bandwidth and 1e-10 contrast for HWO's candidate apertures (on-axis segmented versus off-axis), plus designs that approach them. Shows which architectures cannot meet the 25-exo-Earth goal before money is spent.
science-coronagraph-limits.status_oct2026: HWO needs raw contrast ~1e-10 and 1-sigma photometric precision ~3e-12 (arXiv 2510.02547, Oct 2025); vortex and forked-grating designs under study (JATIS, Sep 2026); coronagraph design is already posed as optimization with electric-field conjugation (JATIS 2022); an analytic error budget from optical disturbances to flux-ratio noise appeared Sep 2026 (arXiv 2609.32023). Ideal-coronagraph limits exist only for idealized apertures (general).
science-coronagraph-limits.why: Coronagraph design reduces to optimization over linear optical operators, where convex duality yields provable upper bounds (a ceiling, P3) and the primal solution yields designs (P4, if manufacturable). Linear-programming designs of apodized-pupil coronagraphs for segmented apertures already certify optimality within a design family (N'Diaye, Zimmerman et al. 2016, general); the new P3 content is a bound across architectures. HWO's architecture down-select was expected over roughly 2027-30, so a ceiling arriving in 2027-28 could prune options while it still matters, but the down-select timing now depends on Congress restoring the HWO line (FY2027 request $5M against $150M enacted in FY2026). It accelerates HWO design closure and wavefront-control work; neither needs it first, because HWO can close on numerically optimized designs.
science-coronagraph-limits.strongest_case_small: Achieved contrast is set by mask fabrication tolerances, polarization aberrations, detector noise and stability, not by the optimality of the design; Roman's coronagraph experience shows hardware dominates.
science-coronagraph-limits.signpost: HWO architecture trade documents citing provable throughput bounds; testbed results at 1e-10 broadband with AI-designed masks.

science-wfsc-certified.title: Picometer-stable telescopes with guaranteed control
science-wfsc-certified.description: Wavefront sensing-and-control loops with proven convergence and robustness bounds against thermal and vibration disturbances, co-designed with the error budget, keeping contrast drift below ~1e-11 over hours-long exposures.
science-wfsc-certified.status_oct2026: HWO EAC1 modeling shows significant thermal and vibrational disturbances (JATIS 12(4) 041012, May 2026); segment-level sensing and control studies (JATIS 041024, Jul 2026). Roman launched Aug 30 2026 and took its first coronagraph observation Sep 30 2026 (NASA), the first space demonstration of active wavefront control for high contrast.
science-wfsc-certified.why: Control and estimation with guarantees is applied math (S2 2027-28); proving it works needs vacuum-testbed campaigns and comparison with Roman's in-flight coronagraph data (first observation Sep 30 2026), which take years and compress only 1.1-1.5x (experiment gate). AI-designed test campaigns and self-running test stands help. Testbed time for HWO-level stability is funded through HWO technology maturation, which depends on Congress restoring the FY2027 HWO line ($5M requested), so even S3 stays Medium. Bands are judgments. Lazuli's coronagraph (data about 2029-31) adds flight wavefront-control data outside the HWO line, at about 1e-8 raw contrast (arXiv 2601.02556).
science-wfsc-certified.strongest_case_small: Control theory is not the bottleneck: metrology, deformable mirrors, detectors and thermal engineering are, and testbed time is scarce.

science-hwo-design-closure.title: Habitable Worlds Observatory design closed by AI modeling
science-hwo-design-closure.description: End-to-end integrated models (structure, thermal, optics, coronagraph, retrieval, survey yield) run and optimized by AI and used to freeze HWO's aperture, coronagraph type, wavelength range and stability requirements with quantified science yield.
science-hwo-design-closure.status_oct2026: HWO is in pre-formulation under NASA's Great Observatory Maturation Program (2023), studying Engineering Architecture Concepts (EACs); industry technology proposals were announced Jan 5 2026; exposure-time and yield tools exist (pyEDITH, arXiv 2608.28477; EXOSIMS dynamic scheduling, JATIS May 2026); launch in the 2040s with a 6-8 m primary mirror, larger if launch vehicles allow (Wikipedia). Budget: Congress enacted $150M for HWO in FY2026, but the FY2027 request is $5M, within a 47% cut to the Science Mission Directorate and a 23% cut to NASA ($18.8B versus $24.4B).
science-hwo-design-closure.why: Two things are needed by 2031: an agency freeze of aperture, coronagraph type, wavelength range and stability requirements, and AI-run integrated modeling materially used in it. Under S2, multiphysics design optimization arrives in 2028 and could close the requirement tree with fewer contractor study cycles, but the freeze is an agency decision that follows appropriations, which compress 1.0x in every scenario, so S3 is no earlier than S2. With the FY2027 request cutting HWO to $5M, a freeze by 2031 depends on Congress restoring the line (science-smd-budget-restored, Medium); with roughly 40-50% for a freeze and about 50% for material AI use, the joint chance is Low in every scenario (judgment). science-vlbi-identifiability.title: What space interferometry can prove about black holes
science-vlbi-identifiability.description: Identifiability and stability theorems for sparse-aperture imaging: which Earth-space baselines (lengths, orientations, frequencies) uniquely determine a black hole's photon-ring diameter and shape, and hence its spin and the Kerr hypothesis, despite unknown plasma emission and station gain errors.
science-vlbi-identifiability.status_oct2026: Reconstructing images from sparse, corrupted Fourier samples is 'a challenging inverse problem' (ApJ, Jan 2026); BHEX targets the photon ring with the first submillimeter Earth-space VLBI (SPIE, Aug 2026). No catalog family applies: the catalog's inverse-problem results (365, 372) concern elliptic boundary data, not Fourier sampling.
science-vlbi-identifiability.why: Orbit and baseline choices for a space-VLBI mission are fixed at proposal time. A theorem stating which baseline sets make ring parameters identifiable (and which cannot, a ceiling) arrives after BHEX's 2026 Small Explorer proposal has fixed its orbit; it can inform a Phase A study if BHEX is selected, and ngEHT siting. Instrument design via inverse-problem theory, acting in 1-2 years. It accelerates BHEX rather than gating it: the team already forecasts spin constraints with Fisher-matrix analysis (arXiv 2608.23672).
science-vlbi-identifiability.strongest_case_small: Mission design already uses simulation-based trade studies; theorems mostly confirm what simulations show, and angular resolution is set by baseline length over wavelength regardless.
science-vlbi-identifiability.signpost: BHEX or ngEHT design documents citing proven identifiability conditions for baseline selection.
science-vlbi-identifiability.revision_note: B-science resolver (2026-10-07): Skeptic + auditor: the theorem arrives after BHEX's 2026 Small Explorer proposal (cap-research-math-public is 2027 in S2), so it cannot steer that proposal; why rewritten. science-bhex-flight.title: First space mission to sharpen black-hole images flies

science-cosmo-certified-inference.title: Cosmology inference that knows its own errors
science-cosmo-certified-inference.description: Simulation-based inference, emulators and covariance estimates with proven calibration and error bounds, so Stage-IV surveys (DESI, Euclid, Rubin, Roman) can separate new physics from analysis artefacts with far fewer expensive simulations.
science-cosmo-certified-inference.status_oct2026: Field-level weak-lensing inference with only 60 N-body simulations (Jun 2026); benchmarks of exact, emulated and simulation-based inference (ApJ, Jun 2026); 3x2pt simulation-based pipelines (arXiv 2609.24946, Sep 2026). Catalog 374 (sharp 1/3 stability of optimal-transport maps, T1) bears on error propagation in optimal-transport reconstruction of cosmic initial conditions; catalog 139 (subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling, T3) assumes well-conditioned log-concave targets that real posteriors are not. Both theory-only.
science-cosmo-certified-inference.premise_tier: n/a (catalog links conditional, T1/T3, not load-bearing)
science-cosmo-certified-inference.why: Coverage guarantees and certified emulator errors let collaborations trust neural inference and cut simulation budgets. The guarantees hold only relative to the simulator, so misspecification (baryonic feedback, photometric redshifts) is not covered. The gate is collaborations' slow, blinded validation: Stage-IV pipelines are frozen 1-2 years before unblinding, and Rubin's first cosmology analyses and Euclid's second release fall around 2029-31 (general), so key-project adoption by 2031 is about even odds in S2 (Medium) and likely only in S3. Simulation-based inference without formal guarantees is already used (KiDS, DES, general); the increment is the guarantee. S3 equals S2 through 2027, so 2028. Bands are judgments.
science-cosmo-certified-inference.strongest_case_small: The dominant survey systematics are astrophysical (baryonic feedback, photometric redshifts, intrinsic alignments, shear calibration), not inference mathematics; and collaborations validate pipelines slowly by design.
science-cosmo-certified-inference.signpost: Euclid or Rubin key-project analyses adopting simulation-based inference with formal coverage guarantees.

science-dark-energy-verdict.title: Is dark energy changing? A decisive answer
science-dark-energy-verdict.description: Confirmation at >=5 sigma of DESI's hint that dark energy evolves, or the preference falling below ~2-3 sigma, using final DESI data combined with Euclid, Rubin, Roman and CMB data.
science-dark-energy-verdict.status_oct2026: DESI DR2 BAO (PRD, 2025) is consistent with DR1; preference for dynamical dark energy does not diminish from DR1 to DR2 (Nature Astronomy, Sep 2025), though some non-parametric reconstructions find reduced support (MNRAS, Dec 2025). Roman launched Aug 30 2026.
science-dark-energy-verdict.why: Photon-limited: the answer arrives with survey data releases (science-stage4-survey-data). The analyses use standard compressed likelihoods, so certified inference accelerates and de-risks the verdict but does not gate it. AI shortens the analysis lag by perhaps a year and lowers the chance a systematic is mistaken for physics; it does not change the answer or bring the data forward.
science-dark-energy-verdict.strongest_case_small: This is the clearest case where AI mathematics barely matters: same band in all scenarios.
science-dark-energy-verdict.signpost: Combined DESI final and Euclid DR1 analyses (2027-28).

science-helio-tomography.title: 3D Sun-to-Earth reconstructions with guarantees
science-helio-tomography.description: Uniqueness and stability theory, plus certified algorithms, for reconstructing the 3D corona and solar wind (density and magnetic structure) from a few viewpoints and polarized light, a problem now solved with ad hoc regularization.
science-helio-tomography.status_oct2026: PUNCH (NASA Small Explorer, launched 2025) uses polarization to place structures in 3D (Solar Physics, 2026); discrete polarimetric tomography of CMEs tested on synthetic multi-spacecraft images (Mar 2026); coronal magnetic-field extrapolation from surface data remains ill-posed (general).
science-helio-tomography.why: Limited-angle tomography has a mature mathematical theory to extend; AI applies it to polarized Thomson scattering and multi-viewpoint geometry, telling forecasters which features are determined by the data and which are prior. Feeds the plasma team's space-weather data-assimilation chain. The theory (P5) lands with applied math, but the signpost is operational adoption by space-weather centers (P6 default Low) and with one to three viewpoints the problem stays underdetermined, so S2 is Medium and only S3 High. S3 equals S2 through 2027, so 2028. Bands are judgments.
science-helio-tomography.strongest_case_small: With one to three viewpoints the problem is genuinely underdetermined; theory can only say what more data would be needed.
science-helio-tomography.signpost: Space-weather centers adopting tomographic CME products with stated uncertainty.

struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.title: Firmer math under elasticity, crack and inspection models
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.description: Independent confirmation of the release's elasticity and fracture results: smooth isotropic Lame moduli are uniquely determined by boundary measurements (372); metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch, plus a conductivity nonuniqueness theorem from full boundary data (365); regularity of planar Mumford-Shah crack sets (366); the 3D Ball-Evans approximation problem (368).
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.status_oct2026: 372, 366 and 368 are T1 (manuscript only). 365's Lean part (T3, unchecked by outsiders) is nonuniqueness for bounded measurable, uniformly positive scalar conductivities on a 3D ball: two conductivities differing on a set of positive volume have identical full Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps. The metric-and-connection recovery from one boundary patch is manuscript-only (T1). No outside Comparator report as of 2026-10-07. PDE formalization is weak in the release (3 of 16 PDE families).
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.premise_tier: T1 (372, 366, 368, and 365's recovery half); T3 (365 conductivity nonuniqueness)
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.why: These four families are the release's only direct contact with structural mechanics. 372 tells inspection engineers that full boundary data determine elastic stiffness in principle; it says nothing about how stably, and Calderon-type problems are typically only logarithmically stable (general), so it raises confidence without changing tools. 366 underpins the Griffith/Francfort-Marigo variational fracture energies behind phase-field fracture codes: minimizing crack sets are well-behaved in 2D. 368 is a technical tool for nonlinear-elasticity existence and approximation theory (invertible deformations), relevant to large-deformation finite elements. The conductivity half of 365 is a negative result: some bounded measurable conductivities cannot be recovered even from full boundary data (T3). This limits electrical-resistance damage sensing in carbon-fiber structures only if real laminate damage fields fall in such rough classes (judgment). Under S2, AI-assisted formalization of PDE catches up (2028), so confirmation by 2031 is likely. The 372, 366, 368 and 365-recovery parts are conditional (T1, no Lean main results), so bands are one step down.
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.strongest_case_small: Engineers already run elastography, guided-wave inversion and phase-field fracture codes without these theorems; uniqueness in principle is not stability; the counterexamples may live in coefficient classes (rough, anisotropic, non-generic) that real laminates never present.
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.signpost: An independent Comparator run on 365, or inverse-problems specialists endorsing 372 in a refereed venue, by end-2027; any SHM paper using 365's nonuniqueness construction to bound resistance-based damage sensing.
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.calibration_note: A3: T1 premise rule: three of the four families (372, 366, 368) are T1; only 365 is T3. One band down: Medium/High/High -> Low/Medium/Medium; why now marks the T1 parts conditional. struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.title: Hot spots conjecture (planar case) confirmed
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.description: Family 369 claims that on any simply connected planar domain, the slowest-decaying non-constant temperature mode of an insulated (Neumann) plate takes its maximum and minimum on the boundary, settling Rauch's 1974 conjecture for that class.
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.status_oct2026: T1 (manuscript only). Human results cover special classes: all Euclidean triangles (Judge-Mondal, Annals 2020; erratum 2022), lip-type and symmetric domains in higher dimensions (TAMS-B Apr 2026), convex hyperbolic domains with small eigenvalues, trapezoids and kites. A certified-numerics project (cert-machine, Zenodo, Oct 5 2026, not refereed; machine-derived with Claude, not from family 369) certified a non-symmetric convex trapezoid case.
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.why: A dead-end leaf for engineering, included to show the mapping honestly. Real radiators and panels are 3D, multi-material, with radiative (not insulated) boundaries, and thermal engineers compute their modes numerically for every geometry. The theorem confirms an intuition (slowest insulated thermal mode peaks at edges) and could inform sensor-placement heuristics for thin insulated plates; it changes no design. Effect on space thermal engineering: nil to negligible. Conditional: 369 is T1 (no Lean main result), so the band is one step below a checked result.
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.strongest_case_small: This node is itself the strongest case: radiative boundary conditions, 3D geometry and numerical design make the planar Neumann theorem irrelevant to hardware.
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.signpost: Expert acceptance (refereed version or endorsement by spectral-geometry specialists) by 2027. No engineering signpost is expected.
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.calibration_note: A3: T1 premise rule: family 369 is T1 (no Lean). One band down: Medium/High/High -> Low/Medium/Medium; why now says conditional.

struct-worst-imperfection-theory.title: Worst-case imperfection theory for thin shells
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.description: Rigorous answers to the open question of which manufacturing imperfections (shape, amplitude, number, location) most reduce the buckling load of thin cylinders and cones, with provable lower bounds on the knockdown factor given a factory's measured imperfection statistics.
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.status_oct2026: Genuinely open. Ubamanyu, Blond, Hutchinson and Reis (arXiv, Jul 2026) show the localized dimple, nearly worst-case for spheres, is not worst-case for cylinders, and find a statistical size effect; Wagner et al. (Proc. R. Soc. A, 2025) propose a regime-aware mechanistic design curve; NASA SP-8007-2020/REV 2 added semi-empirical and analysis-based design approaches to the 1960s lower bounds, but no worst-case imperfection theory underlies them.
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.why: This is a nonconvex variational and stochastic problem in nonlinear shell theory (Koiter asymptotics, energy barriers, extreme-value statistics of defect populations): bespoke research-grade applied math of the kind S2 makes routine by 2028. A provable lower bound tied to measured imperfection spectra is what lets designers replace empirical lower-bound curves with tighter, defensible knockdowns (see struct-flown-lighter-structure, which it now gates, and struct-shell-knockdown-rules, which it accelerates).
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.strongest_case_small: Humans are converging anyway (mechanistic design curve, probabilistic knockdowns, SBKF); boundary conditions and load imperfections, not geometric theory, drive much of the test scatter; any bound is only as good as one factory's imperfection data.
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.signpost: A paper (AI-assisted or not) proving worst-case imperfection families, or computing certified lower bounds, for axially compressed cylinders by 2028.
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.revision_note: B-certification: [skeptic, applied for consistency] status fact fix: SP-8007-2020/REV 2 is the current reference, not the 1960s bounds alone. struct-certified-uq-margins.title: Structural margins with certified uncertainty bounds
struct-certified-uq-margins.description: Reliability-based structural margins with rigorous rare-event probability estimates and quantified model-form error, as a defensible alternative to stacked deterministic factors (ultimate factors of ~1.25-1.4, model-uncertainty factors, test factors). Acceptance as a substitute for factors of safety is modeled in struct-cert-by-analysis.
struct-certified-uq-margins.status_oct2026: Practice is deterministic factors of safety (NASA-STD-5001 family, general) plus model-credibility assessment (NASA-STD-7009); probabilistic design used selectively. The release contains nothing on uncertainty quantification. 139 (subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling, Lean, T3) is theory for the posterior sampling such methods use. NASA-STD-5001B FSR 17 already lets the delegated Technical Authority approve probabilistic criteria case by case, while noting that experience has shown deterministic criteria to be adequate; uptake has been limited (general).
struct-certified-uq-margins.pathway: P1 (method availability; acceptance as a substitute for factors is P6, modeled in struct-cert-by-analysis)
struct-certified-uq-margins.premise_tier: n/a (139 is T3 but peripheral; constants unknown, so P4 effect marginal)
struct-certified-uq-margins.why: Reliability methods, multifidelity Monte Carlo and Bayesian calibration are largely solved in principle but expensive and expert-scarce per program; model-form error and high-dimensional rare events remain open. On-demand AI applied math makes doing this properly on every program affordable. Replacing a stacked factor of ~1.4 with a reliability-equivalent margin is worth up to ~10% of mass on strength-critical members only; stiffness-, minimum-gauge- and buckling-critical parts gain less (general). The binding input is validation test data for model-form error, not method, hence the data gate.
struct-certified-uq-margins.strongest_case_small: Factors of safety cover unknown unknowns (workmanship, unmodeled load paths) that no UQ captures; crewed-system safety organizations will keep deterministic factors; the method is not the bottleneck, test data are.
struct-certified-uq-margins.signpost: A launch provider or NASA/ESA program publishes reliability-based margins with quantified model-form error, computed for a flight structure alongside its factors of safety, by 2029.
