physclock-space-risk-models.title: Insurance-grade models of launch and in-orbit risk
physclock-space-risk-models.description: Risk models that insurers, brokers and operators' own risk-retention programs can price on: hierarchical reliability for launchers with few flights (borrowing strength across vehicles and subsystems with honest uncertainty), in-orbit failure rates with heavy tails and early-life effects, correlated fleet losses from space weather, debris and common-mode defects in serially built satellites, and third-party casualty risk from reentry, each with stated, validated uncertainty.
physclock-space-risk-models.status_oct2026: Space underwriting rests on loss history and engineering review in a small market of roughly half a billion dollars of annual premium (general). Single claims can exceed a year's premium: ViaSat-3 F1's antenna failure (May 2023) led to a claim of about $420 million (Wikipedia), in a year that also saw the Inmarsat-6 F2 loss (general). Most LEO constellation satellites fly uninsured in orbit, their operators relying on redundancy (general); the Feb 2022 geomagnetic storm destroyed 38 of 49 newly launched Starlink satellites (general). Reliability demonstration by test needs about 230 zero-failure trials for 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence (physclock gate table).
physclock-space-risk-models.why: The mathematics of small-sample, correlated, heavy-tailed risk is understood but expert-scarce, and space is an extreme case: few launches per vehicle, few failures, and losses that cluster (one storm, one design flaw, one debris event). Certified rare-event methods (S2 2028) and on-demand applied math let a broker or operator build such a model for each new vehicle or fleet; insurers adopt a year later (S2 2029). Achieved means a disclosed pricing, retention or capital decision based on such a model. The gate is data: failure and anomaly histories are proprietary and sparse, so models can be honest but not precise, and S3 adds a year but not a band.
physclock-space-risk-models.strongest_case_small: Premiums follow market capacity and recent losses, not model refinement; underwriters already combine engineering review with actuarial judgment; and the operators that matter most self-insure.
physclock-space-risk-models.signpost: A Lloyd's syndicate, broker or rating agency publishing a model-based rating method for new launchers or constellations; an operator disclosing a model-based self-insurance or captive decision; parametric space-weather cover offered to constellation operators.

S1 Medium 2033.

physclock-space-risk-models.gate_note: Sparse proprietary failure data binds; insurers adopting the models (adoption) is the runner-up.

physclock-space-insurance-capacity.title: Model-priced insurance for new rockets and constellations
physclock-space-insurance-capacity.description: Insurance capacity extends to risks the market now avoids or prices on scant history: launch cover for a new reusable vehicle after only a few flights at rates near those of mature vehicles, or in-orbit and correlated-loss (space-weather or debris) cover for a LEO constellation, written on model-based rating. Achieved when at least one such program is disclosed.
physclock-space-insurance-capacity.status_oct2026: The space insurance market is small (roughly half a billion dollars of annual premium, general) and cyclical: 2023 claims, led by ViaSat-3 F1 (about $420 million, Wikipedia), exceeded the year's premium (general). LEO constellations are largely uninsured in orbit (general).
physclock-space-insurance-capacity.pathway: P1->P5 (pricing practice; market capacity is not AI-math-driven)
physclock-space-insurance-capacity.why: Chain (S2): risk models 2029 -> one or two underwriting cycles before underwriters trust them -> the first model-priced program for a new launcher or constellation 2031. Capacity, recent losses and reinsurance appetite set this market (capital 1.15-1.3x at most), and the largest constellation operator has no need to buy cover, so better models change the price of a small market at the margin. The node is here so the tree shows the limit: AI math changes space insurance little by 2031.
physclock-space-insurance-capacity.strongest_case_small: The market is small and cyclical; one large loss resets rates regardless of models; and as launch gets cheaper, replacing a satellite can cost less than insuring it.
physclock-space-insurance-capacity.signpost: Launch cover for early Starship, New Glenn or Neutron customer flights at mature-vehicle rates; a disclosed constellation or parametric space-weather program; insurers entering rather than leaving the space market.

astro-noncooperative-capture-envelopes.title: Proven safe capture of tumbling debris
astro-noncooperative-capture-envelopes.description: Design and verification tools for capturing objects never meant to be caught: pose and tumble-rate estimation from passive imagery with stated error bounds, approach and synchronization trajectories proven collision-free under that estimation error, detumbling control with guaranteed convergence, and capture windows bounded by validated contact models. Extends astro-hybrid-rpo-verification, which excludes contact, to non-cooperative targets with no markers, no telemetry and unknown mass properties.
astro-noncooperative-capture-envelopes.status_oct2026: Astroscale's ADRAS-J approached an H-IIA upper stage to 15 m and completed a 360-degree fly-around in 2024, the first approach to a debris object in LEO (Wikipedia). ADRAS-J2, to capture and remove an H-IIA second stage, is planned for launch in 2027; ESA's ClearSpace-1 retargeted to PROBA-1 in Apr 2024 after its original target was hit by debris, and is now expected in 2028 on Vega-C (Wikipedia). Contact and capture behaviour is validated on air-bearing and robotic hardware-in-the-loop testbeds (general); no mainstream contact engine carries certified error bounds (see auton-certified-contact-sim).
astro-noncooperative-capture-envelopes.why: The cognitive part (estimation bounds, reachability under estimation error, detumble-control proofs) moves with applied math and RPO verification (S2 2028), plus a year to adapt it to unknown targets. The contact phase moves on the experiment clock: envelopes are only as good as contact models validated on testbeds, and a real target's tumble is known only in flight. S3 gains nothing over S2 because hardware-in-the-loop campaigns compress 1.1-1.5x. Medium in S2 because a removal operator must choose to put such tools in its safety case.
astro-noncooperative-capture-envelopes.strongest_case_small: Removal missions already fly with conventional guidance and test-based safety cases, and the hard part, grappling an unknown structure, is set by mechanisms and contact behaviour that proofs over unvalidated models cannot certify.
astro-noncooperative-capture-envelopes.signpost: Astroscale, ClearSpace or Starfish citing certified pose-and-tumble estimation bounds or capture reachability in a mission safety review; certified detumble controllers demonstrated on air-bearing tables.
astro-noncooperative-capture-envelopes.revision_note: E-safe-orbits (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2-S4 Medium -> High. S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2-S4 Medium 2030 (was 2029, the earliest year): a removal operator must put the tools in a safety case after a testbed campaign. High 2033 (was 2034) as removal missions fly 2027-35. S1 unchanged. Bands unchanged.
astro-noncooperative-capture-envelopes.note_2035: Several removal and servicing missions fly in 2027-35, so by 2035 one is likely to cite certified capture envelopes in S2-S4. S4 adds nothing because flight tests and contact physics bind.
astro-noncooperative-capture-envelopes.gate_note: Contact-model validation on testbeds and in flight (experiment) binds; estimation bounds, reachability and detumble proofs (cognitive) are the runner-up.

astro-adr-large-object-removed.title: First large debris object removed from orbit
astro-adr-large-object-removed.description: A servicing spacecraft captures a large non-cooperative object (a spent upper stage or dead satellite) and lowers it to reentry. Achieved by the first successful removal, whatever methods it used; the AI-math share shows only if the capture safety case uses certified envelopes (astro-noncooperative-capture-envelopes).
astro-adr-large-object-removed.status_oct2026: ADRAS-J flew around an H-IIA upper stage at 15 m in 2024; ADRAS-J2 is planned to launch in 2027 to remove an H-IIA second stage. Starfish Space holds a $52.5M Space Force contract, awarded through the Space Development Agency in Jan 2026, for an end-of-life disposal mission for Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture satellites, launch targeted 2027, with options for more (Wikipedia). ClearSpace-1 (EUR 86 million ESA contract, Nov 2020) is expected in 2028 on Vega-C to remove PROBA-1, after a 2026 date as recently as May 2023, and Astroscale's ELSA-M for Eutelsat, ESA and UKSA is expected no earlier than 2028 (Wikipedia).
astro-adr-large-object-removed.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
astro-adr-large-object-removed.why: Not an AI-math implication. Demonstrations and service contracts fly on their own schedules and AI math enters only through soft inputs, so this is an exogenous anchor and the P7 Speculative default does not apply. Four first tries from three companies are funded: ADRAS-J2 (2027), Starfish Space's paid disposal mission for the Space Development Agency (2027), ClearSpace-1 (2028) and ELSA-M (no earlier than 2028). Slips are common (ClearSpace-1 moved from 2026 to 2028) and capturing an unprepared object is a hard first. If each try has roughly a 40-60% chance of success by end-2031 (judgment, illustrative), at least one succeeds with roughly 80-90% odds, so High in every scenario. AI math changes the date little. Where it could show by 2031 is a second, cheaper removal with a shorter test campaign and safety review. Recurring removal depends on payers, which AI math does not change.
astro-adr-large-object-removed.strongest_case_small: The removal happens or slips for hardware and funding reasons, and debris removal stays a handful of government-funded demonstrations through 2031 regardless of better math.
astro-adr-large-object-removed.signpost: ADRAS-J2 launch and capture (2027-28); the Starfish disposal mission for the Space Development Agency (launch targeted 2027); ClearSpace-1 launch on Vega-C (2028); ELSA-M results.

physclock-production-acceptance-by-model.title: Satellites screened by statistics, not unit tests
physclock-production-acceptance-by-model.description: For lines building hundreds to thousands of satellites a year, acceptance screening (unit-level vibration, thermal cycling, burn-in) is set by models that combine process data, sampled testing and early-life fleet telemetry, with a certified bound on the rate of defective units that escape to orbit. Per-unit test time falls while infant mortality stays below a stated rate at stated confidence. Distinct from qualifying new designs (physclock-commercial-analysis-first-qual) and from designing development tests (physclock-optimal-test-campaigns).
physclock-production-acceptance-by-model.status_oct2026: Starlink v2 mini production reached six a day by Mar 2023 (Wikipedia, via the physclock gate table), and compute-satellite plans call for hundreds to thousands of units a year (struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet). The tree compresses the satellite-production ramp only about 0.9x (S2) and environmental screening 0.8-0.9x by 2031, because thermal time constants and workmanship screening are physical (physclock gate table). High-rate producers' acceptance practice is proprietary (general). Statistical process control and acceptance sampling are mature; bounding escape rates with correlated defects and fleet-telemetry feedback is bespoke (general).
physclock-production-acceptance-by-model.why: Fleet telemetry is what makes this work: thousands of identical units report early-life failures, so escape-rate bounds can be updated with every production batch. The math (sequential testing, hierarchical models of correlated defects, bounds on escapes) exists in pieces and is expert-scarce; on-demand applied math and certified rare-event methods (S2 2028) assemble it per line, and an operator carrying its own risk can adopt without a regulator (S2 2029). S3 is a year earlier because the adopter owns its data, its line and, increasingly, its own model. The gain is test-stand time and line throughput (a few percent to tens of percent of acceptance flow, assumption), not a better satellite. S1 Low: methods arrive 2030 with one year left.
physclock-production-acceptance-by-model.strongest_case_small: The largest producer may already do this with standard statistics and not publish it; for everyone else volumes are too low for fleet data to bound anything; and thermal time constants, not test planning, set screening time.
physclock-production-acceptance-by-model.signpost: A constellation or bus manufacturer disclosing sampled acceptance with model-based escape-rate bounds; Amazon Leo or a compute-satellite line reporting acceptance throughput; early-life failure rates published per production batch.
physclock-production-acceptance-by-model.revision_note: C-final integrator (2026-10-07): new node from C-sectors (space-sector coverage), accepted; title shortened from 'Mass-produced satellites screened by statistics, not unit tests'. | E-certification (2026-10-07): 2035 horizon and S4 review. S1 Medium 2033.

comms-certified-beamforming.title: Satellite antenna beams with proven emission limits
comms-certified-beamforming.description: Beam weights, element-failure compensation and calibration for large satellite phased arrays (direct-to-device arrays, broadband user beams) computed with certified bounds: guaranteed peak-sidelobe and out-of-band power-flux limits over a stated array-error model, and a proven gap to the best achievable pattern from semidefinite or sum-of-squares relaxations. Achieved means an operator uses certified beam patterns in production or in a regulatory or coordination showing.
comms-certified-beamforming.status_oct2026: Arrays are growing fast: AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 6 (deployed Dec 2025) unfurled the largest commercial communications array in LEO (Space.com via 33FG news, Dec 24 2025), and SpaceX bought AWS-4 and H-block spectrum for about $17B (Sep 2025) for V3 direct-to-cell satellites (33FG analysis, Sep 10 2025). The FCC's 2024 supplemental-coverage-from-space rules cap aggregate out-of-band emissions at -120 dBW/m2/MHz (general). Beam synthesis uses convex optimization and semidefinite relaxation for constant-modulus and quantized-phase constraints (Luo et al., IEEE Signal Processing Magazine 2010, general), but certified optimality gaps and worst-case sidelobe guarantees over element failures and calibration error are rarely computed at thousand-element scale (general). No catalog family addresses beamforming.
comms-certified-beamforming.why: Large direct-to-device and broadband arrays are limited by sidelobes and out-of-band emissions toward terrestrial networks, other operators and radio astronomy; a certified worst-case pattern lets an operator run closer to the limit instead of keeping a blanket margin. The math is nonconvex quadratic optimization with SDP relaxations and interval bounds over array-error models: bespoke, expert-scarce work that AI does on demand (P1) and that enters beam-design and scheduling software (P4). The relaxations are tight or near-tight for many beamforming problems (general), so what is missing is scale, worst-case error models and adoption, not theory. S2 Medium because the achievement must be visible (a showing, filing or operator paper) and vertically integrated operators may not disclose; S1 Low because public applied math arrives about 2029; S3 High. Signal processing had no node in the graph before this proposal.
comms-certified-beamforming.strongest_case_small: Operators already meet emission masks with conventional synthesis plus measured margins; phase-shifter quantization, calibration drift and thermal distortion dominate real sidelobes, and those are measured, not proven. Capacity gains from tighter patterns may be a few percent.
comms-certified-beamforming.signpost: A direct-to-device operator's FCC or ITU showing, or an operator paper, that uses certified worst-case sidelobe or out-of-band bounds over element failures, by 2029.
comms-certified-beamforming.revision_note: E-networks (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035: S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High. S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2 Medium 2029 (was 2028, the earliest year), High 2033 as phone-to-satellite arrays multiply; S3 High 2030 (was 2028). S1 unchanged. Bands unchanged.

comms-certified-beamforming.gate_note: A visible showing, filing or operator paper (adoption) binds; worst-case error models at thousand-element scale (cognitive) are the runner-up.

frontier-sequence-design-limits.title: Classic radar-code problems settled (checked)
frontier-sequence-design-limits.description: Two old problems behind radar pulse compression and spreading-code design, as claimed in the release. Family 179: real circulant Hadamard matrices exist only in orders 1 and 4 (Ryser's circulant Hadamard conjecture), which rules out binary Barker sequences of even length above 4; with the classical odd-length result, Barker codes stop at length 13. Family 076: real Littlewood polynomials can be asymptotically ultraflat, which implies that binary sequences with arbitrarily large merit factor exist (general), against the long-held belief that merit factors stay bounded near 12.3. Achieved means both formal statements pass an independent Comparator run and statement audit (T4).
frontier-sequence-design-limits.status_oct2026: 179: Lean-formalized (T3, unaudited) for the circulant Hadamard classification and the even-length Barker case; the paper's own odd-length classification is outside the formal statement (repo lean/docs/179.md), but odd lengths above 13 were already excluded by Turyn and Storer in 1961 (general), so nothing here rests on the unformalized part. 076: Lean-formalized (T3) for asymptotically minimal maximum modulus and finite-exponent flatness; the formal scope states the results are existential, with no effective convergence rate and no signing algorithm (repo lean/docs/076.md). The merit-factor consequence follows from flatness in the L4 norm and is not stated in the repo note (general). Practice: Barker-13 has been the longest known binary Barker code since the 1950s (general); the best explicit asymptotic merit factor is about 6.34 (Jedwab, Katz and Schmidt 2013, general); radar uses polyphase codes and mismatched filters, and GNSS uses Gold and Weil codes (general).
frontier-sequence-design-limits.premise_tier: T3 (Lean, unaudited): 179 circulant Hadamard classification and even-length Barker case; 076 existence of ultraflat real Littlewood polynomials. The odd-length Barker bound is classical (Turyn-Storer 1961), not an AI result.
frontier-sequence-design-limits.why: Both formal statements are short and well scoped, so independent checking is cheap and the checker already exists (verif-independent-check): High by 2027 in every scenario. Downstream is P3 only. The Barker result confirms what waveform designers already assumed. The merit-factor consequence removes a believed ceiling (about 12.3) on low-autocorrelation binary codes but supplies no code, rate or algorithm, so it can at most motivate AI code search (comms-code-design-on-demand); practical lengths (hundreds to tens of thousands of chips) sit far below where the existence proof says anything. This node is the catalog's coding-theory and signal-design entry point, previously unmapped, and it records that the space effect is nil to small.
frontier-sequence-design-limits.strongest_case_small: No radar, GNSS or comms waveform changes: designers already use polyphase codes, mismatched filters and Gold or Weil codes, and the merit-factor theorem is non-constructive with no rate.
frontier-sequence-design-limits.signpost: A Comparator run and statement audit on the 076 and 179 Lean statements by mid-2027; separately (watch item, not expected from these proofs), an AI search that publishes binary sequences beating the best known merit factors at practical lengths.
frontier-sequence-design-limits.revision_note: C-final integrator (2026-10-07): new node from C-disciplines, accepted with corrections: the odd-length Barker case is classical (Turyn-Storer 1961), so the proposed 'conditional (T1)' dependence was removed; the merit-factor implication is marked (general) because the repo scope note does not state it; title shortened from 'Binary code limits settled: Barker ends at 13, merit factors are unbounded (checked)'. | E-math-frontier (2026-10-07): band_2035 = band_2031; S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Kept High 2027: short, well-scoped statements and an existing checker. Bands unchanged.

frontier-sequence-design-limits.gate_note: Formal checks bind; outside acceptance (adoption) is the runner-up.

struct-hv-power-bus-stability.title: Proven-stable power grids for big spacecraft and Moon bases
struct-hv-power-bus-stability.description: Large-signal stability and fault-protection proofs for high-voltage DC power systems feeding many constant-power loads (compute racks, electric-propulsion power processing units, electrolysis cells): Lyapunov, passivity or sum-of-squares certificates for the bus with its converters, filters and batteries; machine-checked converter control firmware; and certified protection coordination for kilometre-scale lunar surface grids. Replaces small-signal impedance-ratio rules with margin (Middlebrook-type criteria) as the design basis. Achieved means at least one 100 kW-class spacecraft or lunar surface power design uses certificate-based or machine-checked large-signal stability analysis in its design review.
struct-hv-power-bus-stability.status_oct2026: Constant-power loads destabilize DC buses through negative incremental impedance; spacecraft studies date to the 1980s, and existence and stability conditions for DC microgrids with constant-power loads are still active research (IEEE Trans. Power Systems 2018; Scientific Reports 2025; via OpenAlex). Practice uses small-signal impedance specifications with margin (general). Orbital compute raises satellite power to the 150-250 kW class (Starmind AI1, see the orbital-compute-power branch), high-voltage buses are limited by SiC single-event burnout (materials-wbg-rad-hard-power) and LEO plasma arcing (general), and lunar plans need distribution from a 100 kWe-class reactor over kilometres (struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe). No catalog family addresses power-system stability.
struct-hv-power-bus-stability.why: At 100 kW and above, with many switching loads, bus instability and fault propagation become design drivers; certified large-signal stability lets designers shrink input filters and margins and run higher voltage with confidence. The mathematics (Lyapunov or passivity certificates for nonlinear switched systems, SOS programs, verified firmware) is known but expert-scarce, so AI on demand (P1) plus proof agents (P2) can make it routine. S2 Medium because power engineers have working conservative methods and the payoff is mass and risk at the margin; S1 Low (public applied math about 2029); S3 High. Electrical power engineering had one node (SiC parts) in v2 and no system-level node.
struct-hv-power-bus-stability.strongest_case_small: Spacecraft buses are already designed stable with conservative impedance rules; flight failures come from parts, arcing and thermal problems rather than bus dynamics, and the filter mass saved is a few percent of power-system mass.
struct-hv-power-bus-stability.signpost: A 100 kW-class spacecraft or lunar surface power design review that cites machine-checked or certificate-based large-signal stability analysis, by 2029.
struct-hv-power-bus-stability.revision_note: C-final integrator (2026-10-07): new node from C-disciplines (downstream-discipline coverage), accepted; title shortened from 'Proven stability for 100 kW-class spacecraft and lunar power grids'. Achievement criterion added. | E-orbital-compute-power (2026-10-07): 2035/S4 extension. band_2035: S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium a year after the earliest year (2029) because power engineers already have working conservative methods; High in S3 by 2031 (seed had 2028) and in S2 in 2034 as megawatt-class satellites make stability a design driver. S1 Medium 2032.

comms-photonic-inverse-design.title: AI-designed photonics with proven performance bounds
comms-photonic-inverse-design.description: AI-run inverse design of nanophotonic and flat-optics components for space (photonic-integrated couplers, filters and wavelength multiplexers for laser terminals; metasurface lenses and gratings for compact imagers and star trackers; lightsail metasurfaces), delivered with dual bounds that certify how close each design is to the best physically possible under Maxwell's equations and fabrication constraints. Achieved means a space optical-terminal, imager or sail supplier reports a component designed with a computed optimality bound in a design review, qualification unit or flight unit.
comms-photonic-inverse-design.status_oct2026: Inverse design uses local adjoint optimization without optimality guarantees (general). Dual bounds via Lagrangian duality and semidefinite relaxation exist for small devices (Angeris, Vuckovic and Boyd, 'Computational bounds for photonic design', ACS Photonics 2019; 'Bounds as blueprints', Optics Express 2026; via OpenAlex), but scaling to multi-wavelength volumes, fabrication tolerance and multi-objective problems remain open (general). Optical crosslinks are in serial production on broadband constellations (general). No verified flight of a metasurface imaging lens was found in this pass. No catalog family addresses photonic design.
comms-photonic-inverse-design.why: Photonic components for laser terminals, imagers and sails are PDE-constrained nonconvex designs; bounds tell a team when to stop optimizing and when a requirement is physically impossible (a P3-style ceiling), and AI makes both the designs and the bound computations cheap (P1, P4). Foundry turns and environmental qualification (radiation, thermal cycling) bind and compress only 1.1-1.5x, so S2 and S3 Medium, S1 Low. Optics and photonics had only telescope wavefront control (science-wfsc-certified) and sail metasurfaces in v2; no adaptive-optics, photonic-integrated or flat-optics design node.
comms-photonic-inverse-design.strongest_case_small: Terminal performance is set by lasers, amplifiers, pointing and detectors, not by passive-component efficiency; most space optics stay conventional refractive and reflective designs, and the bounds scale only to small devices.
comms-photonic-inverse-design.signpost: A space optical-terminal or imager supplier reports an inverse-designed photonic or metasurface component with a computed optimality bound in a flight or qualification unit, by 2030.
comms-photonic-inverse-design.revision_note: E-networks (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. Years kept. band_2035: S1 Low -> Medium, S2-S4 Medium -> High. S4 = S3. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2-S4 Medium 2030 (was 2029, the earliest year): design tools arrive 2028 and a foundry turn takes the first part to 2029-30. High S2 2034, S3/S4 2033 (several foundry and qualification cycles). S1 unchanged. Bands unchanged.
comms-photonic-inverse-design.note_2035: Laser-terminal and imager suppliers have several foundry and qualification cycles by 2035, so S2-S4 reach High and S1 Medium. S4 adds nothing because foundry turns and environmental tests bind.
comms-photonic-inverse-design.gate_note: Foundry turns bind; environmental qualification (radiation, thermal cycling) is the runner-up.

materials-ecls-isru-sorbents-catalysts.title: AI-found air-scrubber or fuel-plant material qualified
materials-ecls-isru-sorbents-catalysts.description: A carbon-dioxide sorbent, a Sabatier or reverse-water-gas-shift catalyst, or a solid-oxide electrolysis electrode found by machine-learned atomistic screening and autonomous labs passes a space-relevant qualification test (thousands of hours of cycling with humidity and trace contaminants, vibration, thermal cycling) for spacecraft air revitalization or Mars propellant production.
materials-ecls-isru-sorbents-catalysts.status_oct2026: ISS carbon-dioxide removal uses zeolite molecular-sieve beds and NASA's Four Bed CO2 Scrubber architecture is the successor; dusting, contaminant poisoning and regeneration energy are long-standing problems (npj Microgravity review, 2026; ICES 2025-26 papers; via OpenAlex). MOXIE made 122 g of oxygen on Mars in 16 runs (2021-23) by solid-oxide electrolysis (NASA 2023, general). Machine-learned screening is at scale but imperfect: Open DAC 2023 holds about 38 million DFT calculations on metal-organic frameworks (ACS Central Science 2024), and a 2025 correspondence in the same journal argued its top recommended sorbents were artifacts of the method. No catalog family addresses sorbents or catalysis.
materials-ecls-isru-sorbents-catalysts.why: Full chain (P7): (1) certified-uncertainty atomistic models and AI-run labs (materials-mlip-certified-uq, cap-autonomous-labs; S2 2028) -> (2) autonomous labs find a real new material (materials-closed-loop-discovery; S2 2029, Medium) -> (3) a sorbent or catalyst candidate survives humid, contaminated, cycled operation for thousands of hours in a space-representative rig (S2 2030-31) -> (4) an ECLSS or ISRU program qualifies it (S2 2031). Steps 3 and 4 run on the test clock (1.1-1.5x compression) and ECLSS programs fly heritage designs, so S2 Low, S3 Low at 2030, S1 Speculative. The payoff is lower regeneration power and fewer spares for closed-loop habitats and longer-life electrolysis stacks for Mars propellant, mostly after 2031. Chemistry and catalysis for life support and ISRU had no node in v2 (energetics and anodes only).
materials-ecls-isru-sorbents-catalysts.strongest_case_small: Sorbent and catalyst life in space life support is set by contaminants, dust and mechanical attrition that atomistic screening does not model; commercial stations will fly heritage ECLSS through 2031, and ML screening has already produced artifacts.
materials-ecls-isru-sorbents-catalysts.signpost: A NASA, ESA or commercial-station ECLSS test report or ICES paper qualifying an ML-discovered sorbent or catalyst after more than 1,000 hours of representative cycling, by 2030.
materials-ecls-isru-sorbents-catalysts.revision_note: C-final integrator (2026-10-07): new node from C-disciplines (downstream-discipline coverage), accepted; title shortened from 'AI-discovered sorbent or catalyst qualifies for life support or Mars ISRU'. | E-moon-mars (2035 horizon, S4): S1 year >2031 -> 2033; band_2035 S1 Speculative -> Low, S2 Low -> Medium, S3 Low -> Medium, S4 Low -> Medium. verif-ml-statistical-guarantees.title: Error-rate guarantees for onboard machine learning
verif-ml-statistical-guarantees.description: Distribution-free and finite-sample guarantees for learned components that cannot be formally verified: conformal coverage and calibrated false-alarm and miss rates under stated distribution-shift models, sequential change-detection bounds, and sample-complexity bounds for online system identification. Targets: terrain and pose networks, onboard science classifiers, and fleet telemetry anomaly detectors that clear reusable hardware. Complements formal verification (verif-nn-verification-scale) and runtime assurance (verif-runtime-assurance).
verif-ml-statistical-guarantees.status_oct2026: Conformal prediction gives finite-sample coverage under exchangeability, and weighted variants handle known covariate shift (general); flight is the shifted case, so guarantees must be stated under explicit shift models. Aviation guidance asks for generalization evidence for ML: EASA's AI concept paper (Issue 2, 2024, general) and SAE ARP6983 / EUROCAE ED-324 (first issue covers supervised offline learning; ED-324 publication scheduled Q4 2026, per verif-nn-verification-scale). Research GNC stacks pair learned components with verified runtime shields (e.g. arXiv 2606.25366, 2026). Catalog: 140 (Lean, T3): a one-pass learner with o(d^2) bits of memory needs about d log(1/epsilon) noiseless Gaussian samples where unlimited memory needs about d, a small P3 ceiling for memory-limited onboard estimators.
verif-ml-statistical-guarantees.premise_tier: n/a (capability premise); 140 is T3 (side link, small effect)
verif-ml-statistical-guarantees.why: Most onboard learned components will never be formally verified (verif-nn-verification-scale is Low in S2), so the practical alternative is statistical: calibrated coverage, false-alarm and miss rates with stated assumptions about distribution shift. Deriving bespoke guarantees for a given sensor, shift model and monitoring rule is expert-scarce applied probability that AI does on demand (P1). Representative calibration data and honest shift assumptions bind (data gate). High in S2 and S3 for the math being used in at least one flight evidence package; certification credit is a separate step capped at Medium and not claimed here. Statistics and learning theory for onboard ML had no node in v2 beyond formal NN verification.
verif-ml-statistical-guarantees.strongest_case_small: Guarantees under exchangeability break exactly where flight differs from training data; shift-robust bounds may be so loose that programs keep using runtime monitors and test campaigns, and teams already use conformal methods without frontier AI.
verif-ml-statistical-guarantees.signpost: A flight program's assurance case (lander, rover, reusable launcher or science spacecraft) that states conformal or finite-sample error guarantees for a learned component or anomaly detector, by 2029.
verif-ml-statistical-guarantees.revision_note: C-final integrator (2026-10-07): new node from C-disciplines (downstream-discipline coverage), accepted; title shortened from 'Statistical guarantees for onboard learning and fleet anomaly monitors'. | E-verified-autonomy (2035 horizon, S4): band_2035 S1 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 (no four-condition credit). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2 Low 2028, Medium 2029, High 2030: the math is on tap in 2027-28, use in a flight evidence package a year or two later. S1 High 2034.
verif-ml-statistical-guarantees.note_2035: S1 reaches High by 2035. S4 equals S3 because calibration data and shift assumptions bind.
verif-ml-statistical-guarantees.gate_note: Representative calibration data and shift assumptions bind; bespoke applied probability for each sensor (cognitive) is the runner-up.

verif-adaptive-control-proofs.title: Adaptive control of flexible spacecraft, proven stable
verif-adaptive-control-proofs.description: Stability and performance proofs for adaptive and learning-augmented attitude, pointing and structural control of vehicles whose dynamics are poorly known before flight or change during it: large flexible arrays and radiators, close formation clusters, propellant slosh in large tanks, on-orbit assembly that changes mass properties, and capture of objects with unknown inertia. Proofs must cover unmodeled flexible modes, actuator saturation and sampling, the cases where adaptive control is known to be fragile.
verif-adaptive-control-proofs.status_oct2026: NASA's SLS flew Adaptive Augmenting Control on Artemis I (Nov 16 2022; 'Path to First Flight of Adaptive Augmenting Control on NASA's Space Launch System for Artemis I', ESA GNC-ICATT 2023), cleared by analysis and Monte Carlo rather than proofs of robustness to unmodeled dynamics. Loss of robustness of adaptive control to unmodeled dynamics is a classic result (Rohrs et al. 1985, general); L1 adaptive control has flown on NASA's AirSTAR subscale research aircraft (general). Large flexible spacecraft fly with conservative notch filters and gain stabilization (general). No catalog family addresses adaptive control.
verif-adaptive-control-proofs.why: 100 kW-class compute satellites with large radiators and arrays, tight formation clusters, kilometre-class structures and in-orbit assembly all fly with dynamics that cannot be pinned down on the ground; today's answer is conservative fixed-gain control plus margin, which costs pointing performance and structural stiffness (mass). Proofs that an adaptive law stays stable with unmodeled modes and saturation would let designers use adaptation, as SLS already does, with evidence beyond Monte Carlo. The general theory is partly open, so bespoke proofs for specific vehicle classes are the realistic product (P1), changing design confidence (P5). S2 Medium; S3 High when cognitive work is near-free; S1 Low. Control theory in v2 covered optimal control, envelopes and runtime assurance but not adaptive or flexible-structure control. It builds directly on machine-checked GNC stability envelopes (verif-closed-loop-guarantees, S2 2027), now its hard prerequisite.
verif-adaptive-control-proofs.strongest_case_small: Robust fixed-gain control with notch filters works and is certifiable; the pointing and mass gains are small, and programs adopt adaptation for operational reasons regardless of proofs.
verif-adaptive-control-proofs.signpost: A spacecraft or launcher program publishes a stability proof (not only Monte Carlo) for an adaptive or learning-augmented controller with unmodeled flexible dynamics, used in its flight clearance, by 2030.
verif-adaptive-control-proofs.revision_note: C-final integrator (2026-10-07): new node from C-disciplines (downstream-discipline coverage), accepted; title shortened from 'Adaptive control of flexible, changing spacecraft with proven stability'. Hard prerequisite changed from cap-applied-math to verif-closed-loop-guarantees (adaptive-law proofs extend that machinery); no year changes. | E-verified-autonomy (2035 horizon, S4): band_2035 S1 Low -> Medium, S2 Medium -> High. S4 = S3 (no four-condition credit). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2 Medium 2029, High 2032 as large flexible structures fly more often; S3 High 2030 when cognitive work is near-free. S1 Medium 2033.
verif-adaptive-control-proofs.note_2035: By 2035 S2 reaches High and S1 Medium as large flexible structures fly more often. S4 equals S3 because the proofs are cognitive, even though S4 builds more of the structures that use them.
verif-adaptive-control-proofs.gate_note: Partly open adaptive-control theory (cognitive) binds; machine-checking the stability proofs (formalization) is the runner-up.

verif-hardware-proof-agents.title: Proof agents verify space processors and chip logic
verif-hardware-proof-agents.description: AI agents write the formal properties and proofs for space avionics hardware: RTL of radiation-tolerant processors and SoCs, FPGA designs re-verified after triple-modular-redundancy insertion, and error-correction and scrubbing logic, so that hardware gets the same machine-checked assurance proof agents bring to flight code.
verif-hardware-proof-agents.status_oct2026: Commercial hardware formal verification is mature (general), but property writing is the bottleneck. FVEval (DATE 2025) benchmarks LLMs on hardware formal verification and finds them not yet reliable; 2026 work on LLM-generated SystemVerilog assertions still reports wrong signal references and missing timing constraints (arXiv 2604.23100). Agentic chip design is moving fast in commercial EDA (Cadence ChipStack, Jun 2026; Synopsys autonomous workflows, Jul 2026; OpenAI-Synopsys agreement, Sep 30 2026; per capability-ai-eda-space-processor). Space FPGAs rely on TMR and scrubbing whose insertion is checked mostly by simulation and beam test (general). No catalog family addresses hardware verification.
verif-hardware-proof-agents.why: Proof agents for software are High by 2027 in S2 (verif-code-proof-agents); hardware is the same problem with better-established tools and a narrower property language, and the space-specific targets (TMR insertion, scrubbing, error-correction logic, post-mitigation equivalence) are well specified. P2, but in-house hardware sign-off needs no regulator step, so the regulatory cap does not bind; adoption does. High in S2 and S3 by 2031 for agent-written properties or proofs in at least one space processor or FPGA program; Medium in S1. Semiconductor and EDA coverage in v2 jumped from radiation physics to an AI-designed processor with no verification layer.
verif-hardware-proof-agents.strongest_case_small: Space chip and FPGA vendors use the same commercial formal tools as everyone else and will adopt agentic features when EDA vendors ship them; radiation behavior is set by physics and beam testing, which proofs about logic do not replace.
verif-hardware-proof-agents.signpost: A radiation-tolerant processor or space-FPGA program (vendor or prime) reports agent-generated formal properties or proofs in its verification sign-off, by 2029.
verif-hardware-proof-agents.revision_note: C-final integrator (2026-10-07): new node from C-disciplines (downstream-discipline coverage), accepted; title shortened from 'Proof agents verify spacecraft processors and FPGA logic'. | E-orbital-compute-power (2026-10-07): 2035/S4 extension. band_2035: S1 Medium -> High. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium in 2028 (the bar is agent-written proofs in one space processor or FPGA program); High in 2030 in S2 and 2029 in S3/S4, since 2025-26 benchmarks still found LLM-written assertions unreliable (seed had 2028). S1 Medium 2030, High 2033.

materials-hts-magnet-models.title: Validated models of superconducting magnets
materials-hts-magnet-models.description: Predictive, validated models for REBCO high-temperature-superconductor coils: quench onset and propagation, screening-current field errors, mechanical strain and delamination, and radiation damage to the conductor, accurate enough to design magnets with smaller margins and fewer full-coil tests. Space uses: active radiation shielding, magnetic nozzles and high-power plasma thrusters, magnetic spectrometers, and compact fusion devices.
materials-hts-magnet-models.status_oct2026: REBCO magnets underpin compact fusion (a 20 T large-bore HTS test coil in 2021, general) and are proposed for space spectrometers and active shielding (ARCOS HTS demonstrator coil, ICRC 2021; via OpenAlex). Quench detection is hard in REBCO because normal zones propagate slowly (general), and radiation-induced defect effects on pinning are under active study (Sci, 2026 review). The release's condensed-matter families (261 Anderson localization, 267 positive-temperature Bose-Einstein condensation, 271 Bloch's law and ferromagnetic order) are rigorous many-body results with no pathway to magnet engineering (nil); no catalog family addresses superconducting magnets.
materials-hts-magnet-models.why: Magnet makers already run multiphysics codes; what is missing is validated prediction of quench and screening currents across coil designs, which needs coil tests (experiment gate, 1.1-1.5x compression). AI speeds the modeling and inverse fitting to test data (P1) but the product is new theory turned into design tools (P6), whose default band is Low: S2 Low, S3 Medium when cognitive work is near-free, S1 Low. The space consequence by 2031 is small: active shielding stays Speculative (plasma-active-shielding) and magnetic-nozzle and fusion propulsion are post-2031; the main near-term beneficiary is terrestrial fusion magnet design. Condensed matter (superconductors) had no node in v2; this node records that the answer for space is mostly 'not by 2031'.
materials-hts-magnet-models.strongest_case_small: Conductor supply, cost and coil test campaigns, not models, pace HTS magnets; the leading fusion companies already have validated in-house codes, and no space mission by 2031 needs a large HTS magnet.
materials-hts-magnet-models.signpost: A public, validated quench and screening-current model that predicts a new coil's test results within stated error, from a fusion company or national lab, by 2029; any funded space HTS-magnet flight experiment.
materials-hts-magnet-models.revision_note: C-final integrator (2026-10-07): new node from C-disciplines (downstream-discipline coverage), accepted; title shortened from 'Validated models of high-temperature-superconductor magnets'. S2 band lowered Medium -> Low: P6 pathway default is Low and the proposal misapplied it. | E-plasma-nuclear (2026-10-07): 2035/S4 extension. band_2035 S1/S2 Low -> Medium, S3/S4 Medium -> High. Years unchanged. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S2 Medium in 2032 once SPARC's 18 TF coils and other fusion coil programs have supplied several years of test data; S3/S4 Medium 2030 (a year after the earliest year) and High 2034; S1 Medium 2034. Skeptic (validated quench prediction across designs is hard) vs advocate (abundant fusion-coil data): 2032 for S2.
materials-hts-magnet-models.note_2035: By 2035 fusion coil programs have supplied years of test data, so S1 and S2 rise to Medium and S3 to High. Robots could run more tape and small-coil tests, but full-coil campaigns and conductor supply bind, so S4 equals S3.
materials-hts-magnet-models.gate_note: Full-coil tests (experiment) bind; turning quench and screening-current theory into design tools (cognitive) is the runner-up.

robo-foundation-models-field.title: Robot AI models that work on sites they have never seen
robo-foundation-models-field.description: A robot foundation model completes a multi-step task class with at least 90% full-task success on held-out sites it never trained on (factories, warehouses or labs), with results published or audited by a customer. This is the capability that turns robots from single-task cells into general-purpose labor.
robo-foundation-models-field.status_oct2026: Figure's Helix 2.5 raised full-task success across 30 unseen homes from 9% to 56% with human-video pretraining (Figure, Sep 17 2026). Gemini Robotics 2 on Apptronik's Apollo 2 scores 68% on table picks and 32-92% on dexterous tool tasks (DeepMind, Jul 2026). Generalist's GEN-0 trained on 270,000 h of real manipulation data, growing 10,000 h a week, with up to 99% task success after 550+ h of post-training (Nov 2025). Physical Intelligence's partner Ultra ran a full packaging shift at 96.4% autonomy (Nov 2025). Epoch finds household robots 2-10x slower than people (Feb 2026). Training data grows 10-100x a year; Figure's Index collects about 4.9 years of human work on video per day (Aug 2026).
robo-foundation-models-field.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous robotics premise: the robot path defines S4; not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
robo-foundation-models-field.why: Generalization follows a power law in environment and object diversity (Hu et al., ICLR 2025), and diverse data grows 10-100x a year. S4 2028 is the scenario premise that dexterity becomes mainly software by about 2028: held-out success rises from 56% to 90% or more on structured industrial tasks. S3 has the same cognition and is dated 2029 because its slow robot path assumes the premise lands later. The 2x fleet difference in 2028 (0.46M robots against 0.24M) is worth only a few months of data at 10-100x a year growth. S2: 2030. S1 (task horizon doubling every 12-18 months): 2031 (Medium). AI mathematics is a second-order input here, worth about 1.1-1.5x on the robotics timeline through contact simulation and safety proofs.
robo-foundation-models-field.strongest_case_small: Benchmark success may not carry into paid work. Turning 50-95% task success into 99.x% deployment reliability takes real operating hours, and the driverless-car analog took about 13 years from the 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge to commercial service.
robo-foundation-models-field.signpost: A maker reports at least 90% full-task success on held-out factory or home sites (Figure, Physical Intelligence, DeepMind, Generalist) with the evaluation protocol published.
robo-foundation-models-field.note_2035: Reached in every scenario by 2035 (High). S4 is a year ahead of S3 by premise; its larger fleet adds only a few months of data.

robo-safety-standard.title: Humanoid safety standard ISO 25785-1 published
robo-safety-standard.description: ISO publishes 25785-1, the safety standard for dynamically stable industrial mobile robots (humanoids and other legged or balancing machines). It gives makers and notified bodies an accepted basis for uncaged work next to people.
robo-safety-standard.status_oct2026: Committee Draft stage in Oct 2026. Work started about Jul 2025 on a roughly 3-year track, so publication is likely about 2028 (inference from the ISO project stage). The EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 applies from 20 Jan 2027 and requires third-party assessment of safety functions that rely on machine learning (European Commission). Some deployments still run in cages: Digit at Schaeffler reportedly works inside a Plexiglas enclosure. IFR names safety standards as a barrier to humanoid use (Sep 30 2026).
robo-safety-standard.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous standards clock: not an AI-math implication)
robo-safety-standard.why: Uncaged work beside people needs an accepted safety basis. Without it robots stay fenced and lose most of their multi-task value. Chain: CD 2026 -> DIS 2027 -> publication 2028 on the normal ISO track. That is the optimistic end: first-of-kind robot safety standards have often taken longer (ISO 13482 took about 7 years, general), and a year or two of slip lands it in 2029-30. The committee clock barely responds to robot demand, so the year is the same in every scenario. High by 2031 because the project is already at CD and deployments can proceed under existing machinery rules meanwhile. The node is a standards-body publication. The regulator cap applies to conformity assessments, which sit in robo-proven-safety-envelopes and the deployment nodes.
robo-safety-standard.strongest_case_small: Standards trail practice. Firms can certify uncaged cells under existing machinery and collaborative-robot standards, and insurers or unions may set the real pace whatever ISO publishes.
robo-safety-standard.signpost: ISO 25785-1 opens its DIS ballot by end-2027 (a later ballot points to 2029); FDIS; the first notified-body assessment of a humanoid under the EU Machinery Regulation; the first uncaged humanoid deployments next to workers.
robo-safety-standard.note_2035: Published well before 2035 in every scenario. S4 gains nothing on the date. It gains wider use of the standard, because far more robots seek conformity assessment.

robo-proven-safety-envelopes.title: Proven safety envelopes for robots working beside people
robo-proven-safety-envelopes.description: Machine-checked bounds (control barrier functions, reachability sets, runtime monitors) on the behavior of learned whole-body controllers for humanoids or mobile manipulators. A maker uses them in a published safety case for uncaged work near people.
robo-proven-safety-envelopes.status_oct2026: Learned policies now run robot bodies: Figure replaced 109,504 lines of hand-written C++ with a 10M-parameter network trained in over 200,000 simulated environments (Figure, Jan 2026). Runtime assurance and barrier-function methods exist for simpler systems, and no humanoid maker has published a formal safety case. The EU Machinery Regulation requires third-party assessment of machine-learning safety functions from 20 Jan 2027. The capability research names formal safety certificates as one of the two places AI mathematics matters most for robots.
robo-proven-safety-envelopes.why: Code inspection cannot certify a learned controller, so a proof-backed envelope plus a runtime monitor is the shortest route to an assessable safety case. Chain (S2): research-grade applied math public 2027 -> barrier and reachability bounds for whole-body controllers 2029 -> first published safety case (Medium by 2031). S3 and S4: 2028. S4 equals S3 because cognition is the same and the maker incentive exists in both. S1: 2030 (Low). The effect on robot timelines is modest, about 1.1-1.3x, because data, hands and field hours bind harder.
robo-proven-safety-envelopes.strongest_case_small: Makers may satisfy assessors with testing, speed and force limits and conventional safety-rated monitoring. Proofs would then stay a research product.
robo-proven-safety-envelopes.signpost: A humanoid maker publishes a safety case that cites machine-checked bounds, or a notified body accepts one in an EU Machinery Regulation assessment.
robo-proven-safety-envelopes.note_2035: Routine in S2-S4 by 2035 (High). S4 creates more demand for the method, yet the year stays at the S3 value because the method rides the cognitive clock.
robo-proven-safety-envelopes.revision_note: E-robots (2026-10-07): new node in the robots branch (S4 Embodied, horizon 2035). S1-S3 follow the slow robot path, S4 the base path; the fast path is S4 upside. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium a year after the earliest year (S2 2030, S3-S4 2029); High once routine, S2 2033 and S3-S4 2032. S4 equals S3 because the method rides the cognitive clock. S1 Medium 2033. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

robo-contact-sim-to-real.title: Contact simulation good enough to train robot hands
robo-contact-sim-to-real.description: Policies for contact-rich, multi-finger tasks (fastening, connector mating, cable routing) trained mostly in simulation reach at least 95% success on real hands in production, with under 10% of the training data from the target site.
robo-contact-sim-to-real.status_oct2026: Simulation is fast: NVIDIA's Newton 1.0 reached general availability in Mar 2026, MuJoCo Warp runs up to 475x faster than MJX on manipulation (vendor), and GR00T generated the equivalent of 6,500 h of demonstrations in 11 h (Mar 2025). Locomotion already transfers from simulation. Contact-rich and tactile transfer is the open gap: DeepMind says multi-finger dexterity remains challenging, and Gemini Robotics 2 screws in a light bulb 36% of the time (Jul 2026). Part of the gap is parameter identification, which needs measurement.
robo-contact-sim-to-real.why: Synthetic data runs about 600x faster than real time, so a simulator that transfers for contact would lift the data limit on dexterity. Chain (S3): S3-grade applied math for complementarity and hydroelastic contact, plus tactile hands from one more 12-30 month hardware generation -> transfer on structured assembly tasks 2030 (Medium). S4: the same math plus friction and compliance data from a fleet twice the slow path's size, 2029 (Medium). The fleet data pins contact parameters, which is worth months and one year at most, since training data already grows 10-100x a year. S2: 2031 (Medium). S1: 2033 (Low by 2031). Robots and AI mathematics meet here: the math sets the contact models, and fleets supply the measurements that pin their parameters.
robo-contact-sim-to-real.strongest_case_small: Real-data scaling from human video and fleets may solve dexterity first and leave contact simulation a minor aid. Video carries no tactile signal, but robot fleets can record it directly.
robo-contact-sim-to-real.signpost: A maker reports production-grade multi-finger assembly trained mostly in simulation; published sim-to-real gaps under 5 points on contact-rich benchmarks.
robo-contact-sim-to-real.note_2035: Reached in S2-S4 by 2035 (High). S4 leads S3 by about one year through fleet contact data; tactile hands and the math set the pace in both.
robo-contact-sim-to-real.revision_note: E-robots (2026-10-07): new node in the robots branch (S4 Embodied, horizon 2035). S1-S3 follow the slow robot path, S4 the base path; the fast path is S4 upside. R-robots (2026-10-07): S4 2028 -> 2029 and band_2031 S4 High -> Medium: twice the field data is worth months, and tactile hands follow 12-30 month hardware generations (skeptic accepted). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium in the base-path earliest year (S4 2029, S3 2030, S2 2031); High three years later (S4 2032, S3 2033, S2 2034), keeping S4 a year ahead through fleet contact data. S1 Medium 2034. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

robo-requal-standard.title: An accepted route to requalify robot-made flight hardware
robo-requal-standard.description: A prime contractor, NASA, a NADCAP task group or an AS9100 supplement accepts a documented route for requalifying a special process when general-purpose robots replace human workmanship on flight hardware. At least one process at one supplier is requalified under it.
robo-requal-standard.status_oct2026: Replacing human workmanship on flight hardware is a process change under AS9100 and NADCAP special-process rules, and NASA-STD-6030 already requires per-machine qualification for additive parts. Requalification takes 6-24 months per process per supplier (S4 analysis). Specialized robots already pass this route: SpaceX's robotic welders and tile installers, Rocket Lab's fiber-placement machine. No general-purpose robot has requalified a flight-hardware process as of Oct 2026. Tesla's Model 3 missed its 2017 goal partly through over-automation (Automotive Fleet, Jan 2018).
robo-requal-standard.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous robotics premise: the robot path defines S4; not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
robo-requal-standard.why: Robots shipping does not put robots on flight hardware. Every replaced manual process must be requalified, so adopters dip before they gain (3-12 months per process for the first single-task processes at leading firms in 2028-30; an estimated 6-24 months per process per supplier in general). Chain (S4): a leading firm puts robots on single inspection or handling tasks in 2028 -> the first process is requalified and a prime or self-certifying firm documents acceptance criteria in 2029 (Medium by 2031, the regulator cap). This matches the brief's 2029 for handling, inspection and refurbishment and the early end of the S4 analysis's 2029-30. S2 and S3 (slow path): few robots are worth requalifying before 2031-32, so 2032 (Low by 2031). S1: 2034. S4 is High by 2035 because the route runs through mechanisms already in use: AS9100 change control, NADCAP audits and NASA-STD-6030 machine qualification. Multi-task factory usefulness speeds adoption but is not required for one process at one site, so that link is soft.
robo-requal-standard.strongest_case_small: Vertically integrated firms that self-certify their own vehicles (SpaceX) need no external route, so the node may matter only for suppliers and government programs.
robo-requal-standard.signpost: First published requalification of a flight-hardware process performed by a general-purpose robot; a NADCAP checklist or prime specification that names robot workmanship.
robo-requal-standard.note_2035: S4 reaches High by 2035 because thousands of robots in aerospace push the route through existing mechanisms. In S1-S3 few general-purpose robots reach flight hardware, so the route stays Medium or Low.
robo-requal-standard.revision_note: E-robots (2026-10-07): new node in the robots branch (S4 Embodied, horizon 2035). S1-S3 follow the slow robot path, S4 the base path; the fast path is S4 upside. R-robots (2026-10-07): S4 2030 -> 2029: the first requalified process can be an inspection or handling task, which the brief dates 2029 (advocate accepted). The proposed hard edge from multi-task factory work was rejected: one process at one site does not need 100,000 robots in multi-task work, so the link stays soft. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S4 Medium 2030, a year after the first requalified inspection or handling process, and High 2033. S2-S3 Medium 2033: few slow-path robots are worth requalifying before 2031-32; skeptic (2034) and advocate (2032) resolved at the year after the earliest year. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

robo-mtbi-1000h.title: Robot fleets run 1,000 hours between interventions
robo-mtbi-1000h.description: A maker or operator publishes fleet mean time between interventions (teleoperation, resets or repairs) of at least 1,000 h for a task class, backed by at least 2,300 failure-free robot-hours, the zero-failure demonstration at 90% confidence.
robo-mtbi-1000h.status_oct2026: No humanoid maker publishes mean time between interventions. Agility tracks it but reports only over 65,000 customer-site hours and about 98% on-task accuracy over 100,000 totes at GXO (SEC Form 425, Sep 15 2026). Physical Intelligence's partner Ultra ran a shift at 96.4% autonomy, about 17 minutes of help per 8 h (Nov 2025). Figure 02 at BMW logged 1,250+ h over 11 months, with the forearm as the top failure point (Figure, Nov 2025). IFR says most humanoid applications often need human teleoperation (Sep 30 2026).
robo-mtbi-1000h.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous robotics premise: the robot path defines S4; not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
robo-mtbi-1000h.why: Unattended 24/7 work needs interventions rare enough that one technician covers many robots. The best disclosed figures imply an intervention every few hours, so 1,000 h needs a 100-1,000x gain. Demonstrating it takes about 2,300 failure-free hours per task class, which a large fleet logs in days. Wear-out modes such as the Figure 02 forearm need hardware redesign, and hardware generations take 12-30 months whatever the fleet size. Chain (S4): 2028 models plus two hardware generations after 2026 -> 2030 (Medium by 2031). S2 and S3 (slow path): 2031 (Medium). S1: 2032 (Low). For scale, Waymo's miles between disengagements in California reports rose about 10x from 2015 to 2019 (general).
robo-mtbi-1000h.strongest_case_small: Interventions can be cheap. A remote operator who covers 20-50 robots makes a 50-100 h MTBI good enough for most factory work, so this milestone may not gate usefulness.
robo-mtbi-1000h.signpost: A fleet MTBI figure in a merger filing, shareholder letter or customer case study (Agility, Figure, Tesla, UBTech).
robo-mtbi-1000h.note_2035: Reached in S2-S4 by 2035 (High). S4 is about one year ahead of S3. Hardware generations set the pace, and fleet size does not shorten them.
robo-mtbi-1000h.revision_note: E-robots (2026-10-07): new node in the robots branch (S4 Embodied, horizon 2035). S1-S3 follow the slow robot path, S4 the base path; the fast path is S4 upside. R-robots (2026-10-07): S4 2029 -> 2030 and band_2031 S4 High -> Medium: wear-out fixes wait on 12-30 month hardware generations, which fleet size does not shorten (skeptic accepted). | R9-odds (2026-10-27): Medium in the earliest year (S4 2030, S2-S3 2031) since a large fleet logs 2,300 h in days once reliability is there; High two years later as the next hardware generation lands (S4 2032, S2-S3 2033). S1 Medium 2033. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

robo-actuator-magnet-supply.title: Precision actuators for 1 million robots a year
robo-actuator-magnet-supply.description: World output of precision actuators (planetary roller screws, harmonic or equivalent reducers) is enough to build at least 1 million humanoid-class robots in a year: roughly 14-34 roller screws and about 14 reducers per robot.
robo-actuator-magnet-supply.status_oct2026: Actuators are 40-60% of a humanoid's bill of materials. Leaderdrive made 433,655 harmonic reducers in 2025 and plans over 1M of capacity in 2026 and over 2M in 2027, about an 11-month doubling (Humanoid Guide); Harmonic Drive Systems makes about 2.2M a year. Epoch puts the reducer cap near 500,000 humanoids a year today (Apr 2026). Roller-screw grinding capacity is tight through 2027-28 (vendor claims). China makes about 94% of sintered magnets (IEA, 2024). Heavy-rare-earth export licensing has applied since Apr 2025, and the Nov 2025 pause of the Oct 2025 measures lapses about Nov 10 2026.
robo-actuator-magnet-supply.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous robotics premise: the robot path defines S4; not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
robo-actuator-magnet-supply.why: Actuators bind the ramp through 2028 on every path. Reducer capacity is documented: Leaderdrive goes from 0.43M units in 2025 to over 1M of capacity in 2026, an 11-month doubling. Roller screws are not: 1M robots need 14-34M a year, made on precision thread grinders with 6-14 month lead times, and no capacity figure is published. Chain (S4): base shipments reach 0.76M in 2029 and 1.7M in 2030, and the base path is sized to an 11-16 month capacity doubling, so capacity for 1M a year can exist in 2029. Medium by 2031: the slow path, a quarter of S4's weight, does not need it before 2033, and roller-screw grinding is unproven at this scale. S2 and S3 (slow path): suppliers build to demand, and shipments pass 1M a year only in 2034, so capacity lands about 2033 (Low by 2031). S1: 2034. Magnets do not bind at this scale: 2-4.5 kt of NdFeB is about 1% of the ~330 kt made in 2025.
robo-actuator-magnet-supply.strongest_case_small: Design substitution (planetary or quasi-direct drives, ferrite or low-dysprosium magnets) could remove precision actuators as a gate.
robo-actuator-magnet-supply.signpost: Leaderdrive above 2M reducers annualized in 2027; roller-screw output and thread-grinder orders; roller-screw lead times under 6 months; China's rare-earth decision about Nov 10 2026; magnet kg per robot in new designs.
robo-actuator-magnet-supply.note_2035: By 2035 base demand is 26M robots a year. Magnets then bind: 26-118 kt at 1-4.5 kg per robot (8-36% of 2025 output), so magnet capacity must roughly double. S1-S3 need only 1-2M robots a year, so the build-out is an S4 story.
robo-actuator-magnet-supply.revision_note: E-robots (2026-10-07): new node in the robots branch (S4 Embodied, horizon 2035). S1-S3 follow the slow robot path, S4 the base path; the fast path is S4 upside. R-robots (2026-10-07): Renamed to precision actuators; band_2031 S4 High -> Medium because only reducer capacity is sourced and roller-screw grinding is unproven at this scale; magnets moved to note_2035, where they bind (skeptic accepted). Id kept for cross-branch references. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S4 Medium 2030, not 2029: only reducer capacity is sourced and the slow path (a quarter of S4's weight) does not need it before 2033; High 2032. S2-S3 Medium 2033 as built to demand, High 2035. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

robo-structured-factory-useful.title: General-purpose robots do multi-task factory work at scale
robo-structured-factory-useful.description: At least 100,000 general-purpose robots (humanoids and mobile manipulators) do paid, multi-task work in structured factories and warehouses, including robot makers' own lines, at 50% or more of human output per hour and without routine teleoperation.
robo-structured-factory-useful.status_oct2026: Paid work today is single-task and small: only a few thousand humanoids do paid non-research work (S4 analysis). UBTech's Walker S2 reaches 30-50% of human output on simple tasks in Chinese auto plants and targets 80% by 2027 (Merics, Jan 2026). Figure's F.03 has done sequencing at BMW since Jun 2026. Foxconn runs fewer than 10 humanoids on a GB300 server line (Apr 2026). Musk said in Jan 2026 that no Optimus did useful work at Tesla (Electrek). Humanoid factories (BotQ, Fremont, Liuzhou) are built and staffed by people.
robo-structured-factory-useful.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous robotics premise: the robot path defines S4; not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
robo-structured-factory-useful.why: The capability-to-deployment gap for structured industrial work is about 2-4 years, and usefulness is dated by 12-30 month hardware generations. The bar is half a person's output per hour: a robot working three shifts then equals about 1.5 workers, which pays back a $20-30k robot in under a year. An 80% bar would sit near the S4 analysis's 0.85 for robot-first firms in 2031, far above today's 30-50% (UBTech). Chain (S4): models that work on unseen sites 2028 -> one hardware generation -> multi-task work by 100,000+ robots in 2029, when the base fleet is 1.2M (High by 2031). S2 and S3 (slow path, where robots stay narrow): 2031 (Medium). S1: 2032 (Low). Robot makers' own lines adopt first, because they own the robots and the data. Maker targets have missed by about 10x: Tesla planned 5,000 robots for 2025 and shipped about 150.
robo-structured-factory-useful.strongest_case_small: The business case can stay weak. IFR reports a weak case in industry today, and at 30-50% of human output a $35k robot pays back in 3-7 years at Chinese wages.
robo-structured-factory-useful.signpost: UBTech or a peer reports half or more of human output per hour on paid multi-task work; a factory reports 1,000+ humanoids doing multi-task work; humanoids do final assembly of humanoids.
robo-structured-factory-useful.note_2035: By 2035 S4's base path has about 25M robots in manufacturing and the slow path about 2M. S4 differs because usefulness lands two years earlier and the base fleet grows 10x over 2031-35, against 3.4x on the slow path.
robo-structured-factory-useful.revision_note: E-robots (2026-10-07): new node in the robots branch (S4 Embodied, horizon 2035). S1-S3 follow the slow robot path, S4 the base path; the fast path is S4 upside. S2-S3 Medium 2031 and High 2033. S1 Medium 2033. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

robo-fleet-1m.title: One million general-purpose robots in service
robo-fleet-1m.description: The active fleet of general-purpose robots (humanoids and mobile manipulators run by foundation models), counted at year end with a 5-year service life, passes 1 million units.
robo-fleet-1m.status_oct2026: Humanoid shipments were 13,318 in 2025 (Omdia) and about 19,000-25,000 in H1 2026 (Smart Analytics Global, Counterpoint, IDC), over 97% from Chinese makers. Leaders grow linearly within 2026: AgiBot reached 20,000 cumulative units on Sep 24 at about 5,000 a quarter (Humanoids Daily). The active fleet is about 70,000-100,000 at end-2026, against 5.0M industrial robots (IFR, end-2025). Bank forecasts for 2030 shipments run 0.45-1.2M (Goldman 0.89M, BofA 1.2M).
robo-fleet-1m.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous robotics premise: the robot path defines S4; not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
robo-fleet-1m.why: Fleet paths from the S4 analysis, 5-year life. Base (S4): shipments of 0.06M in 2026 grow 2.3x a year in 2027-28, then 2.4x and 2.2x as usefulness lands; the fleet is 0.46M in 2028 and 1.22M at end-2029 (High by 2031). Fast (S4 upside): 1M in early 2029. Slow (S1-S3): growth of 1.8x a year easing to 1.4x; the fleet is 0.86M in 2030 and 1.37M at end-2031, so 2031 (Medium). S1 runs a little slower because cognition lags: 2032 (Low by 2031). Base output doubles about every 10 months in 2026-31, the pace of US aircraft production in 1940-44.
robo-fleet-1m.strongest_case_small: A unit count overstates useful work. In 2026 most humanoids serve research, education, exhibitions and data collection, so a 1M fleet could hold far fewer productive robots.
robo-fleet-1m.signpost: Full-year 2026 and 2027 humanoid shipments. The slow, base and fast paths assume about 50,000, 60,000 and 80,000 in 2026, so 2026 barely separates them; 2027 does: about 90,000 points to the slow path, 140,000 to the base path and 240,000 to the fast path. Also watch whether quarterly output at AgiBot and UBTech breaks from linear growth.
robo-fleet-1m.note_2035: By 2035 the fleet is 4.6M on the slow path, 62M on the base path and 158M on the fast path. Every scenario passes 1M well before 2035; S4 passes it two years sooner.
robo-fleet-1m.revision_note: E-robots (2026-10-07): new node in the robots branch (S4 Embodied, horizon 2035). robo-fleet-10m.title: Ten million general-purpose robots in service
robo-fleet-10m.description: The active general-purpose robot fleet passes 10 million units, about twice today's stock of industrial robots.
robo-fleet-10m.status_oct2026: About 70,000-100,000 general-purpose robots are in service at end-2026, against 5.0M industrial robots built up over decades (IFR). Goldman forecasts 6.5M humanoid shipments in 2035 (Aug 2026). Epoch calls 1.5-3M robots a year by end-2030 clearly achievable after a demand shock and 5-10M a year plausible (Apr 2026).
robo-fleet-10m.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous robotics premise: the robot path defines S4; not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
robo-fleet-10m.why: Base (S4): 3.35M shipped in 2031; growth eases to 1.8x and then 1.6x a year as robots start working in their own supply chain; the fleet is 6.2M in 2031 and passes 10M in late 2032 (12.1M at year end; High by 2035). The year follows the base path, which defines S4. The fast path passes 10M in mid-2031 and gives the Low band by 2031. Slow (S1-S3): growth eases to 1.3x a year and the fleet is 4.65M in 2035, so after 2035 (Low by 2035 in S2-S3, Speculative in S1). After 2031 the caps are capital ($50-100B a year in 2031, $0.4-0.8T in 2035), magnets and the loop's own lead times (machine tools 6-14 months; factories 6-12 months in China, 2+ years in the West).
robo-fleet-10m.strongest_case_small: Every complex-machine ramp has slowed once a downstream gate bound. A base path that saturates at 1.3x a year after 2031 still passes 10M in late 2032, but a slower 2027-31 would push the date past 2035.
robo-fleet-10m.signpost: Bank forecasts for 2030 rising above 1.5M shipments; robot makers reporting multi-million annual capacity; China's 15th Five-Year Plan targets for embodied AI.
robo-fleet-10m.note_2035: S4 passes 10M in late 2032 and reaches about 62M by 2035 (30-104M across the loop sensitivities). S1-S3 stay near 4-5M, so the S3-S4 gap is mostly a 2032-35 story.
robo-fleet-10m.revision_note: E-robots (2026-10-07): new node in the robots branch (S4 Embodied, horizon 2035). S1-S3 follow the slow robot path, S4 the base path; the fast path is S4 upside. R-robots (2026-10-07): Year kept at 2032, the base-path crossing; the advocate's 2031 (fast path) rejected because the brief defines S4 by the base path and the fast path already carries the Low band by 2031. Text now says late 2032. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S4 Low 2031 (fast path mid-2031), Medium 2032 (base path late 2032) and High 2034, since the slow path (25% weight) never reaches 10M and High needs the base path nearly certain. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.

robo-mfg-10pct.title: Robots supply 10% of global manufacturing labor
robo-mfg-10pct.description: General-purpose robots supply productive labor equal to 10% of the ~460 million-person global manufacturing workforce of 2026, counted as human-equivalents (robot hours x productivity x productive share of the fleet).
robo-mfg-10pct.status_oct2026: General-purpose robots supply almost no manufacturing labor: a few thousand humanoids do paid work. Industrial robots number 5.0M, with 603,307 installed in 2025 (IFR), or 132 per 10,000 manufacturing employees worldwide.
robo-mfg-10pct.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous robotics premise: the robot path defines S4; not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
robo-mfg-10pct.why: Labor share = fleet x manufacturing allocation (40-45%) x human-equivalents per robot (0.5-2.0). Base (S4): 0.67% in 2031 and 8.7% in 2035, about 15% short of the line, or four months of growth, so 10% arrives about 2036. Fast: 1.9% in 2031 and 28% in 2035, crossing about 2034. Slow (S1-S3): 0.07% in 2031 and 0.32% in 2035 (Speculative). Within S4 the paths weigh slow 25%, base 55%, fast 20%. Early onset (71M robots in 2035) and a held 12-month doubling (104M) clear the line; saturation at 1.3x a year (30M) does not. The fast path plus the upper part of the base range gives about 30%, so Low by 2035, with the year on the base path. Supplying 10% of manufacturing and construction labor by 2031 would take about 35-70M robots, a sustained 3.2-3.7x a year.
robo-mfg-10pct.strongest_case_small: Robots concentrate where wages are high and tasks are structured. A US or Korean factory sector could pass 10% while the global share stays small, and the global figure may hide that.
robo-mfg-10pct.signpost: National statistics that show robot-hours replacing manufacturing hours; IFR reporting humanoid density per 10,000 workers.
robo-mfg-10pct.note_2035: S4's base path reaches about 8.7% in 2035, close to the line; if the US hosts 10-15% of the fleet, its share is 30-46%. S1-S3 stay under 0.5%.
robo-mfg-10pct.revision_note: E-robots (2026-10-07): new node in the robots branch (S4 Embodied, horizon 2035). S1-S3 follow the slow robot path, S4 the base path; the fast path is S4 upside. R-robots (2026-10-07): Kept at >2035 and Low by 2035. The advocate's 2034 Medium rejected: the fast path already represents the upper tail, so the chance by 2035 is about 30%, at the top of Low. Arithmetic added to why. | R9-odds (2026-10-27): S4 Low from 2034 when the fast path crosses; about 30% by 2035, at the top of Low. Bands at 2031 and 2035 unchanged.
